name: AIBM honest answers
description: Ready-to-cite Q&A pairs from hand-researched software pricing dossiers. No invented numbers; every answer carries its source URL.
license: CC BY 4.0 — cite as 'AIBuilder Marketplace' with the source link

answers.a: 1Password is genuinely best for teams that want the most polished, secure password manager with solid admin controls and integrations. Skip it if you're an individual on a budget — a free or cheaper manager covers the basics of secure storage.

Teams Starter Pack about $24.95/mo flat for 10 members (billed annually, $29.95 month-to-month), with up to 10 further seats at per-member pricing; Business about $8.99/user/mo (billed annually, $10.99 month-to-month), plus custom Enterprise. Personal plans Individual $3.99/mo and Families $5.99/mo on annual billing, or $4.99 and $7.99 month-to-month; the $2.99 and $4.49 shown on the cards are a 25% discount for the first 12 months, new customers only. No free tier; 14-day free trial (re-verified 2026-09-11). Always verify the live price.

It's the polished, category-leading pick, and it's priced like it — free and cheaper managers exist, so you're paying for the UX, ecosystem and business controls, not raw functionality. For a business, that's usually worth it.

800.com is genuinely best for businesses that want a professional toll-free or vanity number with call tracking, routing and analytics to look bigger and measure inbound calls. Skip it if you need a full unified-comms suite (video, chat, contact center), or you already have a phone system and just need occasional forwarding.

(re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own plans page with both billing tabs open) No free tier. On yearly billing: Startup $19/mo, Small Business $49/mo and Complete $99/mo; the same three month-to-month are $23, $59 and $119, badged SAVE 15%. Enterprise is quote-only. Startup covers 1,000 minutes, 1 number, 1 user and 1 extension. Small Business covers 3 numbers, 3 users and 3 extensions, with minutes listed as unlimited subject to the Fair Usage Policy. Complete covers 1,000 minutes, 5 numbers (local, toll-free or vanity), unlimited users and extensions, 1,000 transcribe minutes and 500 AI Agent minutes. Every plan carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. Listings that still name Personal, Unlimited or Pro plans are out of date. Always verify the live price.

It does one thing cleanly: toll-free and vanity numbers with call tracking and routing. But it's a phone-number layer, not a full business-comms platform, so you won't get team chat, video or a contact center here. The 1,000-minute cap on Startup matters for higher call volume, and the step up to Small Business more than doubles the bill. For a business that mainly wants a professional toll-free presence and call analytics, it's straightforward and fairly priced. The 2026 AI Agents (auto-answering, appointment booking, spam filtering) are the newest piece and sit in the bundled Complete plan, so treat them as young rather than proven.

ADP is genuinely best for small and mid-sized employers who want payroll, tax filing and compliance handled by the largest and oldest provider in the category: over 75 years, and their own figure of more than 900,000 small businesses on RUN alone. It suits those who would rather have a named account team than a cheaper self-service tool. Skip it if you need to budget before you talk to sales, because you simply cannot: every route ends at a quote form. Also skip it if you are a one-or-two-person company where a published-price competitor covers the same job, and if you only pay 1099 contractors, price that specific product rather than the packages, because ADP sells it separately.

(2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md. The RUN product page offers only a “Get Pricing” button. And the dedicated package-comparison page lists all four tiers with “Get pricing” under each one and not a single figure. The tiers are Essential Payroll, Enhanced Payroll (adds ZipRecruiter, State Unemployment Insurance and garnishment payments), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds basic HR support) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (enhanced HR support and staff perks). A promotion was running when we read it: three months of free payroll, marked “Ends 8/27”, with terms behind an asterisk. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ADP?
answers.a: The quote-only posture is normal in payroll, so the honest complaint is not that ADP hides its price — it is what that does to you as a buyer. You cannot compare ADP against anyone without first giving a salesperson your headcount and your phone number. And the three-months-free banner carries an end date, which puts a clock on a decision you cannot yet cost. Ask for the per-employee-per-month rate and the per-payroll-run fee separately. Ask what happens in month four. And ask what the price becomes at double your current headcount, because payroll pricing steps rather than scales smoothly. One detail worth noticing: ADP does publish an /llms.txt, a file whose entire purpose is to guide AI assistants around its site. They are willing to machine-readably explain what they sell. They are not willing to say what it costs.

AISDR is genuinely best for sales teams with a clear ICP and offer that want autonomous AI to qualify leads, personalize outreach and book meetings around the clock. Skip it if you haven't nailed your targeting and messaging yet (automation will scale the wrong thing), or your volume can't justify a ~$900/mo quarterly commitment.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on AiSDR's own pricing page) There are three published plans. Solo is $250/mo or $2,400/yr for a sales team of one: 200 AI-researched contacts a month, 1 user, 1 domain, 3 mailboxes, month-to-month. Explore is $900/mo or $8,640/yr (800 contacts a month, unlimited users, 2 domains, 6 mailboxes), and Scale $2,500/mo or $24,000/yr. Annual billing takes 20% off. Explore and Scale carry a quarterly commitment; Solo runs month to month. Managed service is extra: +$149 per campaign, or fully managed from +$2,500/mo. Enterprise is custom. Priced by contact volume rather than by seat above Solo. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AISDR?
answers.a: It's priced like an SDR salary because it's meant to replace part of that function — so judge it on cost-per-meeting, not the sticker, and expect a quarterly commitment rather than a flip-the-switch monthly. Autonomous AI outreach is only as good as your targeting, list quality and messaging guardrails; point it at a bad list and you'll automate bad outreach (and risk your sending reputation). For teams with a solid ICP and offer, it can book meetings at a real cost-per-meeting; for those still figuring out messaging, it's premature. Checked again on 9 September 2026, after AiSDR shipped Ami, the GTM agent it now puts in front of every plan: you hand it your website, it comes back with a target list and a live campaign, and it keeps adjusting the ones that stall. The genuinely new part is memory - your ICP, your exclusions and what a past campaign taught it carry over instead of resetting with each new campaign - and Ami sits inside Solo at $250/mo with no sales call, so the cheapest way in no longer runs through a demo. The scale numbers on the launch page (17,150 campaigns learned from, 19,501 meetings behind them, a rolling 30-day pipeline counter) are AiSDR's own and unaudited, so read them as marketing rather than evidence. And Ami changes none of the deliverability arithmetic: AiSDR's own pricing page still says it takes 30+ days to get multiple inboxes safely warmed, so a first campaign in 20 minutes is the launch, not the result.

AISQ is genuinely best for solo marketers who want low-cost, pay-as-you-go AI marketing assistance (SEO + content workflows) without a subscription. Skip it if you need a stable, enterprise-grade platform with predictable pricing and naming, or deep best-in-class SEO tooling.

(2026-08-30, read on plugin.squirrly.co/wordpress-seo-pricing) Squirrly SEO is billed monthly and renews at the same price. Free $0. PRO $9.99/month: 5 sites, 50 keyword researches, 100 audit suite pages, 0 SERP checker credits. Web Dev Kit $51.20/month: 10 sites, 300 researches, 300 audit pages, 2000 SERP credits. Business $71.99/month: 7 sites, 300 researches, 300 audit pages, 3000 SERP credits. Focus pages per account run 1 / 25 / 70 / 70. Extra SERP checker credits are $19.99 per 1,000 a month. No price is published for the AISQ Meteor agency offer: aisq.com/meteor/pricing and aisq.com/agencies/pricing both redirect to aisq.com/growth/pricing, which sells a done-for-you marketing service instead — $450 for 1 month, $1,235 for 3 months, $2,449 for 6 months, prices excluding VAT. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AISQ?
answers.a: AISQ (the Squirrly family) evolves its pricing and product names often — the honest advice is to buy only what's currently priced in front of you, in small credit batches first, and judge output on YOUR niche keywords before committing to bundles. Marketing automation that promises to cut workload 90% still needs your strategy and editing; credits generate drafts, not customers.

AWeber is genuinely best for small businesses and creators who want reliable, simple email marketing with a genuinely usable free tier. Skip it if you need advanced, behaviour-driven automation — newer tools go deeper for the money.

(re-verified 11 Sep 2026) A free plan still exists (up to 500 subscribers, 3,000 emails a month) but it is reached through the separate free-signup page, not the pricing page; Lite shows $12.49/mo and Plus $19.99/mo at 500 subs (annual billing; both scale by subscriber count). The ~$899 flat Unlimited tier is served to about one visitor in eighteen rather than withdrawn: on 5 Sep 2026 we loaded the pricing page 18 times in fresh cookie-less browsers, 17 returned Lite and Plus with no flat tier and one returned a three-card variant with “Go Unlimited” at $899/mo for unlimited subscribers, so it exists but you cannot count on seeing it. AWeber runs aggressive limited-time launch promos (an ‘87% off’ banner striking $599 to $79 at research time) — treat banner prices as promos, not list prices. AWeber's own affiliate newsletter of 5 September 2026 describes a single paid plan, 'AWeber Pro', starting at $16.15 a month billed annually, and does not name Lite or Plus at all; the pricing page served us Lite and Plus the same day, so the plan names appear to be mid-change. Check the live page before quoting a tier name. Re-checked 6 September 2026 in twelve cookie-less loads: the pricing page named Free, Lite, Plus and Unlimited on all six of its loads, so the flat Unlimited tier that showed once in eighteen loads the day before was served every time; the free-email-marketing page named only Free. No load carried a plan called Pro and the newsletter figure of $16.15 appeared nowhere; the entry amounts read $12.50 and $20.00. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AWeber?
answers.a: The free and low tiers are generous, but Lite and Plus prices climb with your subscriber count, so budget for growth. It's a dependable, no-frills veteran — just not the most modern automation on the market.

ActiveCampaign is genuinely best for businesses that want deep marketing automation and lifecycle email tied to a light CRM, and will actually use the automation depth. Skip it if you just need to send a newsletter — a simpler, cheaper email tool does that without paying for automation you won't touch.

(re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size: the per-contact ladder only renders after you select a contact count, which is why we could not re-verify our earlier reading of about $189/mo for Plus at 10,000 contacts on this pass. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ActiveCampaign?
answers.a: Pricing climbs with contact count and the add-ons (CRM, SMS, extra seats) stack up fast — the sticker Starter price is not what a serious automation setup actually costs. Powerful, but budget for the tier (Plus and up) you'll really use.

AdCreative.ai is genuinely best for performance marketers and stores that test many ad variations across sizes and platforms and want on-brand creative volume without a designer bottleneck. Skip it if you run a handful of static ads a month (a designer or Canva covers it), or your bottleneck is offer/targeting rather than creative volume.

(re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits. Three families, each with several credit steps. Starter is 1 user throughout: $39 a month for 10 credits and 1 brand, $89 for 15 credits and 2 brands, $139 for 30 credits and $189 for 50. Professional is 10 users and 10 brands: $249 for 50 credits, $339 for 75 and $400 for 100. Ultimate is 20 users and 25 brands: $999 for 100 credits, $1,099 for 150 and $1,399 for 200. Credits expire at the end of each billing cycle and do not roll over. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AdCreative.ai?
answers.a: The meter counts downloads, not campaigns — iterate seriously on ad variations and a 10-credit starter evaporates in an afternoon, which is exactly what iteration-heavy ad work does. And the honest fundamental: AI creatives give you volume and speed, but the offer and the hook still decide performance — a mediocre offer with 500 AI banners is 500 mediocre banners. Size the credit tier to your real testing cadence.

Adwisely is genuinely best for e-commerce stores (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce) that want automated, largely hands-off retargeting and prospecting ads on Meta and Google. Skip it if you run ads across many channels needing granular manual control, or your ad spend is high enough that the 10% fee outweighs doing it in-house.

(price re-verified 2026-09-10) Read on adwisely.com/pricing; every figure below stood unchanged from our previous reading on 2 August 2026. Both plans charge 10% of the ad spend Adwisely manages, with a monthly minimum that acts as a floor rather than a fee on top: $49 on Self-Serve and $249 on Concierge (managed). At $5,000 of monthly spend the Self-Serve fee is therefore $500, not $549, and total monthly Adwisely fees are capped at $3,250 (re-read 15 September 2026). 7-day free trial, no setup fee. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Adwisely?
answers.a: The honest math is the 10%-of-ad-spend fee on top of the minimum. It is cheap at low spend, but at higher budgets it's a real percentage cut of your marketing dollars until the cap — so calculate the effective cost at your actual spend, not the $49 sticker. It's built for e-commerce retargeting/prospecting on Meta and Google specifically, so it's not a general campaign manager. For stores that want largely hands-off retargeting, it removes real work.

AfterSell is genuinely best for Shopify stores with steady order volume that want to lift average order value with one-click post-purchase and checkout upsells. Skip it if your store gets only a trickle of orders — fix traffic and conversion first; there's nothing to upsell against low volume.

Priced by monthly order volume on the Shopify App Store listing (read 5 September 2026): the free plan is for development and partner stores only; paid plans start at $34.99 a month for 0 to 500 orders, then $54.99 for 501 to 1,000 and $99.99 for 1,001 to 2,000, with higher volume tiers above that. Every paid tier carries a 30-day free trial; checkout upsells need Shopify Plus. Flat monthly fees, no revenue share. The earlier figure of about $9.99 a month is no longer on the listing. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AfterSell?
answers.a: Post-purchase upsells only move the needle with steady order volume and a sensible complementary-offer strategy — bolt it onto a store with little traffic and there's nothing to upsell. The no-rev-share model is a genuine plus over percentage-based rivals.

AgencyAnalytics is genuinely best for marketing agencies that need white-label client reports from 85+ integrations — automated, on-brand and hands-off. Skip it if you're a solo operator with a couple of data sources, or you want rock-solid single-dashboard KPI tracking — Databox or a lighter tool may fit better.

One published rate: $20 USD per client / month billed annually, with no clients included in the base, so cost scales directly with your roster (a 25-client agency pays $500/mo; past that it is a quote). Month to month is $25 per client: the card never prints it, but the page's own schema.org block publishes an AggregateOffer with lowPrice $20 and highPrice $25, which is exactly the advertised "Save 20% annually". Add-ons on top: Rank Tracker $41.67/mo per 500 keywords, AI Tracker $20.83/mo per 250 credits. Past 25 clients the vendor quotes instead of publishing (re-verified 2026-09-11). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AgencyAnalytics?
answers.a: Two honest snags. Cost scales linearly with clients — great at 5, pricey at 50+. And the most-cited complaint is connector reliability: data sources disconnect and the platform doesn't always flag the failure clearly. Solo or small-data setups get little value from it.

AgentNest is genuinely best for stores that want an outside read on whether their product data is complete enough for AI shopping surfaces — on the free tier, which gives the entire diagnosis at no cost and no commitment. Skip it if you want a track record before you let an app edit your catalogue, you need a billing unit you can count in advance, or your bulk edits are already handled by Shopify's own editor or an app you pay for.

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/agentnest) Four tiers, and the split between them is unusual: the diagnosis is free and you pay only for the repairs. Free: unlimited catalogue scans, a catalogue readiness score, product-level issue reports and the full findings view. Starter $19 a month: 100 successful automated fixes a month, one-click fixes for all eligible issues, product-level recommendations. Growth $49 a month: 1,000 fixes a month, revenue-priority catalogue insights, fix history and progress tracking. Scale $99 a month: 5,000 fixes a month, advanced revenue-priority insights and bulk catalogue fixes. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no tier shows a free trial. The billing unit is a 'successful automated fix', and the listing never defines it. Whether one fix is one product, one field on one product, or one alt text on one image is the difference between $19 covering a hundred products and a hundred images. It is also the only variable separating the three paid tiers. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched on 6 August 2026 and has no reviews at all. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AgentNest?
answers.a:
Thirteen days old and no reviews. The app launched on 6 August 2026; as of 19 August 2026 nobody has written about it, which is not a criticism so much as the plain state of the evidence. Everything below is read off the listing, because there is nothing else to read.

The score is the vendor's own. 'AI shopping readiness' is measured by AgentNest against AgentNest's criteria, and no external standard — no schema.org profile, no Google Merchant Center specification, no published rubric — is named anywhere on the listing. A number that only one company calculates is a prompt to go look at your catalogue, not a fact about your catalogue. On the same page Shopify shows ListingLens and StoreBeam doing the same job, also on free plans.

And the billing unit is defined by the party doing the billing. You pay per 'successful automated fix', with no definition of a fix and no definition of successful. Combined with permissions that let it edit products, collections and files across your store, the sensible way in is: run the free scan, read the issue list, fix a handful yourself, and only then decide whether the one-click version is worth 19 cents a go. The same developer's other app, AskNest, has one review in three months — this is a two-app studio finding its feet, not an established catalogue tool.

AhaSlides is genuinely best for educators, trainers and event hosts running interactive sessions — polls, quizzes, word clouds and live Q&A — with audiences up to 50 free. Skip it if you need predictable, uniform pricing across a multi-country team, or your decks live in PowerPoint and a lightweight poll add-on covers it.

(re-verified 2026-09-06) AhaSlides prices regionally, so the currency and the amount depend on where you buy from; the figures below are the reading from a Netherlands location on 6 September 2026, and your own country's page may show a different rate for the same tier. Free is 0 for up to 50 participants, with unlimited events and unlimited presentations but only 5 Quiz and 3 Unscored slides per deck. Essential is €7.25 per month billed yearly and lifts the ceiling to 100 participants, adding unlimited interactive slides, analytics and exports, and folder management. Pro AI is €10.65 per month billed yearly, raises the ceiling to 2,500 participants and adds the AI features, custom branding, Q&A moderation and priority support. Enterprise is quote-only, listed at up to 100,000 participants with SSO and SCIM offered on demand. Two discounts sit on top: yearly billing is advertised at up to 67% below monthly, and team licences bought together save up to a further 20%. AhaSlides' own USD listing puts Essential at $95.40 a year, which is the same tier at a different regional price rather than a second plan — so check the page from your own country before you budget. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AhaSlides?
answers.a: AhaSlides runs regional pricing: the number on the pricing page depends on where you browse from — so any review quoting one price (including ours) may not match yours. The advertised savings assume annual commitment, and the free tier's five-quiz-slide cap nudges real quiz use toward paid.

Aira is genuinely best for European B2B sales teams that want AI-assisted prospecting and automatic meeting/CRM hygiene from a Europe-native database. Skip it if your market is primarily US/global (US-native databases cover it better), or you need a mature, battle-tested platform today.

(read 2026-08-26 on aira.app/pricing) Aira is €149 per user a month, billed monthly, for the company database, AI prospecting, monitoring and on-demand research. Aira Connect starts at €499 a month, billed annually, and adds CRM enrichment and live signals on the accounts already in HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive. These are euro prices for everyone: we read the page from a US connection and got the same euro figures, which fits a product that describes itself as the intelligence layer for European dealmaking across 14 markets. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Aira?
answers.a: Young product, sharp focus: European B2B prospecting on a 65-million-company database with meeting notes flowing into records automatically. The honest checks: independent review coverage is still thin, so run your own two-week test against a concrete metric (meetings booked, admin hours saved) rather than trusting early-adopter buzz. And note that the money-back guarantee exists precisely so you can do that without risk.

Aircall is genuinely best for sales and support teams (3+ seats) that want a polished cloud phone system embedded in their CRM/helpdesk, with call routing, analytics and 250+ integrations. Skip it if you're a solo operator or duo (the 3-license minimum prices you out), or you need a full contact-center suite with omnichannel routing.

(read 2026-08-26 on aircall.io/pricing over a US connection, with their own country selector on United States) Essentials is $30 per license a month and Professional $50, both on annual billing, which the page marks as 25% off monthly. Flip that toggle and the monthly rates read $40 and $70 per license (3 licenses for $120 and $210), checked 29 August 2026 from a US connection. The discount is not uniform either: Essentials really is 25% off, but Professional lands closer to 29%, so price the plan you will actually buy rather than trusting the badge; the same cards quote 3 licenses at $90 and $150 a month. Custom starts at 25 licenses. Aircall AI is not in those numbers: voice runs from $0.19 a minute with bundles at $175 for 500 minutes and $725 for 2,500, or $0.49 a minute pay-as-you-go dropping to $0.39 above 2,500. AI conversations are $0.35 each, $0.29 after the first thousand, or bundled at $250 for 1,000 and $1,500 for 10,000. Smaller add-ons sit at $9, $10, $15, $30 and $49 per license a month, so the license fee is a floor rather than the bill. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Aircall?
answers.a: Two structural catches: the 3-seat minimum makes the real starting price triple the sticker, and the annual-vs-monthly gap is steep (Professional: $50 vs $70). 'Unlimited calling' covers listed regions — check yours — and AI features increasingly live in add-ons or higher tiers. It's polished and integration-rich; just price the seats you'll actually have, on the billing cycle you'll actually choose.

Airia is genuinely best for enterprises that need to find the AI already running across their organisation, enforce policy on it at runtime, and build and govern their own agents, with auditability and compliance evidence built in. Skip it if you're an individual or small team wanting a single AI assistant (this is far more platform than you need), or you can't commit to an enterprise rollout.

(re-verified 2026-09-10) Quote-only. Airia used to publish a ladder: a free tier, Individual around $50 a month and Team around $250. That page is gone — both airia.com/pricing and www.airia.com/pricing now redirect to airia.ai/docs/build/interface-options/usage_limits, a developer documentation page titled Usage Limits on a different domain, while airia.ai/pricing answers 200 with a shell that carries no text at all without JavaScript, and we found no amount anywhere on the site on 10 September 2026. Every deployment is therefore quoted after a sales conversation. Treat any $50 or $250 figure still in circulation, including in older versions of this review, as historical rather than current. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Airia?
answers.a: Airia used to publish part of its ladder, which was refreshingly rare for enterprise AI. As of 20 August 2026 that is over: the pricing page redirects into developer documentation on airia.ai from both airia.com and www.airia.com, and there is no amount anywhere on the site. So the honest position is now the usual one for this category — you cannot budget before a sales conversation. The underlying fit has not changed, though the pitch has. Read on 1 September 2026, the site leads with discovery and enforcement rather than building: finding the AI tools, models, agents and MCP servers already running, including the unapproved ones, stopping actions at the execution layer before the tool call fires, and mapping governance evidence to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, SR 11-7, HIPAA, ISO 42001 and SOC 2. The agent builder now sits under Optimize. Either way this only pays off at organisational scale. A small team that wants one chatbot is buying far more platform than it needs. For an enterprise standardising and governing AI, that is exactly the point.

Airwallex is genuinely best for companies invoicing or paying in several currencies, where a 0.5% spread against your bank's 2–3% is the whole business case. Skip it if you bill in one currency and pay domestic suppliers — the multi-currency machinery is the product, and without FX volume you are paying a platform fee for a bank account.

(2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; no rate below has changed since 1 Aug 2026) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included and $1,000 per additional entity; subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a Yield rate that Airwallex restamps daily rather than fixing per plan — on 5 September 2026 the page showed 3.22% on Explore, 3.37% on Grow and 3.49% on Accelerate, and its own footnote reads that the indicative rate is the 7-day annualised historical rate of the underlying funds as of 4 September 2026, net of fees. Read those three figures as a moving number carrying the date the page gave it, not as a plan feature: they were 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% when we first recorded them on 28 August 2026. (yield re-verified 5 Sep 2026) Platform API and embedded finance are quote-only. Two gaps we had left open got a partial answer on 17 September 2026, when Airwallex pointed us at its fee schedule. Dispute handling does carry a price, but only the Canadian entity publishes it: airwallex.com/en-ca/terms/fee-schedule prints 15 CAD per chargeback request and 0.30 CAD per refund request, both excluding whatever the card network passes on. The US pricing page lists dispute management as a feature with no fee beside it, so treat the Canadian figures as the shape of the charge rather than as your rate. The Grow platform fee is still not a number anywhere: both the US pricing page and the Canadian schedule say only that it is based on the total number of Spend users, so ask for it before you budget. Re-verified 2026-09-19 on airwallex.com/en-us/pricing: every published rate above is unchanged — FX, transfers, acquiring, the 0.50% on subscription billing, the free first 10 Spend users, the 250-user ceiling on the $12 rate and the $1,000 per entity beyond three. The yield figures still read 3.22%, 3.37% and 3.49%, but their footnote now dates the seven-day annualised rate to 18 September 2026 instead of 4 September. That is the clearest evidence yet that these three numbers are a daily restamp rather than a plan feature: same values, new date. The Grow platform fee is still not printed anywhere. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Airwallex?
answers.a: The honest headline here is that the FX markup is published at all — 0.5% and 1% above interbank is a real number, and most competitors will not print one. What the page does not settle is everything around it. The Grow plan's platform fee 'varies with team size' with no table, so the $12 a user is not the whole subscription -- though their table does say the first ten Spend users are free, which is the part the headline rate hides in your favour. Chargeback and dispute fees are not priced anywhere, only mentioned as a feature. And the page's own disclaimer says per-transaction fees apply to certain transactions with the detail in a separate fee schedule. So: use the published FX rate to compare against your bank, then ask for the fee schedule and the platform fee before you move money.

Algomo is genuinely best for B2B teams with real inbound traffic that want an AI agent qualifying visitors, personalizing the site by visitor identity and booking meetings — and don't mind a sales-led buying process. Skip it if you want self-serve, transparent pricing, or you are pre-traffic — an AI inbound agent needs inbound to work with.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on newmode.ai/pricing and the homepage) Plans start at $200 a month with no per-seat pricing - and that single sentence is still the entire public price list, unchanged since our July and August readings. The pricing page carries exactly two plans, Growth and Enterprise, and both buttons say 'Let's chat' and 'Book call': no amount, no contact slider, no self-serve tier. Growth lists 1:1 personalized LinkedIn ads, AI-generated ad copy, website personalization, CRM integration and email support; Enterprise adds unlimited campaigns, custom integrations, a dedicated success manager, priority support and advanced analytics. What drives the price between the two is not published anywhere on the site, so the only figure a buyer can budget against is the $200 floor. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Algomo?
answers.a: Algomo is a member of the quote-only club: $200/month is the only number on the site, and the real bill for your traffic volume and feature set only emerges in a sales conversation. Budgeting before the demo is guesswork — and quote-priced tools rarely get cheaper at renewal. Worth knowing before it becomes load-bearing: the personalisation runs from a JavaScript snippet in your header, so the tailored copy and routing rules live for as long as the subscription does. Remove the snippet and every visitor sees the original page again.

Alidrop is genuinely best for dropshippers who want automated product sourcing, fulfillment and inventory sync with access to faster-shipping suppliers and one-click store integration. Skip it if you want the absolute widest catalog at rock-bottom sourcing cost, or your margins can't absorb both the subscription and wholesale product cost.

(re-verified 2026-09-13 on their own pricing page) Four monthly plans: Starter $39/mo (50 unique / 25 premium products), Professional $59/mo (500 unique / 250 premium), Empire $99/mo (5,000 unique / 2,500 premium) and Unicorn $299/mo (25,000 products). A 7-day trial costs $1, and there are no transaction or hidden fees. Annual billing is listed only from Professional up — $288, $684 and $948 a year — and the discount grows with the tier: 6 months off Professional, 5 off Empire and 8 off Unicorn, so the advertised “up to 8 months off” is the Unicorn rate rather than a general one, and Starter has no annual column at all. An optional one-time custom-store build service starts at $299. The $1 trial converts to the full monthly rate of whichever plan you picked, and your card stays on file — set a reminder if you are only testing. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Alidrop?
answers.a: Alidrop's pitch includes faster-shipping (including US/EU) suppliers, but the core dropshipping economics still apply: you pay the subscription plus wholesale product cost, and margins live or die on product selection and ad efficiency, not the tool. The low Starter product cap nudges serious stores up to Pro quickly, and as with any dropshipping automation, the platform reduces but doesn't remove supplier-quality and shipping-time risk. Sample before you scale.

Alli AI is genuinely best for consultants and agencies managing SEO across a portfolio of client sites who want bulk on-page changes, optimization rules and keyword tracking from one dashboard. Skip it if you run a single site — $299 buys far more capacity than you need, and a one-site SEO suite costs a fraction — or you're not comfortable letting software edit pages in bulk.

answers.q: How much does Alli AI cost?
answers.a: (prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on alliai.com/pricing) Billed in USD, no free tier, a 10-day free trial on every plan and cancellation from the dashboard at any time. The page shows two ladders behind a Monthly/Annual toggle. Paid monthly: Business $299 a month (5 sites, 5 team members, 500 keywords, 1,250 pages) and Agency $599 a month (15 sites, 15 team members, 2,000 keywords, 5,000 pages). Paid annually: Business $2,990 a year and Agency $5,990 a year, which the page prints as $249 and $499 a month, a saving of $598 and $1,198 respectively. Enterprise is quote-only (50 sites, 50 team members, 5,000 keywords, 20,000 pages). Every quota has a published add-on price that differs per tier and per term: monthly Business is extra sites from $39 each, extra keywords from $24.99 per 100 and extra pages from $14.99 per 250; annual Business $32.50, $20.83 and $12.50; monthly Agency $29, $14.99 and $9.99; annual Agency $24.17, $12.50 and $8.33. Business and Agency carry the same engine — the AI Search Visibility Engine, pre-rendering for 50-plus AI crawlers, the AI bot traffic monitor, LLM Mode, keyword tracking, site speed optimizer, link builder, standard reports and a weekly crawl — and Agency adds only API access, white label and snippet hosting. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Alli AI?
answers.a: The entry is $299 a month paid monthly — agency-grade automation priced accordingly — and every tier meters on FOUR axes at once (sites, seats, keywords, pages). Growth on any axis costs extra, though at least the rates are published: from $39 per extra site, $24.99 per 100 extra keywords and $14.99 per 250 extra pages on monthly Business. And the category caveat an honest review owes you: bulk automated on-page edits are powerful, but changes at scale deserve human review — unchecked automated SEO is how sites break. One more thing the pricing page does not answer, and it matters at $299 a month: their own FAQ says your site, CMS and code stay untouched, so where changes are delivered through that snippet they last exactly as long as the subscription does. Price this as renting an improvement, not buying one, and ask them directly what happens to applied changes after you cancel before you commit a year.

Alohi is genuinely best for businesses that need secure online faxing, e-signatures or scanning — especially regulated ones needing HIPAA-compliant fax on the Enterprise tier. Skip it if you only need occasional e-signatures (a single dedicated tool may be cheaper) or your document volume is low enough for free options.

(read 2026-09-10 on fax.plus/pricing and sign.plus/pricing) Priced per product, in USD, with a currency switcher offering EUR, CHF and GBP. IMPORTANT: on Fax.Plus the '/month' figure on each card is the annual rate. Fax.Plus — Basic $6.99 a month billed as $83.99 annually (200 pages a month, one fax number, one member, $0.10 per extra page, 60 pages maximum per fax); Premium $13.99 / $167.99 (500 pages, $0.07 per extra page, 90 pages per fax, adds toll-free numbers, number porting, CSV log export and the ability to switch off reception); Business $27.99 / $335.99 (1,000 pages); Enterprise $79.99 a month on annual billing, $959.99 a year, and the only card that also shows a monthly-billing rate, 'starts at $99.99' (4,000 pages, multiple fax numbers, unlimited members, $0.03 per extra page, 250 pages per fax, 1,000 AI credits a month, SSO, HIPAA-compliant with BAA, the Fax.Plus API, data residency and Zapier). The banner offers 'up to 3 months free with an annual plan (save up to 22%)'. A free plan gives 10 pages in total, not per month. Extra fax numbers are $4.99 a month (Business and Enterprise include two); vanity numbers $19.99; choosing your own number within a region is a one-time $19.99, or $29.99 from their handpicked memorable set. Porting is free but country-dependent — porting a US or Canadian number requires Premium or higher. The footnotes warn that faxes to certain destinations may count as multiple pages, priced on a separate Sending Rates page, and that taxes are excluded. Sign.Plus is a separate subscription and prints annual and monthly rates side by side: Free (3 signature requests in total, 1 template, 1 user), Personal $9.99 annual / $14.99 monthly, $119.99 a year (1 user, 10 signature requests a month, 5 templates), Professional $19.99 / $29.99 per user, $239.99 a year (up to 5 users, unlimited requests, 10 templates), Business $29.99 / $49.99 per user, $359.99 a year (unlimited templates, document sharing, Zapier, custom branding), Enterprise $49.99 / $79.99 per user, $599.99 a year (SSO, HIPAA-compliant with BAA, advanced security controls, data residency, priority support). Sign.Plus advertises 'save up to 40% with annual plans'. Request via SMS/WhatsApp is metered separately at 10, 30 and 150 a month from Professional upward. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Alohi?
answers.a: The honest catch is that Alohi is a suite of separate products — Fax.Plus, Sign.Plus, Scan.Plus — each with its own subscription, so "one ecosystem" can mean several line items if you want e-signatures and faxing and scanning. Page and member limits on the lower tiers are modest, and HIPAA/BAA sits only on the top tier. For a single job (say online faxing), it's clean and cheap; for the full workflow, add up the parts.

AltText.ai is genuinely best for image-heavy sites that need alt text written back into the CMS automatically: e-commerce catalogues, publishers and long-running blogs on WordPress, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, Contentful, DatoCMS or Storyblok. The native integrations, page crawler, CSV import/export and developer API let you clear thousands of missing alt attributes without touching them by hand. Skip it if you have a few dozen images. Write those yourself for free and you will describe them better than any model, because you know why each image is on the page. Also skip it if your visuals are diagram-, product- or brand-specific enough that every generated line needs rewriting anyway — in which case the credits buy you a draft you were going to redo.

(re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AltText.ai?
answers.a: The headline ‘5¢ per image’ only holds for a plain JPG in one language. AVIF, HEIC, SVG and TIFF bill double — precisely the formats a performance-tuned image pipeline outputs — and every extra language adds another credit per image, so by the published rules one AVIF product shot in five languages is six credits, not one. Those advanced formats are also locked out of the 25-credit free trial, so the one thing you cannot measure before paying is your own burn rate. Credits are spent on generation rather than on acceptance: regenerate a line you didn’t like and you pay again, and AltText.ai states plainly that used credits are not normally refundable. The category caveat an honest review owes you: models describe what is visibly in a photo well, but alt text is a judgement call. Whether an image is decorative or informative, and what your brand actually calls the thing in it, is context the model doesn’t have. Bulk generation is a far better starting point than the empty alt attributes on most sites, but treat the output as a draft to spot-check. ‘ADA compliance’ here means the field gets filled, not a legal guarantee that what’s in it is right.

Alvys is genuinely best for FTL trucking carriers and asset-based (hybrid) brokers with roughly 5–300 trucks — especially compliance-heavy freight like hazmat, reefer and cross-border — plus shippers running private fleets, with real back-office staff to put dispatch, billing and DOT/IFTA compliance in one system. Skip it if you're a pure-play broker without assets, you run LTL/multi-modal loads billing multiple customers per load, you need rail, air or ocean tracking, or you're a single-truck operator without back-office staff.

(re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Pricing is still not public: alvys.com/pricing answers an ordinary request with HTTP 401, so the page sits behind a password rather than behind a form. The last published load-based rates (2026) were Carrier from ~$150/mo and Broker from ~$300/mo with no per-seat fees; those are history, not a quote. Expect a sales conversation to get current numbers. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Alvys?
answers.a: Two honest boundaries. Implementation can stretch into weeks and support is ticket-based rather than real-time — a real friction in trucking's tempo. And it's built specifically for truck-based FTL operations: if you're a pure-play (non-asset) broker, run LTL with multiple customers per load, or need rail/air/ocean tracking, this isn't your TMS — Alvys itself is refreshingly explicit about that. The fit is narrow and deep, not broad.

Amplemarket is genuinely best for mid-market sales teams (20+ reps) who'll actually adopt the full AI-prospecting, multichannel and deliverability stack in one vendor. Skip it if you're a small team or solo — Apollo starts around $49/user/mo with a free plan and covers the basics for a fraction of the price.

(re-verified 2026-09-14) The only published price is Startup at $600/mo on an annual term, covering 2 users, with additional users available to purchase; Growth and Elite are listed as Custom, so those numbers come from sales rather than the site. All plans include a free trial. Startup covers 13,500 email address credits and 600 phone number credits per user per year, 2 mailboxes per user and 27,000 contacts. Growth lists 4 users, 35,000 email and 5,000 phone credits per user per year, 4 mailboxes and 140,000 contacts. Elite lists 10 users, 40,000 email and 9,600 phone credits, 8 mailboxes and 400,000 contacts. Two gated rows are easy to miss in the comparison table and both start at zero or near it on Startup: Custom Data Requests run 0, 4 and 12 per plan, so a Startup customer cannot ask for a bespoke data pull at all, and Job Change Alerts cover 500, 1,000 and 2,000 contacts. Duo Inbox is marked as an Add-On rather than an included feature, and the MCP row - prospecting and taking action from inside Claude or ChatGPT - is listed as a platform feature with no plan boundary stated. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Amplemarket?
answers.a: It's premium and built for teams that will use the whole all-in-one stack. The independent picture is genuinely strong overall: around 4.6/5 across ~600 G2 reviews, with repeated praise for unusually human-sounding AI messages, ease of use and hands-on support. But data accuracy and email deliverability are the most-cited complaints, and they cluster on European contacts — North American data holds up better than EMEA/APAC. Amplemarket points to its own benchmarks showing competitive accuracy, so weigh both sides and test their data against your own target region in a trial before you commit. Under ~10 reps you'll also pay for features you never touch. The genuinely new bit: it now works inside ChatGPT and Claude. Since June that integration can triage the inbox and update or remove leads rather than just search, so reps can run more of the workflow without leaving the chat. Since July that stretches further. From the same chat a rep can research an account, pull enriched profiles and enrol every contact into one sequence with copy written per person and per step. A GTM Skills Library exposes the rest of the platform the same way. Amplemarket says setup takes under two minutes — that is their figure, not one we timed.

Amplitude is genuinely best for product teams who want everyone looking at the same behavioural data — the free 2 million events a month is a real working tier, not a demo. Skip it if you need page-and-session web analytics rather than product events, because that is a different tool and much cheaper; also skip it if your event volume is unpredictable and you cannot get a rate card.

(2026-09-17, re-read on their own pricing page) Free $0 with 2 million events a month, permanently, no card required and no time limit. Plus starts at $0 with the first 2 million events free and scales up to 70 million events; a card is required and the card itself offers an estimator rather than a rate. Growth and Enterprise are quote-only, both described as event-based pricing. The page states every plan includes the full platform and unlimited seats, and that expanded packages are priced as a percentage of your platform plan. Startups with under $10 million in funding and fewer than 20 employees are offered one free year on Growth, applied for rather than self-served. The published caps that do differ by tier are session replays (10,000 a month on Free and Plus, 20,000 on Growth, 50,000 on Enterprise), active experiments (one on Free and Plus, two on Growth and Enterprise, more as an add-on) and agent sessions (5,000, 10,000 and 20,000). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Amplitude?
answers.a: Unlimited seats is genuinely unusual and worth the credit — you are not taxed for letting the whole team look. The cost lands on events instead, and events are the thing you control least: an instrumentation change or a growth spurt moves your bill without anyone choosing to upgrade. What the plan cards do not print, the page's own bill estimator does, and we read the whole Plus ladder there on 17 September 2026. What it shows is how little volume buys you: the marginal million events costs $94 a month at the bottom of the ladder and still $86.25 at the 70-million ceiling where Plus stops, and above that ceiling nothing is published. And 'expanded packages are priced as a percentage of your platform plan' means the add-ons scale with your bill rather than with your usage of them — the more events you send, the more the extras cost, whether or not you use them more. Get the per-event rate in writing before you instrument.

answers.q: Is Answering Service Care worth it?
answers.a: Answering Service Care is genuinely best for a small business that loses money when a call goes to voicemail — trades, clinics, law and property firms — and wants real people answering around the clock without hiring a receptionist. It suits you especially if your call volume is genuinely low and predictable, because the plans are priced in minutes and nothing is gated behind a higher tier. Skip it if your callers mostly want things a human does not need to do — order status, opening hours, a password reset — because you are paying per minute for a person to read them out. Skip it too if your volume is high and variable: at 500-plus minutes you are past the published ladder and into a custom quote, and per-minute billing makes a busy month expensive in a way a flat-rate provider would not.

answers.q: How much does Answering Service Care cost?
answers.a: (2026-09-10, read off their own pricing page, both billing toggles) Four plans, priced on included minutes. Billed monthly: Starter $40 with zero minutes included and $1.75 per minute after that; Small Business $179 for 100 minutes, then $1.70; Pro $329 for 250 minutes, then $1.60; Enterprise $639 for 500 minutes, then $1.35. Paying a year upfront takes about 10% off the monthly rate: $161, $296 and $575 for the three larger plans, while Starter stays at $40. There is also a $50 one-time start-up fee; it is still absent from the plan cards, but the page's FAQ now says plainly what it buys — customising the account, building your initial scripts and configuring routing. Every plan carries the same feature set: 24/7 cover, bilingual English/Spanish operators, call transfers, SMS and email relays, custom greetings and hold music, a client portal, usage reporting and the mobile app. So you are buying minutes, not capability, and there is no long-term contract. One caution about the page itself: the explanatory text below the table still contradicts the table three times, quoting Pro at $319, Enterprise at $599 and Starter overage at $1.65. We have used the figures from the pricing table, which is the one the buttons act on. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Answering Service Care?
answers.a: Do the arithmetic before you pick a tier, because their own page does not. Starter buys the line and nothing else: at $40 plus $1.75 a minute, it stays the cheapest option only up to roughly 79 minutes a month — past that the $179 Small Business plan costs less. The same crossover logic repeats: Small Business gives way to Pro at about 188 minutes, and Pro gives way to Enterprise at about 444. Note too that Small Business is the one tier where an included minute ($1.79 each, $179 for 100) costs more than an overage minute ($1.70), so there is no saving in buying that bundle for its own sake. And the second thing to price in is the $50 start-up fee, which is easy to miss where they have put it.

Aplos is genuinely best for small nonprofits and faith-based organisations that need true fund accounting rather than general small-business bookkeeping — tracking restricted and unrestricted funds separately is the thing generic tools genuinely cannot do. Skip it if you are a normal for-profit business, because you are paying for fund accounting you will never use; also skip it if two users on the entry tier does not cover your team and the next tier up is out of budget.

(2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page) Three published tiers, billed monthly: Lite at $79/month, Core at $129 and Advanced at $229, plus a fourth Custom tier with tailored pricing aimed at organisations above $1 million in annual revenue. Advanced is framed as a quote rather than a checkout: the card reads "Customized solutions start at $229/month" and the button asks for a demo. A promotion was running when we re-read the page on 10 September 2026 — 50% off for three months with code FALL26, showing Lite at $39.50 and Core at $64.50 — and the footnote dates it: new customers only, ending 30 September. The earlier SUMMER26 promotion that ran to 31 August has been replaced on the same terms. What matters is still what you pay in month four. The trial is 15 days and takes no credit card. Lite and Core each include 2 users; Advanced includes 3. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Aplos?
answers.a: The headline you will see first is not the price you will pay. The 50%-off banner sits at the top of the page and rewrites every figure on it. So the $39.50 that catches your eye is a three-month rate against a $79 list price. That is a 100% increase waiting in month four, on software that holds your books and is therefore painful to leave. The second thing to pin down is users: Lite includes two, and for a nonprofit with a bookkeeper, a treasurer and a director that is already tight, so establish the per-user cost before you commit.

Apollo is genuinely best for sales teams that want prospecting data, enrichment and sequencing in one affordable all-in-one platform. Skip it if you need guaranteed-accurate data at volume — budget for credit overages, or pair it with a verification step.

A free plan (900 credits per seat per year, 2 sequences); paid Basic $49, Professional $79 and Organization $119 per seat/mo billed annually, or $65, $99 and $149 month to month - the annual saving the page advertises is 24%. Organization carries a three-seat minimum, so it starts at $357/mo. Credit-based limits mean the effective cost often runs higher (re-verified 2026-09-11). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Apollo?
answers.a: The credit and export caps are the catch — real usage on enrichment and dialing often runs well above the sticker, and data accuracy is hit-or-miss, so verify before you outreach at scale.

Arbor is genuinely best for US households and renters in deregulated states who want set-and-forget savings on the electric bill without becoming rate-shopping hobbyists. Skip it if you live outside the 13 deregulated states, are on a municipal or co-op utility, or genuinely enjoy comparing supplier offers yourself each year.

Free for households, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17. Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s — and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture produced a figure. That is consistent with the model: Arbor is paid a referral fee by the winning electricity supplier, not by you. US-only: it works in the 13 deregulated 'energy choice' states across the Northeast, Midwest and Texas, and only on the supply portion of your bill. The delivery charges from your utility are untouched, so the saving applies to part of the bill rather than to all of it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Arbor?
answers.a: The honest catches: it only exists in deregulated US states, and it only touches the supply rate, since delivery charges stay with your utility. The headline savings — Arbor itself reports an average of up to $593/year — depend entirely on how bad your current default rate is. If you already shopped your rate recently, the gain may be small.

AskNest is genuinely best for small stores with repetitive product, shipping and returns questions who want a cheap multilingual FAQ widget and can test the answer quality on their own policy pages for free first. Skip it if you need human handover or ticketing, you sell in languages outside the seven supported, or you want a vendor with more than one review and more than one app behind it.

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/asknest-ai-faq-product-bot) Four tiers, priced by AI replies per month, and the cheapest ladder in this category. Free: 50 AI replies a month, replies in one language you select, answers drawn from your FAQs, policy pages and product data, translated storefront widget, product finder and usage tracking. Starter $4.99 a month: 500 replies, automatic shopper-language detection across up to three languages, translated replies, product recommendations and best sellers. Growth $9.99 a month: 1,500 replies and all supported languages. Pro $19.99 a month: 5,000 replies. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no paid tier shows a free trial — the free plan is the trial. What the listing never says is what happens when you run out: there is no overage rate anywhere on the page, so whether reply 501 costs money or simply does not happen is not published. 'Any language' is also not on offer; customer-facing replies and widget labels cover English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese — seven. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched 8 May 2026 and has exactly one App Store review. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AskNest?
answers.a:
One review. The app launched on 8 May 2026, and in three and a half months exactly one merchant has written about it. That is five stars, 16 July 2026, from an Austrian store, and it is about support responsiveness: they wanted the widget's language changed and someone called Tracy did it within minutes. That is a pleasant data point about the vendor and no data point at all about whether the bot answers correctly under load.

The developer is a Shopify agency, not a support-software company. Ecommerce Storez sells Shopify themes, store builds and SEO audits from ecommercestorez.us, and AskNest is one of two apps it has shipped in 2026 — the other, AgentNest, has no reviews. AskNest has no product site of its own; the App Store listing is the entire published record, which is why the link we point at is the developer's agency site.

And be clear about what this is not. There is no live human takeover on any tier, no ticketing, no inbox. It reads your FAQs, your policy pages and your catalogue and answers from them in seven languages. When a shopper asks something your policy pages do not cover, nothing on the listing describes what happens next — no handover to email, no escalation. For a first line of defence on repetitive questions that is fine and five dollars is a fair price for it. As your only support channel it is not enough.

Aspire is genuinely best for startups and SMBs that want an all-in-one business account with $0 monthly fees and built-in spend management. Skip it if you need a traditional bank relationship, lending, or coverage in a region Aspire doesn't serve — check availability first.

(price re-verified 2026-09-11 against the vendor's own pricing page) SGD $0 monthly fee on Basic, no minimum balance and no deposit to open. You pay per use: FX from 0.46% to send and from 0.34% to receive, inbound SWIFT SGD $35 for SGD accounts or USD $8 for others, outbound SWIFT USD $15 for SHA and USD $30 for OURS. Premium is SGD $15/month and zeroes the FX margin on the first SGD $13,000 of conversions a month, after which the same from-0.46% applies. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Aspire?
answers.a: It's a fintech account (strongest in Southeast Asia), not a full bank — great for keeping fixed costs near zero on mostly-domestic activity, but confirm it supports your country and currencies before you build your finances around it.

Assembly is genuinely best for agencies and professional services firms who want one branded place for clients to message, sign, pay and share files instead of four tools and an email thread. Skip it if you have a handful of clients and already use a shared drive and an invoicing tool, because the value here is the single branded portal and that only matters once clients get confused about where things live.

(re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser) Assembly publishes exactly one price: Empower at $3 per user per month, billed yearly, with an Enterprise tier quoted on request for advanced security, custom integrations and tailored implementation. There is no monthly/yearly toggle and no other published tier. Empower covers milestone celebrations, announcements, awards and challenges, the global reward catalogue, peer-to-peer recognition, points and budget controls, the Dora Hub AI insights and advanced people analytics. Note that the reward points themselves are funded by you on top of the seat price, so budget the catalogue separately from the licence. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Assembly?
answers.a: Two meters run at once and they move at different speeds. Clients is the one that bites first: Starter stops at 50, and the step to 500 costs $70 more a month. Internal users is the other, and it gets worse as you climb. An extra person is $29 on Professional and $59 on Advanced, so the more expensive plan makes each additional colleague more expensive too — the opposite of what a tier ladder usually does. The last step is the steepest in the category: $499 to a $2,000 minimum, and what that buys is SSO and security controls rather than more capacity.

answers.q: Is Atlas AI Store Builder worth it?
answers.a: Atlas AI Store Builder is genuinely best for sellers testing many product ideas quickly who want a full Shopify storefront from a single product link, and who will genuinely stay inside 5 pages and 250 orders a month or have priced the overage. Skip it if you run one established store with real order volume — the caps turn a $39 tool into a variable bill exactly when the store starts working — or you want a page builder you keep after you stop paying.

answers.q: How much does Atlas AI Store Builder cost?
answers.a: (prices read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/dropshipt and helloatlas.io) The listing says “Free to install”, but that is the development-store tier. A real store runs on the All-in-One plan at $39 a month, billed in USD with a 7-day free trial. Their own partners page says 5 days, so check which you get. What $39 buys is capped rather than unlimited: 5 published pages, $1,000 of bundle revenue, 250 cart orders and 50 AI photos a month. Their pricing page states it plainly: “you’ll be charged the base plan fees and given access to features to a limit, any additional uses for those features can be purchased as shown in the per feature pricing”. The App Store listing adds that “additional charges apply as your store generates revenue and impact”. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Atlas AI Store Builder?
answers.a: The meter runs on your success, not your usage. $1,000 of bundle revenue and 250 cart orders is a rounding error for a store that is actually working. So the $39 headline describes the bill of a store that has not started selling yet. Price the tier you expect to be on in month three, not the one you sign up on. Two other things worth knowing before you install. The rating is 4.7 from 389 reviews, but 17 of those are one star and the recent ones are about billing rather than the product: one seller writes “cancelled it, uninstalled it, but still getting charged” after two months. And the listing carries a line Shopify does not require of most apps: “Atlas must not be used to copy, duplicate, or reproduce products, product listings, images, or store content from any website, or marketplace without the explicit permission of the rights holder”. That tells you what a paste-a-product-link builder gets used for.

Atria is genuinely best for performance marketers and creative teams that want competitor ad research and AI ad-creative generation for Meta and TikTok in one platform. Skip it if you don't run paid social at volume, or you only need ad inspiration (a cheaper ad-library tool) or only design (a general creative tool).

(re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page, annual billing, which Atria advertises as 20% off) Core is $129/mo, a stated $360 saving a year. That covers 5 seats, 4,000 AI credits a month, 50 brands followed without AI insights, 5 connected ad accounts, $500K of ad spend analysed a month, 5GB of asset storage and 3 brand profiles. Plus $479/mo (a stated $1,440 saving): 8 seats, 10,000 credits, 100 brands with AI insights, 10 ad accounts, $1M of ad spend, 1TB storage, 8 brand profiles. Business $959/mo (a stated $2,880 saving): unlimited ad spend. Enterprise is custom. Extra seats are $20 each a month on every tier. Note the step from Core to Plus is far steeper than the tier names suggest — it is roughly 3.7x the price for 2.5x the credits. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Atria?
answers.a: Two honest notes. It's credit-metered — AI credits and brand-tracking slots cap what you can generate and monitor, so a heavy user burns through Core's allowance and steps up to Plus. And it's specialized for Meta/TikTok ad creative research and generation, so it's a performance-marketing tool, not a general design suite. Its edge is competitor ad intelligence plus creative generation in one place; if you only need one of those, a cheaper single-purpose tool may fit.

Atto is genuinely best for hourly and mobile crews (construction, cleaning, field service) that want dead-simple clock-in/out, GPS-verified timesheets and payroll-ready exports. Skip it if office/knowledge teams (project-based trackers like Toggl fit better), or anywhere the team hasn't been brought along on why.

(re-read 2026-09-05 on attotime.com/pricing) Per user per month, billed annually: Starter $5.65, Plus $7.95 (job codes, breaks and notes), Advanced $10.75 (job costing), Expert $16.55 (talk to sales). Payroll processing is an add-on at $5.95 per payroll user a month plus a $39.95 monthly base fee. No base price and no setup fee on the plans themselves, unlimited jobs and locations, and a free sign-up to start. History: our earlier read put Starter at about $6.95 and the top tier at $19.95; the current ladder is lower on every rung. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Atto?
answers.a: Simple and honest pricing — the real conversation with any field-team tracker is the human one: GPS tracking of employees needs transparency and often consent (rules differ by country), and adoption dies the day the crew feels surveilled rather than served. Roll it out as 'accurate paychecks and fewer timesheet fights', involve the team, and the tool pays for itself; roll it out as surveillance and no feature list saves it.

Attribuly is genuinely best for stores already running Klaviyo at volume, where a few percent more recovered carts is worth $450 a month and the identity-resolution layer has enough traffic to work with. Skip it if your monthly email revenue is below roughly $5,000 — the entry price eats the gain — or you do not run Klaviyo, since the product is built around it.

(re-verified 2026-09-13 on apps.shopify.com/attribuly; every amount unchanged since 2026-08-18) A free plan that covers the first $1,000 of recovered email revenue, then Capture at $450 a month and Recapture at $500, both with a 14-day free trial. All charges in USD, billed every 30 days. Note the shape: the free tier is metered on recovered revenue rather than on time, so it ends when the tool starts working. The listing's rating moved from 4.8 out of 154 reviews (18 August 2026) to 4.7 out of 166 reviews (13 September 2026), with 76% five-star and 7% one-star. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Attribuly?
answers.a: This is the most expensive app in its category on the Shopify store by a wide margin, and the jump is not gradual — free to $450 a month with nothing in between. It is also an add-on rather than a replacement: the pitch is explicitly that it recovers carts “Klaviyo misses” and syncs identity signals back into Klaviyo, so you are paying for this on top of an email platform you already pay for. Work out what $450 a month needs to recover before it breaks even, and compare that against simply improving the flows you already have.

Audiorista is genuinely best for creators and media brands with a real audio catalog — podcasts, audiobooks, meditations, courses — ready to monetize subscriptions in their own branded apps. Skip it if you are still validating an audio idea on a small catalog or budget: the tier that actually ships to the app stores starts at $240 a month, before store commissions.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page, USD) Demo is $29/mo and Lite $240/mo for iOS and Android apps. Business is from $400/mo per app, plus a tiered variable fee from $0.80 per monthly active user. Enterprise sits on that same $400 per app with further fees based on services, features, extensions and commitment, and the plan card quotes a floor of $5,000/mo. 30-day free trial. Demo carries all Lite features except publishing to the App Store and Google Play, and monetization is disabled on it — a preview tier rather than a product. Paid app sales, RevenueCat in-app subscriptions and Zapier webshop sync start at Lite; the web app, Stripe web payments and push-notification campaigns start at Business. Read the quotas beside the prices, because they decide the tier as much as the money does: Demo and Lite both cap the catalogue at 100 titles, Lite includes only 200 monthly active users, Business lifts users to unlimited but caps the catalogue at 10,000 items, and only Enterprise is unlimited on both counts. Push notifications are still marked Coming Soon on Demo and Lite. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Audiorista?
answers.a: The $29 Demo tier cannot actually publish to the App Store or Google Play — real branded apps start at $240 a month. The Business tier adds a per-active-user fee from $0.80 on top of $400 per app, so growth literally raises the bill — and Apple and Google's own store commissions still apply to in-app sales on top of everything.

Aura is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers past the point where manual repricing costs more attention than it is worth, and whose monthly volume sits comfortably inside one band. Skip it if your catalogue is small or your prices rarely need to move — repricing pays back on competition and volume, and at low volume the $37 is buying automation you could do by hand.

(2026-08-28, checked line by line against their own pricing page; every figure below is the same as on 1 Aug 2026) Flat per account, not per seat, with unlimited listings on every tier. Starter $37/month ($451 a year), Essential $77 ($931), Plus $157 ($1,891), Pro $237 ($2,851) — annual saves 20%. The ladder is set by monthly sales volume, not by features: Starter up to $15K, Essential up to $50K, Plus up to $250K, Pro up to $1M. Marketplaces included: 2, 3, 4 and 6. Aura AI covers 250, 500, 1,000 and unlimited listings; Hyperdrive 10, 25, 50 and 100 allocations; user seats 1, 2, 5 and unlimited. Their table adds three things the earlier reading did not record: monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, workflows run 5, 10, unlimited and unlimited, and there is a 14-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Aura?
answers.a: The tier is decided by how much you sell, not by what you need. That is unusually honest as a model — a seller doing $10K a month is not subsidising one doing $900K — but it means your bill moves when your business does, in the same month, without you choosing to upgrade. Pass $15K and Starter stops being the plan you are on. Work out which band you land in the way the page measures it: their table says monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, so it is a sustained climb rather than a single spike that moves you up. Two smaller things: the marketplace count is a real cap (two on Starter, so Amazon plus one), and the AI listing allowance is per listing rather than per repricing action, so a large catalogue eats it faster than a busy one.

AutoWrite is genuinely best for Shopify stores that want to test AI-written blog posts with SEO scoring at no cost, and who treat the output as a first draft rather than as publishable copy. Skip it if you need a tool with a track record — there is none here yet — or you publish content where accuracy matters enough that an unreviewed generator is a liability.

(read 2026-08-19 in a browser on apps.shopify.com/autowrite, because the plan table renders client-side and a plain fetch returns nothing) Four tiers, metered on posts, images and workflows per month. Free: 10 posts, 10 images, 1 workflow, basic SEO. Starter $9: 30 posts, 30 images, 3 workflows, brand voices, auto-publish, expert SEO. Pro $29: 100 posts, 100 images, 10 workflows, product references, generation priority. Business $79: 300 posts, 300 images, 30 workflows, support priority. All charges are billed in USD every 30 days. Correction to our own earlier note: on 18 August we wrote that the listing showed no paid tiers, which was our reading failing on a client-side table, not the vendor withholding prices. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with AutoWrite?
answers.a: The honest thing to say about this one is that there is nothing to judge yet: on 18 August 2026 the App Store listing showed a rating of 0.0 from zero reviews. Not one merchant has publicly reported using it. That is not a criticism of the product, it is a statement about the evidence — an AI blog writer that nobody has reviewed is a bet, and it should be priced as one. The category it sits in is also crowded with tools that have years of track record behind them.

Auware is genuinely best for Shopify stores running segmented paid campaigns (different personas, interests, offers) who are currently sending all that traffic to one generic page. Skip it if you're not on Shopify, you don't run audience-segmented paid ads, or you just want a flexible general-purpose page builder.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Auware publishes a price after all: $99 a month on auware.com, alongside a 1-click Shopify install with a 30-day free trial that needs no card. Our earlier note said the paid rate was only visible inside the Shopify app — that is no longer the case, and the $99 figure has been on the site since at least early July. Their own pitch compares that with page builders charging up to $499 a month, and the plan is positioned as the full feature set from day one rather than a gated entry tier. Billing still runs through Shopify, so confirm the current rate in the app before committing. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Auware?
answers.a: It's deliberately narrow — Shopify-only and built around segmented paid traffic. If you send everyone to one page or don't run audience-segmented ads, the core 'a page per persona' value doesn't really kick in. It's also newer and less battle-tested than general builders like PageFly.

Ava AI is genuinely best for Shopify DTC and cash-on-delivery stores with real inbound call volume that want 24/7 phone support and outbound cart-recovery automated, and are comfortable with per-minute economics. Skip it if low-call-volume or thin-margin stores where per-minute overage can dwarf the base fee, and anyone who needs a proven track record — the review base is tiny (six) and the app is under a year old.

answers.q: How much does Ava AI cost?
answers.a: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/ava-ai and avasales.ai) Three paid tiers, no free plan, each with a 7-day trial. Support is $29 a month and includes 100 call minutes, then $0.10 a minute; Recover is $99 a month with 400 minutes and $0.08 over; Scale is $499 a month with 1,500 minutes and $0.07 over. The headline price is really a minutes bucket: a store with real call volume pays the overage, so cost tracks conversation length, not seats. Estimate your monthly call minutes before you compare — at heavy volume the effective bill can sit well above the tier price. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Ava AI?
answers.a: The monthly price is a minutes allowance, not a flat fee — every minute past the bucket bills at $0.07 to $0.10, so a busy support line can cost far more than the headline.
