And keep the vendor's marketing at arm's length: Ava launched in September 2025 with just six App Store reviews, and the promoted 21–24x ROAS figures are the vendor's own, not independently verified. There is no free plan, only a 7-day trial.

BabyLoveGrowth is genuinely best for solo founders and lean startups who want hands-off SEO content velocity fast, are comfortable with AI-generated articles at scale, and value the 90-day guarantee as a safety net. Skip it if you're building a long-term brand where a spam-update hit would hurt, or you operate in a YMYL/regulated niche where thin AI content is genuinely risky — human-in-the-loop tools fit better there.

(prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on babylovegrowth.ai/en/pricing from a European connection, where it prices in euros) Two plans and a Monthly/Yearly toggle that swaps the amounts. Paid monthly, Grow is €99 a month and Scale €399, each shown against a struck-through €247 and €599. Switch to "Pay yearly · save 25%" and the same cards read €75 and €291 a month, labelled "Billed yearly"; the page prints no annual total. Grow carries 30 branded AEO/SEO articles a month, 10 AI prompts tracked daily across ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, $800+ a month in backlinks from the 4,000-site partner network, auto-publishing to WordPress, Shopify and eight more CMSs, a technical GEO audit, Reddit and Quora agents, automated keyword research, one seat and email support. Scale carries 120 articles across four languages, 50 prompts tracked, $1,600+ a month in higher-DR backlinks, unlimited seats, priority same-day support, a dedicated 1-on-1 SEO/GEO specialist and monthly reporting with a human. Both start on a 3-day free trial. The cards promise 90 days money back, but the FAQ on the same page says no refunds are given once the three-day trial ends. The feature table below the cards keeps showing €99/mo and €399/mo in both toggle settings. History: on 5 September we read Scale at €224 a month billed €2,691 a year, and its plan text then added a specialist and extra languages but no extra articles or backlink budget; both the price and the contents have changed since. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BabyLoveGrowth?
answers.a: The honest concern here isn't the price — it's the model, and the guarantee that is supposed to cover you if the model fails. Auto-publishing 30 to 120 AI articles a month while swapping backlinks with 4,000 other member sites is exactly the scaled-content-and-reciprocal-links pattern Google's spam policies are written to catch, and the vendor's own FAQ describes the exchange in those terms: your site places links for others as theirs place links for you. It can lift metrics short-term; on a brand you're building for years, it's a real durability risk. The 90-day money-back guarantee used to offset some of that, and we can no longer say it does: the plan cards promise it, and the FAQ on the same page says no refunds are given after the three-day trial ends. Ask for those terms in writing before you pay for a year.

BackupMaster is genuinely best for Shopify stores under roughly 1,500 orders a month that want the whole store backed up daily — metafields, metaobjects and translations included — without anyone having to remember to trigger it. Skip it if you need backups exported to storage you control on the entry tier, an on-demand backup before every risky change, or a written list of what restore does not cover.

(read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/backup-master) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Agency is free to install but only for Shopify Partner development stores before they are transferred to a client, with all features enabled for three months. Essentials $19 a month or $205.20 a year, a 10% saving, covers stores up to 300 orders a month. That is automatic daily backups of products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventories, restore of supported items, 365-day retention and unlimited cloud storage. Pro $39 a month or $421.20 a year covers up to 600 orders a month and adds downloadable backup copies, Google Drive sync and duplication of data for staging or expansion. Plus $79 a month or $853.20 a year covers up to 1,500 orders a month, and adds multi-store pricing, detailed audit logs, external portal access, a custom backup time and priority support. The listing says higher-volume plans exist on the vendor's own pricing page without printing what they cost. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer BackupMaster, Bondi, NSW, Australia; the app launched 4 August 2017, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in English and German, and had 108 reviews at the time of writing. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BackupMaster?
answers.a:
The listing header says free to install, and there is a free tier, but it is not for you unless you are an agency: Agency is limited to Shopify Partner development stores before they are handed over to a client. For a live store the entry price is $19 a month and it buys 300 orders a month.

Restore is described throughout as restoring supported items, and nowhere does the listing say which items are not supported. That phrase is carrying a lot of weight in a product whose entire promise is that you can undo a mistake. Ask for the exclusion list before you rely on it, and run one real restore into a development store rather than discovering the boundary during an incident.

The most useful review on the page is the critical one. In April 2026 a merchant asked for exports over SFTP to storage the vendor does not control, on-demand backups before risky changes, configurable retention and languages beyond English and German. The same merchant noted that a second store costs extra here where some rivals include one. None of that is damning; it is a fair map of where this app currently stops. Worth adding to the same note: your store data sits with a vendor in Australia, which belongs in your processing register whatever you decide.

Barcodes Talk is genuinely best for sellers and small brands listing on marketplaces or in independent retail who want authentic, one-time-cost UPC/EAN barcodes without an annual GS1 membership. Skip it if your target retailer or brand registry explicitly requires a GS1-issued company prefix in your own name — then buy direct from GS1.

answers.q: How much does Barcodes Talk cost?
answers.a: (prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on barcodestalk.com/buy-barcodes) One-off purchase, no subscription and no renewal. The full published ladder runs eighteen rungs: 1 barcode $5.00; 5 for $10.00 ($2.00 each); 10 for $15.00 ($1.50); 25 for $25.00 ($1.00); 50 for $35.00 ($0.70); 100 for $45.00 ($0.45); 200 for $80.00 ($0.40); 500 for $125.00 ($0.25); 1,000 for $180.00 ($0.18); 1,500 for $225.00 ($0.15); 2,000 for $260.00 ($0.13); 2,500 for $300.00 ($0.12); 5,000 for $500.00 ($0.10); 10,000 for $650.00 ($0.065); 25,000 for $1,200.00 ($0.048); 50,000 for $2,300.00 ($0.046); 75,000 for $3,225.00 ($0.043); and 100,000 for $3,500.00 ($0.035). Larger quantities are quote-only. The unit price drops fastest between one and a hundred codes. Every purchase includes both UPC and EAN formats, high-resolution EPS and JPEG images, a Certificate of GTIN Assignment, Excel and PDF spreadsheets of the assigned numbers, instant download, and the vendor's Works for Amazon Guarantee. Unchanged from our 5 September reading. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Barcodes Talk?
answers.a: The honest caveat is about fit, not the codes. Some large retailers and brand registries — notably certain Amazon Brand Registry and big-box requirements — increasingly ask for a GS1-issued prefix tied to your own company, and a third-party barcode (legitimate and globally unique as it is) may not satisfy that specific gatekeeping. For most marketplaces and independent retail it's completely fine and far cheaper; just confirm your channel's exact requirement first.

Beautiful.ai is genuinely best for founders, sales and small teams that want consistently good-looking decks fast, where design consistency matters more than pixel-level control. Skip it if you need intricate custom layouts or complex animations (designers want full control), or your whole company workflow is deeply PowerPoint-native.

(re-verified 2026-09-02 on the vendor's own pricing page) Pro is $14.50/mo billed annually, up from $12 in our July and August 2026 captures ($45 for a one-off month); Team about $40/user/mo annual ($50 monthly) with brand controls and shared libraries; Enterprise custom for 20+ seats. A single one-off presentation can be bought for ~$45; 14-day trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Beautiful.ai?
answers.a: The smart-template engine is the feature and the fence: decks look polished with zero design skill precisely because the system constrains you, so pixel-perfect custom layouts and heavy brand exceptions fight the tool. And note the billing gap — $14.50/mo annual becomes $45 month-to-month, one of the steeper monthly premiums around. If your organisation lives in PowerPoint workflows, test the import/export round-trip before committing.

Beefree is genuinely best for agencies and in-house teams shipping email at volume across brands or ESPs — a dedicated builder with approvals, brand controls and one-click push to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Pardot and HubSpot, sitting above whatever you send with. Skip it if solo senders whose ESP editor already copes — you would be paying for a second tool to do a job your sending platform already does, and you still need the ESP because RGE Studio sends nothing itself.

(price re-verified 2026-09-10) Sold as RGE Studio since the 14 May 2026 rebrand. Starter free — up to 10 designs, 6 exports/mo, landing-page builder, custom subdomain, 20GB/mo image traffic, unlimited users but no roles or permissions. Professional $25/mo billed yearly ($30/mo monthly) — unlimited designs and folders, unlimited reusable blocks, 2 editing users plus 4 view-only, AI writing assistant. Business $134/mo billed yearly ($160/mo monthly) — 2 editing users plus 10 view-only, 2 workspaces, approval workflows, advanced brand controls, QA assistant. Enterprise: custom, quoted by sales. The free trial is 15 days on the Business plan. The embeddable Beefree SDK is a separate product on its own price list (developers.beefree.io) and is not covered by these numbers. Every tier and both billing rates stood unchanged on reallygoodemails.com/pricing between our readings on 21 July, 2 August and 10 September 2026. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Beefree?
answers.a: Read the seat row before the price row. Professional and Business both cap at two full editing seats, so a "mid-sized team" plan at $134/mo annual still buys two people who can actually build. Everyone else lands in view-only slots — four on Professional, ten on Business — or an Enterprise quote. The free Starter is the odd one out: unlimited users, but with no roles or permissions at all. Exports are metered at six a month, rather than the unlimited free tier its old reputation suggests. And the naming is a live tripwire. Since 14 May 2026 the builder is RGE Studio at reallygoodemails.com, while Beefree remains the company name and the name of the separate developer SDK. So check which product a plan or invoice actually refers to. It is purely a creation environment that never sends, so it always sits on top of your ESP. Worth it when the ESP's native editor is the bottleneck — agencies, multi-brand teams, ESP migrations — and duplicated effort when it isn't.

Beehiiv is genuinely best for newsletter operators who want growth tools, automation, SEO control and ad/referral monetisation — and to keep 100% of subscription revenue. Skip it if you're a beginner starting from zero who wants the simplest setup and Substack's built-in discovery, and don't need automation or SEO.

(re-verified 2026-08-16 from beehiiv's own machine-readable pricing file at beehiiv.com/pricing.md, which states USD) Subscriber-based, and you keep 100% of paid subscriptions — beehiiv takes 0%, against Substack's 10%, leaving only Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30. Launch is $0 up to 2,500 subscribers with unlimited sends. At up to 1,000 subscribers Scale is $49/mo billed monthly or $517 a year (about $43/mo), Max $109/mo or $1,151 a year (about $96/mo). At 10,000 subscribers Scale is $109/mo or $1,151 a year; at 50,000 it is $249/mo or $2,629 a year. The ladder tops out at 100,000 subscribers ($329/mo Scale, $459 Max) and Enterprise is custom above that. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Beehiiv?
answers.a: Next to Substack it's more to learn. Substack's built-in discovery network and dead-simple setup are easier if you're starting from zero with no audience and don't care about automation or SEO. Beehiiv's depth is the point, but it's a steeper start.

BidX is genuinely best for brands and agencies already spending well past €10,000 a month on Amazon ads, who want bid, budget and campaign automation, Amazon DSP and AMC reporting in one platform with a named growth manager attached. It also suits teams who value a German vendor with EU invoicing, SEPA and direct debit, and support in English and German. Skip it if your ad spend is under roughly $10K a month, because BidX itself routes you to a different product at that size. Skip it too if you want to try before you commit: there is no free trial, the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path is a paid three-month proof of concept. And skip it if you need your total cost on paper before a sales call, because the percentage of ad spend is unpublished — or if you advertise mainly outside Amazon and Walmart.

(re-verified 2026-09-11, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, EUR view; every figure unchanged since 6 Aug 2026) Amazon PPC is sold in three tiers, and every one of them is a monthly fee plus an unspecified percentage of connected ad spend. They are Self Service Platform €495/month, Managed Platform €1,995/month and Managed Service €4,995/month. The tiers differ mainly in how much of a human you get. That is one monthly strategy call on Self Service, up to two calls and up to 10h of assistance a month on Managed Platform, and up to four calls and up to 32h on Managed Service. Amazon DSP is priced separately on the same page: Self Service €495/month and Managed Service €995/month, again plus a percentage of ad spend. Amazon Marketing Cloud is sold as reporting: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The Share of Voice add-on covers the first 100 keywords free and charges $250 a month per additional 500 keywords. All prices are net with VAT added on top, and the page states that plans are based on an annual commitment paid monthly; the FAQ adds that new customers can take a paid three-month proof-of-concept period first. Walmart Managed Service, high ad-spend volumes and large agencies are contact-sales. Sellers under €10,000 a month in ad spend are pointed to a separate product, BidX Essential, whose own landing page at get.bidx.io/essentials lists $195/month for up to $10K in monthly ad spend — a flat fee with no percentage attached. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BidX?
answers.a:
The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print. Every Amazon PPC and DSP tier ends with “+ % of connected ad spend per month”, and that percentage appears nowhere — not on the tier cards, not in the footnotes, not in the FAQ. So €495 is a floor, not a price, and nobody spending real money on Amazon ads can work out their monthly cost from this page. Ask for the percentage in writing, and ask whether it is charged on all connected spend or only on what BidX manages, before you get as far as a contract.

The second thing to price is the commitment. The page states plans run on an annual commitment paid monthly, and the FAQ confirms it: the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path on offer is a paid three-month proof of concept. There is no free trial. That makes the cheapest visible door €5,940 a year net of VAT before a cent of the percentage — a very different proposition from the €495 the eye lands on.

Two smaller inconsistencies worth noticing, because they tell you how carefully the price list is maintained. On a page priced in euros, the one add-on with a hard number is quoted in dollars ($250 per extra 500 keywords), so ask which currency you are actually billed in. And BidX Essential — the $195/month product they route smaller sellers to — lives on a completely separate landing page carrying a 2024 copyright line and a different phone number. It is not listed among the tiers on the pricing page itself, so confirm it still exists at that price before you plan around it.

Bill.com is genuinely best for growing companies with real accounts-payable volume and approval chains that want to automate bill pay and sync to accounting. Skip it if you pay only a few bills a month — your accounting software or a free tool like Melio's base plan covers it without per-seat fees.

(re-verified 2026-09-15 on their own pricing page) Accounts-payable and receivable plans priced per user: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise - the same four cards as on 15 August 2026. The separate Spend and Expense product is $0 per user per month and carries credit lines the page advertises as $1,000-$5M, not guaranteed and set on approval. Transaction fees stack on top of the seat, and are where the real cost hides. ACH or ePayment is $0.59, a mailed check $1.99, an international USD wire $19.99, and an international FX wire or a virtual card is free - free of a stated fee, that is, because the same row says the exchange rate applies and BILL only discloses that rate at the time of the transaction. Instant payment is 1.0% with a $9.99 minimum and a $100 maximum, and Pay Faster ACH $11.99. Expedited checks are $24.99 overnight, $19.99 two-day and $14.99 three-day. Paying by card costs 2.9%, and the receiver pays 2.9% on credit or debit card payments; a receiver taking an instant transfer pays 1% to 1.49% with a $1 minimum. A second fee block, easy to miss under the payment table, prices the paperwork and the mistakes: 1099 e-filing to the IRS is $2.99 per form ($1.99 through an accountant console), state filing $1.49 and mailing a 1099 to the vendor $1.99, while voiding a check is $25, a returned check $3, a re-debit after failed funding $25 and an ACH that fails after the receiver has been paid $50. The accountant side is priced separately again: a BILL AP & AR Partner subscription at $49 a month, an Accountant Console the FAQ also prices at $49 a month, and a 10-20% client subscription discount that scales with how many clients you onboard. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bill.com?
answers.a: Per-user pricing plus per-transaction fees means the real cost depends on team size and payment volume — it's built for finance teams with genuine AP workflows and is overkill if you pay a handful of bills a month.

BillingNow is genuinely best for freelancers and small teams that want unlimited invoicing, expenses and client management with zero per-user maths — users are unlimited on both plans, so a five-person team pays $2.00 a head. Skip it if you need accountant-grade features, payroll or deep integrations (the incumbents' ecosystems are bigger), or you have an existing client list to bring across — the help centre documents export but no import, so every client has to be retyped.

(re-verified 2026-08-20, read on their own site) Two plans, both carrying the identical feature list with no limits: $9.99 a month, or $99.90 a year which the page itself works out to $8.33 a month and labels 'Save 17%'. Both include unlimited invoices, expenses, client relations, users, estimates and credit notes, plus payment tracking, tax rates, PDF export and the AI assistant. There are no per-user fees and no feature-gated tier. The trial is 3 days and the page states three separate times that no credit card is required to start it. SOC 2 Type II certified with European-standard compliant invoices. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BillingNow?
answers.a: The pricing is genuinely refreshing — two plans, same features on both, unlimited users, no per-seat maths. The honest watch-out is the trial length rather than its terms: three days is short for migrating billing into a new tool, and the practical constraint is that there is no import path. The help centre documents CSV and Excel export but no import, so an existing client list has to be retyped — which is more than three days of work for anyone with a real book. It is also a young product from a small Geneva maker, so weigh ecosystem depth and longevity before you move your billing history in.

Birch is genuinely best for performance marketers and agencies running real ad budgets who want rule-based automation, scaling and creative insights across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat. Skip it if you run small, simple campaigns a native ads manager handles fine, or you're not comfortable defining automation rules (bad rules scale bad decisions).

(price re-verified 2026-09-11 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026, formerly Revealbot) Essential is $49/mo and Pro $99/mo up to $10K of monthly ad spend, and the price then tracks total spend across all connected accounts. Essential steps to $149 at $30K, $299 at $75K and $499 at $150K, where the tier stops; Pro steps to $249, $499, $799, $1,299 and $1,799 against $30K, $75K, $150K, $300K and $500K. Above $500K only Enterprise remains, priced on request with no spend limit. Every current tier card reads ‘No overages apply’ — the percentage-of-overspend meter now applies to legacy monthly plans only, and the pricing FAQ’s own ‘About overages’ link 301-redirects to an article titled about-additional-charges-legacy-plans. 14-day free trial, no card required. Annual billing is charged as eleven months ($540 Essential, $1,090 Pro at the $10K tier), though the same FAQ still claims ‘12 months for the price of 10’. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Birch?
answers.a: The honest catch is that pricing tracks your ad spend, so a scaling advertiser's bill rises with their budget: Pro alone ladders from $99 to $1,799 a month between a $10,000 and a $500,000 ceiling, and past $500,000 only Enterprise is left. Check the annual arithmetic against their own FAQ, which promises ‘12 months for the price of 10’ while the page charges eleven — $540 for Essential and $1,090 for Pro at the entry tier. It's also a power tool: rule-based automation across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat rewards advertisers who know what to automate, and can amplify mistakes if your rules are wrong. For hands-on performance marketers, it's a serious time-saver.

Bitdefender is genuinely best for small businesses that want top-tier, independently-validated endpoint protection managed from one console. Skip it if you're a solo user with basic needs — built-in OS defenses plus good habits may be enough before you pay for a business console.

Read on their own product pages, 6 September 2026, where a configurator prices each tier by device count and term. At 10 devices for one year the list prices are GravityZone Small Business Security $324.99, Business Security $384.99 and Business Security Premium $879.99 — $32.50, $38.50 and $88.00 per device per year. A 30% discount is applied by default on all three, bringing them to $227.49, $269.49 and $615.99. Small Business Security at 5 devices for one year is $169.99 list, $118.99 discounted. Add-ons are priced separately: at 10 devices, Web Access and Device Control $41.99 and Network Attack Defense and Risk Management $41.99 on Small Business Security, Setup & Go $224.99, and Essential: Tips & Best Practices $54.99 a seat. Enterprise Security, Defense XDR and MDR are contact-sales. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bitdefender?
answers.a: The price you see is already discounted: the configurator applies 30% off list by default on all three GravityZone tiers, so compare on the discounted figure and ask what applies at renewal rather than assuming the same 30% comes back. Add-ons are billed separately too — web access and device control, network attack defense and risk management, and setup each carry their own line. Protection scores are consistently strong, so the real trade-off is cost, not efficacy.

Bitscale is genuinely best for sales and RevOps teams that already run enrichment across several vendors and want the waterfall, the signals and the CRM sync in one place, with enough monthly volume to put 15,000 credits to work. Skip it if you enrich a few hundred records a month -- the free 200 credits or a per-lookup tool costs a fraction -- or you need a flat, predictable bill, because credits are consumption and consumption moves with your prospecting.

(re-verified 13 September 2026 on bitscale.ai/pricing, extended on 11 September 2026 from inside a free account; every headline figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) The meter is credits. Free is $0 with 200 credits, no card required, capped at 20 action columns per grid and 50,000 rows. Growth is $349 a month for 15,000 credits, 30 action columns and 100,000 rows, with a two-way HubSpot integration and inbound integrations like RB2B, Factors and Vector. Booster is $799 for 50,000 credits and 50 action columns, adding curated scraping scripts, a private Slack channel and Salesforce integration. Enterprise is quote-only but publishes a floor most vendors hide: annual billing at $15,000 and above, adding SOC 2 and SSO, priority support, role-based team access and Snowflake pipelines. Annual billing takes 10% off. Two lines in the plan table change the arithmetic and are easy to miss. Credits roll over up to three times the plan allowance on Growth and Booster, and not at all on Free, so a quiet month is banked rather than lost. And a credit is spent only when a data provider returns a valid result -- the pricing FAQ says failed lookups, formula columns and CRM syncs are always free -- so a waterfall that finds nothing costs nothing. The page also contradicts itself twice: the comparison table gives all four tiers 100+ data sources while the Free card says 10+ B2B data sources, and the Growth and Booster cards both promise Unlimited Actions while the same page's table caps action columns per grid at 30 and 50. The step from Free to Growth is still the one to plan for: 200 credits to 15,000 with nothing in between, so the bill goes from nothing to $4,188 a year in one move. Monthly company and people search is metered separately at 2,000 on Free, 15,000 on Growth and 50,000 on Booster. Two things the pricing page does not tell you, both read on 11 September 2026. First, what a credit actually buys: Bitscale's own credit documentation prices a found email or phone number at one to twelve platform credits per successful result, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try, with an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run and a BitAgent website scrape at one. Calls that come in through the API cost nothing. Second, the free tier runs two meters rather than one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits for enrichment and a separate 2,000 search credits for Find People and Find Companies, each resetting monthly. The upgrade panel inside the product also carries a Growth benefit the plan cards leave out -- three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer -- and states plainly what Free locks: credit rollover, more than 20 action columns per grid, the 100+ providers and the inbound integrations. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bitscale?
answers.a:
The free tier is real and needs no card, which makes Bitscale unusually easy to judge for yourself before paying. What to check during that trial is not the feature list but your own burn rate, and Bitscale's credit table tells you the range in advance: one to twelve credits for every email or phone the waterfall finds, depending on how many providers you let it try. That is the whole budget question. The same 15,000 credits on Growth are 15,000 enriched contacts at one credit and 1,250 at twelve, so the plan you buy matters less than the depth you configure. Run fifty real records on the free 200 credits, read the meter before and after, and multiply by your monthly volume -- that number, not the plan price, is your bill.

One free-tier number is worth holding against the other. The plan table gives Free a 50,000-row grid, while Bitscale's own onboarding mail says the free plan scores up to 200 rows at a time -- and both are true, because a Score column, which grades every row against an ideal-customer profile you describe in plain English, is an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run. The grid is not the ceiling, the 200 credits are. Finding the names draws on the separate pool of 2,000 search credits, so building the list is the cheap half; asking the product to judge it is the half that runs out.

Bitvavo is genuinely best for EU-based traders and builders who want a MiCA-regulated, euro-native exchange with low tiered fees, deep EUR pairs and a solid API for automation. Skip it if you're outside the EU (it's euro-centric), you trade exotic altcoins it doesn't list, or you need derivatives-first infrastructure.

(re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own fees page) No subscription — you pay per trade. EUR markets (Category A) run ten volume tiers. It is 0.15% maker / 0.25% taker below €100,000 of 30-day volume, then 0.10%/0.20% from €100,000, 0.09%/0.18% from €250,000, 0.08%/0.16% from €500,000 and 0.05%/0.14% from €1,000,000. Above that: 0.03%/0.12% from €2,500,000, 0.01%/0.10% from €5,000,000, 0.00%/0.08% from €10,000,000, 0.00%/0.04% from €25,000,000 and 0.00%/0.02% above €100,000,000. USDC markets (Category B) are a separate schedule from 0.05% maker and taker, and stablecoin pairs (Category C) from 0.10%; Bitvavo states that stablecoin trades do not count towards the 30-day volume that sets your tier. Deposits are free by SEPA, iDEAL/Wero, Apple Pay and Bancontact; a credit card costs 1%, PayPal 2% and EPS or Giropay 1.75%. Margin positions carry a separate hourly borrowing fee, published at 0.0023% an hour on every listed asset, plus a 2% fee if the position is liquidated. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bitvavo?
answers.a: The honest caveats are crypto-wide, not Bitvavo-specific: fees are only part of the cost (spread matters on small orders), and no exchange removes market risk — the platform being cheap and MiCA-regulated doesn't make the assets safe. Note the disclosure: this is one of the few tools here we genuinely run — our own trading system executes on Bitvavo — which is experience, but also means we're an actual customer, not a neutral bystander.

Blinq is genuinely best for teams and field-sales orgs that want consistent, branded digital cards with contacts syncing straight into the CRM — and events teams via the capture add-on. Skip it if you're an individual (the free tier honestly covers you), or your networking volume doesn't justify per-user pricing.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). For individuals, Premium is $9.99 a month billed monthly or $7.33 billed annually. For teams, Business is $6.99 per user a month billed monthly or $4.99 per user billed annually, with a 5-user minimum, adding CRM sync, templates and custom reporting. Enterprise is custom. A lead-capture add-on for events starts around $199/mo. Note the individual plan costs more per person than the team plan — if there are five of you, the team tier is both cheaper per head and more capable. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Blinq?
answers.a: The core product is honestly cheap — the price jump hides in the event lead-capture add-on (~$199/mo), which is where teams that live on trade shows actually get value. And a truth about all digital cards: the wow factor works precisely because adoption is still low; the durable value is the CRM sync (contacts flowing automatically into your pipeline), so judge Business tier by that integration, not by the tap-to-share trick.

Blocky is genuinely best for Shopify stores below Plus that are losing time to bot traffic, repeat fraudsters or orders from regions they do not ship to, and want blocking rules they control rather than a full security suite. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus, where the paid plans exclude you outright, or you need chargebacks disputed and revenue recovered rather than visitors kept out.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/blocky-simple-country-blocker) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial, and every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026. Development Stores is free but only for development and partner stores; it carries all Pro features and starts billing on upgrade. Basic $9.99 a month or $83.92 a year, a 30% saving: enforcement inside the checkout page, unlimited country blocking, a fully customisable blocked page and online support. Advanced $16.99 a month or $142.71 a year adds unlimited IP blocking for IPv4 and IPv6, an IP whitelist and a geolocation country redirector. Pro $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year adds blocking by email, name, address and phone, the Bot Killer for TOR, proxy and VPN traffic, an add-ons blocker, a right-click blocker and unlimited visitor analytics traffic logs. All three paid tiers carry the same restriction in their own plan text: all stores except for Shopify Plus stores. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, 7722119, Israel; the app launched 7 April 2021, still carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and is available in eleven languages. The review record has moved: 346 reviews averaging 4.7, up from 324 on 22 August, distributed 89% five-star (308), 5% four-star (16), 1% three-star (3), 0% two-star (1) and 5% one-star (18) — three more one-star reviews than a month ago. The developer replies to reviews on the listing, including an August 2026 reply explaining what the Basic plan is meant to cover. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Blocky?
answers.a:
Read the plan text before you read the badge. The App Store header says a free plan is available; that free plan is Development Stores, for development and partner stores only, and it starts charging the moment the store goes live. All three paid tiers then carry the line 'all stores except for Shopify Plus stores', so if you are on Plus this app is not sold to you. Check that with the developer before you plan around it.

A blocker is a blunt instrument, and the review distribution shows it: 346 reviews, 89% of them at the top rating and 5% at the bottom — eighteen one-star reviews, three of them added in the last month. Rules that stop fraud also stop customers. A blocked country catches the expat who genuinely wanted to buy; a VPN rule catches the privacy-minded shopper. The tuning is yours to do, continuously, using visitor analytics that only the Pro tier includes.

And it prevents rather than recovers. Nothing here disputes a chargeback that has already landed or claws back an order that already shipped. For that you need a separate dispute tool, which is a second subscription on top of this one.

Bokun is genuinely best for tour, activity and experience operators who want booking management plus wide OTA distribution (Viator, GetYourGuide and more) from one dashboard. Skip it if you're a tiny operator taking a handful of direct bookings where the fees and setup outweigh the reach, or you want to stay off OTA rails entirely.

(price re-verified 2026-09-11 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) A free version (1 user) plus paid plans from $49/mo (Start, up to 5 users), $149 (Plus, up to 10) and $499 (Premium, unlimited). Service fee on applicable bookings varies by plan (1.5% Start, 1.25% Plus, 1% Premium), and any paid plan lets you pass that fee on to the guest. Crucially, zero Bókun booking fee on Viator and offline bookings — with one exception the tier table does not show: Channel Manager customers, who connect their own reservation system, are charged 0.5-1.5% on Viator reservations. 14-day free trial, no card, cancel anytime. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bokun?
answers.a: Bokun is a Tripadvisor/Viator company, and that's both the draw and the lock-in. Distribution to Viator and 2,600+ resellers is excellent, but you're building your booking backbone inside one OTA's ecosystem, and the per-booking service fee on direct sales is a real cut on top of the subscription — although any paid plan lets you pass that fee to the guest instead of absorbing it. The zero-fee promise on Viator bookings has one exception the tier table does not show: Channel Manager customers pay 0.5-1.5% on Viator reservations. If most of your business is direct, weigh that fee; if you live on OTA distribution, the Viator advantage is hard to beat.

Bolt Business is genuinely best for companies with European/African travel footprints that want employee rides centrally billed, policy-controlled and expense-integrated — at zero platform cost. Skip it if US-only operations (network coverage), or you need guaranteed fixed-price corporate transport contracts.

answers.q: How much does Bolt Business cost?
answers.a: No subscription, no activation cost and no minimum commitment (re-verified 2026-08-20 on Bolt's own business page): you pay per ride or rental taken, with consolidated monthly billing, spend limits and policy controls included. One line the marketing does not carry, but Bolt's own support pages do: Bolt charges a service fee on every trip made with the business payment method, billed at the start of the following month. On credit card it is deducted automatically and does not appear on the individual trip invoice — it arrives as a separate service fee statement on the 3rd of each month; on postpaid it sits on the monthly invoice. The amount is not published. Still commitment-free to pilot, but ‘you only pay for the rides’ is not the whole bill. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bolt Business?
answers.a: The honest boundary is geography: Bolt's network is Europe/Africa-centric across 600+ cities, so US-only operations should look elsewhere, and ride availability varies by city — pilot it on your team's actual routes. Pricing is dynamic like all ride-hailing; the business layer adds control and receipts, not fixed corporate fares, so budget-predictability comes from your spend limits, not from locked prices.

BookX is genuinely best for Shopify merchants running appointment-based services — salons, studios, clinics, rentals, classes and events — who want the booking calendar inside the store they already sell from, with staff and multi-location schedules and payment taken at the Shopify checkout.. Skip it if you do not sell on Shopify; you need a booking system that stands on its own website and payment flow so customers who never visit your shop can still book; or you run more than twenty staff or locations and want a published price before you commit..

(read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/appointment-booking-bookeasy and checked against the vendor's own pricing section on logbase.io, which lists the same tiers) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is locations and team members rather than bookings — every tier, the free one included, carries unlimited bookings. Free costs nothing and covers one service and one team member, minute or hour scheduling, lead and buffer time, email notifications, timezone and multi-language support, blockout dates and slots, and live support by chat, email and Zoom. Starter is $9.99 a month or $107.99 a year (10% off) and lifts that to five locations and team members with unlimited services, full-day, multi-day and bundle bookings, Google Calendar and Zoom, book-now-pay-later and partial payments, customer reschedule and cancel, and a universal booking button. Growth is $19.99 or $203.99 a year (15%) for ten locations and team members, deposits and multi-payment options, workflows and a custom email sender, Shopify Flow and POS, seasonal pricing and advanced bundle and multi-day conditions. Business is $39.99 or $407.99 a year (15%) for twenty locations and team members, the all-in-one booking widget, two-way Google Calendar sync per team member, advanced seasonal pricing, Klaviyo and webhook integrations and priority support. Every paid tier has a 14-day free trial. What the table does not publish is what happens above twenty locations or team members: the ladder simply ends there. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BookX?
answers.a: The free plan is a demonstration rather than a plan. One service and one team member means a salon with two stylists, or a studio running two class types, is already on Starter — so treat $9.99 a month as the real entry price, not zero. From there the ladder is gated on locations and team members rather than on how much you actually book: five, ten and twenty at $9.99, $19.99 and $39.99. A busy single-location business therefore pays the same as a quiet one, which is generous, while a small chain climbs the ladder for reasons that have nothing to do with volume. Above twenty locations or team members the published table stops and you have to ask. And the whole thing only exists inside Shopify — the calendar rides on your storefront, checkout and POS — so there is nothing here for a business that takes bookings anywhere else.

Bookyourdata is genuinely best for sporadic, project-based prospecting where a subscription would idle — buy exactly the verified contacts you need, when you need them. Skip it if you prospect continuously at volume (subscription databases price better), or your market is EU-consumer-adjacent where purchased-list outreach gets legally delicate.

(re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) Pay-as-you-go, no subscription: one credit is one full contact. The published pack table runs 250 credits for $99 ($0.40 each), 500 for $159, 1,000 for $299 ($0.30), 2,500 for $599 and 5,000 for $799 ($0.16). From there it goes 10,000 for $999 ($0.10), 25,000 for $2,099 ($0.08), 50,000 for $3,699 ($0.07), 100,000 for $5,499 ($0.05) and on up to 2,500,000 for $24,999 ($0.010), with anything larger quoted. New accounts get a Free Pack of 10 credits once, with no card. Credits never expire and the 97% deliverability guarantee refunds credits, not money. BeSpoke, the hand-built private list service, is priced separately from $499 for 1,000 records. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bookyourdata?
answers.a: The model is honest — no subscription, credits keep, bad data refunded — so the real scrutiny belongs on usage. Bought lists are only as good as your targeting and your sending infrastructure, and cold-emailing purchased contacts has legal boundaries that vary by country, GDPR territory especially. The data being accurate doesn't make the campaign compliant; that part is yours.

Boulevard is genuinely best for salons, spas and clinics with staff to schedule and a front desk to run — the per-location pricing works out fine for one busy site. Skip it if you are a solo practitioner with a calendar and a card reader, because the entry tier at $140 a month is priced for a team, and multi-location owners should price the add-ons per site before comparing.

(2026-09-17, read on their own pricing page) Priced per location per month, and the page opens on its Annually tab, so the headline figures are annual-billing rates: Essentials $143, Premier $234 and Prestige $328 per location. The toggle's own label puts monthly billing 10% above that. Premier and Prestige still carry the summer sticker — $234 against a 'normally' $293 and $328 against $410, footnoted limited-time and new customers only — but Essentials no longer does: it lost the struck-through $176, rose from $140 to $143 since we read the page on 18 August 2026, and had its allowances raised to 250 texts, 1,000 email blasts and 50 GB of storage. Prestige lists 100 GB. Enterprise is a bespoke quote and a separate Medspa tab carries its own bundles. Paid add-ons sit on top, also per location: Forms from $65 per month per location, QuickBooks $45, ePrescribe $45 per prescriber, and email beyond the included allowance at $0.01 each. Every tier's button is 'Get a demo': there is no self-serve checkout at any price. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Boulevard?
answers.a: Two things about this price list. It is per location, so the arithmetic for a second salon is not a volume discount, it is double — and the add-ons are per location too, which compounds it. And the prices you see are annual-billing rates: the page opens on its Annually tab and the toggle puts monthly billing 10% higher, so the sticker is the cheapest version of the number. Two of the three tiers still show that sticker struck through against a higher 'normally' figure, footnoted on 17 September 2026 as a limited-time offer for new customers only; treat the higher number as the list price a renewal may return to. Essentials shows what that looks like when the music stops: on 18 August it was $140 against a struck-through $176, and a month later the discount and the comparison are both gone and it reads $143. The third thing is not a price at all: you cannot buy this without booking a demo. That is a signal about how the deal is done, and it means the published numbers are a starting point rather than a checkout.

Bouncer is genuinely best for email marketers and outbound teams that clean lists regularly and want accurate verification with fair credit mechanics (no expiry, no double-charging). Skip it if you send rarely to a stable opt-in list (occasional pay-as-you-go beats any subscription), or your problem is content/reputation rather than list hygiene.

Email verification credits, pay-as-you-go and never expiring (re-verified 2026-09-11): $8 per 1,000 credits is the minimum purchase. Volume brings the rate down to $35 per 5,000, $60 per 10,000 and $250 per 50,000. Above that it runs $400 per 100,000, $750 per 250,000, $1,250 per 500,000 and $2,000 per 1,000,000 - about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume, with anything above a million quoted by sales. The same calculator offers a monthly-subscription mode for verification that Bouncer states is discounted against pay-as-you-go; it publishes no fixed monthly tiers, so price it at your own volume. 100 free credits to test; duplicates and 'unknown' results aren't charged. The $25/$125/$250 per month tiers are the separate Deliverability Kit and now carry published allowances - 250, 1,000 and 2,500 test emails and 10, 25 and 50 IPs or domains monitored, with an unlimited Enterprise tier on quote. Shield is a separate real-time product laddered by monthly checks: $2 for 1,000, $20 for 10,000, $300 for 250,000 and $1,050 for 1,000,000. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bouncer?
answers.a: Not charging for unknowns and duplicates is genuinely fair — many rivals do. The honest framing for any verifier: it removes invalid addresses, which protects deliverability, but it can't make a cold list warm or a purchased list legitimate. Verify before every big send (lists decay measurably per month), and treat 'accept-all' domain results as the gamble they are, not as verified.

Bread & Butter is genuinely best for marketing and revenue teams that want engaged visitors — people who filled a form or left an email — automatically enriched, scored and nurtured, on a genuinely usable freemium tier. Skip it if you want IP-based company guessing at anonymous visitors — that’s a different tool class (Leadfeeder-style) with a different accuracy and compliance profile — or you run many small sites, where per-website pricing adds up.

answers.q: How much does Bread & Butter cost?
answers.a: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against breadbutter.io) (2026) Fully functional 30-day free trial that moves to a freemium tier after (200 lead profiles, unlimited traffic). AI Enabled Pro $49 per month PER WEBSITE: full AI lead intelligence, enrichment, intent scoring, nurture and attribution with 5,000 lead profiles. AI capacity scales via add-on blocks: +$49/mo per Scale-AI-Enrichment block (+10,000 compute credits) and +$89/mo per deep-profile-research block (100 → 300 profiles/month). Enterprise is custom. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bread & Butter?
answers.a: Two meters to watch: it prices per WEBSITE (multi-site setups multiply the $49) and the AI features run on compute-credit blocks that stack as usage grows. On privacy, refined twice in open dialogue with the vendor (16 Jul 2026, verified against their docs). The anonymous journey IS tracked from the first visit, server-side via their site plugin. So ad-blockers and Safari’s ITP don’t strip it the way they kill client-side scripts — the vendor estimates 30-50% of high-value traffic is lost to client-side blocking. What stays dormant until someone submits an email is identity resolution — the ‘hand-raise’ that connects the captured history to a verified person. You still owe normal GDPR care on enriched data, and the real trade-off is simply this: no IP-based guessing at which company an anonymous visitor works for.

Breezy HR is genuinely best for small teams hiring for a few roles at once that want a visual, drag-and-drop pipeline without enterprise-ATS pricing. Skip it if you hire once or twice a year — the free single-position plan is plenty, and the paid jump only pays off with concurrent open roles.

answers.q: How much does Breezy HR cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A genuinely permanent free Bootstrap plan: one open position, unlimited users. Paid, annual against monthly: Startup $157/mo or $189, Growth $273/mo or $329, Business $439/mo or $529, plus a custom-quoted Pro tier. Every paid tier includes unlimited users and unlimited positions, which is what separates it from per-seat applicant tracking. Onboarding is a separate product, starting at $49/mo for automated role-based workflows that sync with the ATS. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Breezy HR?
answers.a: The jump from free (one position) to the first paid tier is steep if you only hire occasionally — the free plan is genuinely usable, so live in it until you're filling several roles at once.

Brevo is genuinely best for businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size. Skip it if you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency.

Read on brevo.com/pricing on 6 September 2026 with the currency switched to US dollars and the yearly tab open: Free at $0 with 300 emails a day; Starter from $9 a month for 5,000 emails, or $8.08 on yearly billing; Standard from $18 ($16.17 yearly) adding marketing automation and A/B testing; Professional from $499 ($449 yearly, from 150,000 emails) with multi-user access and contact scoring; Enterprise on quote. Email volume is the headline meter, but every send tier also caps stored contacts: Free stores up to 100,000 contacts (automation on 2,000 of them); on Starter and Standard, 5,000 monthly sends store up to 500 contacts, 10,000 sends up to 1,500, 15,000 up to 2,500 and 20,000 sends or more up to 500,000; Professional stores up to 2 million and only Enterprise is unlimited (help.brevo.com, About Brevo's pricing plans, read 15 September 2026). So a big list you rarely mail still needs the send tier that stores it. Re-verified 19 September 2026 in a browser, this time in the euro view the page serves from the Netherlands and with the plan builder open: Starter €7 a month or €6.33 on yearly billing (the toggle is labelled -10%), Standard €15 or €13.50, Professional €499 or €449.08 with 10 seats included, and Free unchanged at 300 emails a day once Brevo has approved the account for sending. Two things the builder now puts on the public page that we previously had to cite the help centre for: the 5,000-email step lists 500 contacts and 1,000 web-push subscribers as included, and removing the “Sent with Brevo” footer is an €8.10-a-month add-on on Starter while Standard includes it. The Sales Essentials CRM is billed separately at €26.08 a month per seat, Sales Advanced at €53.08. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Brevo?
answers.a: Charging by sends looks cheaper for a big list you email rarely, but the send tiers cap stored contacts too: 5,000 sends a month stores only 500 contacts, and a 20,000-contact list needs the 20,000-send tier whatever you send. Model both numbers first — and the free daily cap and add-on fees on top.

Bright Data is genuinely best for data teams and enterprises with real, ongoing web-data needs (pricing intelligence, market research) that justify committed volume and pass use-case vetting. Skip it if you need occasional small scrapes (Browse.ai-class tools or datasets are far cheaper), or your use-case wouldn't survive a compliance review.

answers.q: How much does Bright Data cost?
answers.a: Usage-based (re-verified 2026-09-11): residential proxies start at $4.00/GB with no commitment, against a struck-through $8 — the $2.50/GB rate the overview page leads with is the $1,999/month tier, not the entry price. The committed residential tiers read $3.50/GB at $499/month (141 GB included), $3.00/GB at $999 (332 GB) and $2.50/GB at $1,999 (798 GB). Per-IP products are laddered the same way, and the headline rates are volume floors rather than starting points: datacenter runs $1.40/IP at 10 IPs, $1.00 at 100, $0.95 at 500 and $0.90 at 1,000, while ISP runs $1.80, $1.45, $1.40 and $1.30 across the same steps — so the real minimum is $14/month for ten datacenter IPs, not the $0.90 on the nav. API side: Unlocker, Crawl and SERP APIs from $1/1k requests (free tiers available), Scraper APIs $1.50/1k records pay-as-you-go with a 5K/month free tier and a $499 Scale plan bundling 384,000 records at $1.30/1k overage, Data Firehose $0.20/1k, Datasets from $250/100k records; managed offerings from $1,500/mo (Managed Data Acquisition) and Retail Insights from $2,000/mo. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bright Data?
answers.a: This is enterprise-grade web data infrastructure at enterprise-grade prices — the per-GB meter looks small until you multiply by real scraping volume, and the committed tiers only pay off if your usage is steady. The bigger honest note is compliance: Bright Data is strict about KYC and use-cases (a feature, not a bug), and whatever you collect still has to respect the target sites' terms and applicable law. Budget legal thought alongside the gigabytes.

Browse.ai is genuinely best for ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers. Skip it if you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot.

(price re-verified 2026-09-14 on browse.ai/pricing, both billing columns read) Credit-metered (2026): Free ~50 credits/mo (2 sites); Personal about $19/mo annual (12,000 credits/yr, 5 sites); Professional ~$69/mo annual (60,000 credits, 10 sites); Premium custom (600k+ credits, managed). A credit ≈ 10 extracted rows; premium sites cost more credits. Seats come with the plan: 3 users on Free and Personal, 10 on Professional. Extra websites cost $4/mo on Personal and $2.40/mo on Professional, paid annually. Bigger credit buckets are sold inside a plan rather than by upgrading: Personal 24,000 credits a year at $38/mo, Professional 120,000 at $129, 240,000 at $239 and 360,000 at $319. Credits reset at the end of the billing cycle and do not carry over unless you upgrade first; data retention is 90 days on all three self-serve plans, and the shortest monitor interval is hourly on Free against 5 minutes on the paid plans. Watch out for one vendor-side inconsistency: browse.ai/llms.txt, the file AI assistants are pointed at, still lists Starter $49, Professional $149 and Team $399 plans that do not appear anywhere on the pricing page (both read 14 September 2026). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Browse.ai?
answers.a: Two honest realities of no-code scraping. Credits burn faster than expected: row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter, so monitor a big site daily and do the math first. And scrapers break when sites redesign — robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.

BrowserAct is genuinely best for teams that need a reusable web scraper or browser bot without writing selectors, want the browsers, residential proxies and CAPTCHA handling managed for them, and can commit to yearly billing -- at $13 a month Basic is a cheap way to run a few scheduled bots. Skip it if you will bill month to month (20 to 25 percent more than yearly, not the doubling the struck-through prices suggest), your jobs are proxy-heavy (one gigabyte of residential traffic is 5,000 credits, half of Basic's monthly pool), or you need a published overage rate before you commit, because the credit-pack price is not on the page.

(prices read 2026-09-13 on browseract.com/pricing, both billing tabs open, and cross-read against browseract.com/llms.txt the same day) A credit-metered subscription with a free tier. CHANGED SINCE 2026-09-02: the monthly tab no longer charges the list price. Basic now bills $16 a month with $20 struck through, Essential $70 with $100 struck through and Advanced $120 with $200 struck through -- exactly the discounted monthly figures that were visible only inside the app on 2026-09-04, now published on the pricing page itself. Yearly billing is unchanged: $13/month ($156), $56/month ($672) and $96/month ($1,152). ALSO CHANGED: the Free Trial card now reads 200 Free Credits on signup, 2 Free Agent Builds, 2 simultaneous tasks and 5 free local browsers, where on 2026-09-02 it read 1,500 credits on signup. Uniquely, the vendor's own llms.txt read the same day says the Free Trial carries 2,000 free credits -- a tenfold disagreement between two vendor documents on the same day, and we quote the pricing-page figure because that is the card a buyer sees. Paid allowances are unchanged: 10,000, 50,000 and 100,000 credits a month with 10, 20 and 40 simultaneous tasks, up to 5, 25 and 50 static proxies, 10, 50 and 100 free local browsers, a 7-day free trial per paid tier (1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 credits) and access to extra credit packs; every paid tier now also lists Unlimited MCP Servers. The meters are published on the same page: a workflow step costs 5 credits, a local fingerprint browser 100 credits, residential proxy traffic 5,000 credits per GB; static proxies are priced by location and tier without a figure, and the cloud browser is free for a limited time. The page also claims about $0.10 per 100-row run, roughly $0.001 per data row. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BrowserAct?
answers.a: The yearly toggle wears a -20% badge and the crossed-out prices suggest much more, but read what you would actually be charged on 13 September 2026: monthly is $16, $70 and $120, and yearly is $13, $56 and $96, so paying month to month costs roughly 20 to 25 percent more -- not the doubling the struck-through $20, $100 and $200 imply. Those list prices are the discount's anchor, not a rate anyone is currently offered. The free tier is the bigger catch: its card now reads 200 signup credits where it read 1,500 on 2 September, which at 5 credits a workflow step is 40 steps, while the vendor's own llms.txt still advertises 2,000. And the 'as low as' figures under the meters do not come from these tiers either: at Advanced a credit works out to about $0.00096, so a 5-credit workflow step is roughly $0.0048, not the advertised $0.0032 -- that lower number must belong to a credit pack whose price the page does not show. In the hands-on run of 4 September the meter was honest at account level (1,500 to 1,174 credits over one build and two runs, reconciling exactly with the history list), but the same Bot cost 21 credits on one run and 27 on the next for identical output, and the task panel briefly reported 0 credits for a run the list priced at 21.

BuddyPunch is genuinely best for small-to-mid teams that need straightforward employee time tracking with GPS and payroll-ready exports. Skip it if you're a team of two or three — the fixed base fee makes the per-head cost sting until you scale up.

Per user plus a base fee, read on buddypunch.com/pricing on 5 September 2026: Starter $5.99 per user a month, Pro $7.99 and Advanced $13.99, each with a $19 base fee a month. Scheduling is $1 per user on Starter (included from Pro), real-time GPS $2 per user, onboarding and task checklists $4 per user, extended data retention $2 per user; the payroll add-on is $8 per user plus a $49 base fee a month. 14-day free trial, no card. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BuddyPunch?
answers.a: That flat $19 base fee makes it pricey for very small teams — at three or four users the base fee dominates the bill, so it's better value once you're past a handful of employees.

BugHerd is genuinely best for web agencies and site teams that want clients to point-and-click feedback directly on the page — and, new in 2026, want AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and others) to read, triage and action that feedback via BugHerd's MCP server, free in beta. Skip it if you don't work with external clients or website revisions (a plain issue tracker is enough), or you need deep dev-workflow tracking that belongs in Jira.

Standard about $42/mo (5 members), Studio ~$67/mo (10), Premium ~$125/mo (25), plus custom Enterprise — all with unlimited projects and unlimited client users; annual billing runs $500/$800/$1,500 per year (two months free), extra members $6.60/user/mo billed annually ($80 a year each). Free trial. Prices in US dollars before tax (re-verified 2026-09-05; unchanged since our July read). The MCP server and the other AI features now sit inside the Standard plan on the pricing page, still marked beta. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with BugHerd?
answers.a: The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly: your clients report for free as guests, but everyone on your side who works the feedback needs a seat, so a growing agency steps up tiers. It's deliberately a visual-feedback layer, not a full project-management or dev-issue tracker — most teams run it alongside Jira/Trello rather than instead of. The new MCP feature is genuinely interesting but currently beta: treat AI-agents-triaging-your-feedback as a bonus to evaluate, not the reason to buy.

Buzz.ai is genuinely best for GTM teams that want AI to run outbound end-to-end — prompt-driven prospecting of intent-ready buyers, multichannel sequences and meeting booking without adding SDR headcount. Skip it if you send low-volume, hand-crafted outreach (per-seat-plus-credits is overkill), or you're not ready to QA an AI that writes to your market on your behalf.

(price re-verified 2026-09-05) Teams: Core is $79 per seat a month with 500 credits a month, AI Employee $695 per seat a month with 5,000 credits; both are billed monthly and show a $0 setup fee, footnoted 'waived on prepaid annual'. Enterprise is custom: 25,000 credits a month, five seats included and a $2,500 setup fee. An 'Annual, 25% off' toggle sits above the cards, but the page kept showing the monthly figures when we switched it, so treat the annual price as unpublished until sales confirms it. A White-label tab adds Core White Label at $1,000 a month with 20 seats included, billed annually, and AI Employee White Label at $250 per seat a month billed annually with a five-seat minimum (advertised as 64% off, 'save $445 a seat'), 25,000 credits a month and a $2,500 setup fee on both. Free start on Core. History: in August 2026 the page said Core $125 (launch offer $75 for three months) and AI Employee $795 with a warning it would move to $1,000; on 2 September we read $79 and $695 and wrote that the credits were no longer stated and that one plan carried the $2,500 fee — on 5 September the credits are stated per plan and the $2,500 fee sits on Enterprise and the white-label plans, not on Core or AI Employee. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Buzz.ai?
answers.a: Two meters run at once: seats AND credits — the seat price includes a credit allowance (500 a month on Core, 5,000 on AI Employee, read 5 September 2026), and real outbound volume means credit packages on top, so budget past the sticker. Watch the moving numbers too: the page changed twice this summer — a $75 teaser, then $79 a seat; $795 with a promised rise to $1,000, then $695 — and the $2,500 setup fee now sits on Enterprise and the white-label plans, so decide on the total for the plan you are actually offered, not the sticker. And the honest fundamental for any AI-SDR: it only books meetings as good as your list and offer, so keep a human reviewing what goes out in your name.

Bybit is genuinely best for active traders who want deep liquidity, low derivatives fees and a broad product range (spot, perps, options) with volume-tiered discounts. Skip it if you're a buy-and-hold beginner (a simple euro-native exchange is safer territory), or derivatives aren't available to you locally.

No subscription — per-trade fees, re-verified 2026-09-05 against Bybit's own fee schedule, which the page says was last updated on 2 September 2026. At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker; perpetuals and futures 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker; options 0.0200% maker and 0.0300% taker. The VIP ladder cuts those toward zero — at Supreme VIP spot is 0.0300% maker and 0.0450% taker, derivatives 0.0000% maker and 0.0300% taker, options 0.0050% and 0.0150%. Note that the top derivatives maker rate is zero rather than a rebate: we found no negative maker fee in the published table. That base table is not the only one, and the others start higher: fiat-crypto spot pairs cost 0.2000% taker and 0.1500% maker under $100,000 of 30-day volume, the Spot Adventure Zone and xStocks 0.2000% both ways at VIP 0, and Pre-Market Perpetuals and the Innovation Zone 0.0400% maker and 0.1000% taker — so a new account trading the newest listings pays about double the headline rate. Your VIP level is set by your asset balance, your 30-day average net borrowing or your trading volume over the past 30 days, whichever qualifies you higher, and it refreshes daily at 07:00 UTC. Bybit adds that actual rates can vary by region and points you to your own My Fee Rate page. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Bybit?
answers.a: Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways, and funding rates on perpetuals are a real recurring cost the fee table doesn't show. Regulation-wise, check what Bybit may offer in YOUR jurisdiction before funding an account — availability and product range differ per country, and that's the part most fee comparisons skip.

Calilio is genuinely best for startups and small teams that want a modern, affordable cloud phone system with international numbers and clean dashboards. Skip it if you need a battle-tested enterprise contact center with deep integrations and SLAs, or your call volume makes metered credits unpredictable.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Standard $15 per user/mo, or $12 billed annually ($144 a year); Premium $35 per user/mo, or $28 annually ($336 a year); Enterprise custom. Annual billing saves 20%. Each plan includes a stated value of free calls and SMS/MMS to US and Canada numbers — $6.75 on Standard and $33.74 on Premium — and beyond that calls and SMS draw from a credit balance, with numbers billed separately. Standard suits solopreneurs and small businesses; Premium is aimed at growing businesses, franchises and call centres. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Calilio?
answers.a: The subscription is the platform, not the talking: numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active calling team's real bill sits meaningfully above the per-seat sticker — model a month of your actual call volume before comparing vendors. It's a young player in a crowded VoIP field; the price is keen, so test call quality on your real routes in the trial.

CallHippo is genuinely best for budget-conscious sales/support teams wanting virtual numbers in 50+ countries with a free entry point and CRM integrations. Skip it if your calling is mostly international at volume (metered minutes stack up), or you want one simple plan without add-on shopping.

(re-verified 2026-09-15 in a browser on callhippo.com/pricing, currency selector on USD, phone-number region US/CA, team size 1-4) Starter is $19 per user per month on annual billing and $25 month to month, Professional $30 and $40, Ultimate $42 and $55. Read the tab before the number: the grid opens on yearly, so the lower column is what most write-ups quote, and the toggle beside it advertises "Save 3 Months' Cost" -- paying annually is a third cheaper per user. The $18 that a plain fetch kept printing for Starter was the placeholder sitting in the HTML before the pricing script runs, not a column any visitor is shown. Basic still costs nothing, but fair-usage note 8 lower on that page says it is free only for the first 6 months from signup, after which the account must move to Starter to keep working - so Basic is a long runway, not a permanent free tier. Starter also states a MINIMUM OF 2 USERS and includes 1,000 calling minutes within US/CA plus 100 SMS; unlimited US/CA minutes start one step higher at Professional (500 SMS), which is also where call recording, AI voicemail transcription and multilingual IVR begin. Ultimate adds smart DID, multilevel, holiday and CRM-based VIP routing with 1,000 SMS. Two different Enterprise cards sit on this page and they state different floors: the Core one a minimum of 20 users, the call-centre 'New Enterprise' a minimum of 50, both quote-only with unlimited calling to 48 countries. The call-centre 'Pro Suite' ran $32-48/user/mo annual when it was last read on 15 August 2026. 10-day free trial on the paid tiers. Add-ons are priced apart: AI Voice Agent $45/user/mo with calling billed separately at $0.25/min, AI Copilot $10/user/mo, a dashboard-user seat $15/user/mo, CNAM $100 one-time, SMS Services from $3/mo with a $20 one-time setup fee, Spam Watch $3 per number/mo for US and Canada, $100 per number for spam remediation, $239 for 1,000 UAE minutes and $0.12 per branded call. Overages are in the notes: incoming minutes on standard numbers $0.02/min, incoming SMS $0.01 per message past fair use, outgoing calls to the same number capped at 10 per hour, and parallel calls capped at 30% of total call capacity. The currency selector prices per market instead of converting: the same grid read EUR 19/29/39 in euros on 15 August 2026, below the dollar column rather than above it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CallHippo?
answers.a: 'Unlimited calling' is unlimited to the US and Canada — international minutes meter separately, so teams calling Europe or Asia should price their real destinations first. The plan grid is busy (two suites, add-ons for the dialer and AI), which makes comparisons slippery: list the five features you actually need and find the cheapest tier that truly contains all five.

CallRail is genuinely best for marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution. Skip it if you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight.

Four plans, read on callrail.com/pricing on 5 September 2026, each 'plus usage': Lead Tracking $55 a month, Lead Tracking Complete $105, Lead Conversion $165 and Lead Conversion Complete $215; on yearly billing the same four read $50, $95, $150 and $195 a month (read 6 September 2026; the page states “Save up to 10% with a yearly plan”). Voice Assist (the AI answering agent) is a separate add-on from $95 a month for 50 calls, then $1 a call. Usage past the included allowance is metered: extra local numbers $3 each, local minutes $0.06, toll-free numbers $5. Users are unlimited on every plan. 14-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CallRail?
answers.a: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling — the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.

Campaign Monitor is genuinely best for brands and agencies that want beautiful, reliable email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management, priced per contact. Skip it if you need deep behavioral automation and CRM-grade journeys (ActiveCampaign-class tools fit better), or your list is large but low-engagement — prune first.

answers.q: How much does Campaign Monitor cost?
answers.a: Contact-based, on three tiers - Lite (with a monthly send cap of five times your contact count), Essentials (unlimited sends) and Premier (priority and phone support). We could not re-verify a plan amount on 2026-09-14 either: the page prints the euro sign and the words '/month' with nothing between them until you pick a contact count in its slider. That is now the fourth reading in a row with no plan price in the page itself. The only figure the page publishes is the Website Builder add-on at EUR 9 a month from an EU address - our July and August captures both read the same line as $10. Annual billing takes 10% off and nonprofits are offered a further 15%, which the page states for the first time in our captures. There is no paid-free tier, though the comparison table now labels its trial column 'the Free plan' while the contacts row under it says 500 contacts for the 30-day free trial and the send row says a 500-email limit - so the word 'Free' there is the trial, not a permanent plan. The contact brackets run 0-500, 501-2,500, 2,501-5,000, 5,001-10,000, 10,001-15,000, 15,001-25,000, 25,001-50,000 and 50,001+. Older readings put Lite around EUR 12 and Essentials around EUR 29 at 500 contacts, climbing steeply with list size - treat those as indicative and take your own figure from the slider. Note also that the product is listed as Campaign Monitor by Marigold. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Campaign Monitor?
answers.a: You pay for contacts, not sends — so a large, quiet list costs the same as a large, active one, and dormant subscribers are literally a line item. Clean your list before comparing prices anywhere. Campaign Monitor's strength is polished, agency-friendly email; its automation depth is lighter than dedicated marketing-automation platforms, so know which of the two jobs you're actually buying.

Campaigner is genuinely best for mid-market senders with larger lists that want mature email plus SMS workflows and are comfortable at the Essential tier and up. Skip it if you're small (the useful features start at $179/mo) or you dislike card-required auto-converting trials on principle.

(re-read 2026-09-05 on campaigner.com/pricing) Campaigner prices by contact count and bills per account, not per user: a slider sets the tier and there is no separate monthly/annual toggle. Two self-serve plans: Essentials from $14 a month at 1,000 contacts ($38 at 5,000, $158 at 25,000, $409 at 100,000) and Advanced from $35 a month at 1,000 contacts ($70 at 5,000, $258 at 25,000, $649 at 100,000), plus a quote-only Custom tier. Essentials excludes automation workflows and conversion tracking but includes the REST API, webhooks and SFTP; landing pages, sub-accounts and white-label are Custom only. SMS/MMS is not bundled into any plan: pay-as-you-go from $0.009 per message, sold through sales. Reputation Defender is an add-on at 20% of plan cost. The 30-day trial is full-feature but takes a card and auto-charges when it ends. History: until July 2026 the page carried a Starter/Essential/Advanced ladder at about $59, $179 and $649 a month; the current ladder starts far lower and moves with the contact count. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Campaigner?
answers.a: Two paragraphs of fine print worth reading. Automation workflows and conversion tracking only arrive on Advanced (from $35 a month at 1,000 contacts) — Essentials is a sending tool with an API, not a marketing-automation platform — and the trial auto-converts to paid if you do not actively cancel, which tells you something about the retention strategy. Contact-based pricing also means dormant subscribers bill like active ones; prune first.

Capsule is genuinely best for small businesses that want a clean, genuinely simple CRM for contacts, pipeline and tasks — one the team will actually keep updated. Skip it if you need marketing automation, complex territory logic or enterprise reporting (bigger platforms exist for a reason).

(price page re-read 2026-09-11) The free tier covers two users and 250 contacts, and every paid card is quoted per user a month with a 14-day trial that needs no card. Read over a US connection on 26 August the annual figures were US$18 for Starter, US$36 for Growth and US$54 for Advanced, with contacts as the rungs: 250, 30,000, 60,000 and 120,000. The reading on 11 September was taken from the Netherlands, where those same four cards render in euros at €15, €28 and €49 on annual billing. Capsule prices through a third-party geo lookup, so read that as a regional difference rather than a cut, and take your own figure from the live page. What did change is the shape of the page: it now carries a fifth card, Ultimate, for teams of five or more, and it is the only one printing no amount at all — Capsule asks you to start a trial and have its sales team get in touch. An earlier note here said the page stopped at Advanced; it does not. A Marketing add-on is sold beside the CRM, and the AI features can be switched off in your account. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Capsule?
answers.a: Capsule's simplicity is the product: it deliberately does less than the CRM giants, which is why small teams actually use it. The honest flip side — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out at the top tiers, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it. Buy it to finally have a CRM the team fills in; plan a migration path if you're heading toward enterprise process complexity.
