Carbon6 is genuinely best for Amazon sellers who want reimbursements, advertising, inventory and sourcing tools from one vendor and are content to buy them tool by tool — the suite trades under the Carbon6 brand again since 30 Jun 2026, so there is a named counterparty on the contract. Skip it if you want one flat subscription and one invoice: this is a suite priced per tool, each with its own contract, and the pieces have moved between owners twice since Feb 2025 — check which entity your existing agreement actually names before you add another one.

What we can verify on the vendor’s own pages today (re-checked 26 Aug 2026): carbon6.io/pricing now redirects to the tool list, so there is no suite-level price at all. SoStocked has dropped its two-tier ladder — where on 21 Jul it listed ProfitFlow at $97/mo and ProfitFlow + Inventory at "starting at" $250/mo, it now shows a single Inventory + Profit plan at "starting at" $175/mo with a free trial. ScanUnlimited lists a free Limited tier and Unlimited at $70/mo, or $60/mo on the annual plan ($720/yr, marketed as two months free); the Unlimited Plus tier that sat above it at $1,080/yr is no longer on the pricing page. The off-Amazon advertising tool is listed as PixelMe by Carbon6 again rather than SPS Ad Performance, and it publishes no price. The 3P FBA-reimbursement service is a contingency arrangement: Seller Investigators by Carbon6 states a 25% commission charged only after Amazon has deposited the recovered funds, stated twice on its own site (re-read 26 Aug 2026), after a free 48-hour audit with no obligation. Our older suite-level figures — entry tools from about $49/mo, PixelMe from about $500/mo with a 6-month minimum, and $300-500+/mo for a working stack — stay withdrawn: none of those is verifiable against a live authoritative source today. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Carbon6?
answers.a: The honest headline here is not pricing but ownership — and it has moved again, this time in the reader's favour. SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 for roughly $210M on 7 Feb 2025 and retired the brand into spscommerce.com. On 30 Jun 2026 it sold the entire 3P (Amazon marketplace seller) revenue-recovery business for $9.5M cash, booking an estimated $20M loss, and named no buyer at the time. There is a name now. The partner-programme notice we received on 17 Aug 2026, from Carbon6's own partnerships contact, states that SPS transferred ownership of the 3P business to Carbon6 and that commission terms and payouts are unchanged. It also states that existing links were redirected to the Carbon6 tool sites on 14 Aug 2026, and that the programme itself rebrands from SPS to Carbon6 on 24 Aug 2026. Reading carbon6.io on 17 Aug 2026 matches that: the whole suite is on sale there again as "by Carbon6". Read the two purchase numbers carefully, because they are not the same thing. The $210M bought the whole Carbon6 stack; the $9.5M was the 3P arm alone, and offloading it at a book loss seventeen months in still tells you how it performed. What remains undisclosed is who stands behind the Carbon6 entity itself, so the question is answered one level down and no further. Two more things to hold. Reuters reported on 23 Jun 2026 that SPS hired Morgan Stanley to explore a sale of itself under activist pressure, with talks early and no deal assured. And the 1P side is no longer a clean split, because SPS kept the deduction-recovery business it bought while Carbon6's own site now lists ChargeGuard for Amazon 1P vendor recovery. Ask which entity your 1P work would sit with before you sign. For 3P reimbursements the July advice has expired — you can name the counterparty on your contract again.

Castmagic is genuinely best for content teams, agencies and serious podcasters with a steady flow of recorded audio or video who want a transcript plus a stack of derived assets — show notes, newsletters, social posts, clips — from every upload, and who record enough hours to fill a tier. Skip it if you record occasionally, you only need an accurate transcript and nothing downstream of it, or you need a month-to-month price you can read off the page before you sign up.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on castmagic.io/pricing) Three published tiers plus an enterprise band. The page opens on “Annually — Save 30% Annually”, and it now labels each card in words: “per month, billed annually”. Hobby $19 a month billed annually, $239 a year: 30 transcribed hours, up to 3 Spaces, 50GB storage, max team size 3 seats, no API access, no onboarding call, standard support. Starter $48 a month billed annually, $579 a year: 100 hours, 10 Spaces, 250GB, 5 seats, API access, onboarding call, standard support. Team $139 a month billed annually, $1,669 a year: 400 hours, 25 Spaces, 1TB, unlimited team size with 5 seats included and extras at $159 a year or $19 a month each, priority support. Business & Scale from $699 a month on annual billing and $999 a month on monthly billing, by demo, for custom volume, seats, storage, SLA and dedicated support. The monthly-billing prices ARE readable now, which they were not on 19 August 2026: the page carries both figures as data attributes on each amount and swaps them with script, giving Hobby $29, Starter $69 and Team $199 a month when billed monthly. Against the annual rates that is a 34% saving on Hobby and about 30% on Starter, Team and Business & Scale, so the “Save 30%” chip understates the entry tier. Unlimited AI outputs, re-generations, media clipping, audiograms, AI image generation, custom prompts, community prompts and 2000+ word outputs are on all three published tiers, as are 60+ transcription languages, unlimited file uploads, a 10GB maximum file size, 50 maximum concurrent uploads, the Media Library, and the Zoom, Google Drive, Zapier, RSS and YouTube/TikTok/Instagram imports. The hours still need care. The table calls them “transcribed hours (library total)” and the FAQ says every plan includes “a growing library of transcribed hours — 30 on Hobby, 100 on Starter, and 400 on Team — that you build up over time”, which still never states whether the allowance renews each month or is a running ceiling. Extra hours can be bought at any time on every tier, and the FAQ says you can upgrade or downgrade whenever you like. New on the site since 19 August 2026: Audience Chat (a chatbot for your own site trained on your episodes, citing the moment and capturing the lead), an API plus a Claude MCP server, an AI content strategist, async interviews, carousels and vertical clips, and a claim of “130+ tools”. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Castmagic?
answers.a:
The prices on the page are the annual prices. The toggle sits on “Annually — Save 30% Annually” by default, so $19, $48 and $139 are what you pay when you commit for a year. The month-to-month figures are readable in the page source and they are $29, $69 and $199, so the gap is real and on the entry tier it is wider than advertised: Hobby is about 34% cheaper annually, not 30%.

The hours are the part to pin down before you subscribe. The comparison table labels them “transcribed hours (library total)”, and the FAQ describes “a growing library of transcribed hours ... that you build up over time”. That wording fits a monthly allowance and a lifetime ceiling equally well, and the difference between the two is enormous. 30 hours every month at $19 is a bargain for a weekly podcast. 30 hours in total is about seven episodes, and then you are buying top-ups. Ask before you pay, and ask what happens to the hours when you downgrade.

And the social proof does not agree with itself — now in three directions. The pricing page says “75k+ Creators Served” and “75,000+ Creators & Businesses”; the homepage hero says “Loved by 100K+ podcasters and creators”; and the site's own llms.txt claims “200,000+ creators — including 100,000+ podcasters and 75,000+ creators and teams”. Three numbers, one site, and they cannot all be current. It is a small thing, and the kind of small thing that tells you which numbers on a marketing site have been checked recently. Treat the totals, the 10M minutes and the named logos as marketing, and judge the product on the trial.

answers.q: Is ChatGPT AI Product Description worth it?
answers.a: ChatGPT AI Product Description is genuinely best for Shopify stores with catalogues in the thousands that need descriptions, titles, meta tags and alt text written in bulk and in several languages, and have the discipline to check a sample before running the whole catalogue. Skip it if you have a small catalogue where 100 free credits a month already covers the new arrivals, or your product copy is a differentiator you would rather write by hand.

answers.q: How much does ChatGPT AI Product Description cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/automated-description-writing) Four tiers, priced in credits per month. Free Trial: 100 credits a month. Basic $19 a month or $190 a year (save 17%): 2,000 credits, product descriptions, titles and meta descriptions, formatted descriptions, automatic descriptions on import. Standard $49 a month or $399 a year (save 32%): 11,000 credits, same feature list. Pro $249 a month or $1,990 a year (save 33%): 110,000 credits, same list plus priority video-call support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Every paid tier carries the same strapline — 'Only $1 per 100 Descriptions' — and it only holds at the bottom of the ladder: $19 for 2,000 credits is 95 cents per hundred, $49 for 11,000 is 45 cents, $249 for 110,000 is 23 cents. So the $1 is a ceiling on the cheapest plan rather than a rate, and it assumes one credit equals one description, which the listing never states. That is the central gap in this pricing: nowhere does the page say what a title, a meta description or an alt text costs in credits, or what the 'Pro Features' that use product images, metadata and web search cost extra. Developer Profitonium, Adugodi, Bangalore; the app launched 12 March 2021, holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge and carries a 4.9 average over 466 App Store reviews. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ChatGPT AI Product Description?
answers.a:
First, the name is not a name. 'ChatGPT AI Product Description' describes a category, and on its own listing page Shopify shows 'ChatGPT‑AI Product Description' — a different app by a different developer, also 4.9, also 331 reviews, also with the Built for Shopify badge. Two more competitors on the same page use nearly the same words. Check the developer is Profitonium before you install, because the App Store search results for this phrase are a thicket.

Second, the credit is undefined and it is the only thing you are buying. Four tiers, one variable, no definition — and the '$1 per 100 descriptions' line repeated on all three paid plans is not the rate on two of them.

Third, and the one that costs real money if it goes wrong: this app edits your live store. Its permissions cover product descriptions and titles, Online Store pages and theme, files, locales, Shopify Markets settings, translations and navigation. Bulk generation across thousands of SKUs is exactly the operation you cannot eyeball, and nothing on the listing describes versioning, a preview queue or a rollback. The 466 reviews are genuinely strong: 96% five stars, one two-star, no one-stars, and the substantial ones come from merchants with 30,000 SKUs and over a year of use. But every one of them describes a merchant who was happy with the output, not one who needed to undo it. Export your product CSV before the first bulk run. That is your rollback.

Checkr is genuinely best for companies hiring hourly or gig workers at volume that need fast, API-driven, compliant background checks. Skip it if you hire only a handful of people a year — a one-off check from a simpler provider costs less hassle than onboarding a screening platform.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Pay-as-you-go per report, no subscription: Basic $29.99, Essential $59.99 and Complete $94.99 per report, with Enterprise quote-only. Tenant screening is priced separately at $24.99, $34.99 and $44.99 per report, and personal checks start from $49.99. Add-ons stack on top: MVR report $9.50 per check, identity verification $4.99 per check, employment verification $59.95 and income plus employment $64.95, billed per verification with no commitment or contract. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Checkr?
answers.a: The headline per-check price is rarely what you actually pay — passthrough fees vary wildly by county and search type, so budget for the effective cost, not the advertised one. It's overkill unless you hire at real volume.

ChemiCloud is genuinely best for small businesses, freelancers and growing sites that want fast, well-supported managed shared or WordPress hosting at a low starting price. Skip it if you need enterprise-grade dedicated infrastructure and SLAs, or you'll be unhappy when the low intro rate renews at standard pricing.

(re-verified 2026-09-02) Shared hosting starts at $1.95/mo on the September campaign: ChemiCloud's Back to Build sale runs from 2 September 4:00 AM EST to 30 September 11:59 PM EST and prices Starter, Pro and Turbo at $1.95, $2.95 and $3.49 a month on the 36-month term, or $3.49, $4.49 and $4.95 on 12 months. We read it on changeover day, with the outgoing 10th-birthday sale still on the hosting page behind a countdown of under twelve hours at $1.49, $2.49 and $3.49, so the entry price rises by 46 cents as that clock runs out. What did not move in either sale is the renewal, and that is the number that matters: $11.95, $17.95 and $21.95 a month for Starter, Pro and Turbo. Across the rest of the range, reseller starts at $17.95/mo (Kickstart, regular $34.95), managed cloud VPS at $32.95/mo (Cloud 1, regular $59.95, on a 7-day money-back guarantee rather than 45 days), and managed WordPress at $25/mo with a $1 first month, or $12.50/mo billed yearly. Shared plans include a free first-year domain on the 36-month term, free SSL, daily backups and free migration. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ChemiCloud?
answers.a: The honest catch is the one every budget host shares: the headline price is an introductory rate, and renewals land roughly three times higher, so judge it on the renewal cost, not the sign-up teaser. Support and performance reviews are genuinely strong for the price band, but this is shared/managed hosting — if you need serious dedicated resources or enterprise SLAs, you'll outgrow the cheap tiers. Great value to start, just enter with eyes open on renewal.

Circle is genuinely best for creators and brands running a paid community — courses, memberships, events and discussions in one branded home, with a built-in payments stack and even branded mobile apps. Skip it if you only need a casual chat space (Discord-style) or your margins are thin on high sales volume — the platform commission plus processing fees stack against you.

Professional about $89/mo billed annually ($129 monthly), Business $199/mo annual, Enterprise around $419/mo annual, plus a custom Circle Plus tier for fully branded apps. On top of the subscription Circle takes a commission on every sale you make through the platform (roughly 2% on Professional, 1% on Business, 0.5% on Plus) plus standard Stripe/PayPal processing, and the Email Hub is a paid add-on around $99/mo for 10,000 contacts. 14-day free trial, but no always-free option. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Circle?
answers.a: The sticker is only the entry: Circle keeps a commission on every sale on top of Stripe's processing fees, and email marketing is a separate add-on — so a monetized community's real bill runs meaningfully past the plan price. Model it at your actual sales volume before choosing a tier.

Claap is genuinely best for revenue teams that want every call captured — by default with no notetaker bot in the meeting, though a customisable bot is there for teams that prefer one — and want those calls to end up as CRM fields, coaching and deal signals rather than as transcripts nobody reopens, with enough seats to make a sales conversation worth having. Skip it if you want to buy and test the product yourself, because the tier with the CRM and coaching features is quote-led and even its trial runs through sales; you need a long retention window, since recordings age out after 2 or 3 years below Enterprise; or you need to be billed in dollars.

(read 2026-09-04 on claap.io/pricing, both billing toggles and the full comparison table; re-verified 2026-09-08) Licenses are priced per license per month in euros. The only dollar figure on the page belongs to an add-on rather than a plan: a tooltip offers the Power Recorder, which adds unlimited recording length to any paid seat for $20 per seat a month. Basic is €0: 10 videos per user, 300 minutes of recording in total rather than per month, calendar and conference-call sync, 99-language transcript, basic AI summary, the Chrome recorder extension, a collaborative workspace and — listed on every tier including this free one — an unlimited-usage API and the Claap MCP connector, capped at 5 licenses, no guests, one team, one channel, 3 video uploads and 3 months of recording storage. Pro is €24 per license a month billed yearly or €30 monthly: unlimited recordings, 1,000 minutes a month, 500 AI credits per license pooled across the workspace, advanced AI summaries, meeting insights, AI video editing, 10+ integrations, speaker and video insights and private channels, with 50 licenses, 50 guests, 10 uploads a month and 2 years of storage. What those credits buy is spelled out in a tooltip rather than in the plan card: one credit is one Claap AI chat, AI email follow-up, coaching tab or generated insight, and summaries, chapters and the AI companion do not consume credits at all. Business is €48 per license a month yearly or €60 monthly: unlimited recording time, 1,000 AI credits per license, Claap AI across all meetings, CRM auto-complete, AI-generated emails, AI coaching, deal insights, smart tables, admin recording controls and priority support, with 50 uploads a month and 3 years of storage. Enterprise is a custom price and adds SSO through Okta, SCIM provisioning, unlimited Basic licenses, white-glove onboarding and migration support. Basic carries a Try for free button and Pro a Start now button; Business and Enterprise both say Contact us, and the pricing FAQ states that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Claap?
answers.a:
The four tiers sell two different products, and only one of them is self-serve. Pro at €24 is the recorder and note-taker. Everything Claap actually markets itself on — CRM auto-complete, AI coaching, deal insights, asking Claap AI a question across all your meetings — starts at Business, €48 per license a month on annual billing, and Business is the only paid tier with no Start now button: it says Contact us. The pricing FAQ closes the other door too, stating that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team. So the features you came for cannot be bought or tested without a sales conversation.

Your recordings also expire. Storage runs 3 months on Basic, 2 years on Pro and 3 years on Business; only Enterprise is unlimited. If the call archive is meant to be your evidence trail, that is a deletion date on your own data, and it is in the comparison table rather than in the plan cards.

Two smaller things worth reading twice, and one correction we owe you. The AI credits — 500 per license on Pro, 1,000 on Business, pooled across the workspace — do not meter the summaries: the tooltip is explicit that summaries, chapters and the AI companion use no credits, and a credit is spent on a Claap AI chat, an AI email follow-up, the coaching tab or a generated insight. What is missing is the rate: no price for an extra credit appears anywhere on the page, so a heavy month of coaching and insights cannot be costed before you commit, and the same tooltip layer is where you find the one dollar-priced item, a $20 per seat Power Recorder add-on on a euro-priced plan. And the free tier's 300 minutes is a total, not a monthly allowance: it is a sample, not a plan you can sit on.

Claude is genuinely best for developers, writers, analysts and researchers who want best-in-class reasoning, coding and long-document work — and a model that's careful and direct rather than eager to please. Skip it if you mainly need image generation or the widest third-party plugin ecosystem (a general assistant like ChatGPT fits better there), or you're a light user the free tier already covers.

(price re-verified 2026-08-27 on their own pricing page) The free tier is $0. Pro is $17/month with the annual discount ($200 billed up front) or $20 billed monthly, and includes Claude Code and unlimited projects. Max starts at $100/month for 5x or 20x the usage of Pro per five-hour session. Team is for teams of 2 to 150: a standard seat is $20/seat/month billed annually ($25 monthly), and a premium seat is $100/seat/month billed annually ($125 monthly) for 5x the usage of a standard seat, adding Claude Code and Claude Cowork. Enterprise self-serve is $20/seat plus usage billed at API rates, so cost scales with the models and tasks the team runs; larger contracts are custom via sales. The API is separate and billed per token across the Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models, with platform features priced on top: Managed Agents at $0.08 per session-hour of active runtime, web search at $10 per 1,000 searches, and code execution beyond the 50 free hours a day at $0.05 per hour per container. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Claude?
answers.a: The honest catch is usage limits: even on Pro you can hit a ceiling mid-session on a heavy day, and the step up to Max is a real $100 to $200 a month — you're buying headroom, not extra features. It also doesn't generate images, so if that's your main need it's the wrong tool, and its third-party plugin ecosystem is smaller than ChatGPT's.

Clay is genuinely best for modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it. Skip it if you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page; both billing terms read from the page markup, and no figure has moved since our August reading) Clay meters two things separately — actions and data credits — and each paid plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier, which is the part most write-ups still get wrong, ours included until the August 2026 update. The free plan is real: 6,000 actions and 1,200 data credits a year, unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls and Claygent, capped at 200 rows per table and with no phone enrichment. Launch is advertised at $167/mo but starts at $54/mo on annual billing or $60 monthly, and Growth at $446/mo but starts at $185/mo annually or $205 monthly — the headline is a configured volume, not the floor, so read the ladder rather than the card. Billed monthly the Launch action ladder runs $60, $150, $200, $290 and $540 for 15K, 40K, 60K, 100K and 200K actions a month; billed annually it runs $54, $135, $180, $261 and $486 a month for 180K, 480K, 720K, 1.2M and 2.4M actions a year. Growth starts one rung higher: $205, $290, $450 and $850 a month for 40K to 200K monthly actions, or $185 to $765 a month on the annual ladder. Data credits are a separate meter again — monthly from $125 for 2,500 credits up to $2,125 for 50,000, or annually from $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill. One discrepancy is worth carrying to checkout, and it survived this reading: the plan FAQ at the bottom of the page describes Launch as “starting at $185/mo”, which is not the Launch floor of $54 but the Growth one. Enterprise is quote-only. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Clay?
answers.a: Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.

ClickUp is genuinely best for teams that want one highly customizable app for tasks, docs, goals and reporting and will invest in setting it up. Skip it if you want something simple your team adopts in a day — ClickUp's depth becomes overwhelm for a light use case.

(re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page with both billing tabs open) A Free Forever plan with unlimited tasks but 60MB of storage; Unlimited $7 and Business $12 per user/month billed yearly, which are $10 and $19 billed monthly; Enterprise is quote-only. AI is priced on top of the plan: Brain AI $9 and Everything AI $28 per user/month. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ClickUp?
answers.a: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Powerful and cheap per seat, but only if you'll actually configure and adopt it.

Clonable is genuinely best for businesses that want a fast, continuously-updated translated version of an existing website without rebuilding it as a multilingual site. Skip it if you need human-quality translation for legal, medical or brand-critical copy, or you only need a one-off translation rather than an ongoing synced clone.

(prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on clonable.net/pricing; the page blocks plain fetches and was read in a browser) Two ladders behind a Website / Online Store tab, each with a Per month / Annually switch that opens on Annually. Website plans, annual setting: Free €0 for 1 clone and up to 20 translated pages (an upgrade to 50 pages is €25 a month), Business €49 for 3 clones and 400 pages, Pro €79 for 5 clones and 1,200 pages, Expert €249 for 10 clones and 5,000 pages, Premium €999 for 20 clones and 50,000 pages. Click Per month and the same five read €0, €59, €95, €299 and €1,199. Online Store plans, annual setting: Ecommerce Small €99 for 1 clone and 1,000 translated pages, Medium €299 for 5,000 pages, Large €499 for 15,000 pages, each with an XML product feed billed separately at €30, €50 and €75 a month per feed, and a non-translation clone from €49, €149 or €249. An additional clone with its pages is €25 a month on Business and Pro and €50 on Expert and Premium. Optional setup assistance is €250 on the website plans (€1,000 on Premium) and €250 on Ecommerce Small against €950 on Medium and Large. One caution about the comparison table below the cards, checked the same day: its 'Max. aantal clones' row reads 1, 3, 5, 5, 20 across Free, Business, Pro, Expert and Premium, giving Expert five clones where the Expert card promises ten. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Clonable?
answers.a: Two honest caveats. First, it's a continuous subscription, not a one-time translation — you pay ongoing to keep the translated clone synced with your site. Second, it's machine translation under the hood, so quality varies by language pair; always have a native speaker spot-check high-stakes pages. Worth knowing before you compare tiers: the pricing page opens on its annual setting, so the figure you see first is not what a monthly subscription costs.

Cloro is genuinely best for SEO and marketing teams who need AI-search visibility as structured data — who gets cited for which query on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Google's AI Overview — rather than as a dashboard someone else designed. Skip it if you want a finished rank-tracking dashboard rather than an API; this returns JSON with markdown, sources and citations, and you build the reporting yourself.

(prices re-read 2026-09-17 on cloro.dev/pricing) Credit-metered, and the credit table matters more than the plan price. Free is $0 for 500 credits a month, one concurrent job and one seat. Paid runs Lite $30 (37,500 credits, $0.80 per 1k, 10 concurrent jobs), Hobby $100 (250,000, $0.40, 20 jobs) and Starter $250 (650,000, $0.39, 50 jobs). Above that come Growth $500 (1,350,000, $0.37, 75 jobs) and Business $1,000 (2,800,000, $0.36, 100 jobs). Four self-serve Enterprise steps follow: $2,000 for 5,871,025 credits at $0.34, $3,000 for 9,306,606 at $0.32, $4,000 for 12,756,261 at $0.31 and $5,000 for 16,391,783 at $0.31, where concurrency reaches 255. Seats are unlimited from Lite up. What a request costs varies by engine. ChatGPT full response is 7 credits, ChatGPT web search 5, Copilot 5, and AI Overview including the SERP 5. Perplexity, Grok, AI Mode and Gemini are 4, and Google Search and Google News 3 plus 2 per extra page. A synchronous call adds 2 credits on top of all of those. Perplexity stood at 3 credits when we read the same table on 17 August 2026. Grok is marked temporarily unavailable, with the page warning that requests to it fail. Credits do not roll over: unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle, and at zero the API returns 403 until you upgrade or the cycle resets. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Cloro?
answers.a: The free tier is a sampler, not a trial of the real thing: 500 credits is about 100 async ChatGPT answers at the 5-credit rate we were actually charged, and their table lists 7 for a full response. Fewer, if you call it synchronously -- and one concurrent job means you queue. Anyone running a daily visibility check across a hundred keywords burns through it in about two days. Read the credit table before the price table -- the same $100 buys 250,000 credits, which is 35,700 full ChatGPT calls or 62,500 Perplexity ones, so your engine mix decides your bill more than your plan does. And nothing carries: their FAQ, read 17 September 2026, states that unused credits expire at the end of every cycle, so a quiet month is money gone rather than headroom for a busy one.

Close is genuinely best for inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place. Skip it if your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you.

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own pricing page) Per-seat: Solo $19, Essentials $49, Growth $109 and Scale $149 per user/mo, or $9, $35, $99 and $139 billed annually — the same twelve amounts we have now read on 23 July, 3, 11 and 14 August and 12 September 2026. No free plan; the trial runs 14 days and close.com states no credit card is required, with $5 of calling and enrichment credits included, and the page carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. AI credits are pooled per tier (500 a month on Solo, then 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 per user up to 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000). Chloe, the AI sales agent Close now leads the page with, is free to access on every plan but spends those AI credits plus telephony as she works, so she is metered rather than included. Call minutes, SMS and dialer credits are billed separately and can meaningfully raise the real cost: outbound calls run about $0.02 a minute and phone lines start at about $1 a month. The Call Assistant add-on is $50 a month per organisation plus $0.02 a minute, and additional organisations are $50 a month each, with Growth and Scale including one free secondary org. Premium Phone Numbers are listed as a feature with no price attached. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Close?
answers.a: The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.

CloudTalk is genuinely best for support and sales teams that want a cloud call center with strong CRM integrations and call analytics. Skip it if you make only occasional calls — a basic VoIP line or your CRM's built-in dialer costs far less.

Lite €19, Starter €25, Essential €29 and Expert €49 per user/mo on annual billing, and Expert needs at least 3 licences (re-verified 2026-08-16). The add-ons are where the bill grows: Power Dialer €15 per user/mo (already included in Expert), Parallel Dialer €39 per user/mo, AI Conversation Intelligence €9 per user/mo. AI voice agents are separate subscriptions: AI Receptionist from €99/mo with 200 minutes, AI Specialist €349/mo with 1,000 minutes, and above 10,000 minutes a month custom pricing CloudTalk advertises as low as €0.15 per minute. There is a 14-day trial that includes 50 AI voice agent minutes. Note the page quotes us in euros from an EU address while the same page carries a $99 figure for the same AI bundle. CloudTalk told us on 31 August 2026 that this is deliberate rather than a display error: they hold the same number in both currencies instead of converting at the exchange rate, so €99 and $99 buy the same bundle. Confirm the currency at your own checkout. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CloudTalk?
answers.a: The per-seat price is only part of it — number rental, outbound minutes and the AI add-ons stack on top, so a call-heavy team's real bill runs above the plan rate. Solid CRM integrations, but model your call volume first.

CloudTask is genuinely best for companies hiring GTM roles — SDRs, BDRs and similar — who want LATAM talent without setting up their own payroll and compliance in another country, and who value the 24-month replacement guarantee. Skip it if you only need one hire ever, where Direct Hire's one-time 20-30% fee is cleaner than a managed monthly rate; also skip it if you cannot get the all-in monthly rate in writing before you commit.

(re-verified 2026-08-19, read on their own pricing page) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No. There is a one-time $299 deposit to start your search. That is the only fee outside the models above.” — and the deposit applies toward your buyout or your first placement. Direct Hire costs 20% to 30% of first-year base salary, paid once and quoted per role, with a 6-month replacement guarantee (one replacement, same job description) and US W2 employment available. Managed Staffing is billed as one all-in monthly rate per person covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that decides what this costs. It carries a 24-month replacement guarantee with replacements not capped, and time and activity tracking on by default, which the hire agrees to before matching and you can switch off when you post the role. Graduating a managed hire onto your own payroll is possible after six months for a one-time placement fee quoted at that moment; no amount is published. Health and equipment benefits are available on request on Managed Staffing only. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CloudTask?
answers.a: The $299 is the honest part and also the small part: their FAQ calls it a one-time deposit to start a search, denies any monthly platform fee, and says it goes toward your first placement. What you will actually spend is the all-in monthly rate per hire, and that figure appears nowhere on the pricing page — you get it after you talk to them, once you are already invested in the process. Work out before you start what a comparable LATAM salary is on your own, so you can see what the managed layer costs on top. The exit is worth reading twice too. After six months you can graduate a managed hire onto your own payroll, but the placement fee for doing so is quoted at the time and no amount is published. So the price of keeping the person is a number you cannot check in advance.

Cloudways is genuinely best for agencies and PHP shops running many sites who want servers managed but not metered. One server holds as many sites as it can carry with no visit caps, billing is hourly and post-paid with no annual term, and Magento and Laravel are first-class alongside WordPress. It suits teams who genuinely do not want anyone patching kernels at 2am. Skip it if you are comfortable in a terminal, or you run a single small site. Going direct to the cloud provider with your own control panel keeps the server in your own account for materially less. And one low-traffic site is better served by shared hosting, or by a per-site managed host that bundles CDN and application support. Cloudways also has no email hosting of its own, reselling a Rackspace add-on instead.

(read 2026-08-26 on cloudways.com/en/pricing.php, DigitalOcean tab) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required. Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract — and the hourly figure is the one that decides the bill: every card divides its monthly price by 672 hours, so $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan. The page now opens on DigitalOcean's Premium (NVMe) column, where Micro is 1GB RAM / 1 vCPU / 25GB NVMe / 1TB bandwidth at $14/month, Small 2GB / 1 vCPU / 50GB NVMe / 2TB at $28, Medium 4GB / 2 vCPU / 80GB / 4TB at $54 and Large 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB at $99. Two of those have moved since July: the entry machine is now half the size for three dollars more (July's Micro was 2GB / 50GB at $11), and the 8GB plan went from $88 to $99. Switch the column to Standard and that same 2GB / 50GB box reads $11 a month — but the hourly figure printed underneath it, $0.0357, works out to $24 at the 672-hour month the other cards use, so the two numbers on that one card cannot both be right; read the live estimate before you commit. Bought direct from DigitalOcean on the same day, an 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB droplet lists at $0.07143 an hour, $48 a month. Add-ons are monthly and separate: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN from $4.99 per domain, Site Manager from $3 per app, Malware Protection from $4 per app, Rackspace email $1 per mailbox, DNS Made Easy $0.50 per domain, offsite backup storage $0.033 per GB. Advance Support is $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, with a limited-time flat rate of $25/month advertised on the page today; the $500 Premium Support tier we recorded in July is no longer listed there. Cloudways Autonomous, the separate autoscaling product, now prices at $35, $240 and $995 a month where July's page showed $99, $199 and $399, and it meters unique visits and bandwidth rather than RAM (30k visits and 100GB on Small, 70k and 200GB on Medium) with a 3-day free trial. Markups on AWS and Google Cloud still cannot be calculated because Cloudways does not publish the underlying instance types. A site-wide banner advertises 40% off for four months until 15 September 2026 — promotions move, so read the live price. US list prices, excluding tax. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Cloudways?
answers.a: "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is. Cloudways' own support page puts infrastructure and platform work in the included tier but treats application help as guidance only. Plugin and theme troubleshooting, database work and performance tuning sit behind Advanced Support at $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum. On a small server that add-on costs more than the server it supports. Content changes, custom code debugging and code audits stay out of scope on every tier, paid ones included. The deeper catch is ownership: Cloudways documents that you get no root access and cannot use your own cloud credentials, so the machine sits in Cloudways' account — you cannot fire the management layer and keep the server, you migrate. And read the billing terms before you rely on it: their help centre states that an unpaid invoice restricts server access and can lead to the server and its backups being deleted, with backups kept for only 14 days after deletion.

Cloze is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a catalogue big enough that shoppers ask which item to buy, who want a chat assistant that reads live inventory and hands off to a person, and who will watch the transcripts. Skip it if your support volume is low, or you want proof from other merchants before you put an AI in front of customers — there are no reviews yet.

(read 2026-08-19, re-verified unchanged 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/cloze, listed as “Cloze: AI Shopping Assistant”) Free plan available: 25 AI conversations a month, up to 100 synced products, core assistant customisation and 7 days of conversation history. Paid tiers are Starter $49, Pro $99 and Scale $199 a month, each with $0.10 per additional AI conversation and a 3-day free trial. Starter covers 250 conversations a month and 1,000 synced products, with full customisation and 30 days of insights. Pro covers 750 conversations and 10,000 products with advanced insights and 90 days of history, and Scale 2,000 conversations, unlimited products, a year of history and priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing before you install. The vendor's own site, cloze.bot/pricing, advertised a different and cheaper ladder on the same day: Free forever with 50 conversations a month, Pro $29 a month and Business $79 a month. On that page both paid tiers say unlimited conversations rather than a monthly allowance. Our link goes to the App Store listing, so the $49/$99/$199 ladder, with its caps of 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations, is what you pay when you install there. The screenshot further down is their own page exactly as we captured it. Developer Optify, Lyon, France; the app launched 24 April 2026, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and had no reviews at all at the time of writing. Re-read on 4 September 2026: both ladders still stood exactly as described above, and the listing had gained its first review — a single five-star note left on 14 August 2026 by a French store eight days in. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Cloze?
answers.a: Two things to weigh, and the first is the price itself. On the same day, the App Store listing sold this at $49, $99 and $199 a month for 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations. The vendor's own site sold it at $29 and $79, with unlimited conversations on both paid tiers. The screenshot below is that page. Two prices and two different meters for one product is not a discount you can claim, it is an inconsistency to ask about before you pay. The second is the track record, or the absence of one. The app launched 24 April 2026 and, as of 4 September 2026, carries exactly one review — five stars, left after eight days of use. So there is next to no merchant experience to lean on, and the “Built for Shopify” badge is a technical bar, not a verdict on the answers. Also note what a conversation costs when it goes wrong. An assistant wired to live inventory and order tracking is answering with your data, and the free tier's 25 conversations a month is enough to test the tone but not enough to see it handle a bad day. The 3-day trial on paid plans is short for a support tool.

Clutch is genuinely best for businesses that want to skip manual agency research and get matched quickly with vetted, best-fit service providers for a specific project. Skip it if you already have trusted agency relationships, or you'd rather research independently without agencies contacting you.

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read in their own help centre) Free for buyers. Clutch's help centre describes the Project Brief as the buyer's route in, and the article on sending one states that Clutch recommends up to 9 service providers that best match your project requirements, with no fee named anywhere in that flow. Clutch is a B2B services marketplace — the providers being listed pay for visibility, the buyer does not, and the help centre says plainly that directory listings are sorted by sponsored providers and Clutch rank. A free provider profile covers the listing, client review collection, badges and widgets, contributed content, awards eligibility, up to 3 sharable case studies and a profile on sister-site The Manifest; Sponsorship, Featured Listings and Clutch Verified (previously Clutch+) are the paid upgrades on top. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Clutch?
answers.a: It's genuinely free to submit a brief — but be clear on what it is: a lead-generation marketplace, not a neutral directory. Your brief goes straight to agencies who will reach out to pitch you, and providers pay to be visible and matched. It's a fast way to shortlist vetted agencies; just expect the outreach that comes with it.

answers.q: Is Code Bulk Discounts worth it?
answers.a: Code Bulk Discounts is genuinely best for shopify stores that already run email or SMS campaigns and need thousands of unique, single-use codes generated out of one existing discount and handed over as a CSV. Skip it if you need one or two codes, which Shopify's own discount screen already gives you at no cost — or the campaign itself is what you want, because this app generates and exports the codes and stops there.

answers.q: How much does Code Bulk Discounts cost?
answers.a: (prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/code-bulk and re-verified there on 2026-09-16, unchanged) Two plans, billed in USD every 30 days. Free costs nothing and covers 500 lifetime codes with CSV export. Pro is $14.99 a month and lifts that to unlimited codes per month, with the same CSV export; both plans say they work with most discount applications. The plan table lists no annual rate, no free trial on Pro and no per-code charge, so the monthly figure is the whole cost. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Code Bulk Discounts?
answers.a: Read the free plan's number twice, because the word doing the work is 'lifetime': it is 500 codes in total, not 500 a month. One influencer drop or one email segment can spend the whole allowance in an afternoon, and after that the only way on is $14.99 a month — so the free tier is a sample, not a plan. What the app does is also narrower than the word 'discounts' suggests. It takes a discount you have already created and multiplies it into unique codes you export as a CSV. It does not create the discount rule, does not send the codes to anyone, and does not report which ones were redeemed, so it sits between your discount settings and your email or SMS tool and needs both of those to be worth anything. The one critical review on the listing shows what that costs in practice: when a merchant's parent discount broke after an unrelated change to their stack, every code generated from it went inactive and they learned about it from customers rather than from the app. The developer's answer is the right one to remember — the rules and logic belong to the parent discount, not to Code Bulk — but it means nothing in this app will tell you that a batch has stopped working. The 5.0 rating also rests on 41 reviews, read 16 September 2026, which is a thin record next to the app's peers.

Cognism is genuinely best for outbound sales teams in Europe who need mobile numbers that are actually verified and care about GDPR provenance — that is the specific thing this is better at. Skip it if you are one or two people prospecting, because both named plans include five seats; also skip it if your market is US-only, where the data advantage is smaller and cheaper options exist.

(2026-09-17, re-read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Two named plans, Standard and Pro, both stated to include 5 seats, with everything routed to 'Talk to sales' and 'Get a personalised quote'. The model is credit-based — their own wording is that 1 credit equals 1 revealed contact — with credits included in the subscription per seat, but no allowance is published. Their FAQ adds that a redeemed contact stays usable for the length of the contract and only costs a second credit if that person changes jobs, and that additional credits can be purchased at any point. CRM Enrichment is sold standalone or as an add-on; Data-as-a-Service is priced by volume, delivery method and the fields required, and its API route requires a prospecting seat. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Cognism?
answers.a: No price, no credit allowance, and a five-seat minimum on both named plans. That combination means the smallest deal is five seats of something you cannot price, so budget conversations start with a sales call rather than a number. The credit model is the part to nail down: one credit reveals one contact, so your real cost per usable lead is the credit price divided by your connect rate, and neither figure is published. Before the call, work out how many contacts a month you actually reveal — that is the only number that lets you judge the quote you get. And it is worth asking whether unused credits roll over, because nothing on the page says.

CometChat is genuinely best for product teams that want proven in-app text/voice/video chat with SDKs for every major framework, without building messaging infrastructure themselves. Skip it if your app is pre-revenue with growing users (the free-to-paid cliff will hit mid-growth), or chat is peripheral enough that a support widget covers it.

(re-verified 2026-08-17 against CometChat's own machine-readable pricing reference, which they publish for AI agents and last verified themselves on 2026-05-20; USD) Build is free for development: all features, up to 100 users and 25 concurrent connections, no card. Paid Chat plans are priced by monthly active users. Billed yearly, shown as a monthly equivalent: at 1,000 MAU Basic is $239 and Advanced $359; at 10,000 MAU Basic $299, Advanced $399 and Enterprise $999; at 25,000 MAU $699 and $949; at 50,000 MAU $1,349 and $1,649. Paying monthly costs about 20% more — $298.75 and $448.75 at 1,000 MAU. Above 50,000 MAU everything is quote-only. Concurrency is included at 5% of your MAU on Basic and Advanced and 10% on Enterprise. On overage CometChat charges $0.10 per extra MAU (falling at higher tiers) or $1 per extra concurrent connection — and where both are exceeded it bills the higher of the two, not both. Enterprise has no listed overage; usage above the plan is upgraded to the appropriate plan instead. Messages and storage are unlimited on every plan, and message retention is 6 months across the board, extendable at extra cost. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CometChat?
answers.a: The pricing cliff is the honest headline: from a 100-MAU free tier straight to ~$239/mo is a brutal jump for an early-stage app, and users report plan structures changing under them. Model your MAU growth curve and the overage math before you architect around it. Chat infrastructure is sticky by nature; the time to compare vendors is before launch, not after.

Compliancely is genuinely best for finance, tax and HR teams with a steady monthly volume of US identity and business checks, who would rather buy TIN matching, KYB, I-9 and sanctions screening behind one API than integrate three separate vendors. It suits those willing to run a sales conversation to price the modules beyond TIN matching. Skip it if you need a handful of one-off verifications a year. The cheapest plan still bills a monthly allowance whether you use it or not, and the per-match rate is at its worst down there. Also skip it if you need the full cost of a compliance stack on paper before you talk to a salesperson, since only the TIN-match tiers are published.

(2026-07-29, re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. Billed annually, Essential 25 is $16.95/mo for 25 monthly TIN verifications ($0.67 per match), Essential 50 $32.54/mo ($0.65), Essential 75 $45.79/mo ($0.61), Plus 100 $57.99/mo ($0.57) and Plus 250 $135.04/mo ($0.54). Switch the toggle to monthly billing and the same five tiers read $19.95, $38.49, $53.95, $67.95 and $159.95 per month, at $0.79 down to $0.63 per match. The page advertises 15% off for annual billing, and the real gap holds at roughly 15% on every tier. Enterprise is quote-only. Everything else Compliancely sells carries no public price at all: the business verification and credit-risk report packages, address verification, Form I-9, IRS tax transcripts and income verification each end in Contact Sales or Book a Demo rather than a number. Compliancely's partner team told us on 5 August 2026 that the published tiers are meant for buyers up to roughly 3,000 checks and that anything above that moves to a custom quote — that threshold is theirs, not a number the pricing page states. They confirmed on 11 August 2026 that buyers over that line are sent to their demo-request form at compliancely.com/demo-request, where the quote is written by hand; there is no published rate card for that range at all. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Compliancely?
answers.a: The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a dozen. Every tier you can actually buy online is an allowance of TIN verifications. The moment you want the things the homepage leads with — KYB business verification, credit-risk assessment, address verification, Form I-9 and E-Verify, IRS tax transcripts, OFAC and watchlist monitoring — the button changes from Get Started to Contact Sales. So the compliance stack this tool is pitched as has no advertised cost, and the number you can see is the smallest part of it. The second thing to read carefully is that the tiers are allowances rather than rates. You commit to a monthly verification count up front, and the per-match price moves against the smallest buyers. It is $0.79 a check on the cheapest month-to-month plan versus $0.54 on the largest annual one — a 46% spread that falls the wrong way for anyone testing the product at low volume. If your usage is lumpy — a filing-season spike and eleven quiet months — an allowance you buy every month is the wrong shape, and the prepaid option the page offers as a third toggle is worth asking about before you subscribe.

Connecteam is genuinely best for deskless and frontline teams (shift work, field crews) that need scheduling, a time clock and comms in one app, on the free-for-10 plan. Skip it if your whole team sits at desks with email and Slack — this is built for the frontline, and a general PM tool fits an office better.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page, USD) The free tier is real and not a trial: the Small Business Plan is $0 for life, covers up to 10 users and includes all hubs and features. Above that you buy per hub — Operations, Communications or HR & Skills — and each hub carries a flat base price covering the first 30 users, plus a per-user surcharge only from user 31 onward. Billed yearly that base is $29/mo at Basic, $49 at Advanced and $99 at Expert; billed monthly it is $35, $59 and $119. The surcharge is where the hubs diverge: on the yearly plans Operations adds $0.80, $2.50 and $4.20 per extra user a month, while Communications and HR & Skills add $0.50, $1.50 and $3.00. Quoting only the per-user rate understates a small team's bill, because a shop of 30 or fewer pays the flat base either way. Price it per hub you will actually switch on, not per user. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Connecteam?
answers.a: The free-for-10 plan is one of the most generous in the category, but the three-hub structure means costs can stack if you need all of them — price the specific hubs you'll actually use, not the full bundle.

Consensus is genuinely best for researchers, clinicians, students and writers who want evidence-backed answers drawn from peer-reviewed papers instead of the open web. Skip it if your questions are practical/commercial rather than research-based (a general AI assistant fits), or you need full systematic-review rigor (this accelerates it, not replaces it).

(re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) Consensus blocks plain fetches of its pricing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount, so today's figures are not independently confirmed. Our dated reading: a free tier with essential search; Pro about $15/mo, or roughly $10/mo billed annually, with unlimited Pro searches and 15 Deep searches; a Deep tier adding around 200 Deep searches for power users; Teams and Enterprise quoted. The unit that matters is Deep searches rather than seats — that is what the tiers ration. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Consensus?
answers.a: It searches peer-reviewed literature, which is its strength and its boundary: it can tell you what published studies found, not whether those studies are good. Study quality, sample sizes and conflicting results still need your judgment, and the AI summary layer can smooth over genuine scientific disagreement. Treat it as a dramatically faster literature scan, not an oracle; click through to the papers that matter.

Consentmo is genuinely best for Shopify merchants selling into several jurisdictions who want one app to carry the cookie banner, the consent signals the ad platforms now demand, and a first layer of accessibility — and who go in knowing that the region-aware banner and the accessibility tools sit on the $37 tier.. Skip it if you sell outside Shopify; you need one plain cookie banner in one country, which the free tier or your theme already covers; or you need an actual accessibility audit and repair of your theme rather than a widget and a scanner..

(read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/gdpr-backpack and on the vendor's own consentmo.com/pricing, which list the same four tiers) Billed in USD every 30 days, with a 7-day free trial on each paid tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier, the free one included, so the ladder gates features rather than traffic. Free costs nothing and covers the cookie banner and preferences, the data-request and Do-Not-Sell pages, one banner language and one cookie scan a month, with minimal Consentmo branding on the banner. Standard is $10 a month or $100 a year (17% off) and adds unlimited cookie scans, multi-region compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA and others), Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok integrations, US opt-out signals, script blocking, multilingual banners with automatic detection, automatic Google Drive backups and removal of the branding. Plus is $37 or $370 a year and is where the accessibility side starts: web accessibility (ADA/WCAG), smart geotargeting, the EU withdrawal page for Directive 2023/2673, automated monitoring, scheduled scans, AI cookie categorisation, advanced analytics and full CSS customisation. Enterprise is $64 or $640 a year for IAB TCF 2.3, cross-domain consent sharing, a checkout banner for Shopify Plus, Hydrogen and headless support, A/B testing, an alt-text manager, bot and crawler protection and priority support. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Consentmo?
answers.a: Read the ladder before you budget $10 for this. The two things the listing leads with — web accessibility and a smart region-specific banner — are not on Standard; they start at Plus, $37 a month, which is 3.7 times the entry price. A Shopify Plus store that wants a banner on the checkout needs Enterprise at $64, and so does anything headless or on Hydrogen. The accessibility side is a widget and a scanner: it overlays controls and flags issues, but it does not change the theme markup underneath, which is where an accessibility audit actually looks — treat it as a first layer, not as a remediation. And the free tier puts Consentmo's own branding on the banner your visitors see first.

Contractor Foreman is genuinely best for small and mid-size contractors who want estimating, scheduling and daily logs in one place and can commit to a year — the company-wide fee makes it cheap per head once you have a crew. Skip it if you are a sole trader with a handful of jobs, because Basic at $49 a month annual is real money against a spreadsheet and a calendar — though the 30-day trial and the conditional 100-day refund mean trying it costs nothing but your time.

answers.q: How much does Contractor Foreman cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 28 Aug 2026 on their own pricing page; all plan prices unchanged since 1 Aug 2026) Priced for the company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier, and every plan opens with 30 days free before the first bill. Annual: Basic $49/month ($588 a year, 1 user), Standard $105 ($1,264, 3 users), Plus $166 ($1,997, 8 users), Pro $221 ($2,654, 15 users), Unlimited $332 ($3,984, unlimited users). Quarterly costs more for the same plans: Standard $132/month ($395 a quarter), Plus $206 ($619), Pro $282 ($845), Unlimited $415 ($1,245). Basic is not offered quarterly. Their own wording: the fee listed is the fee for the company as a whole. Card payments taken through the built-in Stripe integration are billed separately at 2.9% + $0.30 a transaction (3.9% + $0.30 for Amex, 1% + $0.30 capped at $10.00 for ACH). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Contractor Foreman?
answers.a: Credit where it is due first: this is company pricing with unlimited projects and no per-user overage inside your tier, which is rare in construction software and genuinely cheaper than per-seat rivals for a crew. The catch is the billing term. Quarterly costs 26% more than annual on the same plan — $132 against $105 on Standard — and Basic is not sold quarterly at all, so the cheapest way in requires a year paid up front. The user counts are the real ladder: 1, 3, 8, 15, unlimited. A five-person crew is not on Standard at $105, it is on Plus at $166, so count your licence holders before you compare against anything else.

Convert is genuinely best for CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites. Skip it if your traffic is modest — statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use — or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it.

(re-verified 2026-08-21 on their own pricing page) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr), and includes 100K tested users a month; Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo annually ($5,040/yr), and includes 1M a month; Enterprise on request. Overuse is metered — $399 per extra 100K on Growth, $699 per 250K on Pro, and it can be switched off — and each additional custom domain costs $1,000/year. Convert deliberately ships no heatmaps or exit popups, calling this a best-of-breed strategy, and charges no extra fee for its integrations. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Convert?
answers.a: The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them — and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399. One thing people misprice, and it is not the test itself: everyone expects an experiment to end when the subscription does. The trap is the winner. Convert describes itself as a client-side tool where “adding just one snippet of code on your site will then do all of the magic”. So a winning variant you leave running in the visual editor is not a change to your site — it is a rendering by their script. Ship the winner into your own code, or you are paying rent on a result you already bought.

CrankWheel is genuinely best for sales reps, insurance agents and consultants who need prospects to view a screen instantly with no download or install, on any device. Skip it if you need full video conferencing, webinars or team collaboration (Zoom/Meet fit better), or your call volume stays under the free tier.

(read on crankwheel.com/pricing, 2026-08-21) A free plan with no payment details required — unlimited usage for the first 15 days, then up to 15 sessions a month for life. Solo is $29/month for one user with unlimited usage, up to 30 viewers per share and up to 10 video-conferencing participants. Team starts at $99/month for unlimited users sharing 100 meetings a month, rising in steps: Team 200 $194, Team 500 $467, Team 1000 $882, Team 2000 $1,562. Busy User discount plans cost less for a capped number of users — Team 100 at $59 for three users, Team 500 at $287 for fifteen. Enterprise is quoted per year and the page prints no figure. A meeting counts at 40 seconds with a viewer, or when you create a share link or segment, or on an Instant Demo call. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CrankWheel?
answers.a: It's deliberately narrow — instant, no-download screen sharing for sales calls — so it's excellent at that one job and thin everywhere else: no full video-conferencing suite, no deep collaboration or webinar tooling. Mind which plan caps what: the free plan drops to 15 sessions a month after the first fortnight and Team puts everyone on a shared pool of 100, while Solo is the one paid tier with unlimited usage. If you want an all-purpose meeting platform, this isn't it; if you want prospects to see your screen in seconds with zero friction, that focus is exactly why it works.

Crazy Egg is genuinely best for lean marketing teams that want heatmaps, recordings and built-in A/B testing in one consolidated tool — noting that testing starts on the $99 plan, not the $29 one. Skip it if you want generous recordings, automatic heatmaps and qualitative feedback — Hotjar's free tier and product depth suit product teams better.

answers.q: How much does Crazy Egg cost?
answers.a: (2026-08-21, read on their own pricing page) Three plans, all billed annually, with a 30-day free trial and — in the vendor's words — no overages, ever. Analytics starts at $29/month and scales on tracked pageviews across 5,000, 50,000, 150,000, 500,000 and 1,000,000 a month, starting at 50 recordings. Growth starts at $99/month, but its slider starts at 50,000 pageviews rather than 5,000, and includes 500 recordings plus A/B testing, CTAs and targeting by device type. Enterprise is quoted. Note a conflict in the vendor's own material: their machine-readable pricing.md still lists an older Starter/Plus/Pro/Enterprise ladder at $29/$99/$249/$599 with different pageview allowances. The live pricing page is the one we read for the figures above. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Crazy Egg?
answers.a: The entry plan is thin on recordings — 50 a month against Hotjar's far more generous free tier. And A/B testing is not in it at all: that starts on Growth at $99, whose pageview slider begins at 50,000 rather than 5,000. Heatmaps need manual per-page setup and annual-only billing locks you in. Like all these tools it's diagnostic — it shows what's broken, it doesn't fix it. Worth knowing before you treat a result as banked: Crazy Egg states it can run A/B tests “after implementing just a small code snippet directly on the website”, which means a winning variant is served by that snippet rather than written into your pages. Stop paying and the original page is what visitors get. Move the winner into your own templates once a test settles.

answers.q: Is Credit Repair Cloud worth it?
answers.a: Credit Repair Cloud is genuinely best for entrepreneurs building or running a credit-repair business who need client management, dispute automation and done-for-you letter workflows. Skip it if you just want to fix your own personal credit (you don't need this), or you're not prepared for the sales and compliance work a client business demands.

answers.q: How much does Credit Repair Cloud cost?
answers.a: (price re-verified 2026-08-21 against the vendor's own pricing page, and now with the published limits rather than approximations) There are five plans, priced monthly. Personal is $49 for 1 user and up to 3 friends and family, and Start $179 for up to 3 users and 300 active clients. Grow is $299 for 6 users and 600 clients, and Scale $399 for 12 users and 1,200 clients. Enterprise is $599 for 24 users and 2,400 clients. Annual billing takes 20% off and is shown as a monthly equivalent on the four business tiers: $143.20, $239.20, $319.20 and $479.20. Every plan carries a 30-day free trial, the vendor states it charges no startup fees, and monthly plans have no long-term contract while annual plans require a one-year term. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Credit Repair Cloud?
answers.a: This is business-in-a-box software for starting a credit-repair company, not a tool that repairs your own credit — the price only makes sense if you're actually building a client business on it. The middle tiers jump fast as you add clients and seats, and success depends far more on your sales and compliance discipline (credit repair is a regulated space) than on the software. Buy it as an operator, not a consumer.

CrowdStrike is genuinely best for small and mid-size companies that want a serious endpoint agent without running a security team — Falcon Go is genuinely priced for businesses under 100 devices. Skip it if you are under ten devices and already run a maintained operating system with its built-in protection, because at that size the management overhead outweighs the gain; also skip Go if you actually need EDR, since that starts a tier up.

(2026-08-28, taken from the bundle table on their pricing page; the three published per-device rates have not moved since 1 Aug 2026) Priced per device. Falcon Go $7.99 per device per month, or $59.99 per device billed annually — capped at a maximum of 100 devices. Falcon Pro $14.99 monthly or $99.99 annually per device. Falcon Enterprise $19.99 per device per month, or $184.99 per device billed annually — a rate the 1 Aug reading recorded as unpublished. Larger tiers and managed services are quote-only. The free trial is a single 15-day Falcon Free Trial covering Next-Gen Antivirus, Device Control and Express Support, not a trial of each paid tier. Annual subscriptions are billed in full at the start of the term and can be cancelled within 30 days for a full refund. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with CrowdStrike?
answers.a: Two numbers decide whether this is for you, and neither is the headline. The first is the 100-device ceiling on Falcon Go: it is not a soft limit you grow through, it is the point where you change product. The second is the annual rate, which is worth doing the division on — $59.99 a year against $7.99 a month is $95.88, so annual saves 37%, one of the larger annual discounts in security software. Beyond that, be honest with yourself about which tier you are comparing: Go is antivirus with a good agent, and the endpoint detection and response that CrowdStrike is famous for starts at Pro. Comparing Go against a full EDR product from a competitor is comparing the wrong things.

Databox is genuinely best for SMBs and agencies that want clean KPI dashboards from 130+ one-click integrations without building them by hand. Skip it if you need more than the three free sources but only a handful — the next step is Analyst at $71 a month for five — or you want deep custom data modelling, where a free tool like Looker Studio fits better.

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own pricing page) Databox renamed and repriced its whole ladder since our August reading, so the Analyst/Pro/Growth tiers we described are gone. Free is $0 forever: 1 user, 3 data sources, 1 dashboard, 10 custom metrics, 50 AI credits a month, daily sync. Billed annually: Analyst $71/mo (1 user, 5 sources, unlimited dashboards and reports, 150 credits, hourly sync), Team Core $199/mo (3 users, 10 sources, 500 credits), Team Scale $319/mo (10 users, 30 sources, 1,000 credits, sub-accounts) and Agency from $79/mo (unlimited users, 20 sources, 300 credits), plus a quoted Custom tier. Monthly those read $249, $399 and from $99; annual billing is 20% off. Databox states it does not charge per seat. Extra data sources no longer carry a per-source fee: each plan includes a fixed number and more means moving up a tier, except on Agency, which adds client packs of 1 client, 5 sources and 50 credits for $20/mo annually ($25 monthly). Add-ons are priced separately: branding and white-labeling $200/mo, advanced security management $80/mo, OKRs $160/mo, fiscal calendar $40/mo, 15-minute sync $14/mo per source, and flexible AI credit top-ups. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Databox?
answers.a: The pricing model bites, just not where it used to. The per-source fee is gone, and for some buyers that is worse rather than better: each plan includes a fixed number of data sources and going over means moving up a whole tier, so one extra integration can mean the $199 Team Core to $319 Team Scale step rather than $5.60. Only the Agency plan sells capacity piecemeal, in $20 client packs. AI credits are a shared monthly pool for Genie and the MCP server, so heavy AI use moves you up a tier as fast as data does, and 15-minute sync — once part of the top plan — is now a $14 per-source add-on on top of the subscription. Power users may also find the custom-metric and data-modelling depth limited next to a full BI tool.

Datarails is genuinely best for Excel-bound finance teams that have outgrown the spreadsheet plumbing but not the spreadsheets — consolidating several entities or data sources into one governed set of numbers, with planning, reporting and dashboards on top, while the models stay in Excel. Skip it if you are a single-entity company whose budget lives in one workbook, or a team of two that just needs a dashboard — the quote-only sales motion and the tier caps cost more in elapsed time than the problem is worth at that size.

(read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be. The page frames that as a feature: “Get a custom quote tailored to your needs. Complete cost transparency, with no consultant fees—ever.”

What the page does publish is the shape of the ladder, and it is unusually explicit about what changes between tiers. The comparison table lists the same feature set on all three plans: reporting, planning, dashboards, Data Mapper, Lookups, Workflows, Submit Button, File Boxes, Filters, version control, the Datarails AI Suite, the FinanceOS AI Connector and permissions. Only two rows differ. Professional gives 1 integration and 2 users with standard support. Premium, marked most popular, gives 2 integrations and 5 users with premium support, and adds AI Storyboards, described as board decks in one click. Expert gives 3 integrations and 15 users with premium support, plus one “additional product included” — the line beyond FP&A runs to Datarails Month-End Close, Datarails Cash, Datarails Spend Control and Datarails Desk, and the page does not say which of those the extra slot may be spent on.

So the meter is seats and connected systems, not features. The page states no currency, no billing period, no minimum term and does not say whether a quote is annual, and there is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup: the only entry point on every page of the site is Request Demo or Request Quote. Treat any Datarails figure you have seen quoted elsewhere as unverified — on 25 August 2026 the vendor's own pricing page contains no amount at all.

One of those unpublished terms the vendor will answer if you ask. On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grows, and that adding modules or capabilities beyond the core platform can carry an extra cost that depends on the scope of the expansion. That is the vendor's own account rather than a published rate, so it belongs in your quote in writing — but it does answer the term question the pricing page leaves open. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Datarails?
answers.a: You cannot find out what it costs without talking to sales, and the entry plan is smaller than it looks: Professional covers 2 users and 1 integration, so a finance team of three, or one that needs both the ERP and the CRM connected, is priced into the next tier before the conversation starts. There is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup anywhere on the site — every path ends at Request Demo — so there is no way to try it quietly before procurement is involved.

Deel is genuinely best for companies hiring internationally without local entities — contractors paid compliantly in 150+ countries, or full EOR employment where you need someone on the ground fast. Skip it if your team is all-domestic (a local payroll tool is far cheaper), or you hire enough people in one country that opening your own entity beats paying per-employee EOR fees forever.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Pricing is per worker and demo-led, and each product is priced separately. HR and hiring tools start at $14 per worker a month. Contractor management is $49 per contractor a month, or $325 per month per Contractor of Record if you want Deel to carry the compliance risk. US PEO starts at $125 per employee a month. And EOR, where Deel employs your international hire, starts at $599 per employee a month. There is a free demo and final quotes come through sales. The spread is the point: the same headcount costs $14 or $599 a month depending on which relationship you need, so identify the employment model before comparing vendors. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Deel?
answers.a: Every price is a ‘starting at’ and every button says ‘book a demo’ — the real bill depends on countries, benefits and add-ons, and only firms up in a sales conversation. And know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not software — worth it in unfamiliar jurisdictions, expensive where you could open your own entity.

Deputy is genuinely best for shift-based businesses — hospitality, retail, healthcare, any hourly workforce — that need rostering, clocking and labour-law compliance in one system and have enough staff to clear the minimum spend. Skip it if you run a small salaried desk team: the $30 monthly minimum means you pay for roughly six users whether you have them or not, and salaried staff rarely need shift-level clocking at all.

(re-read 2026-09-19 on deputy.com/pricing; amounts unchanged since the browser reading of 2026-07-31, which used both billing toggles) Three plans, per user per month and excluding tax. On annual billing Lite is $5, Core $6.50 and Pro $9; switch the toggle to monthly and the same three read $5.50, $7.25 and $10. Add-ons are billed monthly on top.
