HR is $2 per user, Messaging+ $1.95 per user and Analytics+ $1.50 per user, and the last two are included in Pro. Deputy Payroll enabled by Paycor is $8 per user plus a $49 monthly base fee, available only on annual Core and Pro plans in the US. The page also states a minimum monthly spend of USD $30 / AUD $30 / GBP £20 per invoice on the monthly Lite, Core and Pro plans. Lite and Core start with a free trial; Pro is Contact us rather than self-serve. Two things the page added since: every plan card now carries Deputy AI marked INTRODUCTORY FREE with the line that price and availability may change, so the AI is not a paid-for feature you can hold them to. And a banner across the top offers three months free to businesses that add workforce management and Payroll before 30 November — Payroll being the $8-per-user add-on with the $49 monthly base fee, US-only and annual Core or Pro, so the free months arrive attached to the most expensive thing on the page. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Deputy?
answers.a: The minimum monthly spend is the number to check before anything else: at $5.50 per user on monthly billing, a team of fewer than about six people still pays the $30 floor, so the headline per-user price is misleading at small scale. Beyond that, the plan you probably want is not the one you first price — auto-scheduling, demand forecasting and labour budgets sit in Core, and SSO, custom access levels and location hierarchies only in Pro, which has no public self-serve checkout. The add-ons stack per user as well, and the payroll add-on is US-only and annual-only.

Descript is genuinely best for podcasters and video creators who want to edit by editing the transcript, cutting, overdubbing and stripping filler words as easily as editing a doc. It also suits teams who want those same edits triggered from code or from an AI assistant via Descript’s API and MCP connector rather than from the app. Skip it if you need frame-precise, effects-heavy editing (a traditional NLE fits better) or your monthly volume blows past the media-hour caps.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Free plan with 60 minutes a month and watermarked 720p exports. Paid, per person per month, annual against monthly: Hobbyist $16 / $24, Creator $24 / $35, Business $50 / $65, with annual billing saving up to 35%. Media hours and AI credits are capped per tier: roughly 10, 30 and 40 hours a month, and 400 to 1,500 credits. So the meter that matters is footage rather than seats — a weekly podcast can outgrow Hobbyist on hours long before it needs the features above it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Descript?
answers.a: It's per-editor pricing with two meters running underneath: media hours AND monthly AI credits. Heavy podcast or video volume burns through the caps fast, and the free tier watermarks 720p exports — model your real production hours before picking a tier. The API changes the arithmetic rather than escaping it. Their own API page states access is included for paying users at no additional cost, but the work it does draws from the same AI credits and media minutes — so automating a pipeline burns the caps faster, not slower. It also stops just short of the finish — the same page says direct media file exports are not supported yet, so the export step stays a manual one in the app. (read on their own API page, 2026-08-14)

Devs.ai is genuinely best for teams that want to prototype and ship AI agents and apps across multiple models without engineering overhead, and that can absorb model usage metered on top of the per-seat fee. Skip it if you need SSO, access control lists or white-labelling without going through an Enterprise contract, or you need one predictable all-in bill rather than a seat fee plus metered usage.

(re-verified 2026-08-26, read in a live browser session on devs.ai/home/pricing with both billing toggles) Devs.ai does publish its pricing — on the marketing site at devs.ai/home/pricing, not at the app's /pricing route, which bounces you to a login screen. Free is $0 forever, but Agent Builder and App Builder appear there in "Core" rather than "Full" form, data upload is capped at 2 GB, and workflows, APIs and integrations are marked absent. Personal is $15 per seat / month billed annually or $18 billed monthly; Business is $30 per seat / month annually or $36 monthly; Enterprise is a custom annual contract. The seat fee is not the whole bill: Personal includes $10 of usage per month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. Data upload runs 2 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB and custom across the four tiers. Team governance and collaboration start at Business, while SSO (OpenID/SAML), access control lists, custom connectors and white-labelling are Enterprise-only. Separately, Devs.ai told us by email on 5 August 2026 that organisations upgrading to a paid Personal or Business plan can earn up to $100 in usage credits for completing setup steps: starting a conversation, creating an agent, connecting an integration, deploying an app. The credits are shared org-wide and do not expire. Enterprise is excluded, and orgs already on a paid plan before July 2026 are not enrolled by default. That last paragraph is the vendor's own statement to us, not something we found published on the pricing page. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Devs.ai?
answers.a: The seat price is the smaller half of the bill. Personal includes $10 of usage a month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. The plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate you pay once it runs out — which is exactly the number you need to forecast a real workload. The free plan is a demo rather than a working tier: both builders are limited to "Core", and workflows, APIs and integrations are absent entirely, which is much of what would make the platform useful past a first agent. And for a product sold on IT governance, the governance controls are the ones you cannot buy with a card — SSO, access control lists and white-labelling sit on the Enterprise tier, behind a custom annual contract.

Dext is genuinely best for accountants, bookkeepers and growing businesses drowning in receipts who want fast, accurate capture flowing straight into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage. Skip it if you're a sole trader with few receipts (pricey for low volume), or you want all-in-one accounting — Dext only does the capture layer.

(re-verified 2026-08-21, read in a browser on dext.com/en/business/pricing because the price panel renders client-side) Dext has moved off named tiers: you choose a region and a billing period, then slide an allowance. The base of 250 documents a month and 5 users costs $25.21 per month billed annually ($302.50 a year) or $31.50 monthly in the Rest of the World, £30 monthly in the UK, €31.50 in the EU and A$42 in APAC, all excluding tax. The annual discount is stated as up to 20% everywhere except the UK page, which says up to 19%. Add-ons are billed separately: AI Assist $10.5 a month until 31 October, Commerce Lite from $7.50 and Vault free for 100MB then from $4. Line Item Extraction and Supplier Statement Extraction are from $20.50 a month or $0.50 per document, and Bank Statement Extraction from $13.00 a month or $0.32 per document. Plans include 10 sheets of bank statement extraction, 5 line-item documents and 5 supplier statement extractions as free credits, and the free trial is 14 days with no payment details required. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dext?
answers.a: It's a data-capture layer, not accounting software — it feeds Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, so you still need one of those. Extraction accuracy varies and sometimes needs manual fixes, the UI is tricky for beginners, the mobile app is more limited than desktop, and sole traders find it pricey.

Dify is genuinely best for technical teams that want to build and ship LLM apps and agents on a source-available platform they can self-host and control. Skip it if you want a no-maintenance, non-technical builder — a fully managed no-code AI tool saves you the infra and upkeep.

Source-available and free of a software fee to self-host — the Community Edition ships under the Dify Open Source License, a modified Apache 2.0 with additional conditions — while the managed Dify Cloud adds a free Sandbox, Professional at $59/mo ($590/yr) and Team at $159/mo ($1,590/yr), each priced per workspace (2026). Self-hosting still costs you infrastructure, model usage and any commercial licence those terms require. Cloud plans include message credits for supported model providers; once those run out you connect your own provider API key and pay that provider directly. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dify?
answers.a: 'Free' self-hosting isn't free — you own the servers, updates and reliability, and model usage bills separately once the included message credits run out. Dify Cloud takes that infrastructure work off your hands, but every cloud plan is a single workspace, and multiple workspaces, SSO and a commercial licence sit in quote-only Enterprise. It's powerful, but self-hosting it well needs technical comfort.

Diginius is genuinely best for lean teams and agencies that want PPC, SEO and lead intelligence consolidated in one affordable dashboard instead of five subscriptions. Skip it if your growth lives in one channel where a specialist tool's depth pays for itself, or you need enterprise analytics rigor.

(re-verified 2026-08-21 on diginius.com/pricing/, business pricing) Essential $75 USD a month for 2 users, Pro $250 for 5 users, Core $500 for 10 users and marked Most Popular, Business by contact with sales. The FAQ on the same page confirms a 20% discount for annual payment. The plan limits scale with the price. SEO keywords run 25 / 500 / 1000 / custom, and SEO site pages 1000 / 5000 / 10000 / custom. Lead Intelligence leads run 10 / 25 / 50 per week, and Bombora intent leads 10 / 50 / 100 per week. Contact info credits run 25 / 50 / 100 per month, and support goes from email only to a dedicated customer success rep. The trial banner advertises 30 days including 100 intent leads a week and 100 contact credits, but the mobile plan card on the same page says 14 days. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Diginius?
answers.a: All-in-one marketing dashboards live or die on data depth per module. Diginius bundles PPC, SEO, lead intelligence and reporting affordably, but specialists — a dedicated SEO suite, a dedicated PPC optimizer — go deeper in their lanes. So buy it as consolidation for a lean team, not as a replacement for expert-grade tooling in your primary channel. Verify the integrations you depend on (especially Microsoft Ads, its historical strength) in the trial.

Digit is genuinely best for manufacturers and distributors outgrowing spreadsheets who need inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system, and who genuinely need lot tracking and traceability rather than just wanting them. Skip it if you are a small operation where $400/month for five users is heavy against what a warehouse module in your existing accounting package would cost; also skip it if your integration list is long, because the per-connection model punishes exactly that — $100 to $125 a month for every integration past the second, depending on which part of their pricing page you read.

(re-read 2026-09-17 in a rendered browser on heysutton.com/pricing, the rebranded site; unchanged from the 5 September reading on digit-software.com) Four tiers with three published: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15, and Enterprise on quote. Extra users are $63/month each on every tier. Paying quarterly takes 10% off — $360, $675 and $1,170 a month, shown with the quarter total beside it — and annually 20%, which is $320, $600 and $1,040 with the year total beside it; the page now opens on Monthly, so the first figure you see is the real monthly rate. Two integrations are included on every plan. The third and each one after it is where the page disagrees with itself: the Integrations block says $100 a month, the FAQ on the same page says $125, and the add-on cards side with the FAQ — API access $125 a month, MCP access $125, push notifications and webhooks $63, all the same price on Starter, Growth and Professional. Customer portals are $18.75 per portal per month on every tier, Enterprise included. We asked Digit which of the two they bill on 5 September 2026 and had no answer; twelve days later, on the rebranded site, both figures were still there. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Digit?
answers.a: The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling, and the add-ons are where an inventory system quietly doubles. Two integrations are included — but a working setup usually means an accounting package and a webshop, which is your two, and then Amazon or a second sales channel is another $125 a month by the FAQ (the integrations block on the same page still says $100; we have asked which one bills). Want the API, or your data inside an AI assistant? $125 a month each. A Starter customer on QuickBooks, Shopify and Amazon with API access is at $650 a month on the FAQ's numbers, $625 on the block's, before adding a sixth user. Price the whole configuration you actually need, not the tier.

Disputifier is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a chargeback problem big enough to cost real money and nobody in-house to fight disputes, who would rather pay a share of what is recovered than a monthly fee. Skip it if your dispute volume is low or lumpy, you need a predictable monthly bill, or your margins are high enough that auto-refunding an alerted order costs more than losing the occasional dispute.

(read 2026-08-19 and re-verified 2026-09-17 on apps.shopify.com/disputifier and disputifier.com/pricing) Free to install, with everything billed on use, and unchanged between those two readings. The listing shows a single plan — Basic, free to install, with a 7-day risk-free trial — and names two charges: chargeback fighting at 20% of won-back revenue, and chargeback alerts from $17 to $27.50 per alert. All charges are billed in USD. The vendor's own pricing page fills in the rest. Recovery is 20% of the recovered amount with the fee capped at $250 per win — win a $50 chargeback and they debit $10 — while fraud prevention is $0.05 per order and 'order not received' prevention another $0.05 per order. Alerts are sold there as custom volume-based pricing by quote, so the $17-$27.50 band on the listing is the only public number for them. There is no monthly subscription anywhere in this: the bill is a function of how many disputes and orders you have, so it cannot be read off the pricing page in advance. Developer Disputifier, 294 Trillium Way, Clayton, North Carolina; the app launched 23 September 2020 and carries a 4.6 average over 125 App Store reviews. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Disputifier?
answers.a:
Free to install is doing a lot of work here. All four services bill per event — a fifth of each recovery, $17 to $27.50 an alert, five cents an order twice over — so the cost lands after the fact and scales with exactly the thing you are trying to reduce. Model your worst chargeback month before you switch alerts on, not your average one.

The reviews deserve a straight look too. The 4.6 average across 125 reviews, read again on 17 September 2026, is not a middle: 87% are five stars and twelve of the one hundred and twenty-five are a single star, with almost nothing in between. That shape has held while the count grew — on 22 August the same listing showed 4.6 from 88 reviews with nine one-stars, so both ends have filled at roughly the same rate. The most recent one-star we read, from June 2026, describes a security incident at the vendor and a dispute over unpaid invoices and billing descriptors; Disputifier replied in July that it does not block merchants from moving providers and disputes the account of the charges. We have not verified either side and are not taking one. What the pattern does show is where the friction sits: merchants either rate this perfect or fall out with it over invoices, not over whether disputes were won.

And know what alerts cannot reach. Coverage depends on the shopper's bank and card: smaller issuers do not participate, Amex and Discover frequently cannot be set up, Klarna alerts do not exist yet and PayPal alerts are recent. The prevention rate the vendor quotes is a ceiling for a well-covered card mix, not a promise for yours.

Dondy is genuinely best for Shopify stores whose customers already live in WhatsApp — much of Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia — that want cart recovery, order updates and campaigns on the official API without leaving the Shopify admin. Skip it if your customers are on email and SMS, or you need one predictable monthly figure: Meta's per-conversation charges sit on top of every paid tier here.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/dondy-marketing-ai, listed as “Dondy: WhatsApp Marketing+Chat”) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial, and every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026. Free: a WhatsApp chat button with unlimited conversations, custom size and location, and prefilled messages. Pro $6.99 a month or $67.10 a year, a 20% saving: premium button designs, a WhatsApp widget, text customisation, product URLs in messages, custom hours, reports, and abandoned-cart and order-confirmation messages you send manually. Power Automation $79.99 a month or $719.88 a year, a 25% saving: automated abandoned-cart recovery, WhatsApp marketing campaigns, customisable automated messages, bulk messaging to Shopify segments, an inbox with Shopify integration and the official WhatsApp Business API. It includes 1,000 one-click messages every 30 days and quotes WhatsApp rates starting at $0.0158 in the US on top. Elite $159.99 a month or $1,439.88 a year, also a 25% saving, adds an AI chatbot for sales and support, AI corrections and training, AI product recommendations, a five-agent WhatsApp inbox, green-tick verification assistance, a VIP account manager and unlimited WhatsApp flows; same 1,000 included messages, rates starting at $0.0126. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and Meta's per-conversation charges are separate from all of it. The listing now also advertises work the dossier did not cover in August: collecting WhatsApp reviews through Judge.me, Loox, Yotpo, Trustoo or Google, cash-on-delivery messaging, and AI agents alongside the chatbot; the named integrations are Shopify Flow, Shopify Admin, Judge.me, Klaviyo, Loox, WhatsApp API and WhatsApp Business. Developer Dondy; the app launched 15 March 2023, is available in five languages and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Reviews have grown to 823 averaging 4.9, up from 774 on 22 August, distributed 92% five-star (756), 4% four-star (36), 1% three-star (6), 0% two-star (4) and 3% one-star (21) — the one-star count is the same 21 as a month ago, so all 49 new reviews landed above the bottom. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dondy?
answers.a:
The free plan is a chat button. It is a decent chat button, and conversations through it are unlimited. But none of the marketing this app is named for is in it. Automated cart recovery, campaigns and the official API begin at $79.99 a month, and the $6.99 tier in between only lets you send those same messages by hand.

You will also get two bills. Dondy charges the subscription; Meta charges per conversation on the WhatsApp Business API. Dondy can only tell you the rate starts at $0.0158 or $0.0126, because the real figure depends on the country you are messaging and the type of conversation. A thousand one-click messages a month are included on the two top tiers; past that, your monthly total is not knowable from this listing, and a campaign to a large segment is exactly the kind of thing that produces a surprise. Model it against your own list size and destination countries before you send one.

The rest is Meta's rulebook, not Dondy's. Opt-in, message templates and sender quality are governed on WhatsApp's side, so approval and reach are not things this app can promise you whatever you pay it. The review record is strong — 823 reviews, 92% at the top rating, and the 21 one-star reports have not grown while 49 reviews were added since August — and a misfired broadcast on this channel is still a block rather than an unsubscribe.

Drip is genuinely best for an online store on Shopify, WooCommerce or BigCommerce that already has order data worth segmenting and wants ecommerce playbooks — abandoned cart, welcome series, post-purchase — without assembling them by hand. The pricing model suits a list that grows steadily and mails at a normal cadence, because you pay for people rather than per seat or per feature, and every plan carries the whole feature set. Skip it if you are not selling online: Drip says an ecommerce store is not required but that the platform is built for one, and you would be paying for the half you cannot use. Skip it too if your list is large and you mail often, because the send allowance caps at twelve per contact per month once you are past the small tiers. The same goes past 175,000 people, where the published ladder ends and pricing becomes a conversation.

(ladder re-read on drip.com/pricing on 17 September 2026; every rung below was confirmed on the live slider and matches the page's own pricing object) One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. The page now headlines it as paying for your list size and how many emails you send. 1-2,500 people is $39, then $49 at 3,000, $59 at 3,500, $69 at 4,000, $79 at 4,500, $89 at 5,000, $99 at 6,000, $109 at 7,000, $124 at 8,000, $139 at 9,000, $154 at 10,000, $169 at 12,500, $209 at 15,000, $249 at 17,500, $289 at 20,000, $329 at 22,500, $369 at 25,000, $409 at 27,500, $449 at 30,000 and $489 at 32,500; from there it climbs $40 a rung to $609 at 40,000, $649 at 45,000 and $699 at 50,000, after which every extra 5,000 people costs $50 — $1,299 at 110,000, $1,949 at 175,000, and a last published rung of $1,999 for 175,001-180,000 people. Above 180,000 the price is replaced by “Let’s chat”, though the card keeps printing a send allowance. The trial is 14 days and takes no card, and their FAQ states unlimited emails are not available during it. Three things the ladder does not advertise. Chat support is not included at the entry price: up to 5,000 people the line reads “Email support”, and “Chat and email support” only appears from $99 (6,000 people). “Unlimited email sends” stops being literally true at 30,001 people, where the bullet becomes “390,000 email sends” and every rung above it carries exactly twelve sends a month per person at the top of the bracket — 600,000 at 50,000 people, 2,160,000 at 180,000. And the card is not the same at every rung: free migration and personalized onboarding appear from 15,001 people ($249) and are absent on every rung below that. What is carried at every price is up to 50 workflows, unlimited sub-accounts, open API access, dynamic segments, onsite campaigns and the Drip MCP connection, which their FAQ describes as included at no extra cost. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Drip?
answers.a: The word “unlimited” quietly expires. At the prices most small shops pay, the send allowance really is uncapped. But the switch has an exact address: unlimited holds to 30,000 people, and from 30,001 the bullet becomes a hard number — 390,000 sends there, 600,000 at 50,000 people, twelve per contact per month. Drip never flags the switch. If you run a daily-deal or high-frequency list, do the arithmetic before you migrate: twelve sends per contact is generous for a monthly newsletter and tight for anything that mails several times a week. The second thing to price in is service. The card looks the same at every level, but two lines on it are not: you cannot talk to anyone in chat until $99/month, and free migration and personalized onboarding only appear from 15,001 people ($249). Below those thresholds it is email support and your own move, which is a real difference on the day a broken automation is sending to the wrong segment.

Dripify is genuinely best for sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session. Skip it if anyone whose LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or anyone tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that.

(re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page — note that dripify.io now redirects to dripify.com) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all six numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here, and the page now prints the daily quotas instead of calling them 'limited': Basic sends 20 connection requests, 30 messages, 10 Sales Navigator InMails and 100 profile views a day, against 75, 100+, 30 and 200+ on Pro and Advanced. Basic is also capped at one drip campaign; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dripify?
answers.a: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control sits on the $79 Advanced tier. It is the feature Dripify names as its best protection, and it adjusts your pace automatically. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.

Dripshipper is genuinely best for someone who wants a turnkey private-label coffee or tea brand on Shopify — their roasting and packaging, your label on the bag — and is content to stay inside one product category. Skip it if you want product breadth, fulfilment outside the US, or control over sourcing and packaging cost — this is a single-supplier pipeline and the higher tiers only add coaching.

(re-read 2026-09-17 on apps.shopify.com/dripshipper, listed as “Dripshipper: Coffee & Tea”) Starter $30 a month, Professional $99 and Elite $197, each with a 14-day free trial — all three unchanged since 19 August 2026. Starter is also sold annually at $240 a year, which is $20 a month for the same tier, and it is the only tier with a published annual rate. The listing does spell out what the steps buy: Starter carries unlimited orders, unlimited products, automatic order fulfilment, a dedicated support team and 1-click product add; Professional adds live monthly training, priority support and a dedicated success manager; Elite adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top of the subscription. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The listing now carries 159 reviews averaging 4.8, up from 142 averaging 4.7 on 19 August, distributed 130 / 14 / 7 / 4 / 4 from five down to one. Developer The Doughty Organization; the app launched 11 April 2018. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dripshipper?
answers.a: Read the ladder before you climb it. Starter already carries unlimited orders, unlimited products and automatic fulfilment — the whole product, in other words. Professional at $99 adds live monthly training, priority support and a success manager; Elite at $197 adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. You are buying people, not capability: nothing above Starter makes the coffee ship faster or cost less per bag. The annual rate is the move worth noticing in the other direction, since $240 a year against $30 a month is a third off the same tier. Beyond that the model is narrow by design — one product category, roasted and shipped from their own US facilities in 3-5 business days, with no route to source elsewhere or negotiate the per-order cost.

DropGenius is genuinely best for absolute beginners who want a pre-built Shopify dropshipping store scaffold in minutes and understand it's a starting point, not a business. Skip it if anyone uncomfortable with the documented billing complaints — or expecting an AI-generated store to sell by itself.

Re-verified 19 September 2026 on their own pricing page, unchanged since August. Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 14-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). The meter is catalogue size: Starter 25 unique products, Pro 250 unique plus 25 premium, Empire 10,000 and 10,000, Unicorn 25,000 and 25,000. The FAQ on their own homepage, re-read the same day, still quotes an older $39.99-$299.99 range plus a $1.99 one-time store-creation fee, so the marketing copy and the pricing table continue to disagree. Nothing anywhere on the pricing page mentions the Shopify subscription the generated store runs on. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with DropGenius?
answers.a: We have to be blunt here: the dominant theme in DropGenius’s public buyer reviews is unauthorised charges continuing after cancellation with no route to a refund, and some reviewers report never reaching a dashboard to cancel at all, with support emails bouncing back undeliverable. An AI-generated store in 30 seconds is also just a starting template — the product selection, marketing and margins remain entirely your problem. If you proceed: pay attention to cancellation mechanics from day one, screenshot everything, and treat the Renewal Radar as mandatory equipment.

Dryground AI is genuinely best for businesses that want AI solutions built for them as a services engagement rather than assembling tools themselves. Skip it if you're looking for self-serve software with published pricing — this is custom, quote-based consulting.

answers.q: How much does Dryground AI cost?
answers.a: (2026-08-17, read in a browser because the site renders client-side and a plain fetch returns only the title) There is no public pricing anywhere, and we checked before saying so. /pricing, /plans, /services, /about and /contact all return 404. The words “pricing”, “price” and “$” appear zero times on the homepage, and the navigation carries no pricing entry at all — it runs Solutions, Products, Verticals, Case Studies, Research, Book a Consultation. Tiers do exist with no numbers attached: the AI Velocity line is described as “six tiers from pilot to full enterprise transformation” on 90-day outcome cycles. Budget this as a consulting engagement scoped per project, not a subscription you can read off a page. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dryground AI?
answers.a: This is consulting, not a tool you log into: best when you want AI designed and built for you, not when you'd rather DIY with software. Read the headline numbers carefully too. The 20-50% efficiency and 10-20% revenue figures on their homepage carry the caption “2025 industry benchmarks”, so they describe the market rather than this firm's own results. And the case studies underneath them name no clients.

Dynasort is genuinely best for Shopify stores with large or fast-changing catalogues where product order is a merchandising decision — seasonal ranges, frequent stock-outs, wide margin spreads — and nobody who wants to re-order collections by hand every week.. Skip it if Small catalogues that a person can curate in an afternoon, stores where the order barely changes, and anyone not on Shopify. At $99 a month for the first paid tier, the sorting has to be earning its fee..

(re-read 15 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/dynasort) Four tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Demo is free for as long as you like: 2 collections sorted round the clock, 10 recipes drawn from 40+ signals, 2 managed collections that build themselves, 10,000 serves a month, 7 days of serving analytics and a re-sort every 60 minutes. The three paid cards are described by four capacity lines and three yes/no lines rather than by feature lists. Basic is $99 a month for 25 sorted collections, 10 managed collections, 20 recipes and a 30-minute processing schedule, with custom attributes, partner integration and product boost all switched off. Pro is $249 for 100 sorted collections, 25 managed, 25 recipes and a 20-minute schedule, and switches all three of those on. Enterprise is $499 for 1,000 sorted collections, 100 managed, 250 recipes and a 10-minute schedule. Every paid tier carries a 30-day free trial, which is long enough to actually measure the effect. One number the paid cards do not publish is a serve allowance: only the free Demo card names one, so if serves are what your traffic will consume, ask before you buy. This reading corrects an earlier one made on 14 September 2026, which recorded the Pro and Enterprise capacity blocks the other way round; on 15 September the ladder rises from Basic to Enterprise on every line. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Dynasort?
answers.a: Sorting driven by 40+ blended signals is powerful and opaque in the same breath: a recipe that ranks by margin, velocity and stock at once will sometimes bury a product you wanted seen, and there is real trial and error in getting the recipes to match how you actually merchandise. The jump from free to paid is steep at $99 a month, and it buys capacity without capability — custom attributes, partner integration and product boost all start at $249. The paid cards also publish no serve allowance, so the meter the free tier is capped on (10,000 serves a month) disappears from the page exactly where you start paying. And the evidence base is thin: 4.6 from 15 reviews, with fourteen fives and a single one-star and nothing in between. It is Shopify-only, so it is not an option if any part of your catalogue lives elsewhere.

answers.q: Is Easy Advanced Translations worth it?
answers.a: Easy Advanced Translations is genuinely best for small-to-mid Shopify stores that want affordable, full-store AI translation — including images and third-party-app text — and are comfortable bringing their own OpenAI or DeepSeek key for unlimited volume. Skip it if large catalogues that want predictable all-in pricing without managing API keys or quotas, merchants who require a proven app with a large review base, or enterprises needing SLA and support guarantees.

answers.q: How much does Easy Advanced Translations cost?
answers.a: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/advanced-translation) Four tiers, all monthly. Free installs at no cost and gives you unlimited AI if you bring your own OpenAI or DeepSeek key, or free built-in AI for a small quota (50 products, 50 metafields, 100 variants, 5 articles). Starter is $4.99, Basic $14.99 and Pro $29.99, each raising the free-AI quota (100, 400 and 800 products respectively) — or, again, unlimited if you supply your own key. The model's real pivot is that key: bring your own and you pay the AI provider's token costs directly for unlimited volume; rely on the built-in free AI and you are capped per tier. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Easy Advanced Translations?
answers.a: The 'free AI' is heavily quota-limited — 50 products on Free, up to 800 on Pro — so a genuinely multilingual catalogue pushes you either to a paid tier or to your own OpenAI/DeepSeek key, where you pay token costs separately on top of the subscription. Auto-translation of new or changed content is reserved for the higher plans. And the track record is thin: 5.0 stars but only nine reviews, the app launched in July 2025, and it carries no 'Built for Shopify' badge — cheap and promising, but unproven.

Easy Bundles is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price or volume bundles live in days rather than sprints, with bundle inventory syncing across Shopify and 3PLs and bundles that also sell through POS — and whose bundle revenue is still small enough to sit comfortably inside a published tier. Skip it if your bundle sales already run past $10,000 a month, because that is where the published ladder ends and the overage is not disclosed; or you need one straightforward fixed or mix-and-match bundle, which Shopify's own free first-party Bundles app already covers.

answers.q: How much does Easy Bundles cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is the part that matters: you are charged on bundle sales, not on orders, products or staff. The free plan is free to install and covers up to $500 of bundle sales a month. Essential is $29 a month or $299 a year and lifts that to $3,000; Growth is $49 or $499 a year up to $5,000; Scale is $99 or $999 a year up to $10,000. Annual billing saves 14% to 16% depending on the tier, and every paid tier has a 15-day free trial. Features climb the same ladder: free gives mix-and-match, fixed and volume bundles with templates and a custom or template design; Essential adds the single-step and multi-step bundle builders, landing-page templates, search and filtering, and multi-currency and multi-language support; Growth adds advanced discount logic, custom personalisation fields, add-ons, free gifts and subscription bundles; Scale adds AI-generated designs, advanced analytics, one-to-one onboarding and an account manager on Slack. Two things the block does not say are worth noting before you commit. It does not publish what happens when you pass $10,000 of bundle sales in a month, and it does not publish an overage rate; the plan table simply ends there and links out to see all pricing options. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Easy Bundles?
answers.a: The pricing is tied to the thing the app is supposed to grow. A revenue meter reads as generous at the bottom — $500 of bundle sales a month free is a real trial, not a crippled one — but it means every tier upgrade is triggered by the app working, and the published ladder stops at $10,000 a month with no stated overage. A store doing well on bundles has to ask what comes next rather than read it, and that is the wrong moment to be negotiating. Maturity is not the concern here: the app has been on the App Store since 15 September 2022 and carried 4.9 stars over 1,216 reviews on 4 September 2026 and 1,298 on 19 September, at the same average. The concern is where the money goes as you succeed. Two smaller things: the features most merchants picture when they think bundles are all paid: the guided single- and multi-step build-your-own-box builders sit on Essential at $29, and subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts on Growth at $49 — none of them on the free plan, and the recent reviews that praise the app most warmly also praise the support team by name, which is a compliment to people rather than to a product that never needs them.

EasyDMARC is genuinely best for anyone who sends email from their own domain and has not yet got DMARC to enforcement — the reporting is the part that makes that safe rather than guesswork. Skip it if you have one domain, send little email, and are willing to read raw XML reports yourself, because the free tier plus patience covers the same ground.

(re-read 2026-09-17 on easydmarc.com/pricing, which now redirects to /pricing/easydmarc/businesses; every amount and every plan limit below is unchanged since 26 August 2026) Plus is 44.99 a month, or 35.99 billed annually, for 2 domains, three months of report history and one invited user. Premium is 89.99, or 71.99 annually, for 4 domains, a year of history, TLS reports, EasySPF, alert management and unlimited invited users, with a dedicated CS manager on the yearly plan. Enterprise is quoted and carries three years of history, unlimited users and domains, managed services, a dedicated DMARC engineer, SSO, audit logs, reputation monitoring and API access. Annual billing is marked as 20% off plus bonus features, and MSPs and MSSPs get a separate tab with their own ladder. The number that actually sets your tier is monthly email volume: each card has its own selector, running 100,000 to 1,000,000 messages on Plus and up to 5,000,000 on Premium, so the headline is the floor for the smallest bracket. Prices are exclusive of taxes and taxes may be applied at checkout. On the currency: read from the Netherlands the page prints these as euro amounts and read over a US connection as the identical dollar figures — €44.99 there is $44.99 here, so the symbol changes and the number does not. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with EasyDMARC?
answers.a: You are buying domains and history, not features. Plus covers two domains; a company with a main domain, a marketing subdomain and a legacy domain it forgot about is already over. And the history window is the part that bites later: three months on Plus means that when you are investigating a spoofing campaign that started in the spring, the reports are gone. The page also does not say what happens when you pass the message volume. Their own FAQ does: you lose access to your reports and dashboard rather than being billed for overage. That is a harsher failure mode than an overage charge, and worth knowing before you size the plan.

EcomXray is genuinely best for small and mid-size Shopify merchants who want cost price, gross margin, clean net unit sales and restock advice inside the admin instead of exporting to a spreadsheet. Skip it if you sell across several channels and need cross-platform inventory sync, you already run a dedicated inventory or MRP system, or you want an app with a public track record longer than a month.

(re-verified 8 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/ecomxray; unchanged since 21 August 2026) Two tiers. Free: product analytics inside Shopify, cost price and gross margin, net units sold over 30, 90 and 365 days with refunds, cancellations and test orders excluded, 30-day restock recommendations and a revenue rank for top products. Pro is $29 a month, with a 14-day free trial. It carries everything in Free plus editing product name, description and price in place, SEO fields with automatic URL redirects, publishing to channels and managing collections. There is also a full product activity log, and a Chrome extension showing stock value and editing on your storefront product pages. There is no annual rate on the listing. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer aMemory ApS, Ellegardvej 36, Sonderborg, Denmark; the app launched 20 July 2026 and, seven weeks on, still carries a 0.0 rating from zero reviews. The listing's own summary bullets put in-place editing and the audit log among the app's five headline features without marking them Pro, which is the one place the listing reads as more generous than the plan table it sits above. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with EcomXray?
answers.a:
The split between the two tiers is unusually clean, and worth seeing clearly: everything this app is described as doing, the margins, the net units, the restock advice, is free. The $29 buys editing, not insight. If you are happy making changes in the Shopify admin you already have, the free plan is the whole product and the paid one is a convenience layer over it.

The track record is the real caveat, and it has not moved. The app launched on 20 July 2026 and still had no reviews at all when we checked on 8 September, seven weeks later. Nothing is known about how it behaves at scale, how it handles a catalogue in the tens of thousands, or how quickly support answers, because nobody has said so in public.

And its numbers are only as good as your cost prices. Gross margin comes out of Shopify's own cost-per-item field, so if that field is empty or stale across your catalogue, the margin column is decoration. Fill the cost prices in first, then judge the app.

ElevateForward is genuinely best for scaling companies where growth is outpacing alignment — leadership lacks execution visibility and strategic initiatives keep stalling halfway. Skip it if you already have solid execution discipline, or you just want a simple task or project tool — this is a strategy-and-alignment layer, not a to-do list.

(re-verified 2026-08-21, read on their own pricing page) The prices are published, despite the consultative first impression, and the report figures have not moved since our 12 August reading. An Elevate Insight Report is $500, a bundle of three is $1,350 at a 10% discount, and the Elevate Studio tiers render at $250, $500 and $750 a month. Those three are Elevate Strategy, Elevate Execution and Business Enablement, the last still marked coming soon. A report is scoped to one focus area you choose, delivered within five business days of submission, with up to two rounds of feedback-based adjustments and a review consultation included. Treat the monthly figures as provisional: each price sits in a pair of spans whose second value reads $1,500 per report. For the three monthly tiers those second values are $8, $16 and $149. The page carries no visible label for either state, so which figure a given buyer is shown cannot be settled from the markup. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ElevateForward?
answers.a: It's a strategy-to-execution layer, not a task app or a dashboard — so the value only lands if leadership actually adopts the framework. 'Operational alignment platform' is also a fuzzy and crowded label, so press them on the concrete deliverables (the diagnostics, KPI blueprints and execution plans) before committing.

ElevenLabs is genuinely best for creators, developers and product teams that want the most realistic AI voices available — voiceovers, audiobooks, dubbing, conversational agents and a well-documented API. Skip it if you generate hours of long-form audio on a tight budget (credit math punishes volume — flat-hour tools or the TTS built into your video editor may be enough), or you need acted emotional range only a human voice actor delivers.

(re-verified 3 Sep 2026 on elevenlabs.io/pricing) Every rate held for a second month. Free $0 with 10k credits/mo; Starter $6/mo (30k credits, commercial license); Creator $22/mo — first month 50% off at $11 — with ~121k credits. Then Pro $99/mo (~600k credits, 44.1kHz PCM), Scale $299/mo (~1.8M credits, 3 workspace seats) and Business $990/mo (~6M credits, 10 seats). Extra usage runs roughly $0.36 down to $0.17 per additional minute depending on tier.

Two things the plan cards do not put next to the price. Annual billing is sold as ten months rather than twelve — the FAQ writes it out as annual price = monthly price × 10, which works out to $5 for Starter, $18.33 for Creator, $82.50 for Pro, $249.17 for Scale and $825 for Business. And credits are shared across every product, so speech, music, dubbing and video all draw down the same monthly balance. On a paid plan unused credits roll over for up to two months — the balance caps at three times the monthly quota — but downgrading or cancelling forfeits whatever is left at the end of the cycle, and the free plan has no rollover at all. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ElevenLabs?
answers.a: Credits are the meter and retakes are the tax — you are charged per generation request, and a regeneration is only free while the content and settings are unchanged, so real usage lands well above the calculator estimate. And read the free-tier fine print: $0 gets you 10k credits to play with, but no commercial license — anything you publish commercially needs at least the $6 Starter. Voice realism genuinely leads the market; niche names and jargon can still need manual retakes, so run your hardest paragraph through the free tier before subscribing.

EmailListVerify is genuinely best for teams cleaning real sending lists before campaigns — bulk verification at volume rates, with credits that never expire. Skip it if you verify tiny batches occasionally (the entry rate is the worst per-check price), or you mainly want prospecting — the finder burns credits five at a time.

(re-verified 2026-08-31 on emaillistverify.com/pricing, read from the page's own JSON-LD offer data) Pay-as-you-go credits that never expire: 1,000 for $5 ($0.005/check), 5,000 for $17 ($0.0034), 10,000 for $27 ($0.0027), 25,000 for $54 ($0.00216), 50,000 for $98 ($0.00196), 100,000 for $186 ($0.00186). Monthly subscription at the same volumes: 5,000 for $16 ($0.0032), 10,000 for $25 ($0.0025), 25,000 for $49 ($0.00196), 50,000 for $89 ($0.00178), 100,000 for $168 ($0.00168), 250,000 for $346. The subscription discount runs from 5.9% at 5,000 credits to 9.7% at 100,000, so it grows with volume rather than being a flat rate. API included at every level; the email finder costs 5 credits per address found at medium-or-higher confidence. Free tools: email validator, inbox-placement test, DMARC/SPF generators. Note that /llms.txt and /pricing.md both serve the 404 page under an HTTP 200, so the JSON-LD on the pricing page is the machine-readable source here. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with EmailListVerify?
answers.a: The $5 entry pack is the most expensive way to buy: $0.005 per check versus $0.00196 at the 50k tier — a 2.5x spread that rewards guessing your volume upfront. And the email finder quietly consumes 5 credits per found address, so a 1,000-credit pack finds 200 emails, not 1,000.

Emergent is genuinely best for founders, PMs and builders who want to turn a prompt into a working full-stack web app or MVP fast, without writing the code themselves. Skip it if you need a hardened, security-audited production system with no human review, or your usage would burn through credits faster than the value returns.

(re-verified 2026-08-31 on emergent.sh/pricing) Free $0 (10 credits/mo); Standard $20/mo, or $17/mo billed annually, for 100 credits (the page states a $36 annual saving, 15%); Pro $200/mo, or $167/mo billed annually, for 750 credits (a $396 saving, 16.5%). Above Pro the ladder is quote-only: Business and Enterprise both show 'Custom' and route to Book a demo, adding RBAC, SSO, shared workspaces and co-editing (Business) and user-level credit limits, audit logs, self-hosted database support, VPC deployment and priority SLAs (Enterprise). The $300/mo Team tier with 1,250 shared credits is no longer offered. Credits meter the work -- simple changes 1-2, medium features 5-10, complex refactors 10-20+ -- which comes from earlier research and was not re-confirmed on the 31 Aug read of the pricing page. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Emergent?
answers.a: The real cost is credit consumption, not the flat sticker -- a genuinely complex app burns 10-20+ credits per big change, so serious builders move up tiers faster than the price list implies. Now do the division, because Emergent's own pricing page doesn't. Standard is $20 for 100 credits, so 20 cents a credit. Pro is $200 for 750, which is 26.7 cents. Moving up a tier makes every unit of work more expensive, not less: Pro costs 33% more per credit than Standard, and annual billing keeps the gap (17 cents against 22.3). That is the opposite of the volume discount the ladder looks like -- you are buying a 1M-token context window, custom agents and priority support, not cheaper work. And there is nowhere cheap to go above it: Business and Enterprise are both quote-only, so passing 750 credits a month means a sales call rather than a bigger plan. Check what your month actually needs before you upgrade; one Standard month plus purchased extra credits may beat one Pro month. AI-generated code still needs a human eye: review it for security, correctness and maintainability before anything touches real users.

Employment Hero is genuinely best for Australian and New Zealand employers who want HR and payroll from one vendor and will genuinely use both, where the per-employee rate beats separate systems. Skip it if you are budgeting in US dollars — the page is Australian, in AUD excluding GST, with no US equivalent — or you only need one of the modules, since each is sold separately and priced as though you are buying the platform.

answers.q: How much does Employment Hero cost?
answers.a: (2026-08-28, read on their own pricing page at employmenthero.com/pricing/) EVERY PRICE ON THAT PAGE IS AUD EXCLUDING GST — the page states it in its own disclaimer. It is the Australian page; separate pages exist for the UK, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia and Canada, and there is no US one. Sold as separate modules rather than one plan. Recruitment: a free ATS tier at A$0 that includes 50 complimentary AI video interviews as a one-off trial, then A$199, A$359 and A$639 a month for 50, 100 and 200 interviews. The disclaimer also names a 300-interview plan but publishes no price for it. Those are annual-billing rates — the disclaimer gives A$2,388 a year for the 50-interview plan at a 20% discount, against A$249 a month on monthly billing. Interview credits reset monthly, unused credits do not roll over, and overage is billed automatically with no hard cap. No HR or payroll subscription is required for Recruitment. HR Essentials A$10 per employee per month, HR Engage A$14; HR Elite and Employment Unlimited are quote-only. There is no standalone payroll tier on the page any more: payroll sits inside Employment Unlimited, and Managed Payroll is an add-on at A$20 per employee per month with a A$400 monthly minimum. Other add-ons, each per employee per month with a stated monthly minimum: Chat A$2 (min A$20), Rostering and Time and Attendance A$4 (A$40), HR Advisory A$14 (A$280), Learning 10-course bundle A$8 (A$80), LMS Plus A$17 (A$170), EAP Standard A$8 (A$80), EAP Premium A$10 (A$100). A minimum of 10 Users applies, billed on the higher of the users named in your agreement or the active users. Every price on the page carries an asterisk. CHANGED SINCE 1 AUG 2026: the standalone Payroll module at $10 per employee recorded then is no longer on the page, and the currency was not recorded as AUD. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Employment Hero?
answers.a: There is no such thing as the Employment Hero price, and the first thing to fix is the currency: the pricing page is the Australian one, its disclaimer says every figure is AUD excluding GST, and there is no US page. Then the structure. HR, recruitment, chat and payroll are separate subscriptions, most of them per employee, with a stated minimum of ten users underneath — so a six-person company is billed for ten. Payroll no longer carries its own price at all: it is inside the quote-only Employment Unlimited tier, or an A$20-a-head add-on with a A$400 floor. And the recruitment tiers meter AI video interviews rather than people, with credits that reset monthly, do not roll over, and overage billed automatically with no hard cap.

EngageBay is genuinely best for small teams that want CRM, email marketing, helpdesk and live chat in one affordable suite — the free tier is a genuine trial-for-life, and it undercuts HubSpot hard at small scale. Skip it if your contact list is big (per-tier caps push you up fast) or you need best-of-breed depth in one area — all-in-one means good-at-everything, not best-at-anything.

(price re-verified 2026-09-18 on engagebay.com/pricing) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 250 contacts with email marketing, CRM, helpdesk and live chat, and the plan card adds that it is free for teams of up to 15 members. All-in-One suite per user/month on monthly billing: Basic $14.99 (500 contacts), Growth $64.99 (5,000 contacts, marketing automation), Pro $119.99 (10,000 contacts). The three rates have not moved since our August reading, but the Pro contact allowance has: the plan card now says 10,000 contacts where we recorded 50,000. A note beside it confirms that ceiling in the vendor's own words — “The Pro plan includes up to 10,000 contacts” — and directs anyone who needs more to schedule a call about expanding the limit. The published ceiling is a fifth of what it was, and everything above it is now a sales conversation rather than a price.

Read the toggle before you read the number. The page defaults to a biennial ‘15% off’ display (Basic $12.74, Growth $55.24, Pro $101.99) with a yearly ‘8% off’ step in between ($13.79, $59.79, $110.39), so the friendly figure in the headline assumes you prepay two years. Single bays (Marketing or CRM & Sales) start at $11.04/user/mo on that same biennial display. One oddity worth knowing before you quote a number back to anyone: the page’s own title tag still advertises “Free to $99/Month”, and $99 is not a rate in any of the three billing columns. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with EngageBay?
answers.a: The meter is contacts AND seats at once: prices are per user, and each tier caps contacts — Basic’s 500 contacts fills fast, and the Growth jump is steep ($15 → $65 per user). The advertised ‘starts at $12.74’ assumes biennial prepay — two years upfront for the friendly number. Real automation only starts at Growth.

Envoy is genuinely best for companies with a real office and a front desk problem — visitor compliance, desk booking and deliveries in one system, where the per-location price is spread over enough employees to be worth it. Skip it if you are remote-first or have one small office — a visitor log and a shared calendar cover the same ground, and the per-location floor is priced for buildings rather than teams.

(2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page and their platform page) Five products, each metered differently and all billed annually. Visitors: Basic free, Premium $362 per location per month, Enterprise quote-only. Emergency Notifications $2 per user per month. Reservations $5 per bookable resource per month. Screens $12 per device per month. Deliveries $250 per delivery location per month. All five amounts are unchanged since 1 August 2026, and the pricing page now publishes the Visitors Premium rate in JSON-LD with a billingDuration of one year. The line 'Price excludes platform fee' appears exactly four times, on Emergency Notifications, Reservations, Screens and Deliveries — not on the Visitors card. The platform page supplies the shape of that fee without its number: the platform is required to use Envoy products, it is 'priced as a flat annual fee', and it has its own Premium and Enterprise tiers that you choose before adding modules. That page also lists visitor management as one of the modules. Invoicing by ACH is offered only on Enterprise or with three or more Premium Yearly locations. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Envoy?
answers.a: None of the prices on that page is a price you can budget from. Four of the five product cards are followed by 'Price excludes platform fee', and the platform page says outright that the platform is required to use Envoy products and is charged as a flat annual fee — with its own Premium and Enterprise tiers to pick first, and no number published anywhere on the site. That is the first thing to ask for. The second is how the meters stack, because they are all in different units: per location, per user, per bookable resource, per device, per delivery location. An office with forty bookable desks, six screens and one delivery point is paying on four clocks at once: $362 for the location, $200 for the desks, $250 for deliveries, and $180 for the screens rather than the $72 the card implies, because Envoy's own llms.txt sets a 15-device minimum that the pricing page never mentions. That is $992 a month before the platform fee, and before emergency notifications, which the same file bills at $2 a head across your entire employee directory rather than across the people who use them. Price the combination you actually want, not the product you came for.

Essential Loyalty is genuinely best for Shopify stores with genuine repeat business that want a loyalty programme priced on the orders it influences rather than on total volume — and stores selling in person too, since POS support arrives at $10 and the free tier carries VIP tiers and referrals. Skip it if your customers buy once and rarely return, because a loyalty programme has nothing to work with and the free tier shows you that within a month; or you need API work from the start, since integrations are 'on request' and only on the $79 tier.

answers.q: How much does Essential Loyalty cost?
answers.a: (re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/essential-loyalty-rewards-program) Four tiers, every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026, and the meter is still the whole decision: it counts loyalty-influenced orders — repeat sales and referrals — rather than every order your store takes, which the plan text states outright. Free covers up to 250 of those and is unusually complete: the point program, VIP tiers, a referral program, twelve-plus ways to earn points, product, cart, popup and account placements, built-in email notifications with Klaviyo, and discount, gift, shipping and credit rewards. Starter is $10 a month for up to 500, adding a dedicated loyalty landing page, full customisation, Shopify Flow, POS support for in-store loyalty and 24/7 human support. Essential is $24 for up to 1,500, adding loyalty status on the customer orders and profile pages and points in product cards. Growth is $79 for unlimited loyalty orders, with API integrations on request, white-glove onboarding and priority support. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps. The listing works with Checkout, Customer accounts, Shopify POS, Shopify Flow, Shopify Admin, Judge.me, Klaviyo, Omnisend, Point of Sale and Shopify's native store credit, and names twenty interface languages while a feature bullet on the same page claims 180+ — the vendor's own FAQ (essential-apps.com/loyalty, read 19 Sep 2026) reconciles those two: the twenty are the languages the app's own interface ships in, and the 180+ covers translating the storefront-facing text into any language you sell in. Nothing on the listing says what happens when a plan's order cap is passed; the same vendor FAQ does: you are upgraded in place to the next tier, there is no per-order overage fee, and $79 a month is the ceiling — unlimited loyalty orders, everything included. So the worst case for a store that outgrows Free is the $79 tier, not a surprise bill. The review record has moved: 482 reviews at 5.0, up from 438 in August, distributed 473 five-star, 8 four-star, none at three or two, and 1 one-star. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Essential Loyalty?
answers.a:
Two things to read closely before you pay. The meter is honest — loyalty-influenced orders, not all orders — and that is genuinely in your favour, but it also means you cannot work out your tier from your order count. A store doing 3,000 orders a month with little repeat business may sit on Free; one doing 800 with a loyal base may not. Measure your repeat and referral orders for a month before you choose.

The second is an oddity on the listing itself. The free plan advertises an 'Advanced loyalty point program' while Starter at $10 advertises a 'Free loyalty point program', which read literally means the paid tier offers less on that line. It is almost certainly a labelling slip rather than a real downgrade, but it is the kind of line worth confirming with support before you upgrade for it.

Evey Events is genuinely best for Shopify stores that sell tickets alongside products and want attendees, orders and customer data in one place instead of reconciling a separate ticketing platform against the shop. Skip it if ticketing is your actual business rather than a sideline -- a dedicated platform gives you seating, promoter tools and box-office features that a Shopify app is not trying to match -- or you sell so few tickets that any per-ticket fee is friction you don't need.

answers.q: How much does Evey Events cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 8 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/event-tickets; every figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) Four tiers, and every one of them charges twice: a monthly fee and a fee per ticket processed. Lite is free to install and takes $1.00 per ticket. Growth is $19 a month and $0.75. Standard, the tier the store marks Popular, is $49 and $0.50. Professional is $189 and $0.25. The paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. One feature line changes that arithmetic and sits above the crossover: Collect fees on every ticket sold appears on Standard and Professional only, so passing the per-ticket cost to attendees is itself a paid feature. Beyond that, feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations, the multi-vendor dashboard and priority support live. The app is published by Staytuned and carries a 4.4 rating from 320 reviews. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Evey Events?
answers.a: Nobody gets caught by the monthly fee here; they get caught by the per-ticket one. On Lite the app is free to install and then takes a dollar off every ticket you sell, which is invisible until you sell volume and then is the largest line on the invoice. Work out your monthly ticket count before you install anything, because that single number picks your plan: under 76 stay on Lite, 76 to 120 move to Growth, 120 to 560 move to Standard, above that Professional. Getting this wrong is not a small error -- at 300 tickets a month the gap between the best and worst choice is about $65 every month.

Evolve is genuinely best for enterprises and scale-ups that need structured, measurable training rolled out across hundreds of employees — branded academies, AI-generated courses, job-skill simulations and assessment in one platform. Skip it if you're a small team that just needs a course builder or a lightweight LMS — the enterprise machinery and the procurement process are more than the job requires.

(re-verified 2026-08-31 on evolveplatform.ai) No public price list -- there is no /pricing page and the call to action across the site is 'Book an intro'. The platform is modular by design and the quote is built from which modules you contract and how many seats: Evolve LMS, Course Generate, Evolve Studio course builder, Assessment Center, Knowledge base and Simulations -- six independent but connected products, not four. Budget for an enterprise-tier commitment. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Evolve?
answers.a: It's built for large organizations — the site lists 100+ deployed enterprises like Carlsberg and Danone — and the sales-led, quote-only motion reflects that: there is no self-serve tier to trial quietly, so smaller teams can't just kick the tires before procurement gets involved.

Expandi is genuinely best for sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn (and email) outreach at scale who want smart sending limits, warm-up and multi-account management. Skip it if you send occasional connection requests (LinkedIn's native tools suffice), or you're uneasy about automation against LinkedIn's terms of service.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) 7-day free trial, no free plan. Business is $99 per month month-to-month; paying a year up front takes 20% off, which their own page describes as two months free, so roughly $79 a month equivalent. Pricing is per seat and Expandi states that the discount grows with the number of seats you buy, so a multi-seat agency quote is not simply the seat price multiplied. Higher tiers add role and permission management and centralised billing. Taxes vary by country and are added on top. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Expandi?
answers.a: There is no free tier and no cheap entry — Expandi starts at $99 a month per seat, and the friendlier $79 assumes annual commitment. It's also LinkedIn automation, which sits in a grey zone against LinkedIn's own terms: powerful for outreach, but a platform-risk you own.

ExpertEx is genuinely best for online stores that need a steady stream of product photos and short video ads and would otherwise pay a studio or a freelancer per shoot -- the e-commerce studio pushes results straight to the live store on Ultra and above. Skip it if you need one hero shoot a year (a photographer is cheaper and better), your products are hard to render convincingly, or you want a free tier to evaluate on -- generating always costs credits.

(read 2026-08-22 in a live browser on expertex.ai/pricing -- plain fetches return an empty page, so this is the first reading we have of the real ladder) There are four credit tiers, monthly against yearly with two months free. Starter is $10 or $7 for 1,000 credits, and Premium $30 or $20 for 3,000. Ultra is $75 or $45 for 7,500, and Professional $250 or $149 for 25,000. Paid three-day trials sit alongside them at $1 for Premium (1,000 credits), $2 for Ultra (2,000) and $5 for Professional (5,000), with full access and cancellation before renewal. The page's own calculator prices the work at 25 credits per product photo, 250 per short video ad and 2,000 per full reel, and reels require Ultra or above. Credits roll over month to month while the subscription is active and are lost on cancellation; you can top up on demand or upgrade mid-month, with upgrades prorated immediately and downgrades taking effect at the next billing date. Prompt Builder is free to use before subscribing. One label on that page understates its own offer. The monthly/yearly toggle is sold as two months free, which would be a sixth off, but the yearly rates sit far below that: $7 against $10 is 30% off, $20 against $30 is a third, and $45 against $75 and $149 against $250 are both about 40%. Counted in months rather than percentages, a year costs 8.4 months of Starter, 8 of Premium and 7.2 of Ultra and Professional — so the saving runs from three and a half to nearly five months, not two, and on this page the annual commitment is worth more than the vendor claims for it. ExpertEx told us through PartnerStack on 11 September 2026 that this label and the card-versus-calculator gap are both with their website team as a priority, so expect these figures to move. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ExpertEx?
answers.a: The plan cards and the calculator on the same page do not agree, and the gap is large enough to pick the wrong tier. Starter is sold as 65 product photos and 10 short video ads a month on 1,000 credits; at the calculator's own rates that work costs 4,125 credits, four times the allowance. The card numbers only reconcile if each is taken alone, and at roughly 15 credits a photo and 100 a video. The same 4.2x mismatch repeats on every tier, so it is a systematic difference rather than a typo. Ask which rate governs before you buy, because the calculator will steer you to a plan two rungs above what the card implies. The second thing to price is that this is a credit product with no free tier. Prompt Builder is free; generating is not. And the cheap trials ($1, $2, $5) are three days rather than a month -- enough to test output quality, not enough to test a monthly workflow. And the fundamental one: AI product photography is judged on whether the output is publishable without a retoucher. Run your own worst product through the trial -- a reflective bottle, a garment with fine texture -- rather than the kind of thing that looks good in every demo.

ExpertSender is genuinely best for e-commerce stores from 10,000+ monthly visitors (the vendor's own stated ICP) and high-volume senders doing 100k+ emails a month, who want email, SMS, push and on-site messaging on one unified customer data platform with a managed, dedicated-partner setup. Skip it if your store is still building traffic or you want self-serve, pay-as-you-grow email marketing — a Klaviyo-class tool is the lighter, cheaper start.

(re-verified 10 September 2026 on expertsender.com — on the home page, because the pricing page is gone: /pricing, /pricing-plans/ and /en/pricing/ all return 404) (2026) Quote-based with a documented floor: their home page says 'Start growing your eCommerce business from $450 USD', scaling with volume and channels, and they explicitly target stores with at least 30,000 unique monthly visits. No free tier — a free consultation is the entry point. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ExpertSender?
answers.a: The $450/mo floor and the 30k-monthly-visits target make this an established-store tool, not a starter one: below that traffic the platform can't pay for itself, and there is no self-serve plan to test it cheaply first.

Expertise AI is genuinely best for B2B software teams (especially HubSpot-first) that want a live AI sales agent to qualify website visitors, hold buying conversations and route leads to reps. Skip it if you're not running B2B demand-gen through a CRM like HubSpot, or a simpler support chatbot covers your needs at a fraction of the Business-tier cost.

answers.q: How much does Expertise AI cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 2026-09-03; the ladder itself is unchanged since our 15 August read, but the Business conversation allowance is not) The ladder was rebuilt since our July read: the Growth tier at $500/mo is gone, and Business is now $2,000/mo instead of $1,250. What is left is three tiers. Free Preview costs nothing and covers 1 AI agent, 10 conversations and up to 50 training materials. Business is $2,000/mo on both monthly and yearly billing. It adds conversations for websites with up to 50,000 monthly visitors — the table labels this "Limited", and unlimited conversations now sit on Enterprise — up to 500 training materials, visitor intelligence, proactive live chat in HubSpot, 2-way HubSpot sync, 3 playbooks, a webhook and implementation by their team. Its Voice AI carries 300 voice minutes a month, and $0.25 per minute after that. Enterprise is on quote, adding extra agents, Salesforce and Marketo, SSO, active engagement, API access and dedicated hosting. Two side products are priced separately on the same page: the booking system is free or $30/mo ($24/mo billed yearly), and the Expertise Assistant is free, $50/mo per user ($40 billed yearly) or custom. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Expertise AI?
answers.a: The honest catch is that there is no middle any more. When we re-read the pricing page on 15 August 2026, the $500/mo Growth tier had been withdrawn. So the ladder runs straight from a Free Preview capped at 10 conversations to Business at $2,000/mo. And everything that makes the product genuinely powerful — visitor intelligence that de-anonymizes traffic, the 2-way HubSpot sync, Voice AI — sits on that paid tier. There is no way to grow into it gradually. It's also a RAG agent, so it's only as good as the docs you feed it: give it thin content and it can answer buyers confidently but wrong. Strong for HubSpot-centric B2B teams; less compelling if you're not in that ecosystem.

Fast Bundle is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want every bundle and upsell format from one app — mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks, AI frequently-bought-together — priced against what those offers actually earn rather than a flat fee, and who are comfortable with an app that Shopify delisted for two weeks in July 2026 and then restored. Skip it if you need one bundle type only, where a single-purpose app costs less than the metered ladder; you sell in person, since Shopify POS support sits behind the $299 Enterprise tier; or an app in your path to checkout having been pulled and deactivated once, however well handled, is a risk you cannot carry.

answers.q: How much does Fast Bundle cost?
answers.a:
(read 2026-08-24 on apps.shopify.com/fast-bundle-product-bundles, listed as “FBP | Fast Bundle & Upsell App”, and on fastbundle.co/pricing) The meter here is not your catalogue, your traffic or your seats — it is the revenue your bundles themselves generate. The listing is free to install and shows four tiers. Development stores are free to install and free to run. Standard (1K) is $19 a month or $180 a year and covers up to $1,000 of monthly bundle sales. Standard (3K) is $49 a month or $468 a year for up to $3,000. Standard (10K) is $139 a month or $1,380 a year for up to $10,000.
