The add-ons are where a growing team pays more: extra Social Sets are $11.25 a month each, extra users $3.75 a month each, and extra AI credits $3.75 a month per 100 credits. Starter covers casual scheduling; Growth adds the inbox, approvals and longer analytics; Scale is aimed at enterprise-level analytics without an enterprise contract. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Later?
answers.a: The Starter caps are where the price really lives: 30 posts per profile and 3 months of analytics run out fast for an active brand, pushing real users toward Growth — so compare at the tier you'll actually need, not the entry price. Later's visual-first planning (born from Instagram) is still its strength; if your world is link-in-bio commerce and grids, that focus earns its seat.

Leadfeeder is genuinely best for B2B teams with real website traffic and a sales team that will actually work the list — the free tier is enough to find out whether your traffic contains anyone worth calling. Skip it if your traffic is mostly consumer or very low volume, because company identification needs business networks to match against and thin traffic produces a thin list.

(read 2026-08-26 on leadfeeder.com/pricing over a US connection) Lite is free forever with a 14-day full trial, seven days of visitor history and the last 100 companies a month. Discover starts at $79 a month, Activate at $369 and Scale at $599, all billed annually, which the page marks as 30% off. Worth knowing: the page carries both currencies with the same figures — $79 for an American is €79 for a European, not a converted amount — so the euro price is the more expensive of the two. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Leadfeeder?
answers.a: The words doing the work are 'starting at'. What actually sets your price is how many companies you identify a month, and the page shows that allowance as 'Tiered' with no figures at any level. So €79 is the floor of the smallest bucket, and you cannot tell from the page which bucket your traffic puts you in. Get that table before you talk price. Two other things: month-to-month costs 43% more than annual on the same plan (€113 against €79), and Scale is annual-only, so the tier most growing teams land on cannot be tried for a month.

Leadpages is genuinely best for small businesses building landing pages and simple funnels who want unmetered traffic — no per-visitor anxiety, unlike metered rivals. Skip it if you need deep A/B experimentation or enterprise features — the Conversion tier jumps to $299/mo fast.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 against Leadpages' own machine-readable pricing file, which still carries the same 2026-07-10 update date it had in August; USD) Two lines, six paid plans, no free plan, and a 7-day free trial that requires a credit card and converts unless you cancel. Publishing plans: Starter $10/mo or $8 billed annually ($96 a year), 5 pages, 1 site, no third-party integrations; Pro $29/mo or $23 annually ($276), 25 pages, 1 blog, API access; Business $49/mo or $39 annually ($468), 50 pages, 2 sites. None of those three include A/B testing. Optimization plans add testing and personalisation: Grow $99/mo or $79 annually ($948), unlimited pages, 4 sites, manual two-way A/B testing, dynamic text replacement and lead enrichment; Optimize $199/mo or $159 annually ($1,908), 6 sites, up to four variants, Smart Traffic, heatmaps and auto-personalisation; Scale $399/mo or $319 annually ($3,828), 10 sites, auto-optimisation, cross-page learning, role-based access and 10 seats. Annual billing is 20% off across the board. No plan has a traffic cap. Add-ons: $20 a month per extra seat or extra custom domain, $40 per extra client workspace on Scale, and AI credit top-ups from $2.50 for 2,000 credits down to $0.60 per thousand at the largest pack. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Leadpages?
answers.a: It's the value pick, not the optimisation pick — if you're spending big on ads, Unbounce's Smart Traffic and Instapage's 1:1 personalisation go deeper.

LearnWorlds is genuinely best for course creators and training businesses that want a branded school with interactive video, assessments, certificates and a built-in checkout. Skip it if you sell only occasional courses (a lighter or transaction-fee-only platform may cost less) or you just need to host a few videos behind a paywall.

(re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page, which now carries the browser title New Pricing 2026) Starter $29/mo (or $24 annually) but with a $5 fee per paid enrollment — still the single most important number in this ladder; Pro Trainer $99/mo, or $79 billed annually, with no enrollment fee; Learning Center $299/mo, or $249 annually; Corporate quoted. The High Volume tier we recorded in August is gone: the ladder is now Starter, Pro Trainer, Learning Center and Corporate. Annual billing saves 20% and the trial is 30 days. Limits published alongside: 1,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 monthly active learners, 1 / 5 / 25 admins, 300 / 500 / 1,000 AI credits a month, email support 24/5 on Starter against 24/7 above it, and a 99.90% uptime commitment (99.95% on Corporate). All prices exclude VAT, which is added for EU customers unless a valid EU VAT number is given, and your payment gateway (Stripe at about 2.9% + $0.30) charges on top regardless of tier. A branded mobile app is still a separate add-on, but the page now lists it as having multiple price options and prints no amount, so the roughly $149/mo we carried in August is no longer confirmable. Two reading notes: the page opens by asking which of four goals brings you there and recommends a plan on that basis — the figures above were read with the branded-academy goal selected — and the plan cards print their numbers with no currency symbol at all, the only dollar signs on the page sitting on the $5 enrollment fee and the Stripe example. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with LearnWorlds?
answers.a: The detail most people miss is Starter's $5-per-paid-enrollment fee — at any real sales volume it quietly makes Starter more expensive than the flat Pro Trainer plan, so the "cheap" tier often isn't. Starter also runs on a single admin seat and 24/5 email support against 24/7 above it, and the branded mobile app is a separate add-on whose price the pricing page no longer states. Price it against your expected enrollment volume, not the sticker.

Leavo is genuinely best for teams that want straightforward time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing. Skip it if you need a permanent free plan (this is a 30-day trial), or you're a tiny team where a shared spreadsheet already covers hours.

(price re-verified 2026-08-17 against leavo.com) (2026) 30-day free trial with unlimited members (a trial, not a permanent free plan). Professional $2.49/user/mo billed yearly (about $448/yr for 15 users) adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15). Priced per user, annual billing. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Leavo?
answers.a: The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat — every employee you track adds to the bill, with no volume break shown. And the “free” is a 30-day trial, not a permanent free tier: budget for the paid plan from day 31.

LettrLabs is genuinely best for local businesses and e-commerce brands using robotically handwritten mail (~$0.49/piece incl. postage) to stand out where email gets ignored. Skip it if your audience or offer doesn't justify ~$0.49 per contact — direct mail only pays at decent response rates and order values.

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Postage is included in every per-piece rate. Three published tiers: Starter is free and pay-as-you-go; Premium is $399/month billed annually or $449 month-to-month; Enterprise is custom-priced. On Starter, postcards are $0.76 (4x6), $0.79 (6x9), $0.85 (6x11) and $1.15 (11x18 tri-fold), and handwritten pieces are $1.56 (handwritten envelope with printed letter), $1.66 (handwritten postcard), $2.86 (card and envelope) and $3.11 (bi-fold card and envelope). Premium's card shows $0.54-$0.88 for postcards and $0.85-$1.71 for handwritten, Enterprise's $0.56-$0.88 and $0.81-$1.52 — but both are labelled 'as low as with spend commitment', so those floors need volume as well as the subscription. Handwritten insert media (a card with no envelope, shipped inside a package rather than mailed) is listed from $0.49 and is not offered on Starter. New accounts get $30 in free credit. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with LettrLabs?
answers.a: Direct mail only pays off with a tight list and a real offer — it's a leverage channel, not a cheap thing to test blindly.

Lindy.ai is genuinely best for teams that live in Slack and want one shared teammate that sits in their meetings, runs scheduled routines and drafts replies inside the tools they already use. Skip it if you want flat, predictable automation costs across a large team — Lindy charges for every seat that touches it and the credits expire each cycle, so you pay for people whether or not they used their allowance.

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own pricing page; every amount, credit allowance and FAQ rule unchanged since 4 September) Now sold per user, and the credit allowance is published again. Plus is $29.99/mo per user (3k credits per user per month), Pro $99.99/mo per user (15k credits, 5x Plus) and Max $199.99/mo per user (35k credits, ~12x Plus). Enterprise is quote-only. Every seat's credits pool into one workspace balance, refresh each billing cycle and do not roll over; the page sizes work as 2-250 credits for an everyday ask, 250-1,000 for deep work and 1,000-2,500 for a big build. Anyone who uses Lindy takes a paid seat, including colleagues who only @mention it in Slack — those who join that way get a 7-day free trial first, direct signups are billed straight away. All four tiers connect up to 5 inboxes, and computer use, model selection and MCP support are no longer tier-gated. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Lindy.ai?
answers.a: Cost tracks headcount rather than output: every colleague who so much as @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a paid seat, and a seat you remove runs to the end of the cycle with no mid-cycle proration. Credits are published now, but as ranges: an everyday ask is 2-250, a big build 1,000-2,500. So a month is still an estimate. And when the shared pool runs dry there is no top-up — Lindy pauses credit-using actions until the reset, unless an admin moves the workspace to a bigger plan.

Livestorm is genuinely best for teams running a predictable programme of webinars to a known audience size, where buying a year of attendance up front is cheaper than a per-seat platform. Skip it if your webinar schedule is irregular or experimental, because paying a year ahead for attendance you cannot forecast is the wrong shape; a per-month platform is safer while you find out what works.

(re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) There is still no plan price. Pro is sold as attendee credits, bought as a yearly pack up front, with sessions up to 4 hours and unlimited team members; Enterprise is quote-only with sessions up to 12 hours. The rate depends on the currency you pick on the page, and the two are not conversions of each other: €2.50 per attendee in euros, $3.00 in dollars. Their own definition, worth reading twice because it decides your bill: one credit is spent for each unique participant, per session, over a 12-month period. Someone attending two different sessions costs 2 credits; the same person joining live and later watching the replay of that session counts once. Registrants who never show up cost nothing, and your own team members never consume credits. New since August: the FAQ now says what happens when the pack runs out — you get alerts as you approach the limit, and once you reach it new attendees cannot join a session until you move to a higher yearly tier. What still is not answered anywhere on the page is what becomes of credits you have not used at the twelve-month mark. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Livestorm?
answers.a: This is a bet on attendance that you place a year in advance. You buy credits up front — €2.50 each in euros, $3.00 in dollars, set separately rather than converted — and a credit is spent per unique participant per session, so a four-part series to the same 200 people is 800 credits, not 200, which is €2,000. A webinar that does better than expected runs you out, and the page is now clear about what that means: new attendees cannot join until you buy a higher tier. The page publishes the per-attendee rate but never a total. Before you commit, count sessions times expected attendees for the whole year, and ask what happens to unused credits at the twelve-month mark, because the page does not say.

Lucrovox is genuinely best for local service businesses — HVAC, plumbing, roofing, med spas — losing revenue to missed calls who want a 24/7 AI receptionist that books jobs straight into Google Calendar, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan or Jobber. Skip it if your call volume is tiny (100 Starter calls is the whole point) or your callers expect a human — ring their live demo line first and judge the voice yourself.

(re-verified 2026-09-15 on lucrovox.com/#pricing and lucrovox.com/lucrochat, both read in a real browser with the pages fully loaded) The phone agent has three published tiers and the plan table is back on the page: Starter $199 a month for up to 100 AI-handled calls, Pro $499 for up to 500 calls with CRM integration and advanced lead qualification, Enterprise $999 for up to 2,000 calls with white-label branding and multi-location support. Higher volume is quote-only. Starter and Pro carry a 14-day trial, Enterprise 30 days. On our previous reading, 17 August, the pricing page opened with a missed-call ROI calculator and the tier list could not be retrieved at all; it is worth knowing that the plan table on this site comes and goes, and that the calculator's outputs ($500 average job value producing $750 a week and $39,000 a year of lost revenue) are illustrations rather than prices.

LucroChat, the website chat product from the same vendor, sits on lucrovox.com/lucrochat with its own table metered on monthly conversations rather than calls: Starter $29 for up to 1,000 conversations on one website, Growth $59 for up to 3,000 conversations on up to three websites, Professional $199 for up to 10,000 conversations on unlimited websites, each with a 14-day trial and no card required. Its own FAQ agrees, describing pricing as starting at $29 a month for 1,000 conversations. One number on that page does not agree with the rest: the ROI calculator above the table reports its result “Based on Growth plan ($99/mo)” while the table prices Growth at $59. Read the plan table, not the calculator. LucroVox's partnerships team told us on 15 September 2026 that LucroChat had moved to $49, $99 and $249 and that the calculator now matches the table; we read both pages that same day and neither had happened. The table still prints $29, $59 and $199, the FAQ still says pricing starts at $29, and the calculator still reports $99. Those higher figures may well be where the product is heading, so if checkout quotes you $49, that is the vendor running ahead of its own pricing page. We publish what the page shows. Two products, two meters, one domain — price them separately. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Lucrovox?
answers.a:
The meter is AI-handled calls: Starter’s 100 calls a month is roughly three a day, so a genuinely busy shop outgrows it quickly — and the steps are steep ($199 → $499 → $999). The ‘callers can’t tell it’s AI’ claim is the vendor’s own: they offer a live demo number, so test that before you commit.

One more thing to read carefully on the sibling product's page. LucroChat's ROI calculator reports its return “Based on Growth plan ($99/mo)”, while the plan table on the same page prices Growth at $59 a month (first read 24 August 2026, unchanged when we re-read it on 15 September 2026, and still there after the vendor told us that day it had been fixed). The $99 is the higher of the two, so nobody is being lured with a low number, but a page that quotes two different prices for one plan is a page whose figures you check at checkout rather than take on trust.

MRPeasy is genuinely best for small manufacturers, wholesalers and distributors who want dependable production planning and inventory control without a heavy ERP or a dedicated IT team. Skip it if you're a large or highly complex manufacturer, or you need deep customisation, advanced analytics and forecasting — MRPeasy is built for simplicity, not complexity.

(re-verified 2026-08-24 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, per user per month: Starter $49, Professional $69, Enterprise $99 and Unlimited $149. Only Unlimited carries a two-user minimum. We had that minimum down as applying to every tier; MRPeasy's partnerships team wrote on 24 August 2026 that it applies to Unlimited alone, and their pricing page prints minimum 2 users under that one plan and nowhere else. Those four rates are what you pay month to month. Pay for a year and one month is free, which the vendor works out as effective rates of Starter $44.92, Professional $63.25, Enterprise $90.75 and Unlimited $136.58; the monthly and annual toggle did not change a single figure on the page when we clicked it in either direction, so those four are the vendor's arithmetic and not our own reading. Mind the currency, because it is not a conversion: the same pricing page served our European browser 39, 59, 79 and 125 euro per user per month on 24 August 2026, with the user bundle at 69 euro, which is about a fifth under the dollar list. Check what your own checkout quotes before you budget. All plans include unlimited orders and items. The scaling rule is unusual and worth understanding. The first 10 users pay the tier rate, and from the 11th user you add flat $79 bundles of 10 users. So 11 to 20 users is the base price plus $79, 21 to 30 is plus $158, 31 to 40 plus $237, and so on. Expert support is a separate purchase: one hour a month at $199 billed quarterly ($229 for a single month), two hours at $299 ($349 single) and four hours at $499 ($579 single), with training at $150 an hour. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MRPeasy?
answers.a: Paying ~$50 per user just so a shop-floor worker can clock in and out feels steep when they'll touch a fraction of the features. Customisation and reporting are limited, and there's no advanced demand forecasting or AI — so larger or highly complex manufacturers will outgrow it.

MX AI is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want seasonal or ambient audio on the storefront, want a say in how the player looks and behaves, and would rather use the app's royalty-free tracks than sort out the licensing for a song of their own. Skip it if you only need a single uploaded MP3 looping in the background, because RoarTheme's free app covers exactly that; or your store competes on load speed and accessibility, where unexpected audio is a liability; or you have never measured whether sound moves your conversion rate, because the listing offers no evidence that it does.

answers.q: How much does MX AI cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-09-16 on apps.shopify.com/custom-background-music) Two plans, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free with unlimited access to every feature, but the listing restricts it to development and partner stores and says payment is activated on upgrade. A live store runs on the Monthly Plan: $2.99 a month, or $25.12 a year paid up front, which the listing labels a 30% saving. Both are billed in USD every 30 days, and the paid plan opens with a 7-day free trial. The pricing block lists nothing above the Monthly Plan — no traffic tier, no play-count tier, no second paid step — so $2.99 is the whole app whether the storefront sees ten visitors a day or ten thousand. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MX AI?
answers.a:
The strongest argument against paying for this is one App Store search away. RT: Background Music Player, from RoarTheme, does the core job — upload a media file, it plays in the background — and the listing prices it at Free, full stop. It sits at 4.8 stars over 72 reviews against this app's 4.8 over 66, and it has been on the store since 5 February 2021. What the $2.99 buys over free is real but narrow: control over the player's colour, size, position, volume, loop and autoplay, sources beyond an uploaded file, and a set of AI-generated royalty-free seasonal tracks. If all you want is one MP3 looping on the homepage, you are paying for controls you will set once and never open again.

Two smaller things worth knowing before you install. The "Free plan available" badge on the listing is for development and partner stores only — on a live store there is no free tier, so read that badge as a 7-day trial. And the pitch that background music "can enhance your interaction with customers and improve conversion rate & sales" arrives with no evidence: no study, no store data, no test. Autoplay is not entirely yours to command either, because browsers block audio that starts without a user gesture, so the autoplay switch takes effect once the shopper has interacted with the page rather than on load. At $2.99 the cost of finding out whether sound helps your store is small — but find out, rather than assume.

ManyChat is genuinely best for creators and brands running comment-to-DM and multi-channel (Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp) marketing funnels — its killer feature works reliably. Skip it if you want true conversational AI support, or you have a fast-growing contact list — the flow logic is rigid and contact-based billing climbs fast.

Read on their own pricing page, 6 September 2026. Free: $0, 25 active contacts, 2 channels, 1 user. Paid tiers are banded by active contacts and priced two ways — month to month, or the lower rate if you pay for the year. Essential $17/mo or $14/mo billed annually ($168, 18% off), 250 contacts, 2 channels, 2 users. Pro $39/mo or $29 annually ($348, 25% off), 2,500 contacts, 3 channels, 3 users. Business $99/mo or $69 annually ($828, 30% off), 7,500 contacts, unlimited channels, 5 users. Advanced $199/mo or $139 annually ($1,668, 30% off), 25,000 contacts, unlimited channels, 10 users. Going over your allowance does not stop your automations: each extra active contact is billed at $0.10, $0.05, $0.025 and $0.004 on monthly billing, or $0.082, $0.038, $0.018 and $0.0028 on annual. Essential and Pro carry a 14-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ManyChat?
answers.a: Flows are button-and-script based, not natural language — type something unexpected and the bot falls back. The AI add-on is closer to keyword-matching than real conversational AI, billing scales with contacts (a viral Reel can spike your bill), and support is email-only and slow.

MarketerHire is genuinely best for companies that need a vetted senior marketer (growth, paid ads, email, more) matched quickly, without the time and risk of a full-time hire. Skip it if you need cheap, task-level help (a freelance marketplace fits) or you can't yet brief and direct a senior marketer toward a clear goal.

(read 2026-09-01 on marketerhire.com/pricing) No rates are published. The page says there is "no plan to pick and no retainer to guess at" and that after one call you are matched with a marketer "at a budget you agreed to". The terms it does publish: a free consultation with no obligation, a match within 24-48 hours, a two-week refundable trial, and month-to-month billing you can cancel at any time. The retainer tiers reported elsewhere at roughly $5,000, $10,000 and $15,000 a month, and hourly rates of about $100-$200 with 10-20 hour weekly minimums, do not come from MarketerHire and are not on its pricing page; treat them as a historical anchor for sizing the conversation, not as a quote. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MarketerHire?
answers.a: This is expert freelance talent at expert prices — the value is speed and vetting (their pricing page promises a match within 24-48 hours, against a months-long hire), but it is a real five-figure-a-month commitment for serious engagements, not a cheap gig marketplace. Because it's talent, not software, outcomes depend on the individual and how well you brief them; the rematch guarantee helps, but you still own the strategy. Right when a great marketer would pay for themselves, wrong as a budget stopgap.

Marketing 360 is genuinely best for small businesses that want one vendor handling website, CRM, ads, email and reputation with real humans to help, and prefer done-for-you over DIY. Skip it if you're comfortable assembling your own stack (it'll cost far less), or you need transparent, predictable pricing you can budget upfront.

Quote-based, and deliberately so (verified 6 September 2026 on their own site). Marketing 360 does publish a page called How Plans & Pricing Work, and it carries no prices at all: the only numbers on it are the annual-revenue bands — $0-$250K, $250K-$1M, $1M+ — in the six-question form that stands between you and a quote. Reported core software runs around $395-$419/mo with marketing consultations, but design and custom website work are separate and can run from $2,000 into five figures, and managed ad services layer on top. This review carries no pricing screenshot rather than a placeholder. Get a full written quote. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Marketing 360?
answers.a: Two honest cautions. Pricing is hidden and quote-driven, and reviewers repeatedly flag that the real cost — software plus design plus managed services — climbs well above the headline, sometimes with recurring fees for features you don't use. And it's an all-in-one "we'll do it for you" model, which is great if you want a single vendor and a human team, but it can mean less flexibility and more lock-in than assembling best-of-breed tools. Ask exactly what's included before signing.

Meeri is genuinely best for small Shopify stores that want a cart-recovery channel which costs almost nothing and takes no commission on what it recovers — and that are willing to treat the free 300 notifications a month as a measurement of their own push opt-in rate before paying anything. Skip it if you need the recovered contacts anywhere other than the browser that opted in, you run recovery through Klaviyo, Postscript or another stack you want this to feed, or you cannot get the usage-based charge on Pro quoted as a rate before you enable it.

(read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/meeripush-push-notifications, listed as “Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery”, and on meeritech.com; both re-read 2026-09-19 with no amount changed) Two plans, and the free one is a real plan rather than a demo. Basic is free to install and covers up to 300 push notifications a month, which the listing itself translates as roughly 100 recovered carts. It carries unlimited subscribers and segmentation, the abandoned-cart recovery campaign, scheduled promotional campaigns, AI-generated campaign content, intelligent delivery timing and basic email support, and it takes no commission on recovered revenue. Pro is $4.99 a month with a 7-day free trial and adds up to 3,000 push notification impressions, unlimited campaigns and automations and premium support. All charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The plan text says Pro “upgrades as you grow” and that additional usage-based charges are billed every 30 days, without printing a rate anywhere on the listing. The vendor’s own site sells the same two tiers at the same prices, calling Basic free forever and Pro’s allowance 3,000 notification impressions a month, and it does not print a usage rate either. The app is English-only, works with Shopify Admin and sits in Shopify’s abandoned-cart category. Developer MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ, Dubai; the app launched on 23 February 2024 and carried 9 App Store reviews in August 2026 and 11 on 19 September 2026. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Meeri?
answers.a:
Start with the numbers on the vendor’s own homepage, because they do not match the App Store. Read on 19 September 2026, meeritech.com still says “5.0 on Shopify App Store”, “100% five-star reviews” and “5.0 average — 8 verified reviews on Shopify” — word for word what it said on 23 August. The listing that same morning shows 4.7 from 11 reviews: ten at five stars and one at one star. So the vendor’s figure is what you get by leaving the single bad review out, and its review count has stood still while the real one moved. Nothing about the app is settled by that, but a marketing page that rounds its own rating up by dropping the worst review, and then does not refresh it for a month, is a useful thing to know before you weigh the rest of the page.

The review base is thin whichever number you use. Eleven reviews on an app that launched in February 2024, and the three the listing shows first come from one store in the United Kingdom and two in Pakistan, one of which had been using the app for seven days when it wrote. That is not evidence of anything wrong; it is very little evidence of anything at all, and it cannot tell you how this behaves on a store like yours.

Then there is the channel itself, which is the real decision. Web push needs a browser-level subscription, and the app’s own pitch is that no email or phone number is required to get one. That cuts both ways: the list is easier to build and worthless off the browser that built it. You cannot export those subscribers into an email tool, you cannot reach them anywhere else, and your recovery ceiling is set by opt-in rate rather than by the app. Measure the opt-in rate first — 300 free notifications a month is enough to find out — because it decides everything the paid plan can do for you.

One more limit worth reading before you install: the listing names English as the only language, and Shopify Admin as the only integration. There is no Klaviyo, no email platform, no SMS tool on that line, so this sits beside your existing stack rather than inside it.

MeetGeek is genuinely best for people who run many external meetings and need a searchable record — the summaries earn their keep when you cannot remember which of four calls a detail came from. Skip it if your meetings are internal and few, because the note-taking in your existing conferencing tool covers that; also skip Pro if you record daily, since twenty hours will not last.

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on meetgeek.ai/pricing; amounts unchanged since 2026-09-04) The page loads on annual billing, so the figures it shows first are the annual ones; both terms are given here. Basic is free with 3 hours of transcription a month. Pro $9.99 per user per month billed annually, $15.99 billed monthly, with 20 hours of transcription. Business $17 per user per month billed annually, $27 billed monthly, with unlimited transcription and team multi-meeting analytics. Enterprise is quote-only: SSO, SCIM, org-wide settings, on-premise storage, custom retention, custom voice agents and a dedicated account manager. Extra transcription hours are $0.50 each. Downloads and exports and admin user management start on Pro, not Business; API and MCP access are listed on the free Basic plan. A 14-day free trial runs on Pro. Two limits sit beside the hours and neither is in the plan blurb. A separate cap ends the individual meeting: two hours on Basic and Pro, three on Business, four on Enterprise. And your recordings expire on a schedule — transcripts are kept three months on Basic, a year on Pro and indefinitely above that, audio one month, six months and twelve, with video stored only from Business. On the same page, the annual badge claims up to 40% off, the actual step from monthly to annual is about 37% on both paid tiers, and a line under the heading offers 30% off for startups, non-profits and education on request. Data can be stored in the EU or the US on every plan, the page claims SOC 2, GDPR and HIPAA compliance and states that customer data is not used to train external models, but recording-consent notifications with approval tracking start on Business. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MeetGeek?
answers.a: The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month, which is about an hour a working day. That sounds generous until you count the meetings you would actually record — a sales rep on four calls a day passes it in the first week, and the overage is $0.50 an hour. Unlimited transcription is the real reason to be on Business at $17, so treat Pro as a plan for occasional recording rather than a cheaper version of the same thing. Worth checking before you buy: consent. A recorder that joins every meeting changes what people say in them, and that is a policy decision rather than a pricing one.

Melio is genuinely best for small businesses that want to pay bills by bank transfer or card and get paid, starting free with no subscription. Skip it if you already run AP through robust accounting software with bill-pay built in — a second tool adds little.

(re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. Core is $25/mo, or $20 billed annually, with 20 free ACH a month; Boost $55/mo, or $44 annually, with 50 free ACH; Unlimited $80/mo. The detail our earlier note missed: every paid plan adds $10 a month per additional user, or $8 on annual billing, so a three-person finance team on Core is $45 a month rather than $25. Card payments carry a flat 2.9% fee and check and wire payments have their own charges. There is a 30-day trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Melio?
answers.a: The free plan is genuinely useful for low bill volume, but the value case narrows as you scale into paid tiers — and the 2.9% card fee only makes sense when you're deliberately floating cash on a card for rewards or timing.

MigrationPro is genuinely best for merchants moving an existing store into Shopify who want products, customers, orders and — critically — URLs and 301 redirects preserved, who are willing to pay the $29 add-on that carries those redirects on the self-service route, and who would rather pay once than subscribe to a tool they will use for a week. Skip it if you are migrating away from Shopify or between two other platforms, since this only imports into Shopify; or you want one firm number before you start, because the price still depends on your record counts and on which of the priced add-ons your source platform turns out to need.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/migrationpro-shopify-migration-app and migrationpro.io/pricing/) The App Store listing still prints no number at all: one plan, free to install, with the line that pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate and no subscription fees, and a note that all charges are billed in USD. The numbers live on the vendor's own pricing page, which quotes on your product, customer and order counts. Two routes are sold there, both one-time payments rather than subscriptions. The Automated app plan, where you run the migration yourself, starts at $29 based on store size. The Done-for-you plan, where their team handles mapping, testing and go-live with a dedicated specialist, starts at $300 with every add-on included. Both carry a 30-day guarantee, need no credit card, and begin with a free demo of up to 10 products, customers and orders. What has changed since 23 August is the add-on table: each one now carries a price. 301 redirects, order ID preservation, categories mapped to automated collections and content images are $29 each; customer groups to tags and default stock quantity are $19 each; spam customer detection, active products only and tax-inclusive pricing are $39 each; merging short and long descriptions, generating variants from options and resetting the target store are free. The homepage puts a typical store at $49 to $299 on actual record counts, and the FAQ says most stores finish in one to three hours, with 10,000+ products taking longer but still completing the same day. The app is English-only, migrates from WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, BigCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Shopware, Etsy, Amazon, CSV and Excel among others, and covers products, customers, orders, collections, images, URLs and 301 redirects, with Smart Sync to re-import data changed during the run. Developer Migrationpro, LLC, Dover, Delaware; the app launched 10 May 2022 and now carries 186 reviews averaging 5.0 — 181 five-star, 4 four-star and, for the first time in our record, one at a single star. Note that migrationpro.io/pricing without the trailing slash now answers 308. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MigrationPro?
answers.a:
The listing tells you nothing about what this costs. “Free to install. Additional charges may apply”, and a single plan block saying pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate. To learn a number you have to leave the App Store for the vendor's calculator, and the first number you find there — $29 — is the floor for the smallest store on the self-service route, not the price for yours. Their own homepage says a typical store lands between $49 and $299. Run the calculator before you form an opinion about value.

The add-on structure used to be the unknowable part, and as of 18 September 2026 it is not: the pricing page lists every add-on with a price, from $19 to $39, and marks all of them included on the managed plan. That is a real improvement in what a buyer can read before committing. It also makes the self-service route look less like $29 — the 301 redirects add-on, which is the one thing a migrating store can least afford to get wrong, is a $29 extra on a $29 migration.

The marketing still runs ahead of the evidence. The pricing page says “Trusted by 250,000+ stores”, the homepage uses the same figure for migrations, and the FAQ says 250,000+ migrations over 13 years — one number doing three different jobs. The same page claims 5.0 from 170+ verified App Store reviews while the listing itself shows 186, of which 181 are five-star, 4 are four-star and one is a single star. The reviews are genuinely good; weigh them rather than the banner.

One practical limit sits in the reviews rather than the marketing. The FAQ says most stores finish in one to three hours and that 10,000+ products may take longer but still complete the same day, while a merchant migrating a very large catalogue in July 2026 wrote plainly that large volumes take a very long time and that the team helped speed it up. If you are moving tens of thousands of records, let the free demo and your own record count decide which of those two you are, not the FAQ.

MindStudio is genuinely best for operators and teams that want to build and deploy real AI agents and workflows visually, across many models, without engineering time. Skip it if you need one simple chatbot (simpler tools exist) or deeply custom logic that ends up easier in actual code.

(prices re-verified 2026-09-18 on mindstudio.ai/pricing) The subscription is a floor, not the bill: every tier reads “+ usage”, so model calls are charged on top. Free is $0/month plus usage and caps you at one agent and 1,000 runs a month. Individual is $20/month plus usage, or $16/month plus usage billed yearly, a stated 20% saving, and lifts both caps to unlimited agents and unlimited runs. Business is quote-based. Because the metered part is uncapped by the plan, the tier you pick says little about what you will actually pay — the run volume does.

The metered half is more governable than that makes it sound, and the page is specific about it. A run is one execution of an agent, triggered manually or automatically. MindStudio states it does not mark up model cost — its FAQ says you pay exactly the same price as bringing your own API keys from the providers — and that you can set per-agent and total spend limits and track run cost per agent. All tiers reach 200+ models through its Service Router without API keys of your own, with bring-your-own keys as an option, and hitting a run limit triggers a notification with the choice of upgrading or buying additional runs rather than a hard stop mid-month. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with MindStudio?
answers.a: The no-markup model pass-through is genuinely fair — but it also means your real cost is subscription PLUS model spend, and an agent that loops or processes big documents burns provider credits invisibly until you set limits. The honest build discipline: start every agent with usage caps, and treat 'no-code' as no-code for the plumbing — the logic design and prompt quality are still entirely on you.

Miro is genuinely best for teams that think visually — brainstorms, flowcharts, retros, workshops and planning on an infinite shared canvas with strong templates and facilitation tools. Skip it if your work is mostly documents or task tracking (a doc or PM tool fits better) or most of your company would only ever need to view, not edit.

(price re-verified 2026-09-02 on miro.com/pricing/) Free plan: 3 editable boards workspace-wide, unlimited members, AI published as a limited trial rather than a credit count. Starter $8/member/mo and Business $20/member/mo, both billed yearly; Enterprise custom priced from 30 members. The yearly toggle is marked save 20%, which puts the monthly rates at $10 and $25. AI credits are published per plan: 25 per member per month on Starter, 50 on Business. MCP calls are a separate published meter: 500 a day on Starter, 2,000 on Business. Currency note: the served page defaults to USD, but rendered from a Dutch connection the same numerals appear as €8 and €20, so the symbol follows the visitor region. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Miro?
answers.a: Per-member pricing charges for every member added to the workspace, so an org-wide rollout multiplies at full headcount — and the free plan's 3-board cap is workspace-wide, not per person, so real teams outgrow it in days. Model who truly needs to edit before you buy seats.

Mktg.ai is genuinely best for marketing teams with real media spend across channels who want an always-on AI analyst — unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over their own data. It layers on top of your existing platforms rather than replacing them, with the vendor putting real-time data in week one and full onboarding at two to three weeks. Skip it if your ad spend is modest (the value scales with budget waste, and yours is small), or you want transparent self-serve pricing before a sales call.

No public pricing (re-verified 6 September 2026): mktg.ai/pricing still returns 404 and the navigation carries no pricing item, so every route ends at 'Book a Demo'. The tiers themselves are no longer secret, though — the FAQ names Growth and Enterprise above the entry level and describes what they add (dedicated onboarding on both; a dedicated customer success manager, SLA-backed response times and quarterly business reviews on top of that). Email support is on every plan; custom integrations and EU data residency are Enterprise-only, with US data centres the default. The machine-readable llms.txt is Wix boilerplate advertising an MCP endpoint and carries no price either. Rates require a sales conversation. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Mktg.ai?
answers.a: Two honest cautions. First, the price is still hidden — a 404 where the pricing page should be, and no pricing item in the navigation — which for a tool that promises spend transparency is an irony worth noticing, and the FAQ makes it sharper: its own introduction says it covers what the platform costs, and then no answer in it names a figure. What the FAQ does publish is the tier names, Growth and Enterprise, and the fact that EU data residency is Enterprise-only. Second, the ROI story is the vendor's own: the homepage tile assumes a $5M budget and puts a 3% efficiency gain at $150K alongside $100K of reallocated spend, which is 2% of the same budget. Ask for verified case numbers at your spend level on the demo call.

Modelize is genuinely best for Shopify fashion, jewellery and homeware sellers who need consistent on-model, lifestyle or flat-lay imagery across a large catalogue and cannot justify a photographer per drop. Skip it if you need art direction a preset cannot express, photography of the actual physical item in its real texture, or a vendor with a long public track record — this app is four months old.

(re-read 2026-09-17 on apps.shopify.com/modelize, listed as “Modelize: AI Product Photos”) Free plan available, then Starter $19, Pro $49 and Enterprise $99 a month — the three paid rates are unchanged since 19 August 2026. The free tier was raised from 3 to 10 AI images, still one-time rather than per month, with built-in presets and models at standard 2K. Starter covers 100 images a month with 3 AI custom presets and 3 custom models, standard 2K and email support. Pro at $49 covers 250 images, 10 custom presets and 10 custom models, resolution up to 4K and priority support. Enterprise at $99 includes 500 images with $0.20 per additional image, unlimited custom presets and models, maximum 4K and dedicated support. The annual option is gone: on modelize.studio/pricing, read the same day, all three paid tiers are labelled “Billed month to month” and the page carries no yearly rate and no two-months-free wording anywhere, where in August it sold Free, Starter and Pro annually. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.9 from 25 App Store reviews (24 at five stars, one at three), up from 5.0 from 13 reviews on 19 August. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 20 April 2026 and carries Shopify’s “Built for Shopify” badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Modelize?
answers.a: The economics are flat: at roughly $0.19 to $0.20 an image on every tier, moving up the ladder buys resolution, custom presets and support, never a cheaper image. Read it that way and the pricing is honest; read it as a volume discount and you will overbuy. Two other things deserve a clear head. The output quality rides on Google's Gemini image models rather than on anything Modelize owns, so results and consistency can shift when Google ships a new version, and that is outside the vendor's control as much as yours. And the app is genuinely new — launched 20 April 2026, 25 reviews on 17 September 2026 — so the 4.9 average is a small sample, not a track record. Finally, an on-model photo generated by AI shows a person who does not exist; check what your ad platforms and marketplaces require you to disclose before you build a catalogue on it.

Modge is genuinely best for desk-bound remote or hybrid teams of a few to a few hundred people who want time tracking, app classification, shift adherence, leave and payroll-ready timesheets in one seat priced between $4 and $7 a month, and who are happy to run screenshots as an opt-in rather than a default. Skip it if you need SSO or a SOC 2 report today, both are marked soon; your people work in the field, since the agent is desktop-only with no mobile or GPS on the page; or your security team will not accept a compliance claim without a document.

(read 2026-09-03 on modge.com/pricing, both billing toggles and the comparison table) Per-seat plans with a full-feature 14-day trial and no card. Basic is $5 per seat per month billed monthly or $4 billed annually: app and URL tracking with AI productivity classification, workforce dashboards, automatic time tracking with optional screenshots, timesheets, approvals and payroll exports, invoice creation, email and chat support. Pro is $7 monthly or $5.50 annually and adds shifts, scheduling and adherence, leave, breaks and overtime, client billing through Stripe, on-demand screenshots with 12-month retention, and custom roles, teams and project budgets. Premium, marked popular, is $9 monthly or $7 annually and adds automated project and task time tracking, workflow analysis, suspicious-activity and mouse-jiggler detection, burnout-risk and profitability insights, contract signing, 24-month screenshot retention and a dedicated account manager. Enterprise is custom, on annual billing with volume pricing, custom retention, customised onboarding and an SLA. Two add-ons are priced per seat: More Screenshots at $2 a month lifts capture from 18 to 60 an hour on Basic, Pro and Premium; Extended Data Retention at $2 a month or $1.67 annually keeps records for six years on every tier. The comparison table lists screenshot retention as 3 months on Basic, 12 on Pro and 24 on Premium, and marks SSO (SAML 2.0), SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 as soon. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Modge?
answers.a: The numbers on Modge's own pages do not agree with each other. The homepage says trusted by 1,000+ teams, the affiliate page says 1,800+ teams, the pricing page says over 2,000 users; the pricing page also shows three star ratings, 4.6 from 1,500 reviews, 4.8 from 2,000 and 4.2 from 800, without naming a single platform they come from. None of that touches the product, but it is the kind of copy a buyer should not repeat in a business case. What does touch the product is the comparison table: SSO through SAML 2.0, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 are all marked soon, and HIPAA compliant appears with no report behind it. If your security review needs a document today, there is none to hand over. The desktop agent is macOS and Windows only, and the pricing page mentions no mobile app or GPS, so field teams are out of scope.

Momence is genuinely best for class-based businesses — studios, gyms, salons, schools — that want scheduling, memberships, payments and marketing in one system with a member app. Skip it if you only need a simple calendar-booking link (a lightweight scheduler is cheaper) or you won't accept platform fees on top of card processing.

(re-verified 2026-09-06 on the vendor's own pricing page) The tiers render in plain text again: Basic $0/mo with a 5% Momence fee on every transaction plus 4% passed to the client; Pro $60/mo with your fee halved to 2.5%; Custom $199/mo with no Momence fee, unlimited add-ons and dedicated support. Basic and Pro carry an identical exclusion list in their card tooltips — no add-ons, no phone number, no inbox, no retail products, no reporting or insights, no staff members, no locations — so Pro buys a lower commission and nothing else. Card processing is charged separately and published per country: US 3.9% + $0.30 online, 3.7% + $0.05 in person, 1.8% ACH; UK 2.5% + 20p, 2.4% + 10p, 2% + 20p BACS; Australia 2.75% + A$0.30, 2.75% + A$0.10, 2% + A$0.30 BECS; Canada 3.9% + C$0.30, 3.7% + C$0.05, 2% + C$0.40. One change since our August readings: on 15 and 19 August 2026 these cards were rendered and then covered by a lead form and a blur filter, so the figures existed in the page but were unreadable until you handed over your details. That gate is gone. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Momence?
answers.a: The 'free' plan is the most expensive one once you have real volume: a 5% commission on every sale overtakes Pro's $60 flat fee around $29k a year in processed revenue, and Pro in turn loses to the $199 Custom plan above about $67k a year. Pick your tier by volume, not by sticker — and note what the middle tier does not include. The tooltip on the Pro card lists the same exclusions as the free plan: no add-ons, no phone number, no inbox, no retail products, no reporting or insights, no staff members, no locations. Pro halves your commission and adds no features.

Moosend is genuinely best for small businesses and marketers who want affordable email marketing and automation with a low entry price, a real free trial and a clean drag-and-drop builder. Skip it if you run a very large list where per-subscriber pricing adds up, or you only need transactional/API email — a developer-focused sender is cheaper for that.

(re-verified 2026-09-06) A 30-day free trial with no credit card. Pro is priced by list size across 21 steps from 500 to 1,000,000 contacts, quoted monthly, biannually (sold as 15% off) or annually (sold as 20% off). At 500 contacts it is $9 monthly, $8 biannual and $7 annual. The ladder is not monotonic per contact: paid annually, 8,000 contacts is $51 a month against $70 at 10,000, 75,000 is $333 against $499 at 100,000, and 500,000 is $2,317 against $2,829 at 600,000 — three steps up the slider that cost more per head than the step below them. The discounts round to whole dollars and so land short at small sizes: at 1,000 contacts $16 monthly becomes $14 biannual (12.5% off) and $13 annual (18.75% off). Instead of a subscription you can buy email credits outright with no expiry: 350,000 for $350, 500,000 for $500, 750,000 for $750 and 1,000,000 for $1,000 — a flat $0.001 per email with no volume discount. Above Pro the page shows Moosend+ (a custom plan assembled from add-ons: dedicated IPs, transactional emails, audience discovery, custom dashboards, hosted files, extra team members, SSO and SAML) and Enterprise, both quote-only. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Moosend?
answers.a: The friendly $7-9 headline is the entry rate at the smallest list size (500 contacts), and the ladder above it does not fall smoothly: paid annually, 8,000 contacts costs $51 a month while 10,000 costs $70, so a list of 9,000 sits on the wrong side of the sharpest jump on the slider. The same reversal repeats at 100,000 and at 600,000. Read the comparison table before you assume Pro covers you, too: transactional emails, SSO and SAML, a dedicated IP, hosted files and an account manager are Moosend+ add-ons or Enterprise rather than included.

Motive is genuinely best for fleets large enough that ELD compliance and dash-cam evidence are already costing you money, and who will negotiate a quote rather than accept the first one. Skip it if you run a handful of vehicles and want to know the price before a sales call — that is not available here, and competitors in this category do publish per-vehicle rates.

(2026-08-30, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. gomotive.com/pricing resolves to a lead-capture form at /get-in-touch/?id=pricing — a four-step email capture before any figure appears, preceded by a geolocation prompt offering the UK site. No per-vehicle rate, no plan names with amounts, no contract length and no hardware cost is published on the pricing page, the Pro plan page or the products overview. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Motive?
answers.a: A pricing page with a form where the prices should be. That is the finding, and it matters more in fleet than in software generally. The real cost here is not a monthly rate: it is hardware per vehicle, a contract term that is usually multi-year, and an early-termination position you will not hear about until you want out. None of that is public. Before the demo call, decide your own numbers: vehicles, contract length you will accept, and what you currently pay per truck. In a quote-only category the first number you hear is anchored to what they think you can pay, not to a rate card.

Murf is genuinely best for creators, trainers and product teams that need studio-quality voiceovers in many languages without booking voice actors — explainers, courses, product videos. Skip it if you need real emotional acting range for premium brand work (humans still win), or your volume is tiny enough that free TTS built into your video tool suffices.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 in a browser; the page renders client-side and opens on annual billing, so check which column you are reading) Studio plans: Free $0 for 10 projects, 10 minutes of voice generation and one editor, with no downloads and no commercial rights. Creator $19/mo billed annually ($228 a year): 100 projects, 24 hours of voice generation a year, 1 editor, all 200+ voices, unlimited downloads and commercial rights. Business $66/mo billed annually ($792 a year): 500 projects, 96 hours of generation a year, business licence, PowerPoint integration and audio-to-text. Enterprise is custom and is where voice cloning, SSO and AI translation sit. Annual billing is advertised as saving 33%. Dub and the API are separate products with their own pricing — Murf's own homepage advertises API voice generation from $0.01 a minute, which is a different meter from the Studio hour allowances above. The Studio ladder on the page is Free, Creator, Business and Enterprise; there is no Growth plan, and Creator and Business are capped at one editor seat each, so a second person means Enterprise. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Murf?
answers.a: The meter is generation hours per YEAR, not per month — 24 hours sounds generous until you count retakes, and regenerating a script three times bills three times. Voice quality is genuinely strong, but the honest test for any TTS is your specific language, names and jargon: generate your hardest paragraph in the trial before subscribing, because demo voices always sound better than your edge cases.

Mycroft is genuinely best for companies chasing an attestation they cannot staff for — CMMC or FedRAMP to keep bidding on defence and public-sector work, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 to get through enterprise procurement — that would rather buy the platform, the security stack and the people who operate it on one contract than assemble a GRC tool, a pen tester, a vCISO and a monitoring vendor separately and hold them together themselves. Skip it if you already have a security team and only need the evidence-collection and control-monitoring layer, because the managed half is most of what you would be paying for; or you need to compare cost before capability, because nothing here is priced anywhere and every tier ends in a sales conversation.

(read 4 September 2026 on www.mycroft.io/pricing) Mycroft has no public pricing: three packages, and not one number between them. Platform is the entry tier and the only one whose button says Get started rather than something sales-shaped; it bundles the full GRC platform for SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA and more, a Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, security, AI and privacy awareness training, 24/7/365 threat intelligence and monitoring, a Trust Center, and what Mycroft calls basic Agentic AI workflows. Scale says Book a demo and adds penetration testing, continuous third-party risk management, a customer success manager and expanded AI workflows. Managed says Talk to sales and adds customised frameworks, customised AI workflows and a dedicated CISO who doubles as your success manager. What the page never does is price any of it: no monthly figure, no per-seat rate, no starting-from, no annual floor, not even for the tier you are invited to start by yourself. We looked past the pricing page before writing that down, because the claim is usually wrong. The FAQ page, the product pages, the CMMC-as-a-Service page and the machine-readable llms.txt all describe the packages in detail and none of them names an amount; the sitemap holds no second pricing page; and the raw HTML of /pricing carries no hidden figure either. So the tiers tell you exactly what you get and leave what you pay entirely to a call. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Mycroft?
answers.a: The pricing page is a feature list with the prices taken out, and that is a choice rather than an oversight — Mycroft publishes what is in each package down to the individual capability, then stops short of the one line you came for. It matters more here than it would elsewhere, because what Mycroft sells is not a seat of software: it is a platform bundled with a managed service, secure enclaves, infrastructure and identity management, an audit coordinated on your behalf and, at the top, a dedicated CISO. That is a services contract, and services contracts scope on your environment, so the number genuinely will differ per company. It also means you cannot sanity-check the cost against doing it yourself until you have sat through a demo. The second thing to weigh is how much of the evidence is the vendor talking. What you can verify from outside is a handful of named case studies — SmashSend, Weave, Wisedocs, Unified — and the quotes inside them; there is no published customer count and no independent review base to read. The team is not thin: the CEO holds a CISA, the engineering co-founder a CISSP, and the product co-founder co-founded PartnerStack. But a young company promising CMMC and FedRAMP outcomes is asking for trust on a timeline where being wrong is expensive. Ask what happens if the assessment does not pass, and ask it before the second call.

Navan is genuinely best for companies that want self-serve travel booking with built-in policy control — genuinely free — and optionally unified expense management on top. Skip it if your travel volume is a few trips a year (any booking site does), or you need expense-only tooling without the travel layer.

Navan publishes no price list, re-verified 2026-08-17: the pricing URL is a marketing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. What we can state from our dated reading is the shape. Business Travel is genuinely free to the customer, funded by travel-supplier commissions, and includes booking, policy enforcement and basic expense capture. The Expense product is free for the first 15 users and then charged per user per month, which our reading put at around $15. Enterprise is custom for larger organisations. Because the travel side is commission-funded, the question to ask is not what it costs but what it steers — confirm that your negotiated rates and preferred suppliers survive the policy engine. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Navan?
answers.a: 'Free' is real but has a mechanism: Navan earns commission on bookings made through its inventory, so the platform's incentive is that your travel flows through Navan — pricing on specific routes/hotels deserves an occasional spot-check against direct booking. The paid expense tier is where unified T&E gets real; the 15-free-users threshold makes the trial honest for small teams.

NeuroAds is genuinely best for small and mid-size Shopify stores that want a multilingual, catalogue-aware chat widget with product cards, order tracking and add-to-cart, and want to judge it on the genuinely usable free tier of 200 conversations a month. Skip it if you need a support desk with a track record, you cannot budget against a 'conversation' nobody has defined, or routing customer names, phone numbers and addresses through a ten-week-old vendor is not a trade you want to make.

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/neuroads-chatbot) Four tiers, priced by conversations per month. Free: 200 conversations, AI answers about products, collections and orders, rich product cards with add-to-cart, order status and tracking in chat, replies in the shopper's language. Starter $19 a month: 800 conversations, plus live human takeover and discount codes offered in chat, 7-day free trial. Growth $49 a month or $468 a year (save 20%): 3,000 conversations, plus a revenue and ROAS dashboard, A/B testing on the chat greeting, answer insights and Klaviyo, 7-day free trial. Unlimited $119 a month or $1,142 a year (save 20%): unlimited conversations, WhatsApp and Klaviyo, advanced reporting with CSV export, chat-only discount codes, removal of the 'Powered by NeuroAds' label, a year of conversation history and dedicated onboarding, 7-day free trial. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Two things the pricing table does not settle. What counts as one conversation — a shopper session, a thread, a single message — is defined nowhere, and it is the only unit the whole ladder is built on. And the listing summary advertises a 30-day trial while every paid plan in the table shows seven days. Developer NEUROAD VENTURES LLC of Newport Beach, California; the app launched 5 June 2026 and has six App Store reviews. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with NeuroAds?
answers.a:
The app is ten weeks old. It launched on 5 June 2026 and, as of 19 August 2026, has six reviews — all five stars, all posted between 7 and 15 August, by merchants who had had it installed for five, eleven and thirteen days. Nothing about that is suspicious on its face; new apps have new reviews. But six enthusiastic first impressions from people two weeks in tell you the setup is smooth and tell you nothing about what happens when the bot gets a refund question wrong in month four. On the same page, Shopify Inbox is free with 5,488 reviews.

The listing contradicts itself on the trial. The summary at the top of the page promises a 30-day trial; the pricing table shows a 7-day free trial on all three paid plans. Assume seven days, because that is the number in the row you actually click, and check it in the charge screen before you rely on a month.

And look at what it asks for. This app requests names, email addresses, phone numbers and physical addresses of your customers, plus geolocation and IP, sixty days of order history, your discount codes and your store pages. That is a defensible list for a bot that tracks orders and offers codes, and it is also a lot of customer data to route through a ten-week-old company on the strength of six reviews. Read the privacy policy, and check where the conversations are stored, before you switch it on for a store with EU shoppers.

Nexis CRO is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who already care about being cited in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and who want the audit, the schema deployment, the llms.txt file and the citation tracking in one app instead of stitching them together.. Skip it if Stores that already run a mature SEO app, anyone who wants proven tooling rather than a new one, and merchants for whom AI-chat visibility is not yet a business question..

answers.q: How much does Nexis CRO cost?
answers.a: (read 14 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/nexis-cro-ai-seo-aeo-audit) Free, then Pro $9 a month or $99 a year, Growth $21 or $121, and Agency $44 or $344. All charges are in USD and recur every 30 days, and the paid tiers carry a 2-day free trial — short for judging a tool whose whole promise is a change in how AI engines see you. The meter is AI credits: Free gives 5 a month and a single audit, Pro 100 with unlimited audits and history, Growth 300, Agency 500. Read Agency's “500 AI credits (unlimited usage)” against that number rather than past it: the credits are the ceiling. The yearly discounts the vendor advertises do hold up when you check them — 8% on Pro, 52% on Growth, 35% on Agency. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Nexis CRO?
answers.a: It has no track record at all. The app launched on 9 June 2026 and its App Store listing still showed a 0.0 rating from zero reviews when we read it on 14 September 2026 — so every claim about what the audit catches, how good the AI rewrites are and whether the citation tracking is accurate rests on the vendor's own description. That matters more than usual here, because AEO tracking is a young field: nobody has yet shown that being cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity moves revenue, and the numbers a tracker reports are hard for a merchant to check independently. The free tier is also thin — 5 AI credits and one audit a month is enough to see the interface, not to test the product.

Nextify.ai is genuinely best for advertisers who need a steady stream of short product clips and will deliberately choose the cheap model for drafts, and teams who would rather have video, avatars, lip-sync and product imagery drawing on one credit pool than pay for four separate subscriptions. Skip it if you are budgeting from the “up to N videos” figures on the pricing page, you need talking-head or avatar video at any volume — that route is 6.7 credits a second, so Pro buys seven sixty-second ads a month — or you expected the free tier to work as a trial: it is 50 watermarked credits and it cannot reach the Seedance models at all.

(read 7 September 2026 on nextify.ai/pricing, signed in and signed out, in both billing modes) Five ways to pay, and the free plan is only visible when you are logged out — the signed-in pricing page starts at Starter. Free is $0 for 50 credits a month, watermarked, on the basic models only, and the page sells that as up to 2 videos and 25 images. Billed monthly the paid tiers are Starter $29, Pro $79 and Business $189. Billed annually the same tiers are $21, $52 and $114 a month, charged $244, $617 and $1,361 a year — the 30%, 35% and 40% badges check out at 28%, 34% and 40% against the monthly rate. Credit allowances are 1,000, 3,000 and 8,000 a month; Business is the only tier with a second seat. A one-off pack of 1,250 credits is $50, never expires and does not auto-renew, which works out at $0.04 a credit against $0.017 on annual Pro — so topping up costs more than twice what the subscription does. Subscription credits do not roll over between cycles. Refunds are limited to three days from a first subscription, and add-on packs are non-refundable. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Nextify.ai?
answers.a: The plans are sold in videos and images; the meter runs in credits per second, and the two do not reconcile. Every tier's headline count works out at 20 credits a video and 2 credits an image — 1,000 credits become “up to 50 videos” and “up to 500 images”, 3,000 become 150 and 1,500, 8,000 become 400 and 4,000. The app's own credit table prices video per second of output: Seedance 2.0, the model the editor pre-selects, is 12 credits a second at 720p, so the default four-second clip costs 48. We generated one and watched the balance fall from 3,000 to 2,952. That makes Pro 62 clips a month rather than 150, and 16 if you use the 15-second maximum. The 20-credit figure is reachable, but only on the 5-credit-a-second model at four seconds. The image claim has no such escape hatch: the cheapest image model in the table is 7 credits and the pre-selected one is 10, so nothing in the product costs the 2 credits those counts assume, and Starter's 500 images is nearer 100.

Ngram is genuinely best for product and marketing teams that want to turn docs, screenshots and recordings into polished, on-brand videos quickly and repeatably. Skip it if you need bespoke, high-end studio production, or your video volume would make the per-export credit model expensive versus a flat-fee tool.

(re-verified 2026-08-17) Credit-based, three published tiers plus a quote-only Enterprise, with annual billing 20% off. Free is a one-time 600-credit allocation capped at 60 seconds of premium AI generation and 720p exports. Basic is $29/mo, or $23.20/mo billed annually at $278.40 a year, with 3,000 credits a month. Premium is $59/mo, or $47.20 annually at $566.40. Ultimate is $299/mo, or $239.20 annually at $2,870.40, for maximum creation capacity. The credit allowance rather than the seat is what forces an upgrade. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Ngram?
answers.a:
The sticker price buys a credit allowance, not finished video, and the two are easy to confuse. Premium AI generation runs from 10 credits a second, so Basic's 3,000 credits a month come out at roughly 300 seconds — about five minutes of generated footage. Ngram says as much on the page: generation seconds measure premium AI-generated footage, not final video length, and manual editing and exports are unlimited on paid plans. So the tier you need tracks how much AI footage you generate, not how many videos you publish.

The top-up economics run the wrong way for small buyers. Extra credits cost 1,000 for $40 on Free, $20 on Basic, $15 on Premium and $10 on Ultimate — the cheapest plan pays four times per credit what the dearest one pays. Anyone topping up regularly on Basic is paying a premium for staying on the cheap tier, and should price the next tier against a month of actual top-ups rather than against the headline gap between the two.

Two smaller things before you pick. Export quality is tiered — 720p on Basic, 1080p on Premium, 4K on Ultimate — so the resolution you need may set your plan before the credits do. And image and audio generation still consume credits on Basic, going unlimited only from Premium up.

NiceJob is genuinely best for local and service businesses that want reputation marketing on offense — automatically asking happy customers for reviews and showcasing them — rather than only managing damage when a bad review lands. Skip it if you need deep reporting or highly customized review workflows, or your service quality isn't ready for more visibility yet — fix that first, then amplify it.

(re-verified 2026-09-11 on their own pricing page) Software plans are Reviews at $75/mo and Pro at $125/mo, both USD, with a 14-day free trial, no credit card up front and no contracts. The website plans are Sites at $99/mo and Grow + Sites at $174/mo, each with a one-off $199 setup fee; the software-only plans carry no setup fee. The page also runs a contact-count ladder that the headline figures hide: Grow is $75 for 1-2,500 customers, $95 above 2,500, $145 above 5,000 and $290 above 10,000, and Grow + Sites is $174, $194, $244 and $389 across the same steps — an even $99 apart at every rung. Sites add-ons are billed on top: an extra landing page is $145 one-time plus $15/mo, and a CMS for blogs, services or locations is $245 one-time plus $15/mo. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with NiceJob?
answers.a: Reporting and customization are fairly basic and there's a setup fee on top of the monthly. It automates review collection genuinely well, but if you want deep analytics or granular control over timing and wording, it can feel restrictive. And the honest fundamental: automation only amplifies the service you actually deliver. It keeps the review stream fresh and steady (which matters — stale reviews lose trust fast, and AI search increasingly recommends businesses on review signals), but it cannot manufacture a reputation you haven't earned.

Niural AI is genuinely best for US companies that want payroll, benefits, PEO and international hiring from one vendor and want to see a number before the call — and especially teams above about fifty people, where the $100 platform fee stops distorting the per-employee rate. Skip it if you are under about ten employees, because the $100 platform fee doubles the effective per-head cost at that size; you need to buy without talking to anyone, since every tier is demo-led; or you only need global payroll for entities you already run, where the $29 tier is the only part of this catalogue you should be pricing.

answers.q: How much does Niural AI cost?
answers.a: (read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on niural.com/pricing) Eight products, each priced separately, and unusually for this category every one of them carries a published figure. US Payroll Standard is $100 a month as a platform fee plus $20 per employee a month, covering multi-state payroll with W-2s and 1099s, unlimited pay schedules and payroll runs, PTO and leave policies, workforce analytics, same-day deposits, full benefits administration with 401(k) and brokered health, dental and vision, and CRM and ATS integrations; US Payroll Enterprise is custom. On the PEO side, PEO Basic starts at $59 per employee a month without benefits, and PEO Plus at $120 with them — adding benefits enrolment, life and disability cover, 401(k), commuter benefits, medical, dental and vision, and HSA, FSA, COBRA and HRA accounts, with terms noted for groups under five employees. Internationally: Contractor Management is $49 per contractor a month, Contractor of Record (branded Niural Armor) is $299 per employee a month, Employer of Record starts at $299 per employee a month across 150-plus countries, and Global Payroll for entities you already own starts at $29 per employee a month. One caveat about reading this page: it asks your company size first (under 25, 25 to 50, 50 to 100, or more than 100) and adjusts what it shows, so the figures above are the under-25 view and a re-read should select the same step. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Niural AI?
answers.a:
Every tier says Book a demo. The prices are published — which in payroll is genuinely rare and worth crediting — but there is no self-serve sign-up anywhere on the page, so the published figure is the opening of a conversation rather than something you can act on. Expect the real number to arrive by quote, and expect it to depend on the company-size step you selected before you ever saw a price.

The page changes under you, and that is easy to miss. It asks your headcount band first and adjusts the ladder to match, so two people comparing Niural can honestly quote each other different numbers. Note which band you read when you write the figure down.

The platform fee is the part that decides whether this is cheap. US Payroll is $100 a month before anyone is paid, plus $20 a head. At five employees that is $200 a month, or $40 an employee — double the headline rate. At twenty-five it is $600, or $24 each. At a hundred it is $2,100, or $21 each. The per-employee price you are quoted only becomes the price you pay somewhere north of fifty people, and small teams are the ones most likely to read $20 and budget $20.

The naming needs care too. Contractor of Record and Employer of Record are both $299 per employee a month and they are not the same product: the first keeps the worker a contractor while Niural carries the misclassification risk, the second makes Niural the legal employer in 150-plus countries. Buying the wrong one is an expensive mistake that the identical price does nothing to prevent.

NordVPN is genuinely best for teams that want simple, reliable secure network access and a business VPN without heavy setup. Skip it if you're a solo user chasing the cheapest personal VPN — the consumer plan, not the business tier, is what you want.

(consumer plans re-verified 2026-09-14 in the browser; the page is geo-priced and served us euros from a Dutch address) Consumer two-year plans: Basic €3.49/mo, Complete €4.49/mo and Ultimate Max €8.49/mo, each with three extra months. They are charged as €94.23, €121.23 and €229.23 for the first 27 months, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. Read the renewal line before you buy: those same plans renew at €139.08, €219.48 and €338.28 a year, so Basic goes from about €3.49 a month to about €11.59 — roughly a threefold step.
