Skip it if your catalogue is larger than 5,000 products, or you want the safest bet in a category where three rivals on the same page carry 850 to 2,400 reviews at 4.9-5.0 against this app's 4.4 over 114.

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/minifier and on seomatic.io) Four tiers, and the only thing that changes between the three paid ones is how many products they cover. Free: 10 products, 50 image optimisations, AI SEO audit, auto-pilot AI meta title and description, schema markup, HTML sitemap. Starter $15 a month or $144 a year (save 20%): 500 products, unlimited image optimiser, broken links, XML and HTML sitemaps, 14-day free trial. Basic $25 a month or $240 a year: 2,000 products. Advanced $40 a month or $384 a year: 5,000 products. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page at seomatic.io publishes the identical ladder, which is worth noting because the two often disagree — here they do not. There is no plan above 5,000 products on either page, so a larger catalogue has no listed price at all. Developer Aheadworks, 12495 S Parkland Bay Trail, Parkland, Florida; the app launched 18 August 2015 and carries a 4.4 average over 114 App Store reviews, and it holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SEOmatic?
answers.a:
This app is eleven years old and has 114 reviews. That is the number to sit with. On the same listing page Shopify shows three direct rivals. SEOLab is 5.0 over 2,368 reviews and free, Tiny SEO 5.0 over 2,261 and free to install, and Smart SEO 4.9 over 851 with a free plan. All three carry between seven and twenty times the review volume, all are rated higher, and none of them charges by product count. SEOmatic's 4.4 is a real rating from real merchants, but it is the weakest track record on its own page.

The distribution behind that 4.4 matters too: 81% five stars against 8% one star, with almost nothing in the middle. The most substantial recent review, from March 2025, is a merchant of six months saying it appears to work on images and nothing else, and that support is difficult and slow. The vendor replied that the reports do exist, and asked them to get in touch. An older one-star from a merchant who lasted seventeen minutes reads 'Paid for it to tell me 0% savings'. Both are about the same thing — what the app actually did after installation was not visible to the person paying for it.

And the product cap is a hard ceiling, not a soft one. There is no tier above 5,000 products on the listing or on seomatic.io, so if your catalogue is larger than that, the published ladder simply does not have a row for you.

SMTP.com is genuinely best for businesses and developers needing dependable high-deliverability transactional or bulk email via SMTP relay and API, with dedicated IPs at scale. Skip it if you send low volume and a free/cheap SMTP tier covers you, or you want a full marketing-email platform with templates and automation built in.

(price re-verified 2026-09-05) Fixed-volume plans, all billed monthly: Essential $25 (50,000 emails, shared IP), Starter $80 (100,000, dedicated IP begins here), Growth $300 (500,000), Business $500 (1,000,000). Above that, High Volume Senders is quote-only and starts at a minimum of 250 million emails a month, with a dedicated platform instance, dedicated IP and MTA and no shared mail queue. Reputation Defender and Insight Engine are optional add-ons at 20% of plan cost each, available on all plans. No free tier or published trial. Payment by card or PayPal. The site is operated by J2 Global Canada, a Ziff Davis company. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SMTP.com?
answers.a: It's a veteran, reliable relay, but two honest notes. Pricing is volume-tiered, so a shared IP on the cheapest plan is fine for low volume while serious senders need the dedicated-IP tiers (and the IP warm-up discipline that comes with them). And the value-add features — reputation and verification — are metered on top at ~20% of plan cost, so the real bill is higher than the base tier. It's infrastructure, not a marketing suite; you bring the campaigns.

SMTP2GO is genuinely best for businesses that want dependable transactional/bulk sending via SMTP or API with human support and clear per-volume pricing. Skip it if you're inside a marketing platform that already sends for you, or you need advanced template/campaign tooling bundled in.

(read 2026-09-07 on smtp2go.com/pricing with the volume slider walked through all nine stops; the plan cards carry the amounts in their data-rate-monthly and data-rate-annual attributes) Free: 1,000 emails a month, 200 a day, 5 days of reporting, ticket support only (toll-free phone and live chat limited to 14 days), extra emails not permitted. Starter: $15/mo or $150/year for 10,000 (overage $1.20 per thousand); $30/mo or $300/year for 50,000 ($1 per thousand). Professional: $75/$750 for 100,000 ($0.85), $170/$1,700 for 250,000 ($0.70), $280/$2,800 for 500,000 ($0.60), $520/$5,200 for 1,000,000 ($0.50), and it adds a dedicated IP address and email-testing tools. Premier: custom, over 3,000,000 a month. Annual is exactly ten months' money at every step (their 'two months free'). All invoices are billed in US dollars; EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD are shown as approximations. 30-day money-back promise. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SMTP2GO?
answers.a: It's the pragmatic middle of email infrastructure: simpler and better-supported than the hyperscale APIs, cheaper than most, with genuinely useful reporting — but sending reputation is still yours to earn. A relay delivers what your domain deserves: without proper SPF/DKIM/DMARC and list hygiene, no provider saves you. Check the overage rate for your tier before you size up: on the 10,000 plan an extra thousand emails costs $1.20 against the $1.50 a thousand you already pay, and the 50,000 plan at $30 works out cheaper per email than Professional at $75.

Salesflare is genuinely best for small B2B teams whose reps hate data entry — Salesflare auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar. Skip it if you need deep customisation, a big integration marketplace, or built-in calling and invoicing — Pipedrive or a fuller CRM fit better.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on salesflare.com/pricing, per user a month) Three plans, and the page carries both billing terms plus a $/€ switch: Growth $39 a month or $29 billed annually, Pro $64 or $49, and Enterprise $124 or $99 with a minimum of five users. The euro column prints the same numerals — €39/€29, €64/€49, €124/€99 — so a European buyer pays the same figure in a different currency rather than a converted one. Our earlier reading called this “$29–99 per user” with Growth at about $29–39 and Pro at about $49. The range was right and the label was not: the low number in each pair is the annual rate and the high one is what month-to-month costs, and the five-seat floor on Enterprise never appeared. Lead credits are part of the ladder rather than an add-on — 5 on Growth, 100 on Pro, 250 on Enterprise. There is a 30-day free trial with no card. On that same page the vendor commits to no onboarding fees and to no caps on contacts, users, email templates, tracked emails, custom fields, workflows, dashboards or pipelines. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Salesflare?
answers.a: It's deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and reporting feels basic unless you export. Integrations cover the essentials (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier) but niche tools lean on Zapier — and at higher seat counts the price overlaps fuller CRMs.

Salesflow is genuinely best for outbound sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn sequences across several seats, where the per-seat price drops and the admin panel earns its keep. Skip it if you are one person sending a handful of connection requests a week — the quotas are far above what you need and the seat price is at its highest.

(2026-09-09) Read on Salesflow's own pricing page. It returns a 403 to our server but renders normally in a browser, so these are their published figures rather than third-party ones: Basic $99 per seat from 1 seat, Starter $70 from 5 seats, Pro $39.95 from 20, Agency $29.98 from 50 and Enterprise $24.99 from 100. Agency and Enterprise require an annual commitment billed monthly. Longer terms are discounted on top of that: 15% off at six months and 30% off at twelve. There is no free tier and the trial is seven days without a card. The monthly quotas — around 400 LinkedIn invites, 2,000 follow-up messages and 800 Open InMails — are reported by independent reviews and do not appear on the pricing page itself. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Salesflow?
answers.a: The per-seat rate falls with team size but the monthly bill does not follow it: 19 seats on Starter is $1,330 while 20 seats on Pro is $799, so a team that stops one seat short of a tier pays $531 a month more for less. The same cliff sits at 49-to-50 seats and again at 99-to-100. And the monthly quotas are the real ceiling: 400 invites and 800 Open InMails is a fixed budget, not a starting point.

Salesmessage is genuinely best for sales and service teams that want two-way texting and calling in one CRM-linked inbox, and can estimate their monthly credit burn — messages plus call minutes — before they sign. Skip it if your audience doesn't respond to SMS, or your volume is low enough that the fixed 10DLC overhead outweighs the sending. Also skip it if you need a lot of seats cheaply. And skip it if your real usage lands in the gap between the $25 and $329 plans, since the only bridge on offer is a bigger credit bundle on the small plan.

(2026-08-08, re-verified 10 September 2026 on www.salesmessage.com/pricing in both billing modes) Repackaged since our last check into two named plans plus Enterprise, metered in message credits. Monthly billing: Basic is $25 a month for 500 credits a month; Pro is $329 a month for 10,000 credits a month; Enterprise is contact-for-pricing with custom credits. Both plans carry a credits dropdown that raises the allowance for a fixed add-on. On Basic, 1,000 credits is +$24, 2,500 is +$74, 5,000 is +$154 and 7,500 is +$224 a month. On Pro the ladder runs from 15,000 credits at +$150 up to 50,000 at +$1,170 a month, in 5,000-credit steps. Annual billing is shown as two months free. Basic is $21 a month billed yearly for 6,000 credits a year (12,000 credits +$252, 30,000 +$756, 60,000 +$1,560, 90,000 +$2,268), and Pro $277 a month billed yearly for 120,000 credits a year (180,000 +$1,512, rising to 600,000 at +$11,796). Seats and numbers are priced apart from the plan: the first seat is free and each additional seat is $10.00 a month or $100.00 a year; the first number is free and each additional number is $5.00 a month or $50.00 a year. The page defines the meter itself: SMS is 1 credit per 160 characters, MMS is 2 credits, calling is 1 credit a minute and call forwarding is 2 credits a minute. A 14-day free trial runs, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered, refunded less the message credits used. The page no longer publishes a per-credit overage rate, nor terms for taxes, carrier fees or country availability, so we quote none. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Salesmessage?
answers.a: Two things changed here and both cost money. First, calling now runs on the same meter as texting — 1 credit a minute, 2 a minute when forwarding — so voice minutes eat the allowance you budgeted for messages. Second, the plan ladder is a canyon: $25 to $329 a month with nothing between them, and the credits dropdown raises your allowance without adding a single seat. Size the credits, not the headcount. An MMS is 2 credits, so one picture message to 1,000 contacts is 2,000 credits — four times the entire monthly allowance on Basic. Seats and numbers bill on top of every plan beyond the first of each: a five-person team on one number is $40 a month over the sticker, and the annual headline of $21 and $277 is a per-month display of a bill charged yearly. Note what the page has stopped saying since our previous check: there is no published per-credit overage rate anymore, so what happens when you run out mid-cycle is not stated where you buy — ask before you commit. And US business texting carries a regulatory layer of its own: 10DLC registration and carrier surcharges bill separately from anything quoted here, and opt-in and opt-out handling stays your legal responsibility — the platform enables compliance, it does not absolve you.

SaneBox is genuinely best for heavy-email professionals drowning in a cluttered inbox who want AI triage that works across any mail client. Skip it if your inbox is manageable or your mail client's built-in filtering already handles it — you don't need to pay for this.

(read in a live browser on their own pricing page, 18 Aug 2026 — the figures are rendered client-side, so a plain fetch shows nothing) Three plans, and the advertised price is the two-year rate. Snack $4.54/mo billed $109 every 2 years, $5.42/mo billed $65 annually, or $9.49 month to month: 1 email account and 2 of the Sane features. Lunch $7.46 / $9.08 ($109 a year) / $15.99: 2 accounts and 6 features. Dinner $22.04 / $26.58 ($319 a year) / $42.99: 4 accounts and every feature, plus phone support. The free trial is 7 days with all features on up to 4 accounts. Education, non-profit and government get another 25% off on request during the trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SaneBox?
answers.a: It works with any email provider, which is a genuine advantage over the built-in tools in Gmail and Outlook. But you are paying monthly to filter mail that modern clients increasingly sort for free. The value is real only if your inbox is genuinely overwhelming and native filters are not cutting it. Price it on the plan you would actually keep: the headline rate is a two-year commitment, and month to month the same Snack plan is $9.49 rather than $4.54.

Scarcity.AI is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who genuinely run low stock or timed promotions and want to surface that on the product page — the low stock counter is tied to real inventory, which makes it the honest one of the three when your stock actually is low. Skip it if your stock is not low and your sale does not end, because a claim a shopper would read as false is one the FTC treats as deceptive; or your brand sells on trust, where a blinking counter costs more in credibility than it returns.

(read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com, across all three listings) These are three separate apps from one developer, each installed and billed on its own. The Low Stock Counter is $4.99 a month or $41.91 a year at a stated 30% saving, with a 7-day trial; its free tier is Development Stores, meaning development and partner stores only rather than a working free plan. The Visitors Counter is $1.99 a month or $16.71 a year, with a genuine free plan that carries the counter itself, customisation, product-level targeting and holiday presets — the $1.99 adds an upsell banner for your most-viewed product, on a 3-day trial. The Countdown Timer listing shows a free tier and no paid ladder. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, who also publish Blocky, TiXel and Way. Ratings at the time of writing: 4.7 from 84 reviews on the low stock counter, 4.8 from 36 on the visitors counter and 5.0 from 22 on the countdown timer. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Scarcity.AI?
answers.a:
All three read real data, which is worth saying before anything else — the low stock counter shows inventory levels and the visitors counter reads unique visitors, live traffic and product views. Nothing here invents a number.

But the visitors counter carries two settings that shape which true number a shopper sees. It can show the counter only after a set number of views, so a quiet product simply displays nothing rather than a small figure. And the time frame is yours to set, so 'twelve people viewed this' can mean twelve in five minutes or twelve since yesterday, presented identically. Neither setting fabricates anything; together they let you present a true number that a reasonable shopper would read as something else.

That distinction is where the legal line sits. The FTC treats false urgency and scarcity as deceptive practice under section 5 of the FTC Act, and the examples in its dark-patterns guidance are close to these mechanics: a low-stock claim when stock is plentiful, or a cart-activity figure well above the real one. The test is whether a reasonable consumer would be misled about a material fact. That test does not apply to the app; it applies to how you configure it, which means the compliance question lands on your desk rather than the developer's.

Scrolly is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want a free, one-click back-to-top button on long collection and product pages without touching theme code — and who can treat infinite scroll as a separate $2.99-a-month decision rather than part of the same install. Skip it if you run a large catalogue that depends on paginated collection URLs being crawled, your theme already ships its own load-more or filtering behaviour, or you need conversion work rather than navigation polish — this only changes how the page scrolls.

(read 2026-08-25 and re-read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/custom-scroll-to-top) Two plans now, where there was one. On 25 August 2026 the listing carried no paid tier, no usage meter and no surcharge — the pricing block most App Store listings use to sell an upgrade was simply absent. On 19 September 2026 it carries a Free Plan and an Unlimited Plan at $2.99 a month, or $25.11 a year with a 30% saving and a 7-day free trial. The split does not fall where the app’s name suggests. Free keeps the scroll-to-top button and its styling: multiple presets, button colour and hover colour, and the option to hide it on the mobile storefront. Unlimited adds infinite scrolling and the load-more button, plus uploading your own SVG icon for the button. So the feature the app is named after, and the one the first three of the listing’s five selling points describe, is now the paid half. All charges are billed in USD every 30 days. The app has been on the App Store since March 2020, carries Shopify’s Built for Shopify badge — the store’s own bar for performance, design and integration — and the listing names eleven interface languages. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Scrolly?
answers.a:
The two features carry very different risk, the app presents them as one install, and since August the money has been split across them in a way the name does not warn you about. Infinite scroll replaces the paginated collection URLs a crawler uses to walk a large catalogue, pushes your footer permanently out of reach, and on some themes collides with the load-more or filtering logic already in the theme — that is a merchandising decision, not a styling toggle. The app also edits Online Store script tags and the theme, so it adds a third-party script to every page and an uninstall can leave remnants.

What changed is which half you pay for. Read on 19 September 2026, the free plan keeps the scroll-to-top button and infinite scroll sits on the $2.99 Unlimited plan, where on 25 August the whole app was free. The amount is trivial; the shape is not. The half that can quietly alter how your collection pages are crawled is now the half with a billing relationship behind it, and the seven-day trial is the only window in which you will find out what it does to your store before the charge starts. Anything written about this app before September — including a free-forever recommendation — describes an install that no longer exists.

Seamless.ai is genuinely best for teams that want a huge real-time contact database and AI list-building for less than ZoomInfo, and can tolerate cleaning the data. Skip it if data accuracy is your top priority (ZoomInfo bounces far less), or you want simple no-contract pricing — the bounce rates and auto-renewal bite.

(read 2026-09-07 on seamless.ai/pricing and seamless.ai/llms.txt) Still no published amount above the free plan, in a fourth reading. Free: 1 user, 50 credits. Pro: 'Per User', unlimited exports, annual credit packages, '1 Credits = Phone + Email', Contact sales. Enterprise: unlimited users, unlimited exports, custom packages, customer success and enterprise support, Contact sales. The only quantity they publish above Free is in the FAQ: Pro plans start at 10,000 annual credits, and custom accounts get a daily allotment at five or more licence tiers. The FAQ also says there are no setup fees, and that 'the prices shown on this page reflect this annual discount' — on a page that shows none. Four capabilities are marked Add-on in every column, Enterprise included: AI Assistant, Data Enrichment, Autopilot and Buyer Intent Data. Connect (email, calling and tasks) is flagged as included on all plans for a limited time. Third-party guides report an entry around $147 a month for roughly 250 credits and up to $150-500 per user a month; those are not Seamless's numbers, and 250 credits a month is 3,000 a year against a published Pro floor of 10,000. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Seamless.ai?
answers.a: Data accuracy is the recurring complaint — independent tests put email deliverability around 74% (20–30% bounce) versus ZoomInfo's ~2–3%, so real cost per usable contact climbs. The buying experience is the other weak spot: sales-led, auto-renew with 30–60 day written cancellation, and reports of charges after a 'confirmed' cancellation.

Section Library is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want ready-made theme sections and the occasional AI-generated layout inside the native theme editor, and who can live with an app that has almost no public track record. Skip it if you are rebuilding a store you cannot afford to break and want a page builder with thousands of merchants behind it, or you need your monthly cost known in advance — the credit unit is never defined.

answers.q: How much does Section Library cost?
answers.a: (re-read 2026-09-17 on apps.shopify.com/section-library, now listed as “Section Library: AI Sections”; every amount is unchanged since 19 August 2026) Free plan: 8 credits a month, access to the free sections only, basic AI generation. Starter $9 a month: 25 credits, all sections accessible, AI section generation, email support. Pro $19 a month: 55 credits, all sections, priority support. Business $29 a month: 90 credits, all sections, priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and the listing shows no free trial on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial. One thing the pricing table still never states is what a credit actually buys. Whether one credit is one AI generation, one section added to a theme, or something else is defined nowhere on the listing — and the credit count is the only thing separating the four plans. The vendor’s own site is worse than priceless: sectionlibrary.com is itself a Shopify store and on 17 September 2026 it answered HTTP 402 with Shopify’s “Store unavailable” page instead of a site, so the App Store listing we link to is now the only public record of the product at all. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 10 October 2023. It still carries a 5.0 rating from exactly one App Store review, left in October 2023 by a merchant who had the app installed for four minutes. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Section Library?
answers.a:
Almost three years on the App Store and one review. The app launched 10 October 2023 and, as of 17 September 2026, exactly one merchant has written about it: a five-star note from October 2023 by someone who had it installed for four minutes. That is not evidence of quality and not evidence of trouble — it is an absence of evidence, and on an app that writes sections into your live theme, that absence is the main thing to weigh. On the same listing page Shopify shows Section Store with 2,929 reviews, also free to install, which is what a track record looks like in this category. And on 17 September 2026 the vendor’s own site, sectionlibrary.com, answered with Shopify’s “Store unavailable” page instead of a website.

Second, the credit is undefined. Every plan is priced in credits and nothing on the listing says what one buys, so you cannot price your own usage before you commit.

Third, the AI half of the product is Google's. Sections are generated by Gemini 3.1 Pro, so output quality and consistency shift when Google ships a new model, which is outside the vendor's hands as much as yours. The library half — the 200+ pre-built sections — is the part that depends on nobody else, and it is the part worth judging the app on.

Securify is genuinely best for stores seeing real fraud or bot traffic that want country, IP, VPN and email-risk rules plus automatic holds on suspicious orders, and who will review the block log rather than set and forget. Skip it if you are blocking on a hunch rather than on measured fraud — start by reading your order data, because a blocked legitimate customer never tells you they were blocked.

(read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/easy-block-customer-ip-country) Free plan available with a free trial on the paid tiers. Paid runs Pro $5.99, Advanced $9.49 and Growth $49 a month. Rating 4.4 from 68 reviews, and it carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. The App Store lists it as “Country Blocker Fraud Securify” from siimple.ai. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Securify?
answers.a: Blocking by country and IP is a blunt instrument and it cuts both ways: every rule that keeps out a fraudster also keeps out a customer travelling, using a corporate VPN, or living behind a carrier NAT. The app is honest enough to give you a live log of what it blocked, and that log is the part to actually read — a rule set nobody reviews quietly costs sales. Also worth separating in your head: blocking bots from your analytics is a reporting fix, while blocking fraud at checkout is a money fix, and the two need different rules.

Seel is genuinely best for stores selling final-sale, high-consideration or hard-to-size products, where return anxiety is the thing killing the order — merchants report conversion lifting around 5% and shoppers taking the option roughly 24% of the time. Skip it if your margin already absorbs returns comfortably, or you need control over what appears on your own checkout — the fee is set by Seel and shown to your customer either way.

Three plans on seel.com/pricing, re-read 7 September and again 19 September 2026 (on that second reading the plan cards no longer print a monthly figure at all — all three say “Contact us” — and the $99 survives only in the FAQ below them, which states it three times; the rate card and the usage caps are unchanged): Free at $0 per store per month (no monthly platform fee), Growth at $99 per store per month, Enterprise at custom pricing. Worry-Free Purchase (formerly Return Assurance), Worry-Free Delivery and Extended Warranty are listed as included on all three, so the returns-protection product stays shopper-paid: customers who add it pay roughly $2-$5, reported elsewhere as 3-5% of order value, set by Seel's algorithm. The plans differ on the AI agencies. Free is pay-as-you-go for one agency at $0.99 per resolved ticket, $0.40 per listing, 3% of attributed GMV, $5 per store review and $29 per storefront regulation scan. Growth covers all five with capped usage — up to 100 resolved tickets, 100 listings, $500 attributed GMV, one Voice of Customer report (sentiment across your brand and three competitors), up to four 5-star reviews and one storefront regulation scan — and order tracking for 2,000 orders instead of 250; overage bills at the Free rate card. Their FAQ states the subscription is fixed per store per month and that attributed GMV does not feed it. Enterprise usage scope and commercial terms sit in the merchant agreement. Insurance benefits are provided by Seel Insurance Inc. or Arch Specialty Insurance Company, with availability varying by jurisdiction and state (re-verified 2026-09-07; on 2026-08-02 the page showed no plans or rate card). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Seel?
answers.a: Two things to weigh, and neither is the price you pay — because you do not pay one. First, you cannot set the fee. Seel's algorithm prices it, so if it lands too high for your niche and shoppers stop opting in, your only lever is switching the feature off entirely. Second, the charge appears on your checkout, not Seel's: shopper-side complaints filed with the BBB describe the fee arriving in the cart with the opt-out easy to miss, and that lands on your brand. Test it as a customer before you enable it. Also check the platform list — Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce only, with no WooCommerce, Wix or custom storefront support.

Selixer is genuinely best for Shopify fashion and apparel brands with real ad spend that want profit per SKU and per campaign in one place, and can carry the $299 tier where those features actually live. Skip it if your store is small enough that a spreadsheet still works, you need more than three connected ad accounts without paying $399, or you want a longer public track record than an app launched in May 2026 with one review.

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/selixer; unchanged since 10 September 2026) Three tiers, no free plan, each with a 14-day free trial. Essence $149 a month: two user seats, one connected ad platform, a year of historical data, the ad dashboard with campaigns and trends, stockout, overstock and dead-stock views, an inventory health score, 500 AI credits with top-ups from $25, and a site speed analyzer. Catalyst $299 a month adds four seats, two ad platforms and no date cap on history, the full True Profit waterfall, POAS, CAC and product-level ad revenue, per-product P&L and an SKU action matrix, a WhatsApp inbox with AI agent and campaigns, 50,000 emails a month with branded invoices, and 2,000 AI credits. Aether $399 a month adds eight seats, three ad platforms, all nine profit-leak detectors, multi-touch attribution and ad cohorts, demand forecasting and return on inventory, RFM scoring and retention cohorts, automations with 200,000 emails a month, and 3,000 AI credits. The listing publishes no annual rate, so all three are monthly. Charges are billed in USD, and the listing files recurring and usage-based charges together on the same 30-day cycle — the AI credits are the usage part, with top-ups starting at $25. Developer Akaame Export Private Limited; the app launched 19 May 2026 and carries a single App Store review. Two details on the same page as the plans: the entry card is labelled Essance while the Catalyst card's feature list calls the same tier Essence, and the App Store record still shows a single five-star review, from a merchant who had used the app for 15 days. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Selixer?
answers.a:
Read the feature lists rather than the prices and the entry tier stops looking like the product. Essence at $149 a month gives you two seats, one connected ad platform, a year of history and an inventory health score. The full True Profit waterfall, the per-product P&L and the POAS and CAC tracking — the reason anyone installs a profit dashboard — all start on Catalyst at $299. So the real price of what this app is sold on is double the headline.

The ad-platform caps decide the tier as much as the features do: one, then two, then three. If you run Meta, Google and TikTok you are on the $399 plan for connectivity alone, whatever your revenue looks like.

The monthly figure is also not the whole bill. Each plan carries an AI credit allowance — 500, 2,000 and 3,000 — and the listing sells top-ups from $25, with usage-based charges billed on the same 30-day cycle. Find out what spends a credit before you budget around the headline.

And this is a new app. It launched on 19 May 2026 and has one public review. There is nothing bad in the record, but there is barely any record, and this is a tool you hand your cost prices, your ad spend and your margins to. Use the 14-day trial to reconcile its numbers against a month you have already closed in your own books before you trust a dashboard you cannot yet audit.

Selleasy is genuinely best for shopify stores that want bundles, add-ons, cart funnels and post-purchase offers out of one app and would rather be billed on order volume than hand over a share of the upsell revenue — and small stores in particular, since under 50 orders a month the full strategy set costs nothing. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus and came for checkout upsells, or you want AI recommendations at any real volume: both start at Pro, $49 a month, which the App Store listing never shows — and a high-order store that runs no upsells still pays the top Starter step.

(prices read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsell-cross-sell-kit-1 and on logbase.io/products/shopify-upsell-app-selleasy) Billed in USD. The App Store listing shows one ladder, Starter, and it is priced by your store's total monthly order count rather than by anything the app does: free up to 50 orders a month, $9 from 51 to 500, $19 from 501 to 1,000, and $29 above 1,000. All four steps carry the same 18 upsell and cross-sell strategies, 50 free AI recommendations, free setup on a call and chat, email and Zoom support, with a 30-day free trial on the paid steps.

Logbase's own pricing page adds two tiers the listing does not show. Pro is $49 a month or $499 a year — $42 a month, which the site says saves $89 — and lifts the order limit entirely while adding 1,000 AI recommendations a month, an AI campaign optimizer, checkout upsells for Shopify Plus, advanced campaign targeting and metafield bulk recommendations. Max is $99 a month or $1,009 a year — $84 a month, saving $179 — adding 2,500 AI recommendations a month, advanced customization, a rules engine, an AOV advisor and priority support. An Enterprise tier is quoted on request. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Selleasy?
answers.a:
The meter is your whole store, not the app. Every Starter tier counts total store orders, so the free plan's 50-order ceiling is reached by any shop doing two orders a day whether or not a single upsell ever fired — and, read the other way, a 5,000-order store running one quiet bundle pays the top step of the ladder all the same. That cuts both ways and it is cheap in either direction, but it is not the meter most people assume they are signing up to.

Second, the App Store listing shows only the Starter ladder, so it reads as though $29 is the ceiling. It is not. Pro at $49 and Max at $99 exist only on logbase.io, and that is where AI recommendations at volume and checkout upsells for Shopify Plus sit — the two upgrades a growing store is most likely to want.

Third, every Starter tier says '50 free AI recommendations' with no period attached, while Pro says '1,000 AI recommendations/month' and Max says '2,500 AI recommendations/month'. The contrast in wording suggests the 50 is a one-off allowance rather than a monthly one, but neither page says so outright. Ask before you plan around it.

And treat the vendor's headline claims as claims: the 20% AOV increase and the 40,000+ brands are Logbase's own figures on its own site, with no methodology attached to either.

Seller Investigators is genuinely best for established FBA sellers with enough inventory movement that discrepancies add up and nobody in-house has time to file case-by-case claims — the contingency model means an audit costs you nothing but the access you grant. Skip it if you are a small seller whose monthly discrepancies are modest, where 25% of a small recovery buys less than the hour it takes to file yourself. Also skip it until you have asked what share of the claim Amazon would have paid automatically, because that is the part of the bill that buys you nothing.

answers.q: How much does Seller Investigators cost?
answers.a: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice. Once on the home page — “only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you” — and again in the FAQ: “no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”. The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover fall into five groups: inbound shipments (cancelled shipments, receiving discrepancies, carrier damage), items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, customer returns (refunds not returned within 60 days, overpayments, the wrong item returned, chargebacks), and overages and discrepancies (removal orders, incorrect weights or dimensions, overcharged orders); unfair reimbursement appears as a sub-case under both the lost and the damaged group. Re-read 29 August 2026: the 25% figure, the free 48-hour audit and the absence of any subscription are unchanged. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Seller Investigators?
answers.a: Contingency pricing is the honest kind — you pay only out of money that arrived — but 25% of a recovery is not the same as 25% of a profit, and there is one question that decides whether this is worth it for you. Amazon reimburses some categories automatically, and its policies on that have changed more than once. So ask, before you sign: which of these cases would Amazon have settled on its own within the claim window, and what exactly is the 25% charged on — the gross amount recovered, or what is left after Amazon's own fees? A free audit that finds $20,000 sounds decisive until you learn how much of it was already on its way. Ask for the split, in writing, before the audit turns into an engagement.

Seller Snap is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers past the hobby stage who compete for the Buy Box on a catalog of up to a few thousand SKUs, and want AI repricing and deep seller analytics in one place. The 15-day no-card trial makes it cheap to test against your own listings before any commitment. Skip it if you sell mainly outside Amazon and Walmart, since those are the only two marketplaces supported. Also skip it if your catalog and revenue are small enough that a rules-based repricer at a fraction of the price does the same job, or if what you actually need is multi-channel competitor price monitoring rather than marketplace Buy Box repricing.

answers.q: How much does Seller Snap cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column; every figure below was read again on that date and none of them had moved since 24 Jul 2026) There are four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features. All four list the same six feature groups: Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity and integrations. The four tiers are set out above; what the page does not tell you is what each step actually buys. Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed — while the seller ID and user counts never move at all. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The revenue ceilings themselves are printed without any period attached; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000 and $30,000 a month. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself. One thing on the page has changed and it is not a price: a banner above the plans offers 'your first month for only $1 when you subscribe before 2026', a deadline that had already passed when we read it on 26 Aug 2026, so treat it as decoration rather than an offer until support confirms it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Seller Snap?
answers.a: Read the caps before you read the prices, because the caps are what you are actually buying. Two of them deserve scrutiny. First, the revenue limits — $15,000 on Starter, $30,000 on Accelerator — are printed with no period attached on the pricing page. We asked, and Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month. That is the reading that costs you money. $15,000 a month is roughly $500 a day, so a seller who already clears that sits above Starter before signing up — and $30,000 a month puts the ceiling of Accelerator within reach of a shop doing $1,000 a day. Measure your own monthly revenue against the tier first, because the page will not do it for you. Second, the SKU limit sits at 1,000 on both of the lower tiers, so catalog growth alone — not revenue, not users — can push you up a step. And the steps are steep: leaving Accelerator for Standard means $425/month annually or $500 monthly, roughly 2.4 times what you were paying, for capacity rather than for any feature you did not already have. The cheapest door is also not quite $100: Starter is annual-billing only, so the lowest month-to-month entry into the product is $250/month. Finally, 'Starting at' appears above every monthly price on the vendor's own page — treat all of these as floors and confirm your own quote. Worth checking first, though: Amazon already includes a rule-based repricer. Automate Pricing comes with the Professional selling plan and supports rules such as Competitive Featured Offer and Competitive Lowest Price with a seller-set price floor, so if your problem is simply matching the competitive price without going below cost, test that before paying for anything. And note what sets your tier: their FAQ says pricing follows the total number of SKUs in your Seller Central account, not the active ones, so a dormant catalogue costs you money. One more thing to time correctly. In September 2026 Seller Snap began telling affiliates that its most advanced repricing engine yet had just launched, built on the premise that Amazon no longer awards one Buy Box but thousands of local ones, buyer by buyer and city by city. Their own repricing-engine page, read on 3 Sep 2026, is more careful than that: it says a redesigned app today, a new repricing engine coming soon, and it offers a waitlist and an early-access form rather than the engine itself. What has actually shipped is the redesigned app — a live Buy Box filter at SKU level, one preset across every store, repricing from a phone, and historical inventory value tracked over time. The local Buy Box logic sits behind that, still ahead of the product rather than in it. So judge the subscription on what the app does today; if the local pricing engine is the reason you are signing up, ask support for a ship date in writing before you pay for a year of it.

Sellfy is genuinely best for creators selling digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand who want a simple store with zero platform commission. Skip it if you sell occasionally (percentage-fee platforms like Gumroad cost nothing idle), or you need a full e-commerce ecosystem (Shopify territory).

(re-verified 2026-09-07) Starter is $29/mo billed monthly or $22/mo billed yearly, for up to $10k of sales a year; Business $79 or $59, up to $50k; Premium $159 or $119, up to $200k; above that Sellfy quotes you. Yearly billing saves 25%, there is a 14-day trial, a 30-day money-back guarantee and no free tier. 0% transaction fees on every plan, though PayPal or Stripe still take roughly 2.9% + 30c per transaction. The revenue limits are soft: Sellfy's own pricing.md says the store is never suspended and you are never forced to upgrade, while the page's FAQ says you are expected to upgrade and that Sellfy may instead charge a 2% overage fee on revenue above the limit. Read in US dollars from a Netherlands connection. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Sellfy?
answers.a: The honest mechanic is the revenue ladder: plans cap by your ANNUAL SALES, so success moves you up. But the caps are soft - Sellfy's FAQ says it may charge 2% on revenue above your limit rather than forcing an upgrade, so ask whether that applies to you before jumping a tier. The 0% transaction fee is genuinely rare and beats percentage-taking platforms at volume; below a few hundred in monthly sales the flat subscription is the tax instead, and your processor still takes about 2.9% + 30c regardless.

Sendcloud is genuinely best for European e-commerce stores that want easy multi-carrier shipping (DHL, PostNL, Colissimo, GLS, DPD), branded tracking and a returns portal live in under 30 minutes. Skip it if you ship mainly in the US, need inventory management and complex fulfilment, or you're a very high-volume shipper wanting deep customisation — ShipStation fits that better.

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Free plan €0/mo: up to 20 parcels a month, no courier contract, no subscription, €0.50 a label beyond that. Paid tiers at the monthly rate: Lite €28/mo + €0.10 per label, Growth €87/mo + €0.09, Premium €175/mo + €0.08, Pro €639/mo + €0.07. Every tier also has a MONTHLY label cap (Lite 400, Growth 1,000, Premium 10,000, Pro 30,000) and past it each extra label costs €0.15 on top of the plan rate. Users: 1 free, 3 Lite, 5 Growth, 10 Premium, unlimited Pro. 14-day free trial, no card. The page advertises a yearly option at -20% but the discounted figures are not in the served HTML. You can only ship FROM eight European countries. (2026) Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Sendcloud?
answers.a: The pricing has layers — a per-label fee on top of the subscription, plus carrier surcharges that can land on invoices weeks later. It's built out-of-the-box, so deep customisation is limited, there's no inventory management (ShipStation has it), and high-volume shippers (€12k+/mo) plus pickup-reliability complaints suggest it's happiest with small-to-mid EU stores.

Sentaro is genuinely best for SMBs on Google Workspace/M365 that want an extra AI layer against phishing and BEC without infrastructure changes. Skip it if you already run a mature email-security stack (Ironscales/Abnormal-class), or nobody internally will review the flagged-mail queue.

(read 5 September 2026 on sentaro.com, pricing section) Two plans. Professional is $6 per user per month billed monthly, or $5.50 per user per month billed annually — the toggle labels that discount as -8%. A currency switcher sits beside the billing toggle and offers the identical numerals in euros: €6 and €5,50. That is not a conversion, so a European buyer pays roughly 15% more for the same seat. Enterprise publishes no figure at all, only 'Custom pricing'. What Professional includes: real-time email risk analysis, Threat / Suspicious / Safe labels in the inbox, phishing, spoofing and impersonation detection, working directly inside Gmail and Outlook, and organization-wide deployment. What sits above it on Enterprise: SSO / SCIM, advanced admin controls, API access, custom policies, dedicated support, and compliance and audit support. Sentaro connects to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 through the API rather than by changing MX records. History: until August 2026 no price was published at all. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Sentaro?
answers.a: The category claim (AI catches what filters miss) is plausible — Microsoft/Google native filtering misses sophisticated BEC — but any vendor's accuracy percentage is measured on their own test set, not your mail flow. The honest procurement move: run their trial alongside your current filtering, count real catches and false positives for two weeks, and price per mailbox against the incumbents with that data in hand.

Serpstat is genuinely best for solo SEOs and small in-house teams who want the whole workflow — keywords, rankings, audit, competitors — under one subscription at roughly a third of what the incumbents charge, and who will judge the data on their own market during the trial. Skip it if your work depends on deep backlink analysis, since the 10,000 results per report ceiling does not move no matter which tier you buy; or you need more than three seats, because seats are not sold separately and the next tier roughly doubles the bill.

(2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four plans, and the page opens on the annual view — so the first number you see is not the month-to-month price. Individual $69/month, or $50 on annual billing. Team $129, or $100 annually. Team x2 $209, or $169. Agency $499, or $410. There is a hidden middle step: two dropdowns inside the Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000) move Team to $169/month monthly or $135 annually, so Team is really three price points. Seats are capped rather than sold: Individual is single-user, Team 3, Team x2 6, Agency 30, and no per-seat price is published anywhere — a fourth user means the next tier. The limits matter more than the prices: 100 searches a day on Individual (500 / 1,000 / 5,000 above it), export rows 50,000 a month, and no API at all on the entry plan. The 7-day trial takes a card, charges $1 to verify, turns on auto-renewal and bills the plan after seven days unless you cancel. Re-verified 2026-08-26: the four annual prices are unchanged, and the page now heads the table with 'save up to 27% with annual discount' and prints the saving per plan — $228, $348, $484 and $1,068 a year. That is the arithmetic that turns $50, $100, $169 and $410 back into $69, $129, $209 and $499, which matters because the monthly column itself is not in the page's HTML at all; only the annual one renders. The comparison table still carries the two-value Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000), so the hidden middle step is still there, but its price is printed nowhere on the page today. Three limits worth reading before anyone picks Individual: Site Audit does no JavaScript rendering on that plan, it scans at most 5,000 pages, and its data retention figure is 2 where Team gets 10 and Agency 100. Re-verified 2026-09-19 on the same page: the four annual figures, the four annual savings and the two-value Team column are all unchanged, as are the seat caps of 1, 3, 6 and 30 and the seven-day trial with its $1 card verification and automatic renewal. What is new on the page is what the plans now sell rather than what they cost — Team upward advertises a ChatGPT and Claude integration over MCP and an AI Overview brand-opportunities report, and a separate LLM Brand Monitor is promoted underneath the plans with its own free scan and no price attached to it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Serpstat?
answers.a: The thing you are actually buying is data coverage, and that is the one thing you cannot verify — Serpstat's own published figures do not agree with each other. Re-read on 24 July 2026, their homepage says 529 billion backlinks, their data hub says 1.1 trillion, and their backlinks page says 1.7 trillion in the prose while its own spec block on that same page says 1.1 trillion. The keyword count reads 8.62 billion on one page and 7.46 billion on another. That is not evidence the data is thin; it is evidence that these numbers cannot serve as a basis for your decision. Judge it on your own searches during the trial instead. Two other things to weigh. Backlink reports are capped at 10,000 results per report on Team, Team x2 and Agency alike, so paying from $129 to $499 buys more of everything except a deeper backlink report. And 'maximum pages to scan' in a single crawl (5,000 / 25,000 / 50,000) is a far smaller number than the monthly 'pages to audit' allowance it sits next to.

ServiceM8 is genuinely best for trades and service businesses with a crew, where per-user pricing elsewhere punishes you for having enough people — this is one of the few tools in the category that does not. Skip it if you are a sole trader doing a handful of jobs a month — the free tier covers that, and at low job volume the paid tiers are buying capacity rather than features.

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on their own pricing page, USD) Priced by jobs per month, with unlimited users on every paid tier. Free $0: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, SMS at 10c each. Starter $29: unlimited users, 50 jobs. Growing $79: 150 jobs. Premium $149: 500 jobs. Premium Plus $349: 1,500+ jobs, with additional jobs at 20c each — the only tier where the page prices an overage. Text messaging is listed as free on all four paid tiers, but the FAQ states there is an overage fee per SMS above each plan's monthly SMS cap, and neither the caps nor that fee are printed. Going over the job ceiling is not a hard stop: the FAQ gives seven further days of normal use, after which you either reach your monthly reset or are prompted to upgrade. A 14-day free trial with full feature access is offered and needs no card; there are no lock-ins and changes are pro-rata. The AI Smart Helper is listed as available on All Plans and the page prints no daily usage cap for it (our August reading recorded ten uses a day on Free; that limit no longer appears on this page). The full app is iOS; Android is served by the cut-down ServiceM8 Lite. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with ServiceM8?
answers.a: Unlimited users on every paid tier is genuinely unusual in this category and worth saying first: put your whole crew in without the bill moving. The meter is jobs instead, and jobs are the thing you least control. Fifty a month on Starter is roughly two a working day, which a two-van operation passes in a busy month — and the next step is not a small one, it is $29 to $79. Count your jobs in your best month rather than your average, because that is the month that will bump you, and a seasonal trade will spend part of the year paying for a tier it does not need. The free tier at 30 jobs and one user is a real trial, not a plan.

Shiftie is genuinely best for shift-based businesses (hospitality, retail, leisure) that want quick rota building, clock-ins and leave management without spreadsheet pain. Skip it if you need full HR, payroll and performance management in one system, or your team doesn't work in shifts at all.

(price re-verified 2026-09-05) £2.75 per active employee per month for the first 30, then £1.50 for each employee above 30 — the reduced rate is marginal, not retroactive. Measured on the vendor's own pricing slider: 1 employee £2.75, 5 £13.75, 10 £27.50, 15 £41.25, 30 £82.50, 31 £84.00, 50 £112.50, 100 £187.50, 150 £262.50, 199 £336.00. At 200 employees the slider stops quoting and switches to Custom Pricing. There is no minimum and no entry-plan floor: one employee costs £2.75. Monthly billing only — no annual option is offered anywhere on the page. Billing is in arrears: at the start of each month you are charged for users marked active during the previous month. 28-day free trial, no card details required, and 7-day UK-based support included. Note the domain move: shiftie.co.uk now redirects to shiftie.co. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shiftie?
answers.a: It's focused, affordable rota software — which means it does scheduling, clock-ins, leave and swaps well, but it isn't a full HR or payroll platform, so a growing business will still bolt on payroll and HR tools around it. Pricing is genuinely low, but the per-active-employee model means a large seasonal team in a busy month costs more than the headline suggests. For shift-based scheduling specifically, it's a clean, cheap fit.

Shipdock is genuinely best for Shopify merchants shipping in Central and Eastern Europe who want pickup points, multi-carrier label printing and cash-on-delivery tracking in one app rather than one integration per carrier — and who are on Shopify Plus, where the pickup-point picker sits inside checkout instead of after it. Skip it if your carriers are not in its list, which is the first thing to check, since the app's centre of gravity is Packeta and the Central European networks; or you need a label only occasionally, when a CSV export and your carrier's portal cost nothing.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/packeta) Three tiers, no free plan, every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026, and the entry tier still names its own limitation. Lite is $9.99 a month or $107.88 a year and is labelled 'only CSV': pickup point and home delivery, an email reminder, the pickup-point widget on the thank-you and order-status pages, unlimited carriers across more than twenty, and an order export to custom CSV. Basic is $14.99 or $161.89 a year and is the first tier that prints shipping labels, adding parcels created automatically after fulfilment and cash-on-delivery payment tracking. Shopify Plus is $24.99 or $269.89 and moves the pickup-point widget into the checkout itself rather than the pages after it. Annual billing saves a stated 10% on each. Trials are five days on Lite and Basic and ten on Plus. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. The listing now names its carriers rather than counting them: Packeta, Balíkovna, DPD, Magyar Posta, InPost, DHL24, Posti, GLS and myGLS, Omniva, Foxpost, PPL, One, Telli, Eserviss, Esiunt, Slovenská pošta, Česká pošta, Fan Courier, Easyship, Econt and PostNord. Developer happyapps.cz; the app sits in Shopify's delivery and pickup category, is offered in English and Czech, and carries 42 reviews at a 5.0 rating — the same total as in August, but now with every one of the 42 at five stars where our earlier reading recorded one at four. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shipdock?
answers.a:
Read the carrier list against your own country before anything else. The listing slug is 'packeta', the developer is happyapps.cz, and cash-on-delivery tracking is a headline feature — all three point at Central and Eastern Europe, where Packeta and Zásilkovna are everyday carriers and COD is a normal way to pay. More than twenty carriers are supported, but a US or UK merchant should confirm theirs is among them before the five-day trial starts.

The second thing is the trial length against the job. Five days on Lite and Basic is short for a shipping integration, because the test that matters is a real order going out with a real label to a real address. Install it on a day you are actually shipping, not on a quiet Sunday.

Shippo is genuinely best for e-commerce sellers shipping across multiple carriers who want rate comparison, label printing and tracking in one place with genuine rate discounts. Skip it if you ship a handful of packages monthly through one carrier (their native tools are fine), or you're big enough for direct carrier contracts to beat aggregated rates.

Read on their own pricing page, 6 September 2026. Starter is free: up to 30 labels a month, discounted USPS, UPS, FedEx and DHL Express rates, 1 user login, and 5¢ per label if you connect your own carrier account. Pro is banded by monthly label volume, priced monthly or annually: 1-200 labels $19/mo or $205/yr; 201-500 $29 or $313; 501-1,000 $54 or $583; 1,001-2,500 $79 or $853; 2,501-5,000 $139 or $1,501; 5,001-10,000 $199 or $2,149. Annual billing saves about 10% at every band. Labels beyond 10,000 a month cost $0.08 each. Pro makes your own carrier accounts free and adds branded tracking, chat and phone support. Premier is contact-us: unlimited shipments, 15+ logins, a dedicated account manager. Non-US address validation is metered separately at 9¢, 8¢ and 6¢ per validation on Starter, Pro and Premier. API calls not tied to a Shippo label, and the Estimate API, bill at API Starter rates. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shippo?
answers.a: The pricing is honest but layered. The free tier stops at 30 labels a month, and its 5¢ per label on your own carrier accounts quietly adds up. Pro looks like a flat $17 a month until you read the comparison table: it covers up to 10,000 shipments and then bills $0.08 for every label beyond that, so a good sales month adds a variable line to a subscription that reads as fixed. Address validation outside the US is metered too, at 9¢, 8¢ or 6¢ depending on plan. The real money is elsewhere anyway — in the carrier rate discounts, which vary by lane and weight. Run your five most common shipments through it against your current rates; that comparison decides, not the subscription price.

Shoeboxed is genuinely best for businesses drowning in PAPER receipts — trades, field crews, owners with shoeboxes of history — who want them humanly digitized, verified and IRS-ready. Skip it if your receipts are mostly digital already (lighter OCR apps cost less), or your accountant's tooling ingests receipts natively.

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Four plans, each quoted both yearly and monthly: Starter $97/yr or $9/mo (30 digital scans/mo, 20 paper scans/yr, 1 Magic Envelope/yr, 1 user, 3 years of scan storage); Pro $297/yr or $29/mo (200 digital scans/mo, 20 paper scans/mo, 1 Magic Envelope per quarter, Gmail receipt sync, QuickBooks Online/Xero, 3 users); Plus $797/yr or $79/mo (750 digital scans/mo, 50 paper scans/mo, 1 Magic Envelope/mo, 10 users); Paper Plus $1,997/yr or $179/mo (500 digital scans/mo, 200 paper scans/mo, 2 envelopes/mo). Overages by tier: $0.30/$0.15/$0.10 per digital scan, $2.00 or $1.50 per paper scan, $9 per extra envelope. Unlimited mileage tracking on every plan. A 30-day money-back guarantee rather than a free trial — the card is charged at signup, and the vendor asks you not to claim the refund once a Magic Envelope has shipped. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shoeboxed?
answers.a: Its unique trick is the Magic Envelope, where you literally mail a stuffed envelope of paper receipts and humans digitize them. That trick is also the meter to watch: envelope frequency defines the tiers, and heavy paper businesses land in the $179/mo bracket quickly. If your receipts are already digital, cheaper scan-only apps exist; Shoeboxed earns its price precisely when physical paper is the problem.

Shorby is genuinely best for creators and businesses that sell via messenger conversations or retarget link-in-bio traffic with ad pixels. Skip it if you just need a links page (free tools abound), or your audience doesn't click through to chat apps.

(re-verified 2026-09-06 at dash.shorby.com/pricing) Three paid plans, no free plan on the table. Rocket $15/mo, or $12/mo billed annually ($36 off the year); Pro $29/mo, or $24/mo annually ($60 off); Agency $99/mo, or $82/mo annually ($204 off). Pages included: 5 on Rocket, 50 on Pro, 250 on Agency, with Agency adding Projects and Teams from three up. Direct messenger buttons, Click Insights and Shor Rewards are on all three; Google Analytics, custom domains (per project) and Dynamic Feeds (5 per page) start at Pro. The table states all prices are in USD and all sales are final. Note that the marketing site's own /pricing/ page renders nothing — this table is only reachable at dash.shorby.com. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shorby?
answers.a: In a category where the market leader has a generous free plan, Shorby charges from day one, so it has to earn the gap. Its case rests on two genuinely differentiated features: messenger deep-links, one tap into WhatsApp/Telegram chats, and retargeting pixels firing on every click. If you use neither, Linktree's free tier wins; if messenger-first selling or ad retargeting is your funnel, the $15 pays for itself.

Shore is genuinely best for salons, barbers, spas, wellness studios, physical therapists, craftspeople and local retailers that want bookings via Google and Instagram, no-show-reducing reminders, marketing and (optionally) POS in one fixed-price system. Skip it if you just need a simple scheduling link (a Calendly-class tool is lighter) or you run a business without appointments at all.

(2026-09-07, read on their own pricing pages in English and German, in euros) Three packages, each showing two figures that are a billing choice rather than a discount: the higher is the monthly-billing rate, the lower is the rate per month when you pay for the year. Starter EUR 59.90 / EUR 49.90 with 2 employees included, Growth EUR 89.90 / EUR 79.90 with 4, and Team EUR 129.90 / EUR 119.90 with unlimited employees. The toggle reads 'Yearly (Save EUR 120)' against 'Monthly', and EUR 120 is exactly the EUR 10 monthly gap over twelve months. Card payments run at up to 1.35% on every tier. There is a 14-day free trial. POS hardware is published separately: the Shore Complete bundle is EUR 1,499, with a card reader at EUR 69, dock EUR 49, stand EUR 199, cash drawer EUR 99 and Epson receipt printer EUR 269. Add-ons: a professional website at EUR 65/month and a branded web app at EUR 40/month. The POS is only sold in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Paying yearly carries a 12-month initial term; monthly billing cancels with 14 days' notice to the end of the period. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Shore?
answers.a: It's built for local appointment businesses, and that's also the boundary: the integration list is short (calendar, Google, Instagram, Meta), and once you add POS and payments the monthly total climbs well past the entry price. If you only need a booking link, this is more machine than you need.

SignNow is genuinely best for teams that sign at volume and want unlimited users at a flat rate — roughly 60% under DocuSign for the same core job. Skip it if you need the deepest enterprise integrations and workflows — that's where the incumbent still earns its premium.

Three seat plans, read on signnow.com/pricing.md on 7 September 2026: Business at $8 per user a month on annual billing, Business Premium at $15 and Enterprise at $30, with month-to-month priced higher (read at EUR 20 / EUR 30 / EUR 50 from the EU on 5 September 2026). A Site License is billed at $1.50 per signature invite instead of per seat, aimed at organisations sending 1,000+ documents a year, and is where SSO, full API access and phone support appear; HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11 and QES are add-ons on top. airSlate Business Cloud is $50 per user a month and bundles signNow with airSlate, pdfFiller and US Legal Forms. signNow states unlimited users on all paid plans and no envelope cap. Free 7-day trial, no credit card required. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SignNow?
answers.a: It's built for straightforward everyday signing — if you need deep contract-lifecycle (CLM) features, a heavier platform fits better.

Signal House is genuinely best for teams sending real SMS volume in the US who already know what an A2P 10DLC campaign is and want a cheaper per-segment rate than Twilio’s list without giving up published pricing. The volume ladder is genuinely steep — from $0.0065 down to $0.0030 — so the case gets stronger the more you send, and the number discounts above 500 numbers suit anyone running many local presences. Skip it if you are mainly buying voice, because there is no published rate to compare and no way to model the cost. Skip it too if your volume is small: at a few thousand messages a month the per-segment saving against Twilio is a few dollars, and you would be trading a mature ecosystem and documentation for that. And if you are not already registered for A2P 10DLC, budget the brand and campaign fees plus the approval wait before you compare anything — those apply wherever you send from.

answers.q: How much does Signal House cost?
answers.a: (2026-09-11, re-read on their own pricing page) Usage-based, no platform subscription. SMS on a 10DLC local number costs $0.0065 per segment with no minimum, falling on volume: $0.0050 from 500k segments a month, $0.0045 from 1m, $0.0040 from 2m, $0.0035 from 5m and $0.0030 from 10m. Numbers are $1.00 a month, dropping to $0.50 between 500 and 1,000 numbers and $0.25 above 1,000. MMS is $0.0200 per segment, $0.0170 above 500k. Toll-free numbers are $1.00 a month with SMS from $0.0079 down to $0.0050. Number lookup is $0.005. A2P 10DLC registration is billed separately: $4.50 for the brand, $15 one-time per campaign, then $1.50 a month for a low-volume campaign or $10 a month for a standard one. Carrier fees are passed through on top and are published per carrier for both directions: outbound SMS is AT&T $0.0035, Verizon $0.0045, T-Mobile $0.0045 and US Cellular $0.0025, while outbound MMS costs two to three times as much — AT&T $0.009, Verizon $0.007, T-Mobile $0.01, US Cellular $0.005. Inbound SMS is AT&T $0.0035, T-Mobile $0.0025, US Cellular $0.0025 and free on Verizon. A2P approval is quoted at 72 hours or less, dropping to 48 hours above 500k segments a month. Every rate table carries the note that all rates are negotiable on volume and agreement terms, and the site's roadmap still lists Voice, Short Code, RCS and Alphanumeric as Coming Soon. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Signal House?
answers.a:
Two things are missing from a page that is otherwise unusually specific. The first is voice. The product is sold as an SMS and Voice API and the pricing page publishes no voice rate at all — nor short code pricing. If the voice half is why you are looking, you cannot budget it from public information and will have to ask.

The second is the arithmetic behind the Twilio comparison, which is the whole pitch. Take the entry rate with no minimum. Signal House is $0.0065 a segment against Twilio’s $0.0083, which reads as a 22% saving. But carrier fees are a pass-through and identical either way: add T-Mobile’s $0.0045 to both and you get $0.0110 against $0.0128 — about 14%, not 22%. Numbers narrow it further, $1.00 against $1.15. So the saving is real and it is worth having at volume, but it is a discount on the platform margin rather than on your bill, and the headline does not make that distinction. On a million segments a month that difference is roughly $1,800 a month against Twilio’s list — worth switching for, provided the voice side does not turn out to be where the money goes.

Worth noting on the other side: Signal House prints its A2P 10DLC registration fees on the pricing page, and Twilio’s equivalent page says only that fees apply and points elsewhere. Being able to see the whole bill before you sign is not nothing.

Signeasy is genuinely best for small teams that want straightforward unlimited sending and signing per seat, with contract management one tier up. Skip it if you only sign occasional documents, or you are a solo sender at volume — Personal is single-seat and sending-limited.

(price re-verified 2026-08-17 against signeasy.com) (2026) Free trial. Personal $10/mo billed yearly ($120) — single seat, built around signing. Business $20/mo per seat billed yearly ($240/seat) adds unlimited sending and collaboration; Business Pro $30/mo per seat ($360/seat) adds end-to-end contract management with roles. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Signeasy?
answers.a: The $10 Personal plan is annual-billed and single-seat — and note that sign-unlimited is not send-unlimited: proper unlimited sending starts at Business, $20 per seat on a yearly commitment, while contract-management features gate at Business Pro, $30 per seat.

Signitic is genuinely best for European organisations of roughly twenty people and up, on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, that want every signature centrally controlled and the banner slot run as a measurable campaign channel — and that need EU hosting and ISO 27001 on the record. Skip it if you have fewer than twenty employees, where the free plan is the whole offer and the paid tier cannot be bought below its 20-licence minimum, or your people sit on Outlook 2013-2021 or Apple Mail and would land on the agent with its plain signatures rather than the add-in.

(price read 2026-09-14) Signitic's own pricing page, read in euros from a European connection, carries three tiers. Free covers organisations up to 19 employees and gives one signature template, one banner campaign, and a Signitic badge at the bottom of every signature that the plan does not let you remove. The paid tier — the card the page marks Most popular — is €1 per user with a minimum of 20 licences, and it is where the caps come off: unlimited signature templates, unlimited banner campaigns, a custom subdomain for deliverability, multi-entity segmentation, A/B testing with click statistics, and no badge. That card prints the euro and the word user but never a period; the ROI calculator further down the same page settles it, pricing 100 employees at 1 200 € a year, which is twelve euros per user per year — so the euro is monthly, and the 20-licence minimum puts the real floor at twenty euros a month. The third tier is Custom and carries no public figure: advanced permission management, campaign targeting from CRM lists, HRIS/SFTP integration, vCard digital business cards and a dedicated support team all sit behind a quote. Registered non-profits are offered 50% off subject to an eligibility check. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Signitic?
answers.a: The homepage sells deployment 'without going through IT', and Signitic's own help centre contradicts that on every path in. Connecting Google Workspace is possible only from the Super Admin profile, and if that admin ever changes you have to reconnect or call support. Microsoft 365 needs an Azure Active Directory administrator account. Rolling out the Outlook add-in — the fuller of the two Microsoft options — needs a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator plus the Exchange Administrator role carrying the ReadWriteMailbox permission, must not be installed by end users themselves, and can take up to 72 hours to appear in people's Outlook. Marketing does keep the keys afterwards, which is the real promise; it does not get them without IT first. The add-in also needs a Microsoft 365 Outlook licence at version 16.0.14026.20000 or later, so Outlook 2013 to 2021 and Apple Mail fall back to the Signitic agent, which pushes plain signatures instead.

Similarweb is genuinely best for a single analyst or marketer who needs competitor traffic and channel estimates often enough to justify $125 a month, and teams who are prepared to negotiate an annual contract for more than one seat. Skip it if you want a quick check on one competitor — the free tier and public estimates cover that, and the cheapest paid plan is $125 a month for a single user.

(read 2026-08-25 on their own pricing page) The entrepreneur plans are published: $125 per month on annual billing for Competitive Intelligence, $333 for Competitive Intel & SEO & AEO, and $542 for Competitive Intel, SEO & AEO & Ads — or $199, $399 and $649 respectively on monthly billing, each for a single user. Included history differs by plan and is easy to miss: 3 months on the entry plan, 6 months on the two above it. What is not published is the business and enterprise tab: it carries no figure at all and routes every tier to 'Talk to sales' for a custom package, and the FAQ repeats that premium features require one. A free trial is offered without a stated length. Up to 37 months of data history is sold as an add-on rather than an inclusion, and API access is either standalone or inside a custom package. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Similarweb?
answers.a: Similarweb does publish a price — $125 a month for one seat on annual billing, or $199 if you pay monthly. What it does not publish is anything above one seat: the business and enterprise tab carries no figure at all and routes straight to a sales call, where the number depends on what they think you can pay. So the decision splits in two. One analyst can price this today and start a trial without speaking to anyone. A team walks into a negotiation, and should walk in with a ceiling already written down — plus the two line items priced apart from the seats: 37 months of data history is an add-on, and API access is quoted separately.

SimpleTexting is genuinely best for US businesses that want straightforward, compliant SMS marketing and two-way texting with rollover credits. Skip it if you don't have a real opted-in list or a compelling offer — texting a cold audience burns money and trust.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on simpletexting.com/pricing) Credit-based by monthly volume, and the headline is not the plan price: the page's "estimated monthly cost" bundles a $10/mo local number into every figure. The credit plans themselves are $29 (500 credits), $49 (1,000), $79 (2,000), $109 (3,000), $229 (7,500), $399 (15,000), $549 (25,000) and $899 (50,000) a month, so the printed $39 to $909 range is those figures plus the number. SMS = 1 credit, an extended message up to 306 characters = 2, MMS = 3; incoming SMS is free and incoming MMS costs 1 credit. Extra credits beyond the plan taper with the tier, from 5.5 cents at 500 to 2 cents at 50,000. Yearly billing takes 20% off the credit portion only — the entry tier becomes $23.20 of credits plus the same $10 number, i.e. $33.20 a month billed yearly at $398.40 — and grants the year's credits as one upfront bucket (6,000 at the entry tier) instead of a monthly allowance. The rollover rule the page states is for monthly plans: unused plan credits roll over until the end of the following month. Every paid plan includes three user seats, with additional seats at $20/mo and additional numbers at $10/mo; a local number carries a $4 activation fee and there is a separate one-off $4 carrier (10DLC) registration. A toll-free number has no additional monthly fee but carrier approval can take up to a week; dedicated short codes begin at $1,000/mo and take 6-8 weeks to provision. Carrier fees are passed through without markup at roughly $0.0025 per message in the US and $0.0068 in Canada. Nonprofits, churches and other tax-exempt organisations get 15% off any monthly plan, and there is a 30-day refund. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SimpleTexting?
