answers.a: The credit model plus US carrier (10DLC) fees and per-number/per-seat add-ons mean the sticker isn't the whole bill — and SMS marketing only works with genuine opt-in and a real offer, not blasting a cold list.

SimplyBook.me is genuinely best for service businesses that take appointments and want a booking page, reminders and online payment without building one. Skip it if you only need a simple calendar link for one person — a free scheduling link does that without a booking system on top.

(2026, re-verified 2026-09-11 on their own pricing page, in euros; every figure below unchanged since 2 August 2026) Free EUR 0: 50 bookings a month, 1 custom feature, 1 provider, no card needed. Basic EUR 11.90/month billed annually or EUR 13.90 monthly: 100 bookings, 3 custom features, 5 providers. Standard EUR 24.90 annual or EUR 29.90 monthly: 500 bookings, 8 custom features, 15 providers. Premium EUR 49.90 annual or EUR 59.90 monthly: 2,000 bookings, unlimited custom features, 30 providers. Enterprise is quote-only. Annual billing saves a stated 17%. Their own page says no setup fees, no transaction fees and no per-user charges — payment processors bill their own rates separately. A 14-day trial of premium features runs without a card. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SimplyBook.me?
answers.a: The plan ladder is set by bookings per month and by how many custom features you may switch on, and those two ceilings move independently — so you can outgrow a plan on features while nowhere near the booking cap, or the reverse. Free and Basic also carry SimplyBook.me branding on your booking page; white-label starts at Premium.

answers.q: Is Skip To Checkout worth it?
answers.a: Skip To Checkout is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want a free sticky buy button, or who need to hide add-to-cart and express-payment buttons on products they list online but sell in person. Skip it if your cart page carries shipping thresholds, discount codes or upsells you depend on, you manage the store on add-to-cart rate and cannot afford to lose that signal, or you are unwilling to grant read and write access to customers, products and analytics for a display widget.

answers.q: How much does Skip To Checkout cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/cart-auto-update) Free, and free is the only plan. The listing carries no pricing table at all: no paid tier, no usage meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan. The app has been on the App Store since 29 November 2019 and carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, which is the store's own bar for performance, design and integration. One of the 34 reviews alleges being billed twice, which is worth knowing about an app the listing prices at nothing; we cannot verify that claim from the outside, and the listing shows no charge to make. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Skip To Checkout?
answers.a: The cart skip blinds the measurement you would use to judge it. The vendor's own help article confirms that bypassing Add To Cart and Start Checkout makes your add-to-cart rate read lower, and recommends watching overall sales trends instead — so the feature is sold on conversion while switching off the funnel that would show it. Skipping the cart also bypasses the page where shipping thresholds, discount codes and cart upsells normally work. For a free widget the permissions are broad: view and edit customers, products, store analytics, Shopify Functions and the online store, plus customer device and activity data. And because there is no paid tier there is no support contract behind it; what you get is the vendor's goodwill, which a six-year run and a 4.6 average suggest is real, but is not something you can buy more of. The app also carries at least three different names across the listing, the help centre index and its own setup article, which makes it harder to know what you are running.

SmartSuite is genuinely best for teams consolidating projects, CRM and operations into one flexible, database-driven work-management platform. Skip it if you need a lightweight to-do or a single-purpose tool — SmartSuite's breadth is wasted and its learning curve isn't worth it.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page, USD; unchanged since our August reading) No free plan — a 14-day trial of Professional with no credit card, and the page states there is no auto-charge when it ends. Team is $15 per seat a month billed annually, or $20 billed monthly, with a minimum of 3 billable users, 5,000 records per solution, 50GB of storage and a 30-day recycle bin. Professional is $32 per seat annually, or $36 monthly, with a minimum of 5 billable users, 100,000 records, 100GB and 45 days. Enterprise is quote-only and lifts those to 400,000 records, 500GB and 60 days, adding SSO, SCIM, audit logs, IP restrictions, data-loss prevention and European data residency; a further Signature plan sits above it, also on request. The minimums matter more than the rate: a three-person team on Team pays for three seats whether or not all three log in, and Professional cannot be bought for fewer than five, so the real entry price is $45 a month on Team and $160 on Professional rather than the per-seat figures on the cards. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SmartSuite?
answers.a: It's a broad, do-everything work-management platform, so the power comes with a learning curve and a per-seat cost that adds up for bigger teams — a single source of truth if you commit, overkill if you just need a task list.

Smartli is genuinely best for e-commerce sellers who want an affordable all-in-one AI suite to draft product listings, ad copy, SEO text and basic brand assets in one place. Skip it if you need best-in-class depth in one area (a specialist copy or image tool), or you won't edit and fact-check AI output before it ships.

(re-verified 2026-09-11 on smartli.ai/pricing; Monthly and Yearly tabs both unchanged since 5 Aug 2026) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 7-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Starter was $29/mo when we first checked, so the entry price has gone up. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Smartli?
answers.a: Smartli bundles nine AI tools — copy, SEO, images, logos — into one suite, and that breadth is also the honest catch: each individual tool is competent rather than best-in-class, so a team that leans hard on one job may outgrow it toward a specialist. And like all AI copy, its product descriptions and ad copy need a human edit and a fact-check — never publish specs or claims it invents about your product. For a store that wants many content jobs handled cheaply in one place, it's efficient.

Smarty Discounts is genuinely best for Shopify merchants whose promotions have outgrown the native discount engine — capped amounts, a fixed amount that behaves correctly in several currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts, mix-and-match — and who want to build them with rules rather than with a developer, targeting by product, customer, cart, market, country or company. Skip it if your promotions are ordinary percentage or fixed-amount codes, which Shopify's built-in discounts already do for free; or you want a long support and reliability record before a young app gets write access to the discounts in your checkout.

answers.q: How much does Smarty Discounts cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/smarty-discount) Three tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Forever Free costs nothing, Lite is $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, and Pro is $25.99 a month or $259.99 a year; the annual price on both paid tiers saves 17%, and both carry a 7-day free trial. What you are buying is capability, not volume: there is no order cap, no revenue meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan anywhere in the block. Free covers product and order discounts with basic targeting and what the listing itself calls low support. Lite adds shipping and mix-and-match discounts, enhanced targeting and priority support. Pro unlocks every discount type, every targeting rule, active time periods and free shipping on a single rule. One detail in the plan table is worth reading twice, because it is unusual and it is in your favour: each tier gives unlimited discounts at its own level plus up to two at the level above. On Free you can build two Lite-grade discounts, on Lite two Pro-grade ones. That is a working trial of the next tier rather than a locked door, and it means you can prove the rule you actually need before you pay for it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Smarty Discounts?
answers.a: The evidence base is thin. The app launched on 14 January 2025 and carries six reviews as of 4 September 2026 — all five stars, but six is not a track record, and the vendor, Neezon, is a small developer in Ho Chi Minh City rather than a company with a support contract behind it. The listing is unusually candid about what that means at the bottom of the ladder: the free plan's own feature list says low support. Add to that what the app needs to do its job. The data-access panel says it reads customer data flagged as sensitive and can view and edit customers, products, discounts and the Online Store, which is the access any discount engine needs but is still broad. And because the ladder gates discount types rather than volume, the plan you land on is decided by the one rule you cannot live without: if the campaign you have in mind needs time-period scheduling or free shipping on a single rule, you are on Pro at $25.99 regardless of how few discounts you run.

Social Bar is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want branded social icons and a WhatsApp chat button on product pages without touching theme code, and who will use the built-in click counter to check whether anyone taps them. Skip it if your theme already places social links where you need them, you are unwilling to pay a recurring fee for a display element, or you are looking for real social proof such as reviews, user content or engagement analytics rather than a row of icons.

answers.q: How much does Social Bar cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/sticky-social-media-icons-bar) Two plans, and the free one is not the one you will be on. Development is free but the listing limits it explicitly to development and partner stores, with billing activated on upgrade — so a real storefront does not run on it. The Monthly Plan is $4.99 a month, or $41.88 a year which the listing presents as a 30 percent saving, after a 7-day free trial. All charges are billed in USD and recurring charges are invoiced every 30 days. The app has been on the App Store since 27 April 2020 and carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Social Bar?
answers.a: This is a styling subscription, and the listing's own framing oversells it: social icons and share buttons build no trust on their own, and 'boost sales with social proof' is a claim the app has no way to support. The free plan is free in a way that will not help you, since it is restricted to development and partner stores, so any live store is on $4.99 a month or $41.88 a year for something most themes already do in the footer. The 5.0 average deserves reading rather than trusting: two of the three reviews on the listing were written after 11 and 13 minutes of use and praise setup rather than results, while the one longer-running reviewer reports that icon placement is limited and the app is tricky to figure out at first. And more than 80 platform options mainly tempts you to advertise accounts you no longer maintain.

SocialBee is genuinely best for solo marketers and small agencies who post to several networks on a schedule and want evergreen recycling rather than a queue that empties. Skip it if you post to one or two networks by hand and are happy doing it, because the value here is category-based recycling across many profiles and that only pays back at volume.

(2026-08-30, read on their own pricing page) Bootstrap $29/month ($290 a year, 16% off): 5 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Accelerate $49/month ($490 a year): 10 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Pro $99/month ($990 a year): 25 profiles, 5 workspaces, 3 users per workspace. Agency tiers billed monthly: Pro50 $179, Pro100 $329, Pro150 $449 for 50, 100 and 150 profiles, with 10, 20 and 30 workspaces and 5 users per workspace; billed yearly they are $149.20, $274.20 and $374.20 a month. Add-ons: 5 extra profiles $15/month or $150/year, an extra user $10/month or $100/year, an extra workspace $10/month or $100/year. AI generation is unlimited on every tier. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SocialBee?
answers.a: You are billed per social profile, not per person, and a profile is one brand account on one network. A single business posting to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok has used the whole Bootstrap allowance before a second brand or a client exists. The second thing is that people cost extra on top: Bootstrap and Accelerate are single-user plans, so a two-person team on eight profiles is $49 plus $10, not $29. Count your profiles across every network first — that number, not your team size, decides the tier.

Softr is genuinely best for teams building internal tools, client portals or member apps on top of Airtable or Google Sheets without code. Skip it if you're building a public consumer app with unpredictable, high user counts — the per-user model works against you there.

(re-verified 2026-09-07) A free plan with unlimited apps, up to 3 builders, 5 app users, 5,000 database records, 500 workflow actions and 5 AI credits a month. Paid on yearly billing: Basic $19/month, Pro $99/month and Business $329/month, with Enterprise on custom limits; the pricing page opens on the Yearly tab and advertises two months off, so month-to-month costs more. App-user allowances are published per tier: Team 5 + Client 5 on Basic, Team 10 + Client 50 on Pro, Team 30 + Client 100 on Business, where Team users share a business email domain with one of your builders and everyone else counts as a Client user. Extra app users beyond the allowance start at $1/month on Pro and $2/month on Business. Extra builder seats are $5/month on Basic, $10 on Pro and $20 on Business, and builders can be added as app users free. Records run 50K / 500K / 1M and workflow actions 2.5K / 10K / 25K a month. Non-profits and education get a stated 50% discount. Refunds: in full within 14 days of a first monthly payment, 30 days of a first yearly one. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Softr?
answers.a: Builder seats are billed on top of the plan, and pricing counts builders and app users separately, so a public-facing app with a lot of end users gets expensive fast. Watch the overage rate as well as the plan: extra app users are $1 a month on Pro but $2 on Business, so the dearer plan meters growth at double the rate. It fits internal tools and client portals with a known audience, not an open signup.

Spiky.ai is genuinely best for sales and customer-facing teams that already run most conversations on video and want the coaching layer — talk-time, keyword tracking and call review — without buying a full revenue-intelligence platform. Skip it if your team's calls are mostly ad hoc or on the phone rather than video, or the meeting volume per rep sits well above 30 a month, in which case only the top tier fits and the cheaper plans are a false economy.

(re-verified 28 Aug 2026 on their own pricing page; unchanged since 31 Jul 2026) Read across both billing toggles. There is a genuine free tier, capped at 3 meetings per user per month. On annual billing Plus is $15, Pro $24 and Premium $40 per user per month; switch to monthly and the same three read $18, $29 and $49. Annual saves up to 18%. Trials need no card. Meeting allowances: 3 on Free, 30 on both Plus and Pro, unlimited on Premium. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Spiky.ai?
answers.a: The number to check first is the meeting cap, not the price. Plus and Pro both stop at 30 meetings per user per month, so the step from $15 to $24 buys features, not capacity. A rep taking two calls a day passes 30 in three weeks, which pushes you to Premium at $40 — nearly triple the entry price — for volume rather than capability. Price this from your team's actual call count and you will land on the right tier; price it from the feature table and you will not.

Spocket is genuinely best for dropshippers who want vetted US and EU suppliers with faster shipping and one-click store integration, prioritizing delivery speed over raw catalog size. Skip it if you want the widest possible catalog at the lowest sourcing cost (AliExpress-based tools fit), or your margins can't absorb both subscription and wholesale cost.

(re-verified 2026-09-07) Four monthly plans, metered on unique products: Starter $39.99 (25 products), Pro $59.99 (250 products, 25 premium), Empire $99.99 (10,000 / 10,000) and Unicorn $299.99 (25,000 / 25,000). Annual billing is advertised as eight months free and the annual rates are printed on the cards: Pro $24 a month, Empire $57 and Unicorn $79, with stated savings of $432, $516 and $2,563. Unicorn's two figures do not reconcile - $299.99 a month for a year less $79 a month for a year is $2,651.88, not $2,563. There is a 7-day trial and 0% transaction fee on every tier. Multiple-store support is listed on all plans, but the page states a separate subscription is required for each store. Unicorn carries the MOST POPULAR badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Spocket?
answers.a: Spocket's pitch is faster-shipping US and EU suppliers, and that's real — but you still pay twice: the monthly subscription and the wholesale product cost, so margins depend on picking items with room to mark up. Catalog breadth is narrower than giant AliExpress-based tools (that's the trade for vetting and shipping speed), and the low Starter product cap pushes serious stores up to Pro quickly. It reduces, not removes, the usual dropshipping risks.

Stackable is genuinely best for shopify stores running several promotions at once — an order discount, free shipping and a collection deal — that want shoppers to redeem them with one code instead of choosing, or that want the progress type which raises the discount as the cart fills. Skip it if you run one promotion at a time, because Shopify's own combined discounts already cover that at no cost — or the checkout upsells are the part you actually want, since those only exist in the $99.99 tier here.

(prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/stackable-discounts) Two paid tiers, billed in USD every 30 days, and no free plan. Growth is $19.99 a month, or $199.99 a year with the annual saving the listing puts at 17%, and covers unlimited combined discounts; that plan carries the label 'For Non-Plus'. Unlimited is $99.99 a month, or $999.99 a year on the same 17%, and adds unlimited checkout upsells and unlimited linked discounts on top of the same combined discounts. Both tiers come with a 7-day free trial. The plan table lists no order caps, credit allowances or per-use charges, so what the tier costs is what the app costs. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Stackable?
answers.a: The two halves of the pitch are priced five times apart. Discount stacking — order, collection and shipping discounts redeemed with a single code — is the $19.99 Growth plan, the one the listing labels 'For Non-Plus'. The checkout upsells and linked discounts the app leads with sit in the $99.99 Unlimited tier only, so a merchant who came for the upsells is reading $1,199.88 a year rather than $239.88. There is no free plan to settle whether the stacking alone lifts an order, so the seven-day trial is the entire evaluation. One more thing to check before you commit: the Website link on the listing, www.stkbl.app, now redirects to the documentation for Discount Kit — a different, pricier Optizio app — and that documentation does not mention Stackable anywhere (checked 6 September 2026). For an app that launched on 13 October 2020 and has collected 54 App Store reviews since, ask support where the current documentation lives before the trial clock starts.

Stamped is genuinely best for mid-market Shopify brands that want reviews and loyalty in one platform instead of juggling separate apps. Skip it if you're an early-stage store — the removed free plan and $199+/product pricing are steep before you have the volume to justify them.

(re-verified 12 September 2026, read in a browser on their own pricing page across every step of the order-volume selector and both the single-product and bundle tabs) There is no free plan, and what you can actually buy depends on your monthly order volume. Below 5,000 orders a month the page sells only one product: Reviews, at $23/month at the 200-order step and $99/month at 1,000 orders. Repeat and Loyalty do not appear at those volumes at all. At the 5,000-order step the full line-up shows up — Repeat $499/month, Loyalty $299/month, Reviews $199/month — and the Multi-Product Bundle, which advertises 20% off, is a flat $798/month. The bundle tab locks the 200- and 1,000-order steps, so $798 is the entry price for taking more than one product, not a figure from the top of a ladder. From 20,000 orders upward, Unlimited included, every card turns into "Custom plan — Talk to Sales". Their FAQ says the same thing in words: plans start at $199/month for a single product and $798/month for multi-product access, and smaller brands are pointed at the self-serve plans in Stamped's Shopify App listings instead. Plans include up to two domains, each additional store gets its first month free, and additional domains are $100/month each. Sales tax is added as a separate line item. The redesigned page no longer says anything about overage charges. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Stamped?
answers.a: The $798/month figure that circulates for the full suite is real, but it is a floor rather than a ceiling: that is what multi-product access costs from the 5,000-order step, and below that step you cannot buy the bundle at all — the pricing page sells Reviews on its own, $23/month at 200 orders and $99 at 1,000, and does not show Repeat or Loyalty. So the ladder has a cliff in it rather than a slope. Crossing 5,000 orders doubles Reviews from $99 to $199, and wanting a second product moves you to $798. A second storefront is another $100 a month on top, and past 20,000 orders every card turns into "Talk to Sales". Start with one product and price the step above the volume you actually expect.

Stampezee is genuinely best for local businesses (cafés, salons, retail) that want a simple digital stamp-card loyalty program starting free. Skip it if you need POS-integrated loyalty with CRM depth (bigger platforms exist), or your offer isn't repeat-visit shaped.

(read 2026-08-30 on stampezee.com/en/pricing from a US exit) Four tiers, all now named and priced on the public page. Stamp Start free: 1 branch, 1 stamp card, up to 100 customers or 100 stamps, whichever comes first. Stamp Lite $29.99/month: 2 branches, 3 stamp cards, unlimited customers and stamps, signup rewards, EzeeCodes, birthday/anniversary/referral automations. Stamp Pro $49.99: 3 branches, 6 cards, spend-based stamping, tiered and exclusive rewards, 4 push notifications. Stamp Elite $99.99: 10 branches, 12 cards, scratch-card campaigns, email marketing, 1 custom stamp card design, dedicated account manager. The page advertises 17% off on the annual term but does not print the annual amounts. StampEzee prices by region and the European rates are materially lower, not just relabelled: the same page read from the Netherlands gives EUR 19.99, 39.99 and 69.99. Note the entry tier's own contradiction: the plan card frames Stamp Start as a 14-day free trial, the comparison table on the same page lists it as Free with no time limit. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Stampezee?
answers.a: The category is honest and proven (digital stamp cards beat lost paper cards), and the platform is young with limited public pricing and review coverage — so start on the free plan, run one real campaign, and measure repeat-visit lift before paying. The deeper truth of loyalty programs: the mechanics are 10% of the outcome; a reward worth returning for is the other 90%.

StoreFAQ is genuinely best for small Shopify stores that want SEO-tagged FAQ pages with JSON-LD schema and a light AI chatbot for deflection, without standing up a full support stack. Skip it if you have real traffic, because the page-view meter charges you for the FAQ pages doing their job, or you need ticketing, agent workflows and multichannel support reporting.

(read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/storefaq) Four tiers, metered on FAQ page views and AI chatbot conversations rather than on the number of FAQs. Free: 100 FAQ page views, unlimited FAQs and FAQ groups, the AI chatbot and AI-written FAQs, 25 AI conversations for the lifetime of the account, AI training on up to 50 products, export and import, instant answer with live chat and standard support. Professional $7.99 a month: 500 FAQ page views, 50 AI conversations a month, training on 150 products, multilingual FAQs and dedicated support, with overage at $0.0159 per extra page view and $0.30 per extra AI conversation. Growth $14.99 a month: 2,000 FAQ page views, 100 AI conversations a month, 300 products, with overage at $0.0075 a view and $0.30 a conversation. Enterprise $49.99 a month or $479.90 a year, a 20% saving: unlimited FAQ page views, 500 AI conversations a month, 2,000 products, priority support and $0.30 per extra conversation. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Storeware, 124 Broadkill Rd #599, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 3 January 2024 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with StoreFAQ?
answers.a:
The meter is FAQ page views, and that is the thing this app exists to increase. You install it to get SEO-friendly FAQ pages that rank and get read; every read is a billable unit. The free plan stops at 100 views and Professional at 500, which a product-page FAQ on a store with any traffic burns through in days, and then it is $0.0159 a view. Unlimited views arrive only on the $49.99 tier. Success on the cheap plans costs you money, which is an odd shape for a pricing page and the first thing to model before you install.

The AI allowance is the second meter and it is tight. Twenty-five conversations for the entire life of a free account, fifty a month at $7.99, a hundred at $14.99, and $0.30 each after that. Two hundred extra conversations in a month is $60, more than the top tier costs outright, so if the chatbot is the reason you are here, price the conversations rather than the subscription and jump straight to the tier that fits.

And know the boundary of the tool. This builds FAQ content, schema and a light chat layer. It is not a helpdesk: no ticketing, no agent queues, no multichannel reporting. Anything a shopper asks that an FAQ cannot answer still lands in whatever inbox you had before.

StoreSEO is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a few hundred products and no in-house SEO help, who want metadata, schema, alt text and indexing handled in bulk and reported against Search Console. Skip it if you have fewer than 25 products, in which case the free tier is the whole product, or you expect an app to fix a demand problem rather than a metadata one.

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/storeseo) Free Forever covers 25 products with SEO scoring, 200 AI credits, 25 image optimisations, up to 5 tracked keywords, an LLMs.txt generator and Agents.md editor, an SEO migrator, alt-text optimisation and 24/7 chat support. Paid tiers are Lite $14.99, Essential $39.99 and Advanced $249.99 a month, each with a 7-day free trial. Lite covers 100 products, 500 image optimisations and 1,000 AI credits and adds one-click schema markup, instant indexing requests, Google Analytics and Search Console and automatic sitemap submission. Essential covers 250 products, 2,000 images and 5,000 credits. Advanced covers 10,000 products, 50,000 images, 50,000 credits and adds multilingual SEO. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing: storeseo.com sells a Growth plan at $99.99 a month (1,000 products, 5,000 images, 12,500 AI credits, 200 keywords) that does not appear on the App Store listing at all, and also sells credit top-ups from $10 for 5,000 credits and $50 for 25,000. Rating 5.0 from 751 App Store reviews, re-read 19 September 2026 (it was 674 on 19 August). Developer Storeware, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 19 October 2021 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with StoreSEO?
answers.a: Know what an SEO app can and cannot do before you buy any tier. This one fixes the mechanical layer well — meta titles and descriptions in bulk, alt text, compressed images, JSON-LD, sitemaps, indexing requests — and none of that creates demand for products nobody is searching for. It is maintenance, not marketing, and on a catalogue of 25 products the free tier already does most of it. Two specifics worth a raised eyebrow. The pricing gap between Essential at $39.99 for 250 products and Advanced at $249.99 for 10,000 is filled by a $99.99 Growth plan. That plan lives on the vendor's own site but not on the App Store listing our link points to, which is a strange place to hide a tier. And the AEO/GEO features — the LLMs.txt generator, the Agents.md editor, the separate “agentic” ranking — are a bet, not a channel. No major search or AI vendor has committed to reading llms.txt, so treat those numbers as a hypothesis you are testing rather than traffic you are buying.

Storista is genuinely best for Shopify stores that already produce TikTok or Reels content and want it on the storefront as shoppable video, with the free tier's unlimited views making it cheap to test whether social video converts on your product pages at all. Skip it if you have no UGC or short-form pipeline to feed it — the widget displays content, it does not create any — or you want automatic product-to-video tagging without paying $49 a month for it.

(read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/storista-stories, listed as “Storista Shoppable Video UGC”) Four tiers. Free covers 10 videos with unlimited views, TikTok Shop and Shop app integration, GEO/SEO optimisation and the Carousel and Spotlight widgets, and it keeps Storista branding on the widget. Basic is $15 a month for 50 videos, unlimited views, basic analytics and videos on any page. Business is $49 a month for unlimited videos, AI Smart Tagging, advanced analytics and all widget types. Scale is $199 a month for Shopify Plus stores and adds VIP support and multiple stores. Every paid tier carries a 14-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The app is English-only, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and works with Checkout, Shopify Admin, TikTok Shop, the Shop app, Instagram Reels, TikTok Videos, GemPages, Rebuy, Skio, Shogun and Subscriptions. Developer Storista LLC, Sheridan, Wyoming; the app launched on 19 February 2021 and had 49 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing. Note that storista.io, the vendor's own domain, sells a different product on a different meter — AI-generated UGC video at roughly $1 to $4 a render, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan — and not the widget ladder above. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Storista?
answers.a:
The first thing to know is that the brand sells two different products, and the one you find by searching the name is not the one this link installs. storista.io is an AI UGC video generator priced per render, roughly $1 to $4 a video, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan. The Shopify app is a shoppable-video widget priced at $0, $15, $49 and $199 a month. Same company, same name, unrelated ladders, and nothing on either page maps one to the other. If you arrive at a price expecting the other product, you will be wrong by a factor of ten in either direction.

Second, read the headline against the pricing table. AI Smart Tagging is one of four bullets in the app's own pitch and one of the four features named in the listing summary. It appears on Business at $49 and above. On Free and Basic you tag products to videos yourself.

Third, the rating deserves its detail. 5.0 from 49 reviews is excellent, and the breakdown is 47 five-star, one four-star and one one-star — so the round number is a rounding, not a perfect record. That is a small point, but it is the kind of thing worth checking on any app whose average sits exactly on the ceiling.

Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views customer device and activity data and can view and edit customers, products, store analytics, custom data and Shopify admin. That is a wide grant for a widget that displays video, and it belongs in your processing register whatever you decide about the product.

Storylane is genuinely best for sales and marketing teams who show a product before a call and want to know which prospects clicked what — the free tier is genuinely usable for one demo. Skip it if you need more than one live demo but nowhere near 2,500 identified visitors a month, because that is exactly the gap the price ladder does not serve; a screen recording and a calendar link may do the job for less.

(2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0: 1 seat, 1 published demo live at a time, unlimited views. Starter $50/month ($40 annual), 1 seat, extra seats $40 each, unlimited demos, de-anonymises 250 visitors/month. Growth $625/month ($500 annual), 5 seats, extra seats $100 each, 2,500 visitors/month. Premium $1,500/month ($1,200 annual), 10 seats, 10,000 visitors/month. Enterprise quote-only. Their RepX chat product is separate again, starting at $2,000/month for up to 10,000 monthly visitors. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Storylane?
answers.a: The jump from Starter to Growth is $50 to $625 a month — twelve and a half times — and the free tier is capped at one live demo, so the moment you want a second demo published you are on the ladder. What is actually being sold at each step is visitor de-anonymisation: 250 a month on Starter, 2,500 on Growth, 10,000 on Premium. Price that against what you already pay a separate tool to do, because it is the meter that decides your tier, not the number of demos. Extra seats are charged on top at $40 to $100 each, which means a five-person sales team on Starter is not $50 a month, it is $210.

Streak is genuinely best for solo founders and small Gmail-native teams whose pipeline genuinely lives in email threads and who want zero context-switching. Skip it if your team needs shared process outside the inbox (a standalone CRM scales better), or you're price-sensitive — the Gmail convenience now costs full CRM money.

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Pro $49/user/mo annual or $59 monthly; Pro+ $69 annual or $89 monthly; Enterprise $129 annual or $159 monthly — a flat 20% annual discount, with Enterprise available on annual billing only and only to teams of 10 or more. Everyone on a team must be on the same plan. AI credits are a second meter: 20 per user per month on Pro, 150 on Pro+, 500 on Enterprise, pooled across the team and expiring each period; top-ups run $100/mo for 1,000 credits up to $1,000/mo for 25,000. The free CRM tier was eliminated in 2024-25, but the free email tools remain — email and link tracking, snippets, Streak Share, a thread splitter, and mail merge at 50/day against 1,500/day on the paid plans. Pro+ has a 14-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Streak?
answers.a: The pitch — CRM living inside Gmail — is also the ceiling: everything happens in the inbox, which power users love and growing teams outgrow (reporting, permissions, cross-team process). And note the trajectory: the free tier is gone and per-seat prices sit at real-CRM levels now, so the 'lightweight Gmail add-on' framing no longer matches the invoice. If the inbox is truly where your deals live, few tools feel this natural.

Success.co is genuinely best for leadership teams that already run on goals and want one place to set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, and keep strategy execution on cadence. Skip it if your team won't commit to a regular goal-review rhythm (the software alone won't create it), or a simple shared doc already keeps you aligned.

(read 2026-08-21 in Success.co's own structured data on success.co/pricing and re-read there unchanged on 2026-09-08) There is a Free Forever plan at $0, and the paid product is tiered per user with the rate falling as the team grows. Monthly billing: $12 per user a month for 1-25 users, $11 for 26-75, $9 for 76-125, $7 for 126-250 and $6 for 251-1,000. Annual billing takes roughly a dollar to two off each step: $11, $10, $8, $6 and $5 per user a month paid annually. Two enterprise add-ons sit outside that ladder and are quoted on the page itself at $250 a month each: Single Sign-On (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or any SAML/OIDC provider) and Directory Sync via SCIM for automatic provisioning and de-provisioning. A 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits get 50% off. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Success.co?
answers.a: The ladder rewards size rather than commitment: moving from 25 to 26 users drops the rate a dollar, and the annual discount is worth about the same single dollar per user. So the number that decides your bill is headcount, not billing term — and at the small end, where most teams start, $12 a user is the least favourable rate on the whole page. The two capabilities a security team will ask for first, SSO and SCIM, are not in any plan: they are $250 a month each, which on a 20-person account doubles the bill.

Sunsama is genuinely best for people whose problem is deciding what to do today rather than tracking what exists — it pulls from your existing tools and forces a daily plan, which is the whole product. Skip it if you already plan your day and just want a task list, because that is free everywhere; also skip it for a team, since there is no team pricing and the per-person cost multiplies straight through.

(2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) The page gives two different numbers and it is worth knowing both. The plan card says $17 a month billed yearly, or $22 billed monthly, for the Pro plan, with unlimited usage and integrations; Enterprise is quote-only. The FAQ on the same page says Sunsama costs $25 a month per person, or $20 a month on yearly plans, and gives a worked example of $50 a month for two people. There is a free trial with no card required. The page also explains, unprompted, that they price at $25.00 rather than $24.99 because they consider the latter 'deceitful psychological trickery'. Their own llms.txt, read the same day, lists Pro at $17 per person a month billed yearly and $22 billed monthly, plus a 14-day trial at $0 with no card required — so the machine-readable file agrees with the plan card and not with the FAQ. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Sunsama?
answers.a: The pricing page contradicts itself: the plan card says $17 yearly and $22 monthly, the FAQ on the same page says $20 yearly and $25 monthly. One of those is stale, and until you know which, treat $25 as the number you might actually be charged. That is an odd thing to have to say about a company that goes out of its way on that same page to explain why it refuses to use $24.99 pricing — the transparency is real and so is the inconsistency. The other thing to be clear about is that this is per person with no team discount mentioned: two people is two subscriptions, and their own example says $50.

SupaEasy is genuinely best for Shopify merchants — especially non-Plus stores — who want custom discount, checkout, payment and shipping logic without hiring a developer, and above all those forced to migrate deprecated Shopify Scripts to Functions before the cutoff. Skip it if you only need a simple volume discount (a dedicated discount app is cheaper), you are comfortable writing Shopify Functions in code yourself, or you will not pay $99 a month to use the AI generator on a live store — the free plan runs on a dev store only.

(verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/supaeasy and supaeasy.com/pricing) A free plan plus three paid monthly tiers, each with a 7-day trial. The catch is in the free plan: it works only on a development store, not a live one. Premium is $49 a month ($470 a year), Advanced is $99 a month ($950 a year) and Ultimate is $399 a month ($3,830 a year). The headline feature — the AI Functions Generator, which writes a function from a plain-language description — does not appear until Advanced at $99, alongside the Scripts Editor and Functions Wizard. So using SupaEasy the way it markets itself, on a live store, realistically starts at $99 a month. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SupaEasy?
answers.a: Two things the marketing glosses over. First, the 'free' plan is development-stores only, so any live use is paid, and the AI generator that headlines the app is not in Premium ($49) but in Advanced ($99), possibly plus metered AI credits as an add-on — so the AI promise realistically costs $99+ a month. Second, the rating is suspiciously spotless — 5.0 across 205 reviews, all five-star — and the praise dwells on fast human support (Andrea, Fabio) more than on the no-code AI running unattended, which hints the tool can need hand-holding.

Super is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a real gifting season — jewellery, cosmetics, speciality food, anything bought for someone else — that want paid or free gift wrap, a gift message and a price-hiding gift receipt in the cart or on the product page without theme surgery, and want those orders tagged automatically for fulfilment. Skip it if all you need is a gift-message box, which a line-item property in your theme does for nothing; gifting is a handful of orders a month, so the subscription outruns the upsell; or you are on Shopify Plus and were budgeting from the $19.99 top tier on the listing.

(price read 2026-09-12) Four paid tiers, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify, and the Shopify listing prints only three of them. On apps.shopify.com/super-gift-wraps: Basic is $9.99 a month or $83.92 a year for a paid or free gift message and a gift receipt that hides prices; Advanced $12.99 or $109.12 adds one paid or free gift wrap and an animated gift label; Pro $19.99 or $167.92 adds unlimited wraps, pop-up and checkbox display types, cart and product-page placement, custom images and gift revenue reporting. All three carry a 7-day trial, and all three say in the plan card itself: all stores except Shopify Plus stores. The fourth tier lives in the vendor's own pricing article on effectify.help, stamped 28 July 2026 and read 12 September 2026 — Plus Plan, $24.99 a month or $149.94 a year, Shopify Plus merchants only, everything in Pro plus the gift options inside the actual checkout page through Checkout Extensibility. That gap matters, because showing gift options in the Plus checkout is one of the five bullets at the top of the listing and the tier that delivers it is not in the listing's price block. The free plan in the listing header is the Development tier: development and partner stores only, Pro features, billing switched on when the store's Shopify plan is. answers.q: What is the catch with Super?
answers.a: If you are on Shopify Plus, the price block on the listing is not the one you pay from — the three published tiers exclude Plus stores in their own text, and the tier that covers you is $24.99 in a help-centre article. Beyond that, this vendor moves prices without announcing it. On 24 August 2026 another Effective Apps title, TnC, carried a ladder we had verified the day before; twenty-four hours later every tier had gone up with no change to the feature lists. Treat any price for this developer that is older than the day you read it as a guess, this one included. The review base is broad and middling: 4.7 over 254 reviews on 12 September 2026, 227 of them five-star but seven at one star, on an app listed since 17 August 2020. The app reads customer device and activity data and can view and edit products, orders and the Online Store. And be honest about what it sells. Gift wrap lifts average order value at the margin, so the app has to clear $9.99 to $24.99 a month in extra gift revenue before it pays for itself — and the revenue reporting that would tell you whether it does only arrives on Pro at $19.99.

Superfiliate is genuinely best for e-commerce brands turning customers and creators into affiliates with branded co-branded storefronts — if the volume justifies a demo-quoted platform fee. Skip it if you're testing affiliate marketing for the first time — there is no self-serve entry and no published price, so the first step is a sales call about a program that is not yet producing.

(read 25 August 2026, re-checked 5 September 2026) Superfiliate publishes no price on its own site. superfiliate.com/pricing returns 404 with and without www, /llms.txt returns 404, there is no pricing item anywhere in the navigation, and the only commercial call to action is Book Demo. Additional charges may apply', the note that the app 'Requires an active Superfiliate subscription for app activation and use. Contact Superfiliate for plan details', and one hard fact — 'All charges are billed in USD.' So the free-to-install label covers the app, not the platform. Our dossier has carried a range of roughly $299 to $999 a month which we cannot trace to their site or to any dated reading; treat it as an unverified order of magnitude rather than a price, and ask for the number in writing on the demo call. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Superfiliate?
answers.a: The price is the part you cannot check. Their pricing page returns 404 with and without www, the homepage carries no figure at all, and the only route to a number is a sales call — so the honest warning is not that it is expensive, but that you cannot compare it against anything until you have spoken to them. Ask for the figure in writing on that call, and ask what separates the ends of whatever range they quote. On fit rather than price: this is built for brands already running creator and affiliate programs, and it is overkill if you are testing your first affiliate offer.

SupportBee is genuinely best for small support teams working out of a shared email inbox who want assignment, internal comments and a knowledge base without dragging customers into a portal or learning a helpdesk suite. Skip it if your customers reach you on chat, phone or WhatsApp, or support and billing need separate queues with their own rules; this is one channel, one team and one knowledge base on both published plans.

(read 2026-08-27 on supportbee.com/pricing) Two plans, both priced per seat, and no free tier. Month to month, Startup is $20/seat/month and Enterprise is $25/seat/month. Switch the toggle to annual and the page shows a total of $204 per seat billed annually on Startup and $252 on Enterprise, a saving it advertises as 20 per cent, which works out at effective rates of 17 and 21 dollars a seat a month. Startup covers the shared inbox, snippets, filters, basic integrations, API access, unlimited email inboxes and tickets, customer satisfaction ratings, customer management, audit trails and one knowledge base with one team. Enterprise is described as everything in Startup plus five things: enterprise integrations, business hours, the customer portal, an audit log with data history, and portal access for customer groups. The trial is 14 days and the home page says no credit card is required. Billing runs through Stripe, you can switch between monthly and annual at any time with a prorated credit, and plan changes take effect immediately. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SupportBee?
answers.a: It is an email helpdesk and only an email helpdesk. There is no live chat, no phone, no WhatsApp and no social inbox, and the integration list confirms it: Asana, Trello, ClickUp, Linear, Notion, GitHub Issues, Pipedrive, Insightly, Capsule, Customer.io, QuickBooks, PostHog, Slack and webhooks are all places to push a ticket outward, not channels a customer can arrive on. Read the two published plans as printed and neither lifts the cap of one knowledge base and one team, even though the vendor's own FAQ describes teams as the way you mirror departments. Enterprise is listed as everything in Startup plus five named items, and more teams is not one of them. Watch the seat count too. The pricing FAQ defines users as everyone with access across all three permission levels, collaborators included, and the docs add a collaborator through the same add-a-user flow. So the invite-the-whole-company pitch runs through the same per-seat meter, and collaborator activity does not even show up in reports. And the two pages disagree about leaving: the pricing FAQ says you can cancel your subscription anytime, while the billing doc routes cancellation through contact us, which is the one billing action on that page that is not self service.

Surfer (SurferSEO) is genuinely best for content marketers, SEO specialists and agencies that need on-page optimization against live SERP data and want to start tracking how often they are cited in AI answers. Skip it if you are a solo blogger who needs keyword research rather than document-level optimization, or you cannot commit to a year — every listed rate assumes annual billing.

(re-read 2026-09-19 on surferseo.com/pricing from the Netherlands; earlier reads 2026-08-25 from the Netherlands and 2026-08-26 over a US connection) Billed yearly: Discovery $49/mo, Standard $99/mo, Pro $182/mo and Peace of Mind $299/mo, with Enterprise at $999/mo and AI Search Analytics sold on its own from $82/mo. Monthly billing is on the same cards behind the toggle and is no longer something you have to work out: $59, $119, $219, $359 and $95, with the annual commitment saving between $120 and $720 a year, up to 17 percent by their own FAQ.

AI Search Analytics is a ladder rather than a single price, which is the part that catches people out. Its card carries a prompt dropdown and each step is a complete monthly price: 50 prompts at $82 a month on the annual commitment or $95 monthly, 100 prompts at $158 or $185, 200 prompts at $308 or $365. The tier the card opens on changed on 8 September 2026 from 100 prompts to 50, so a quote of $158 from August and a quote of $82 from today are both correct readings of the same unchanged ladder — they are different rungs. Check which rung your checkout page is on before you compare it with anything.

Worth knowing if you are outside the US: we read this page from both sides and the numbers do not convert. A European is quoted €49 to €299 where an American is quoted $49 to $299, which at today's rate makes the same subscription materially more expensive in Europe. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Surfer (SurferSEO)?
answers.a: Every tier quotes its monthly rate on annual billing, so the number you see is a year's commitment rather than a monthly one. The meter that actually forces an upgrade is documents: 120 to 360 optimizations depending on tier, which a working content team passes faster than it expects. And the AI-visibility tracking that the product now leads with is capped by prompt count per tier, so watching more of your market costs a step up rather than an add-on.

SurveyMonkey is genuinely best for teams that need research-grade survey logic (skip logic, randomisation, quotas) with compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2) and 200+ integrations. Skip it if you just need a simple form (Google Forms is free) or you're cost-sensitive with high response volumes — the overage fees add up.

(read 2026-09-08 in surveymonkey.com/pricing.md, the vendor's own machine-readable pricing reference, whose header dates the content 2026-08-31) Team plans are annual-only in practice: pricing.md lists Team Advantage Monthly and Team Premier Monthly as Canada-only and "currently not available to any user". The geography tables separate a core seat from each additional seat, and the per-user figure the pricing page advertises is the additional one. United States: Team Advantage Annual is $468 a year for the core seat plus $360 for every seat after it; Team Premier Annual is $1,668 plus $1,104. Euro storefronts carry the same shape at €432 plus €360 and €1,188 plus €900. Team plans require three or more users, Enterprise five or more on a custom quote. Overage above the included response limit is priced per storefront: $0.15 a response in dollar countries, €0.10 in euro countries, £0.15 in sterling. That included limit is stated nowhere in pricing.md, whose feature matrix marks responses "Unlimited" on every paid plan. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SurveyMonkey?
answers.a: The free tier is a teaser. Response caps trigger $0.15-per-response overages that become a hidden cost on big studies. Branding and customisation are limited, and a lot of the good analytics and logic sit behind higher tiers.

SurveySparrow is genuinely best for teams that want engaging, conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience. Skip it if you just need a quick, occasional form — a free tool like Google Forms or Tally covers it without a subscription.

(re-verified 2026-09-14) The plan prices do render on the pricing page once the plan selector loads; our July and August 2026 captures simply never retrieved them, and the indicative figures we carried until this reading were wrong. Read on 14 September 2026, the survey line runs Basic €19, Starter €39 and Business €79 per month billed yearly, above a forever-free plan (75 responses a quarter, 3 active surveys, 10 questions each) and below a custom-priced Enterprise tier. Response allowances are what separate them: 2,500 a year on Basic, 15,000 on Starter and 36,000 on Business, with 1, 1 and 3 users respectively and extra users at €49 each a month. There are separate product lines for CX, brand, research, documents and 360 assessment, each with its own ladder. One caveat on the currency: the page prices on the visitor's location and we read it from Europe, where those amounts are shown in euros, so a US buyer sees a dollar column we have not yet been able to read — the ladder is verified, the currency is not. Discounts: yearly billing saves up to 40%, students and education 50%, nonprofits 15%, and a startup programme offers $2,000 of credit for $500. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with SurveySparrow?
answers.a: The conversational-survey UX is the draw, but response limits on lower tiers and the 'contact sales' wall on advanced features (API, higher volume) make budgeting fiddly — and there's no true monthly billing.

Survicate is genuinely best for product and CX teams running always-on feedback — NPS, CSAT and in-app surveys — piped into the CRM and analytics stack they already use. Skip it if you just need an occasional one-off questionnaire (a simpler form tool covers that) or your response volume is huge — response-metered pricing punishes scale.

(read 2026-09-08 in the plan data embedded in survicate.com/pricing) A 10-day trial of all features, no card. Growth is metered on feedback rather than seats and is a ladder, not a single price: $56 a month for 100 responses and 500 data points, $114 for 250 and 1,000, $169 for 500 and 1,500, $229 for 1,000 and 2,000, and $289 for 1,500 and 2,500 — billed annually, with 10 user seats across 2 teams and one dashboard at every rung. Pro is $349 with a custom yearly response pool, advanced survey logic and 10 dashboards; Enterprise is $569. Starter is monthly-only and has its own ladder with an explicit overage rate: $89 for 100 responses at $0.89 for each one beyond, $179 for 250 at $0.59, $279 for 500 at $0.39. A response is counted per respondent, partial or complete; data points are new external feedback from integrations (calls, tickets, reviews) and exclude survey responses. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Survicate?
answers.a: The plan is metered by response volume, not by surveys — a viral NPS month can push you a tier up, and the free plan's 30-day retention quietly deletes your history. Mind the billing asymmetry too: Starter is monthly-only while Growth and up expect an annual commitment.

Switcher Studio is genuinely best for creators, churches, events and small businesses that want multi-camera live production and streaming using iPhones and iPads they already own — no broadcast hardware. Skip it if you're on Windows, you need rock-solid wired production for high-stakes broadcasts, or a single-camera stream is all you'll ever need.

answers.a: (read 2026-09-08 on switcherstudio.com/pricing) Studio is $65 a month month-to-month and $45 on annual billing; Suite is $99 month-to-month and $79 annually, discounted to $71 a month for a first year that then renews at $948. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Switcher Studio?
answers.a: The app runs on Mac and iOS only — Android phones can join as cameras, but there is no Windows version — so the machine doing the switching has to be an Apple one. And wireless multi-cam is only as reliable as your venue's Wi-Fi; a shaky connection is the failure mode nobody markets. The monetization features (pay-per-view, subscriptions) are genuinely strong, but only matter if you're actually selling access.

Synthesia is genuinely best for teams making talking-head training, explainer and onboarding videos without cameras, actors or editing. Skip it if you need lots of video or cinematic, human-shot production — the minute caps and avatar style won't fit.

(re-verified 2026-09-14; the plan cards are geo-priced and served us euros from a Dutch address, where our August reading was in dollars, so check your own currency before budgeting) Basic is free and includes 1,200 credits a month, good for about 10 minutes of video. Starter is €19 a month, or €12 a month billed yearly, with 14,500 credits a year — roughly 120 minutes of video or 580 minutes of dubbing. Creator is €79 a month, or €49 billed yearly, with 44,000 credits a year, about 360 minutes of video. Enterprise is quote-only with unlimited minutes. The banner across the top now reads “Plans now starting from €12/month — Save 38%”, where in August it advertised the same 38% from $18. Everything is priced by credits rather than by seat, so the minute allowance and not the sticker is what decides which plan you need, and a Studio avatar remains a paid add-on billed in dollars at $1,000 a year even on the euro page. One caution we have now documented three readings running, and it has got worse rather than better: the FAQ block lower down that same page still quotes Starter at $29 a month or $264 a year and Creator at $89 a month or $804 a year. Those dollar figures are the monthly prices the cards carried in August, and the annual ones work out at $22 and $67 a month, which matches neither the old cards nor the new ones. Treat the FAQ as stale and confirm the figure at checkout. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Synthesia?
answers.a: The video-minute caps are tight — 10 min/mo on Starter goes fast when you iterate, and re-generating edits burns minutes. Fantastic for avatar-led training and explainers without a studio, but not for high-volume or cinematic production.

answers.q: Is Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder worth it?

Skip it if you intend to bulk-publish AI articles unedited, or you need to know what a tool costs before you install it — as of 19 September 2026 this listing publishes no plan block and no credit allowance at all.

answers.q: How much does Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder cost?
answers.a: (re-read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder) The paid tier has left the listing. Where the page carried a Pro plan in August, it now publishes no plan block at all: the Pricing field in the header reads simply “Free”, the word Pricing appears exactly once on the whole page, and the only dollar figure anywhere on it belongs to a different app in the “More apps like this” rail. answers.q: What is the catch with Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder?
answers.a:
Publishing volume is the trap this tool makes cheap. It generates posts quickly and schedules them daily or weekly in bulk, and a Shopify blog filled with unedited AI articles is precisely the pattern search engines have spent the last two years demoting: the app lowers the cost of production, not the bar for ranking. Used the other way round, as a drafting and structuring tool for posts you actually edit, it is sensible.

The price is the second thing to watch, and on 19 September 2026 there is none to read. The listing publishes no plan block and gives its pricing as Free. That is not the same as free being the whole story: the features it advertises — AI generation, bulk creation, translation, scheduling — were metered in credits until August, and no credit allowance or overage rate is stated anywhere on the page now. The same developer's other listing still prints a complete ladder, so this one is not simply a developer who does not publish prices. Go in expecting to ask what the limits are, and do not plan a content calendar around an allowance nobody has told you the size of.

answers.q: Is Tapita SEO Optimizer worth it?
answers.a: Tapita SEO Optimizer is genuinely best for Shopify merchants on the Basic or Grow plan who want SEO audits, bulk metadata, image alt text and speed fixes out of one app instead of hiring a specialist. Skip it if you are on Shopify Advanced or Plus, where the same tier costs $30 to $60 a month more, or you need a published per-credit rate before you build a month of AI metadata around it.

answers.q: How much does Tapita SEO Optimizer cost?
answers.a: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/google-seo-schema-meta-data) Three tiers. Free: SEO audit and LLMs.txt on basic pages, unlimited on-page SEO audit, essential JSON-LD schemas, and image compression 900 a month capped at 30 a day. Also bulk and AI metadata optimisation, bulk image alt text and file names for 50 products, one-click page speed and 24/7 support chat. Basic $9.99 a month or $101.88 a year, a 15% saving, adds SEO audit and LLMs.txt on main pages, auto image optimisation 100 a day, 100 AI metadata credits a month, full JSON-LD schemas, broken-link detection with auto-redirects and advanced speed features. Pro $39.99 a month or $408 a year adds all main pages, 500 images a day, 500 AI credits a month, higher speed capacity, full automation of image alt text and file names, unlimited keyword research and hands-on help fixing SEO and Search Console issues. Both paid tiers carry the same surcharge line, and it is the number that decides what this costs: +$5 on the Shopify Grow plan, +$30 on Advanced and +$60 on Shopify Plus. So Basic is $9.99, $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99, and Pro is $39.99, $44.99, $69.99 or $99.99, depending on which Shopify plan you are on. Extra audit pages and extra AI credits are billed on top and the listing does not print a per-credit rate. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Tapita, M5 Building, 91 Nguyen Chi Thanh, Hanoi; the app launched 15 March 2023 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tapita SEO Optimizer?
answers.a:
The price on the listing is a Shopify-Basic price, and almost nobody reads the line underneath it. The same Pro plan is $39.99 on Shopify Basic, $44.99 on Grow, $69.99 on Advanced and $99.99 on Shopify Plus, because Tapita adds $5, $30 or $60 on top depending on your Shopify plan. That is a two-and-a-half-fold spread on identical software, and it is the single largest factor in what this app costs you. Work out which row you are on before you compare it to anything else.

The second meter has no published rate at all. Basic gives you 100 AI metadata credits a month and Pro gives you 500, and beyond that the listing says only that more audit pages and more credits carry an extra charge. It does not say how much, and it does not say how many credits one product's metadata consumes. Tapita's own sister app publishes $0.06 a credit on its listing; this one publishes nothing, so you cannot price a month of AI metadata before you install.

And the free tier is a demonstration rather than a plan: 50 products for bulk alt text and file names, 30 images a day, and the SEO audit and LLMs.txt limited to basic pages. Any real catalogue is on a paid tier within a week, which is fine as long as you know that going in.

Tapstitch is genuinely best for creators building a real apparel or streetwear brand who care about fabric, fit and how the product feels in hand. Skip it if you want the cheapest option or the widest catalogue — for pure margin and product breadth, traditional POD like Printify wins.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on tapstitch.com/collections/all; the site publishes no /pricing page — that URL returns 404) No subscription, no monthly fee and no minimum order quantity — you pay per item, production plus shipping, so there is no plan price to compare. The 48 blanks listed on the all-products page run from $5.99 to $32.99, median $19.99, at fabric weights from 110 to 470 gsm. The honest catch is margin rather than fees. Printify's lower product and shipping costs mean noticeably higher profit per sale, while Tapstitch's premium heavyweight blanks — 250 to 260 gsm tees and 350 to 380 gsm hoodies — sit at the expensive end of that range. Price the finished garment against your retail price, not the platform. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tapstitch?
answers.a: Printify is cheaper, higher-margin and has a far bigger catalogue — if you're optimising for profit per sale or product breadth, that's the real trade-off. Tapstitch earns its place when garment quality and brand feel matter more than squeezing the last point of margin.

Tax1099 is genuinely best for businesses and accountants who need to e-file 1099s, W-2s and related forms accurately and cheaply, especially seasonal or higher-volume filers. Skip it if you only file one or two forms a year (the IRS's own free options may suffice) or you want full bookkeeping rather than just the filing step.

(read 2026-09-08 on tax1099.com/tax-1099-efile-pricing) Filing is graduated volume pricing, not a flat rate that falls: each band is billed at its own rate and the bill is the sum across bands. The page works the example itself for 600 forms — the first 20 at $2.99, forms 21-150 at $2.30, forms 151-500 at $1.31 and the last 100 at $0.68, totalling $885.30, an average of $1.48 a form. Three eFiling plans: Essential is free, Teams (formerly eFile Plus) is $249 a year and adds multi-user access and 250 free TIN matches, and Scale (formerly Enterprise) is $349 a year and adds workflow, user and action management, API access and Notice Management (otherwise $199 a unit). TIN matching is not free on Essential: real-time is $1.00 a unit, within 24 hours $0.37, bulk $150 per 10,000 records — free on first use up to 10,000 records under one payer for Scale customers only. Other add-ons: eDelivery $0.25 a unit, print and mail $1.90 a form (plus a $1 rush fee in the last five days of the season through 2 February), foreign mail $4.99 a form, state reconciliation $4.99 a payer, and W-9/W-8 requests at $1.00 for one, $7.00 for 25, $45.00 for 200 and $95.00 for 1,000. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tax1099?
answers.a: Per-form pricing is genuinely cheap for a handful of 1099s, but it's metered: TIN matching, W-9 requests, state filing and corrections can each carry their own charge. A business filing across many recipients and states should tally the add-ons, not just the headline per-form rate. It's a filing tool, not a bookkeeping system; it assumes your payee data is already clean.

TaxCycle is genuinely best for Canadian accountants and bookkeepers who prepare and e-file client returns and want fast, checked, CRA-integrated professional tax software. Skip it if you're an individual filing your own personal return (consumer software is far cheaper), or you're outside Canada.

Prices are published on www.taxcycle.com/pricing (read 9 September 2026, Canadian dollars before tax, per year, single user) and are currently sale prices: Tax Basics 2026 $1,600 (reg. $1,680) with additional users at $540; the Complete Tax Suite $2,625 (reg. $2,800) with extra users at $756; the Complete Tax Suite plus TaxFolder $2,752 (reg. $3,102) with extra users at $944. The page dates the discount — 'Sale Ends Sept 24' — and advertises a 12-month payment plan available only during the sale. Every module is also priced separately: TaxCycle T1 $618 (+$238/user), T2 $1,102 (+$248), T3 $532 (+$211), T5013 $516 (+$211), T2202 $558 (+$211), T3010 $268 (+$86), Forms $270 (+$27), and the slip modules T4/T4A, T5, T5018, NR4 and RL $268 each (+$27). TaxFolder is $375 (+$215) and licensed to the end of 2027; DoxCycle $280 (+$167); Data Mining a $242 site licence; Québec TP1 a $198 site licence. Three-user and ten-user tiers are listed on their own tabs. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TaxCycle?
answers.a: This is professional preparer software priced for firms, not a consumer filing app: the cost only makes sense if you're preparing returns for clients at volume. The suites start at about CAD $1,600 a year for one user and each extra seat adds several hundred dollars, so a two- or three-person practice should budget the suite price plus seats, plus GST or HST, before comparing it with per-return alternatives.

Team Pulse is genuinely best for solo operators and small teams who want projects, tasks, chat AND a lightweight CRM pipeline with AI in one simple tool, and value the real free tier to start. Skip it if you need more than a handful of team members (seat caps climb the tiers fast), or you only need project management — dedicated PM tools give far more generous member limits.

answers.q: How much does Team Pulse cost?
answers.a: Genuinely free tier: $0/mo for 1 member, 2 projects, unlimited collaborators, chat/tasks/files. Paid (billed annually): Starter $29/mo ($348/yr) — 1 member, 5 projects, NO pipelines; Growth $79/mo ($948/yr) — 3 members, 10 projects, 1 pipeline, AI; Pro $159/mo ($1,908/yr) — 10 members, 20 projects, 2 pipelines; top tier $299/mo ($3,588/yr) — 40 projects, 1,500 AI credits. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Team Pulse?
answers.a: The tiers gate on TWO axes at once — member count and project/pipeline count — so you can hit a wall on either. The CRM pipeline is a big part of the pitch, but it doesn't exist below the $79 Growth plan (Free and Starter have none), and member limits are tight: Starter is a single seat, Growth just three. The listed rates also assume annual billing.

Teikametrics is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers spending enough on ads that a few points of efficiency covers the fee — under $10K a month the flat $149 is straightforward. Skip it if your ad spend is small or seasonal, because the flat fee at low spend is a large share of your budget and the percentage model at high spend needs modelling before you commit.

(2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) Essentials, for up to $10K a month in ad spend: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Advanced, for over $10K a month in ad spend: custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. Enterprise, for over $100K a month in ad spend: also custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. A free trial and a free opportunity assessment are offered. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Teikametrics?
answers.a: Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription — it is a subscription plus a percentage. Three per cent of ad spend above $10,000 means a seller spending $40,000 a month pays an extra $900 on top of whatever the custom base is, and that line scales with the thing the product is supposed to make more efficient. That is not automatically wrong — it aligns them with your growth — but it does mean your bill rises when your advertising does, and you should model it at your expected spend rather than your current one. The $10K threshold is the number to watch: crossing it changes the pricing model, not just the price.

Tellent is genuinely best for European scale-ups hiring continuously that want a collaborative ATS they can extend with HRIS and performance modules, and can put a sales call in the buying process. Skip it if you hire occasionally (job boards + a spreadsheet honestly suffice), or you want one all-in-one HR suite rather than modules.

Tellent publishes no prices. Its pricing page (read in a live browser on 9 September 2026, and separately in the served HTML) lists three ATS tiers for Recruitee — Start, Advance and Optimize — and the two Tellent HR modules, Manage (HRIS) and Grow (performance), and every one of them ends in 'Get a demo' rather than a figure; agencies are told to ask for a custom quote. Neither the rendered page nor the served HTML contains a single currency amount, and recruitee.com/pricing carries none either. What the page does state is scope: Start covers 5 active job posts and a single-page CareersHub; Advance adds unlimited posts, a multi-page branded careers site, ReferralsHub, 100 AI screening credits a month, 3 AI matching searches, workflow automations, candidate self-scheduling, offer-letter generation and up to 3 custom job fields; Optimize adds SSO, API support, a testing environment, requisition approval workflows, unlimited custom fields, 65 matching searches, onboarding support, a dedicated CSM and BI integrations. SSO, Texting, Journeys, AgencyHub and WhatsApp Hiring are optional add-ons on the lower tiers. A free trial is offered on every tier and needs only a company account; the page states no trial length. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tellent?
answers.a: Tellent's modular shape is genuinely useful — you can buy just the ATS, or just the HRIS — but nothing is priced in public: every tier on tellent.com/pricing ends in 'Get a demo' (read in a browser on 9 September 2026), and recruitee.com/pricing carries no figures either. Ask for Start, Advance and Optimize quoted together with their renewal prices, because you have no anchor to check a single number against. And as with every ATS, workflow fit — approval chains, careers-site needs, integrations with your assessment tools — matters more than the feature list; the free trial is enough to run one real vacancy through, so do that.

Tenable is genuinely best for security teams and IT-mature companies that need continuous, authoritative vulnerability scanning and can remediate what it finds. Skip it if you have no one to triage and fix findings — a managed security service or a lighter scanner fits a small team better.

(read 2026-08-30 on tenable.com/buy and the Nessus Essentials page) Nessus Essentials is free — a 30-day licence for 5 IPs, non-commercial only, with plugin updates delayed 30 days and no reporting, data export, compliance checks or support. Essentials Plus $199/year: 20 IPs, real-time plugin updates, basic PDF/HTML reporting, still non-commercial, free for verified students and instructors. Nessus Professional $4,790/year, $9,330.95 for two years, $13,637.54 for three — the first tier licensed for commercial use. Nessus Expert $6,790/year, $13,208.13 for two, $19,304.19 for three. Advanced Support (24x365 phone, email, community and chat) is a $400/year add-on on both. Training: $275 for a year of the Nessus Fundamentals course for one person, $385 with Nessus Advanced added. Cloud Tenable Vulnerability Management $3,500/year for 100 assets ($6,825 for two years, $9,975 for three); $3,700/year buys up to 250 assets online. Web App Scanning $6,790/year, or $3,578 for 5 FQDNs. Anything larger is a quote. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tenable?
answers.a: Note on how we link this one, updated 28 Jul 2026: between 21 and 28 July our partner link was dead — Tenable's shop subdomain stopped resolving, so we pointed the link at Tenable's own product page and earned nothing from it. Tenable confirmed on 28 July that the links are repaired; we re-tested them that day and the link now works again, lands on the same Nessus product page, and does pay us a commission. This is serious, enterprise-grade security tooling with an enterprise price and a learning curve — not a set-and-forget scanner. You need someone who can act on the findings, or you're paying for reports nobody reads.

TestDriver.ai is genuinely best for teams already living inside GitHub pull requests who want end-to-end tests to exist at all — mention @testdriverai in a PR, get a written, run and committed test back with a recording — and who would otherwise keep postponing a Playwright suite nobody has time to maintain. Skip it if your contributor list is much longer than your test needs, because seats are billed per GitHub user who touches a PR rather than per tester; you ship a Mac, iOS or Android app, which Pro does not cover at all; or your suite is long enough that sandbox minutes, not seats, become the real bill.

(read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on testdriver.ai/pricing) Two tiers. Pro is $20 per seat a month plus $0.14 for every testing minute, with 120 testing minutes included and a 14-day free trial. Read the seat rule carefully, because you do not choose it: the page states that seats are automatically billed for every GitHub user who gets a pull-request review or runs a test. Testing minutes are billed for as long as the sandbox is running — which starts automatically on pull-request generation and on test runs — so the meter covers the machine's uptime rather than the duration of your assertions. Pro is cloud-hosted and covers web apps, Chrome extensions, VSCode extensions, Windows desktop apps, Linux and Windows, with unlimited team users and unlimited AI generation and test runs. Enterprise is quote-only and self-hosted, with unlimited testing minutes, root access, custom VM images, bring-your-own-keys, VPN deployment and private Slack Connect support — and it is the tier where Haxor's team builds and maintains the tests for you.
