Mac desktop, Android and iOS are listed as coming soon, and only under Enterprise. The company is Haxor Inc. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TestDriver.ai?
answers.a:
You do not control your own seat count. The pricing page says a seat is billed automatically for every GitHub user who gets a pull-request review or runs a test — so the bill is set by who touches your repository, not by a number you chose. On a team of ten that is $200 a month before a single test has run, and it scales with contributors rather than with usage.

The included allowance is thinner than it looks. 120 testing minutes at the published $0.14 overage rate is $16.80 of metered value against a $20 seat, so the bundle is close to a rounding error on the seat itself. Worse, the meter runs on sandbox uptime rather than test duration: the clock covers booting the machine and loading your app, not only the part where it clicks things. A suite that takes eight minutes of wall time per pull request exhausts 120 minutes in fifteen pull requests.

And the page never says whether those 120 minutes are per seat or per account. At $0.14 a minute that ambiguity is worth $151.20 a month on a ten-person team — the difference between 120 minutes and 1,200. It is the first thing to put in writing before you turn this on, and it is not answerable from anything they publish.

One coverage trap: if you ship a Mac desktop app, or anything on iOS or Android, Pro does not cover you. Those platforms are marked coming soon and sit under Enterprise, which is quote-only.

What is genuinely good here is the part that usually breaks. Tests are written against what a user does rather than against selectors — the generated file reads `td.find("signup button").click()` and `td.assert("dashboard is visible")` — and the documentation tells you to describe behaviour instead of implementation, which is the opposite of the brittle CSS-selector suites this category is famous for. That is also the risk: an element resolved by an AI from a description can drift for reasons a diff will not show you.

TestGorilla is genuinely best for companies hiring steadily enough that a year of testing is cheaper than one bad hire, and who will actually use the library rather than writing their own questions. Skip it if you hire a few people a year — the annual commitment is the whole problem, and the free tier plus a well-designed take-home task covers occasional hiring.

(2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat. Core $142/month on an annual commitment, $1,704 billed annually, with the full test library, analytics and 2 full-access seats; the Core card carries a credits selector and its sign-up link defaults to a 400-credit tier. Plus starts from $400/month with an annual commitment starting at $4,800, described as scaling with your hiring needs. The page also sets out what a credit buys: 0 for resume scoring, qualifying questions and custom questions, 1 per candidate for skill tests, video questions, ID verification or a talent-pool invite, and 2 per candidate for AI interviews. Prices are shown in USD with GBP, EUR, AUD and INR available. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TestGorilla?
answers.a: Both paid tiers are annual-commitment only. Core is not $142 a month in any meaningful sense — it is $1,704 up front, and there is no monthly option to test it with real candidates first. That matters more here than in most categories, because hiring is lumpy: a company that hires in two bursts a year is paying for ten quiet months. Plus is worse to budget for, because it 'starts from' $400 and the page will not say what moves it. The free tier is credit-metered rather than feature-limited, which makes it a genuine trial — use it on a real vacancy before you sign a year.

TextExpander is genuinely best for support, clinical-admin and recruiting teams that need everyone sending identical approved wording — the shared library, permissions, auto-subscribe and SSO are what the paid tiers actually buy, and the SOC 2 and HIPAA-with-BAA posture is the one thing no free expander offers a compliance-bound team. Skip it if you are one person on a Mac with a couple of dozen fixed snippets. macOS Text Replacement is built in and free, Espanso is free and open source across all three desktop platforms, and TextExpander's own free plan now covers 5 active snippets. A subscription only starts earning its keep when you need fill-in fields, scripting, or a second person editing the same library.

(re-verified 2026-08-18 on the vendor's own pricing page; USD per user/month billed annually, excluding tax) The line-up was rebuilt since our July reading and it now starts at free. Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted. Annual billing is sold as two months free against paying monthly; the page does not print the monthly amounts next to the plans, so we do not quote them. The free plan is real but deliberately narrow: 5 active snippets out of an unlimited library, one snippet swap every two weeks, 3 teams, 5 team members and no snippet activity history at all. That history — what lets you see changes and restore deleted snippets — is 24 hours on Pro, 7 days on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. Team members stay capped at 5 on Free and Pro; unlimited members start on Business, which is also the first tier with single sign-on (Google SSO on Business, all providers plus SCIM on Enterprise). A 30-day trial with full access to every feature and no credit card sits alongside the free plan. The page still carries an important pricing note for international customers, which we could not open on this reading, so treat the listed USD amounts as pre-tax. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TextExpander?
answers.a: On a Mac the operating system already does the basic job free: Apple's built-in Text Replacement syncs static snippets across your Apple devices, though Apple's own documentation notes it is not available in every app. And Espanso covers the power-user case free and open source on Mac, Windows and Linux. On Windows there is no built-in equivalent (contrary to a widely repeated claim, PowerToys has no text-expansion utility), so the case for paying is genuinely stronger there. Do not buy it for mobile. The vendor's own mobile page is an early-access signup form for Android and iOS betas, not a shipping product — even though the surrounding copy is written in the present tense. Then add the snippet activity history: nothing at all on the free plan, only 24 hours on the $5 Pro tier, 7 days on Business, and unlimited only on Enterprise. Add the vendor's own note that buyers in VAT/GST countries including the EU, UK and Australia may see an estimated 20% uplift on the listed USD price (read 21 July 2026). For one person with a few dozen fixed snippets, the honest answer is usually don't.

Textline is genuinely best for support and sales teams that already text customers from personal phones and need a shared, compliant inbox with a record of who said what. Skip it if you send marketing blasts rather than conversations — that is a different product and priced per message elsewhere; also skip it if your volume is low enough that a shared inbox on your existing helpdesk covers it.

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Amounts unchanged since 2026-08-01. Add-on message credits $0.03 each, bought in advance; backup message credits $0.04 each, Textline's automatic fallback when you run out mid-conversation. A $15 monthly 10DLC campaign fee applies if you use a 10DLC long code; the same page states that toll-free numbers do not carry a monthly registration fee. NEW since the last reading: the page now names three tiers with their inclusions but still no prices — Essentials (600 minimum included message credits a month, three agents, three-year conversation history), Pro (2,000 minimum credits, five agents, unlimited history, Salesforce, custom roles) and Enterprise (quote). HIPAA-compliant plans are charged an additional fee. Note for future readers: the per-feature tooltips on this page are unfilled placeholder copy, so the feature names carry no explanation. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Textline?
answers.a: Two costs are easy to miss and both are monthly. The credit system has two rates: $0.03 for credits you buy deliberately and $0.04 for backup credits that fire automatically when you run out — a 33% premium for not noticing. And a $15 monthly 10DLC campaign fee appears on your bill if you use a 10DLC long code, charged by the carrier registry rather than by Textline, so no plan removes it; the same page notes that toll-free numbers carry no monthly registration fee, so the number type is the lever, not the tier. Plan prices are still not published — the page names Essentials, Pro and Enterprise and what they include, but no dollar figures.

TheTop is genuinely best for enterprises running AI across several departments, models and applications that cannot answer what the bill bought — organisations with a real AI invoice to explain, a CFO asking for return per team, and a security function that wants oversight without reading employees' conversations. Skip it if you are one person or a small team looking for an assistant: this is no longer that product. The $8 morning-brief tool this page used to describe has been withdrawn, there is no self-serve plan, no published price and no signup — the only route in is a sales call about your existing AI estate.

(read 19 September 2026) TheTop publishes no price. The navigation carries no pricing link, every button is Book a demo, and the page this review's figures came from is gone: thetop.com/pricing returns a hard 404, as do /pricing/ and /plans.

The $8 a month and $80 a year this review used to quote were withdrawn along with the product they belonged to, and cannot be bought today. Until September this was a personal assistant on a single tier, built around a morning brief from Gmail and a calendar. TheTop is now enterprise software sold through a sales call.

Read the figures on their site carefully, because it is full of dollar amounts that are not prices: the dashboard mock-ups show an AI invoice of $196,090, a month billed at $137,644 against a $176,920 baseline, and $39,276 saved. Those illustrate what the product reports, not what it costs. Nothing on the public site says what you would pay for TheTop itself.

What the site does commit to about commercial shape: deployment is single-tenant, one dedicated instance per customer; onboarding runs in three steps that start read-only (connect analytics, watch for about a month to establish your number, then point traffic at the Engine); and no traffic migration is needed on day one. Expect a contract quoted against your own AI spend rather than a list price — ask for the pricing basis in writing before the demo, because a layer that bills against measured savings and one that bills a flat platform fee are very different deals. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TheTop?
answers.a:
The price is the knock, because there isn't one. TheTop publishes no rate of any kind: no list price, no per-seat figure, no percentage, and no pricing page — we checked on 19 September 2026 and the old one returns a 404. Everything runs through Book a demo, so the first number you hear will be quoted to you, with your own AI spend already on the table. That is a weak position to negotiate from, and it is worth asking for the basis (flat platform fee, per request, or a share of measured savings) before you show anyone your invoice.

The savings claim is measured by the vendor, against a baseline the vendor computes. The site says eligible traffic is priced against your own baseline and shows 22% and 43% saved in its examples, but the party doing the measuring is also the party being paid. Ask how baseline is defined, which traffic counts as eligible, and whether you can audit the calculation — a reuse or reroute that quietly swaps a frontier model for a cheaper one also changes the output, and only your own evaluation will tell you whether that trade was worth it.

One more thing to weigh: this product sits in the request path. The Engine applies memory, caching, routing and policy before traffic reaches the model, which is exactly where the savings come from and also exactly where an outage or a bad routing rule lands on every AI feature you run. The vendor's answer is that you start read-only and move traffic when you choose, which is the right shape — but the day you point production at it, a middle layer has become a dependency.

Thordata is genuinely best for data teams scraping at scale — price intelligence, SERP tracking, AI-training data — who want proxy infrastructure plus ready-made scraping APIs at aggressive per-unit rates. Skip it if you need predictable flat pricing, or your use case skirts site terms — residential proxying carries compliance questions no discount fixes.

(price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Usage-metered, with free trials on the APIs. Every advertised "from" rate is the largest package on its ladder: residential $0.65/GB at 5,000 GB ($3,250) against $2.00/GB at 1 GB, $1.50 at 50 GB and $0.80 at 350 GB; mobile $2.20/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB; SERP API $0.70 per 1K at 1M responses against $1.20 at 15K; Web Scraper API $0.50 per 1K at 3M against $1.00 at 30K; Web Unlocker $1.00 per 1K at 200K against $1.30 at 10K; Scraping Browser $2.50/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB. Static ISP and datacenter proxies advertise $0.75/IP against a $1.50 list, while the ISP packages themselves list at $1.50 and $4.50 an IP. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Thordata?
answers.a: Everything is a meter — per GB, per IP, per 1K responses — so the bill scales with usage. And every rate the site advertises is the largest package on its ladder: $0.65 a GB means buying 5,000 GB, while 1 GB of the same product costs $2.00. Budget at your own volume, not at the headline. Plus the category-wide caveat we'd give any residential-proxy vendor: those '100M+ real residential IPs' come from consumer devices, so check sourcing ethics and your target sites' terms before building on it.

Thryv is genuinely best for small service businesses — trades, salons, clinics — that currently run on a diary, a spreadsheet and a separate invoicing tool, and would genuinely retire all three. Skip it if you already have a CRM you like, because this is an all-in-one and its value is the bundle; buying it alongside what you have is paying twice for the overlap.

(read 2026-09-19 on thryv.com/pricing in a real browser with the billing toggle switched both ways; the page refuses plain HTTP clients with a 403) Two published tiers and a quote-only third. The toggle opens on Monthly, where Starter is $99 a month and Signature $399. Switching to Annual, marked 'Save 15%', takes them to $85 and $340 — both still printed per month. The page prints no yearly total and does not say whether the annual term is charged up front, so any four-figure annual figure, including the $4,068 this review used to quote, is arithmetic rather than a published price. The third tier is Custom, 'Tailored pricing and solutions', sold through Talk to Sales; the Amplify name this dossier carried is no longer on the page. Both paid tiers offer a free trial. Alongside the plans sit four done-for-you services — Ads, Brand, Search and Social Boosts — none of them priced on the page, and the FAQ states they can be added to Signature and Custom plans only, not to Starter. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Thryv?
answers.a: Two published tiers, $85 and $340, and nothing between them. That makes the decision unusually blunt: not which plan fits, but whether a fourfold step is worth taking all at once. And price the commitment from what the page actually says, which is less than you would like — it prints both annual figures per month, states only that the year saves 15%, and never says whether the term is charged up front. Before that call, list which of the bundled parts you would otherwise buy separately: Thryv's case rests on replacing four or five tools, and if you only want two of them the arithmetic usually favours keeping them. Worth knowing too that the Boosts services, the part sold hardest, cannot be attached to Starter at all.

TiXel is genuinely best for Shopify merchants running Meta and TikTok ads who need more than the free channel apps give them — several pixels on one store, pixels scoped to individual products, or server-side Events API tracking alongside the browser pixel to recover events that ad-blockers and Safari strip. Skip it if you run one pixel for one brand, since Shopify's Meta and TikTok channels do that for nothing; or you cannot put real traffic through the store inside the seven-day trial, because the reported failure is a pixel that installs cleanly and then tracks nothing.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/tixel) One paid plan and no ladder to climb, and the amounts are unchanged since 22 August 2026. Unlimited Plan is $19.99 a month, or $119.94 a year at a stated 50% saving, and carries unlimited pixels, server-side Events API pixels, regular pixels via pixel code, pixels scoped to specific products, automatic event triggers with no manual event configuration, accurate tracking and online support. One term has changed and it matters: the free trial is now seven days, where the listing advertised three in August. The other tier, Development Stores, is still free but only for development and partner stores, with billing activated on upgrade — the same shape as this developer's Blocky listing. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched 19 October 2020. The review record has moved a long way: 93 reviews at 4.6, up from 78 at 4.1 in August, distributed 84 five-star, 3 four-star, none at three or two, and 6 one-star — one fewer bottom-rated review than a month ago, against fifteen more reviews overall. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TiXel?
answers.a:
The rating is the most useful number on this listing, but not for the reason an average usually is. Read on 18 September 2026 it is 4.6 across 93 reviews, and the shape behind it is 84 five-star, 3 four-star, nothing at three or two, and 6 one-star. A month earlier it was 4.1 across 78, with 7 at the bottom. Nothing sits in the middle on either reading. That is not a mediocre product; it is a binary one — it works immediately, or it installs cleanly and then tracks nothing at all.

The one-star reviews describe the same failure in the same words: the pixel is set up by the instructions, no page views or add-to-carts ever arrive, and support does not reply. We cannot verify what happened in any individual account, but the consistency of the complaint is itself information.

What is new since August is that the developer now answers them in public. A reply dated 2 September 2026 attributes the empty data to manual pixel configuration, where one mismatched ID or event setting is enough to stop events being recorded at all, and says that step is no longer needed: TiXel now integrates officially with Meta and TikTok and links the pixel to your ad account automatically. That is the vendor's account of its own worst reviews, so treat it as a claim to test rather than a fix to trust. It is at least a specific and checkable one, and the trial has gone from three days to seven, which is enough room to check it.

TicketTailor is genuinely best for event organizers with their own audience (venues, communities, creators) who want flat low per-ticket fees, full branding and no subscription. Skip it if you depend on marketplace discovery to sell tickets (Eventbrite's traffic is the fee you're paying for), or you run two events a year at tiny volume.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on tickettailor.com/pricing with the currency switched to USD) No subscription and no contract: pay-as-you-sell $0.85 a ticket, or prepaid credits from $0.70 down to $0.34 depending on volume — 100 credits (the minimum) cost $70, 500 cost $300, 1,000 cost $520 and 20,000 cost $6,800. Credits carry no time limit. Free events are free up to 5,000 tickets a year, the first five paid tickets cost nothing, and charities, B Corps, PTAs and not-for-profits get 50% off, as do very low-priced tickets. Seated tickets cost two credits rather than one. Prices switch across GBP, EUR, USD, AUD and CAD. Stripe, PayPal or Square fees apply separately and Ticket Tailor never touches the payment. Note one contradiction in their own FAQ: one answer puts the free-ticket allowance at 5,000 a year, another at 2,000. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TicketTailor?
answers.a: The fee honesty is the product — flat cents per ticket instead of percentage skims makes it dramatically cheaper than the big platforms on higher-priced tickets (a $0.30-0.85 fee on a $50 ticket vs a percentage is no contest). The trade: you bring your own audience. There's no discovery marketplace pushing your event, so if you rely on a platform's browsing traffic to sell out, the cheap fees won't fill seats.

Tidio is genuinely best for support teams that want an AI agent and a help desk from the same vendor and can size all three meters — billable conversations, Lyro AI conversations and Flows visitors — against their own volume before they commit, and Shopify, WordPress or Wix stores that want to run live chat at zero and treat the 50 free Lyro conversations as a measurement of whether the AI answers their questions at all. Skip it if you need the AI agent to keep answering past the first 50 conversations without paying, you cannot get the over-cap rate and the Plus usage rate quoted before signing, you want one per-seat price rather than three independent meters, or you are buying on the strength of the 67 percent resolution figure and need it as a commitment rather than an average.

(read 2026-08-24 on www.tidio.com/pricing/ with both billing columns clicked, and on www.tidio.com) The plan table opens on the annual column, so the first figures on the page are not what month-to-month costs. Starter is 24.17 a month billed annually against 29 paid monthly, Growth starts at 49.17 annually against 59 monthly, and the two stand-alone add-ons follow the same 20 percent step: the Lyro AI Agent from 32.50 annually against 39 monthly, Flows from 24.17 against 29. Plus is 300 a month in both columns and adds usage on top; Premium is contact-for-pricing. Tidio's own homepage quotes the higher, monthly number (“Paid plans from $29/mo, no surprise upgrades”), which makes the marketing page the more conservative of the two places you can read a price. The table rendered in euros on our reading while the same numerals appear with dollar signs on other retrievals of the same URL, so treat the figure rather than the symbol as the fact and confirm the currency at checkout.

What you pay is decided by three separate meters, not by the plan name. The free plan carries 50 billable conversations, 100 Flows visitors reached and 50 Lyro AI conversations, and the comparison table's own footnote makes that last allowance a lifetime one rather than a monthly one. Starter covers 100 billable conversations, Growth starts at 250 and the table caps it at 2,000, both with 10 seats and a 7-day free trial. Lyro conversations are upgradable from 50 to 1,000 and Flows visitors from 2,000 to 100,000. Two things the page does not say: what a conversation over the cap costs, and what the “discounted usage rates” next to Plus's “+ monthly usage” actually are. On Plus that unquoted rate is the whole variable, because the 300 is only the entry fee. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tidio?
answers.a:
The AI number on the homepage and the AI number on the pricing page do not agree, and the pricing page is the lower of the two. The homepage, read 24 August 2026, says Lyro “resolves 67% of conversations instantly” and repeats it as a statistic: 67% of conversations resolved instantly. The pricing table, read the same day, lists “Guaranteed 50% Lyro AI resolution rate” as a Premium feature — the most expensive tier on the page. So the figure the marketing quotes is 17 points above the figure the company is willing to guarantee, and the guarantee is only available if you talk to sales about the top plan. Both numbers can be true at once; a typical result and a contractual floor are different things. But it does mean that if you are buying on the strength of 67 percent, you are buying an average someone else achieved, not a commitment to you.

Second, the plan table opens on annual billing. The headline 24.17 and 49.17 become 29 and 59 the moment you click Monthly, and the two add-ons move 32.50 to 39 and 24.17 to 29. Nothing is hidden — the toggle is right there and the annual column is honestly labelled “2 months free” — but the number you remember from the pricing page is about 20 percent below the number you pay unless you commit for a year. Tidio's own homepage quotes the monthly figure, so the two pages leave a buyer with two different first impressions of the same plan.

Third, “Free plan forever” is true for the help desk and not for the AI. The free tier's 50 Lyro AI conversations are one-off: the comparison table footnote reads that your first 50 conversations are free (lifetime), and the same applies to the 100 Flows visitors. The live chat and ticketing side really does keep working at zero, but the AI agent that the whole homepage is built around stops after 50 conversations ever, which for a shop with any traffic is a matter of days. Read the free plan as a trial of Lyro inside a permanently free help desk, not as a free AI agent.

TnC is genuinely best for Shopify merchants on a standard plan who need a recorded “I agree” gate before payment — for GDPR, an age gate, digital-goods withdrawal rules or chargeback defence — and who go to Advanced at $12.99 for the consent timestamp rather than stopping at the $7.99 headline. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus and want the checkbox inside the real checkout page, where the plan you need is the $19.99 Plus tier the App Store listing does not show; you expected a free tier from the listing's badge, which covers development and partner stores only; or a checkbox on the cart and the express buttons is not the enforcement your legal requirement actually asks for.

(read 2026-08-25 and re-verified 2026-09-09 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article at www.effectify.help) The monthly ladder is $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99, and it has held there since the August rise: read on 24 August 2026 the same three plans, carrying the same feature lists, cost $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99. What moved between 25 August and 9 September is the annual price. It used to be $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, roughly a 30% saving; the listing now shows $47.94, $77.94 and $89.94 and says “save 50%”. That is exactly six months' money for a year at every tier, where in August it was seven-tenths of the year, so the annual route got cheaper while the monthly one did not move at all.

Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $7.99 a month or $47.94 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $12.99 a month or $77.94 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $14.99 a month or $89.94 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing article, re-read on 9 September 2026, has not followed. It still prints the old annual rates of $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, still puts the annual saving at approximately 30%, and still answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above” — while the App Store listing, which is where the charge is actually raised, prints a different number for the same plan. It is also the only page where a fifth plan appears at all: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one monthly rate that has never moved, so the gap between the top listed plan and the hidden one is $5. The article also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge.

Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and stood at 550 listing reviews with a 4.9 average on 9 September 2026, up from 514 two weeks earlier. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with TnC?
answers.a:
Start with the badge at the top of the listing, because it is the one thing on this page that misleads. “Free plan available” is displayed twice, and the free plan is Development Stores — for development and partner stores only, with payment activated on upgrade. A store that takes real orders has no free tier here. It is the same shape as this developer's Blocky and TiXel listings, where the advertised free plan is also development stores rather than a working free tier, so read it as a house pattern rather than an oversight.

Second, the App Store's pricing table is incomplete. The vendor's own help-centre article lists a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month, Shopify Plus only, and describes it as the plan that shows the checkbox in the actual checkout page. The App Store listing shows four plans and not that one. The same article answers its own hidden-fees question with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above”, which is true of that article and not of the listing most buyers will read first. If you are on Plus and you want consent captured in checkout rather than in the cart, the price is two and a half times the headline.

Third, the feature that makes the app defensible costs extra, and what it costs is not stable. Basic at $7.99 shows the checkbox; it does not record when anyone ticked it. Consent-date logging starts on Advanced at $12.99. Read a day earlier, on 24 August 2026, those same two plans were $6.99 and $9.99 with identical feature lists, so the step from checkbox to audit trail went from $3 to $5 overnight while the listing said nothing about it. For an app whose pitch is chargebacks and legal risk, an audit trail as a paid upgrade is worth knowing before you compare $7.99 against anything else.

Fourth, be clear about what this can and cannot enforce. On a store that is not on Shopify Plus the checkbox lives in the cart and on express-checkout buttons, not inside Shopify's checkout, because Shopify does not open that page to apps below Plus. The listing is honest about the surfaces it does cover — cart drawers, Buy It Now, express checkout buttons, floating carts, PayPal and Apple Pay — but a shopper who reaches payment by another route has not passed a gate. Whether that is sufficient consent is a question for your own counsel rather than for an app listing.

Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views device and activity data including geolocation, IP address, browser and operating system and browsing behaviour, and can view and edit customers, products, orders for the last 60 days, store analytics, web pixels and the Online Store script tags and theme. Geolocation is what the country targeting on Advanced and above runs on, so the scope is explicable, but an app installed for compliance reasons that itself processes IP addresses and browsing behaviour belongs in the same register as everything else you had to write down.

Todoist is genuinely best for individuals and small teams who want a fast, elegant task manager that gets out of the way. Skip it if you need full project management with timelines, workloads and dependencies — this is a to-do app, not a PM suite.
Free (up to 5 projects, one automatic reminder per task); Pro about $5/mo (annual, ~$7 monthly), Business about $8/user/mo (annual, ~$10 monthly) (2026). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Todoist?
answers.a: The free plan's 5-project cap, and reminders that fire only at the moment a task comes due, push most serious users to Pro quickly — but Pro is genuinely cheap. It's a personal/team task manager, not a full project platform, so don't expect Gantt-level PM.

Toggl is genuinely best for freelancers, consultants and agencies that bill by the hour and want frictionless tracking with budgets, rates and profitability per project. Skip it if you need surveillance-style monitoring (screenshots, activity scoring — deliberately not Toggl's philosophy), or free-tier tracking already covers you.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on toggl.com/track/pricing) Free is $0 for a limited number of users and the page calls it free forever. Starter is $9 per user a month billed annually and $12 monthly; Premium is $16 annually and $24 monthly; Enterprise is quoted. The introductory $14 Premium rate renewing at $18 that we recorded in August is gone — Premium now carries one annual price. The billing toggle advertises 'Annual (Save 33.3%)' and '4 months free', which holds exactly for Premium but not for Starter, where $12 to $9 is 25%. Trial is 30 days; Enterprise adds volume discounts on annual and multiple workspaces under one organisation. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Toggl?
answers.a: Toggl's honesty problem is the good kind: the free tier is so capable that many teams never need to pay — the paid line is drawn exactly at 'do you bill clients' (budgets, rates, profitability). If you do, Starter earns itself fast; if you track time for personal discipline, resist the upgrade. Time tracking's real cost everywhere is adoption: the tool is frictionless, but the habit still has to be built.

Top Echelon is genuinely best for recruiting agencies and SMB staffing firms that want an applicant tracking system and CRM in one place, especially ones that would actually work split placements with other recruiters. Skip it if you are an in-house talent team hiring for your own company — this is built around agency and split-placement workflows, so you would carry a network you never use.

answers.q: How much does Top Echelon cost?
answers.a: (2026-09-10, read on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) TE Recruit (the ATS and CRM) runs $79 per seat per month billed annually or $95 month-to-month on Standard, and $95 billed annually or $115 month-to-month on Professional. Those seat rates rose during 2026: the same cards read $75/$89 on Standard and $89/$110 on Professional when we read them on 25 August 2026. TE Network, the split-placement network, is priced per agency rather than per seat and is unchanged: $135 per month billed annually with the $350 startup fee waived, or $150 per month billed monthly plus a $350 one-time startup fee. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Top Echelon?
answers.a: Almost everything people shop for sits in Professional, not Standard: Smart-TE AI, automations, sequences, inbound email sync and API access are all one tier up, so Standard is a competent but plain ATS. The bigger thing to price honestly is that TE Recruit and TE Network are two separate subscriptions. The network is billed per agency on top of your seats, so "Top Echelon" can mean two bills. And taking the network month-to-month adds a $350 one-time startup fee that annual billing waives.

Trackr is genuinely best for Shopify stores shipping a few hundred to a few thousand parcels a month that want where-is-my-order traffic off the support desk — one branded tracking page across every carrier, estimated delivery dates, and proactive email, WhatsApp or US SMS updates — and that like the idea of tracking living in Apple and Google Wallet instead of in an email thread. Skip it if you ship under a hundred parcels a month, where $10 buys 400 shipments you will not use and the carrier's own page is free; you need SMS outside the United States, which is not offered; or you cannot carry the risk of a tracking page that went down inside the last year.

(price read 2026-09-12) Four tiers and no free plan, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify: Basic $10 a month or $96 a year for 400 shipments a month, Standard $45 or $432 for 2,000, Advanced $150 or $1,440 for 9,000 and Enterprise $250 or $2,400 for 18,000. Annual billing saves 20% and every tier carries a 14-day trial. The feature list is identical on all four — branded tracking page, estimated delivery dates, email, WhatsApp and US-only SMS updates, Apple and Google Wallet tracking, Klaviyo, Omnisend, Segment and chatbot integrations, product upsell and translation — so the only thing the ladder sells is shipment volume. The Shopify listing does not say what happens past your allowance. The vendor's own page does: parceltrackr.com/pricing, read the same day, prints $0.05 per extra shipment on every tier. That number decides whether you upgrade or overrun, because in-plan a shipment costs 2.5 cents on Basic, 2.25 on Standard, 1.7 on Advanced and 1.4 on Enterprise — so an overrun is priced at two to four times what the same shipment costs inside the plan. The two sources also disagree about the trial: the listing offers 3,000 and 5,000 bonus trackings on Advanced and Enterprise, the vendor page 1,500 and 2,000. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Trackr?
answers.a: The rating is 4.1 over 56 reviews on 12 September 2026, and the shape says more than the average: 45 five-star, three three-star, one two-star and seven one-star, which is a split verdict rather than a soft middle. The reviews name the reason. On 14 June 2026 a merchant wrote that the app was down again and asked for it to be fixed; the vendor replied the next day confirming a service disruption that had since been resolved. For an app whose entire job is the page a customer opens when they are already worried about a parcel, downtime is the failure mode, not an inconvenience. The listing is also careless with its own numbers: it says more than 1,900 carriers in one line and more than 2,200 in another, while the vendor's site says 2,100-plus. And one advertised feature deserves a straight look before you switch it on — a dropshipping mode that hides the carrier and the Chinese origin of a shipment from your customer. The listing presents it as a selling point; whether your tracking page should withhold that is a decision about your own store, and worth making deliberately.

Tradify is genuinely best for electricians, plumbers, HVAC and other trades businesses that want quoting, scheduling, job tracking and invoicing from the field in one simple app. Skip it if you're a solo operator who invoices from a spreadsheet happily, or you need heavy project-management/accounting depth rather than trades job management.

Per user, per month, quoted in USD on tradifyhq.com/pricing and re-verified 2026-09-14: Lite $47, Pro $51 and Plus $61 per user, plus a Custom tier for large teams that is priced on request. The 14-day free trial includes all features. The Instant Website add-on is $12 a month. There is no free plan and no volume ladder published on the page — the per-user rate is flat within a plan. One thing to get right before you search: the product lives at tradifyhq.com. The shorter tradify.com is a parked holding page that reads "Launching Soon" and is not the vendor (checked 14 September 2026). Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tradify?
answers.a: Per-user pricing is honest and simple, but it means the cost scales linearly with headcount — a ten-person crew is a real monthly number, not the single-seat sticker. It's purpose-built for trades job management (quoting, scheduling, invoicing), so it's not a general project-management or accounting suite; you'll still run Xero or QuickBooks alongside it. For a trades business that's a feature, not a flaw.

Trainerize is genuinely best for personal trainers and studios delivering structured workout/nutrition coaching through a polished client app, scaling by client count. Skip it if you coach a handful of clients over WhatsApp and sheets happily, or you want one flat price without add-on shopping.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on www.trainerize.com/pricing; prices in USD and subject to applicable taxes, annual plans billed once a year) Basic is free for 1 client; Grow is $9/mo for 2 clients; Pro starts at $23/mo for 5 client seats and steps up through 15, 30, 50, 75, 100 and 200 seats, with the comparison table showing $275/mo at the 200-client end; Studio Plus is $248/mo for each location added, with 5+ locations quoted. Add-ons are priced per tier: on Pro, Advanced Nutrition Coaching $45/mo, Business $25/mo, Stripe Integrated Payments $10/mo, Video Coaching $10/mo and a Pro-level Custom Branded App at a one-time $169. On Grow, nutrition is $20/mo (struck through from $45) with Business, payments and video at the same $25/$10/$10 and no branded app. Studio Plus includes all five. The branded app also requires your own Apple Developer Account at $99/year, charged directly by Apple. FitMetrics is a separate add-on from $6 per client. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Trainerize?
answers.a: The client-count ladder looks gentle, but the add-ons are flat and they land hardest on the smallest coach: at five seats a $23 Pro plan dressed with nutrition, payments and video is $88, while the same three turn the $275 two-hundred-client row into $340. Price the stack you'll actually coach with, and note that the branded app is $169 to Trainerize plus a $99/year Apple Developer Account billed by Apple. That said, the client experience and ABC ecosystem are genuinely mature; churn-prone coaches lose more to a clunky app than to a fair subscription.

Trainual is genuinely best for growing teams (roughly 10+ staff) that need to document SOPs and onboard new hires consistently instead of training by osmosis. Skip it if you're a team of two or three — a well-organized Notion or Google Doc captures your processes without the seat-band pricing.

(re-read 2026-09-18 on trainual.com/pricing) No prices at all. The page lists four plans — Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise, grouped under a Training, an Operations and a Performance suite — and every one of them carries a “Get a demo” button where a rate would be. The only figure the page publishes is a one-time implementation fee of $1,000, stated in its own FAQ alongside a 4–6 week engagement with an implementation specialist. The FAQ also answers the sizing question directly: “Trainual is best suited for companies with 25 - 1000 employees”, and says pricing varies with team size and the features you need. Pricing is quote-only. An earlier version of this entry carried monthly figures attributed to unnamed third-party sources; those are not on the vendor's page and could not be traced to a named source, so they have been removed rather than repeated.

There is also no self-serve way to try it. The FAQ question “Can I try Trainual before committing to a subscription?” is answered with an invitation to book a demo, not with a trial, so a sales conversation is the only route in. Two things are quantified beyond the fee: the implementation team aims to have interviews completed and content in the account within 10 business days, and 500+ templates are included, with 400+ expert-built courses sold separately as a premium courses add-on whose price the page does not give. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Trainual?
answers.a: You cannot find out what it costs without booking a demo. All four plans — Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise — are quote-gated, and the single number the pricing page publishes is the one-time implementation fee of $1,000. The same page answers the sizing question plainly, best suited for companies with 25 to 1000 employees, so a small team is being told twice that it is not the buyer here: once by the fit range and once by a setup fee that arrives before the subscription does. Under a handful of staff, a shared doc may do.

Tresorit is genuinely best for businesses and professionals with confidentiality obligations (legal, health, finance) that need end-to-end-encrypted storage, granular sharing controls and compliance features. Skip it if you want cheap bulk storage or deep app integrations (mainstream clouds win), or a personal-grade E2EE like Proton Drive covers your needs at lower cost.

(re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own business and personal pricing pages) There are three business plans: Professional for 1 user, Business from 3 users and Business Pro from 5 users. Priced from our location in euros, they run €29.99, €20 and €25 per user per month on monthly billing, and €23.99, €16 and €20 on yearly — which the page badges as 20% off. Personal runs a permanent free Basic tier plus Lite, Essential and Pro (€4.99, €11.99 and €29.99 a month from here). Our dollar reading of the same plans on 4 August 2026 gave Professional $33.99, Business $24 and Business Pro $30 per user per month. Storage runs 4 TB on Professional, from 6 TB on Business and from 15 TB on Business Pro, with maximum file sizes of 10, 15 and 20 GB. Every plan carries a 14-day trial with no feature limits, but Tresorit requires payment details up front to start it. Enterprise is quote-only. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Tresorit?
answers.a: You pay the Swiss-E2EE premium — noticeably above mainstream clouds and above Proton Drive per GB — and the encryption trade-offs are inherent: no server-side content search, more deliberate sharing flows, and credential/recovery discipline is on you. For regulated teams that's exactly the deal; for casual storage it's over-engineering.

Turbotic is genuinely best for teams that want an AI-assisted way to discover, document and run automations without deep RPA expertise. Skip it if you need a huge, battle-tested integration ecosystem right now — an established platform has more connectors and community.

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own product page) The Turbotic AI Assistant is $25 per seat per month and includes 1,500 credits a month, with additional credits bought as needed. The broader orchestration platform is not priced publicly at all: turbotic.com/pricing now redirects to the site's own demo-booking form, with no figures on it, so everything above the assistant seat is quoted after a sales conversation. No free plan is mentioned. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Turbotic?
answers.a: It's a newer, enterprise-leaning automation platform, so it's less proven with a smaller community than the big names — and the credit-per-execution model means heavy volume needs cost-checking. Verify it integrates with your actual stack first.

Typewise is genuinely best for customer-service teams with real ticket volume that want AI agents to resolve requests end to end and act inside the systems they already run — CRM, ERP, billing, commerce — with approval steps and human handover as they raise the automation level. Skip it if your helpdesk's built-in AI answers already absorb the volume, or your channel mix leans on phone support — their home page lists voice among the channels while their own SMB page still marks it "coming soon", so pin that down before you sign.

(re-read 2026-09-05 on typewise.app/pricing, a page that did not exist in August) A base plan plus a per-resolution rate. Starter is $99 a month or $999 a year with 1 user, email and chat, a $20 monthly AI Operator budget and pay-as-you-go resolutions at $2 each. Growth is $599 a month or $5,999 a year with 5 users, all digital channels, a $100 AI Operator budget and volume packages that bring resolutions down to $1. Business is $2,000 a month billed annually with unlimited workspaces, a $1,500 AI Operator budget, a custom DPA and a success consultant. Additional users are $89 a month. Every plan starts with a 14-day trial of 100 resolution credits and $10 of AI Operator credit, no card. The page defines the meter: a full resolution counts once, and unresolved tickets are free. Prices are in USD and shown in EUR, GBP or CHF at parity depending on your location. History: in August 2026 the only published number was 'starting from $1 per resolution' on the home page and /pricing returned a 404. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Typewise?
answers.a: The bill has two parts and both are published: a base fee from $99 and a resolution rate from $2 (pay as you go) down to $1 with volume packages. The meter is published too — a ticket closed end to end counts as one resolution, a hand-off to a person counts as half, and a ticket passed straight through or flagged is free. So a conversation the AI cannot finish still bills, at half rate, which is fair but worth budgeting for. What the page still does not say is whether a reopened ticket counts again; get that in writing before the trial. The ROI calculator on their site is the vendor's own arithmetic; the pilot is where you replace it with yours.

UENI is genuinely best for small-business owners with no time or tech skills who want a professional site built for them, not another tool to learn. Skip it if you want full control over design, run a real e-commerce store, or need deep customisation and integrations — a DIY builder gives you more freedom.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on www.ueni.com/pricing; every figure below unchanged since the August reading) A done-for-you website, now sold in four tiers rather than one. Every tier carries the same setup fee of $599, currently promoted at $79. Launch is $24.99/mo and covers a custom-designed site, domain and SSL, hosting, one professional email address and 30 days of done-for-you edits. Plus is $59.00/mo and adds unlimited done-for-you edits, four email addresses, advanced SEO, integrations such as live chat and lead forms, promotion on Google, Facebook and Instagram, and VIP phone support. Ecommerce is $99.00/mo and adds a full online store with abandoned cart recovery, social selling, subscriptions and courses, advanced bookings and deposits, automated sales tax and a loyalty programme. Growth is $124.99/mo and adds a dedicated VIP Growth Team, a custom marketing plan, monthly one-on-one sessions and 2,000 words of fresh content a month. A yearly toggle advertises about 17% off: our August capture records $20.83 a month ($249.90 billed annually) on Launch and $49.17 ($590) on Plus, with two-year rates of $18.74 ($449.82) and $44.25 ($1,062). Transaction fees are 0% on every tier and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with UENI?
answers.a: It's done-for-you, which is the appeal and the catch. DIY editing and customisation are limited, e-commerce and integrations are basic, and the most common complaint is the gap between the 7-day promise and reality — slow design turnaround and patchy communication with the team. Expect some upselling.

UltaHost is genuinely best for budget-conscious owners, developers and small businesses that want cheap, fast NVMe hosting (shared or VPS) with free migration and DDoS protection, and will prepay a multi-year term. Skip it if you run a business-critical, high-traffic site that needs premium managed hosting with guaranteed enterprise support, or you don't want to lock into a multi-year term to get the good rate.

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on ultahost.com/shared-hosting) The term ladder is Monthly, Yearly -30%, 2 Years -40% and 3 Years -50%, and the page opens on the two-year term. At that term the shared plans are Starter $3.44/mo (list $6.89) for 1 domain, ~10,000 visits a month and 30 GB NVMe; Basic $5.18 (list $9.19) for 4 domains and ~15,000 visits; Business $10.35 (list $17.02) for unlimited domains and ~25,000 visits; and Pro $13.23 (list $21.62). Every card now states 'Billed for 24 month term. Renews at [the same rate] /mo for 2 years. Cancel anytime.', which settles the renewal contradiction our August capture recorded. The banner above the table advertises a different entry price, $4.13. 30-day money-back guarantee, free SSL, free backups, cPanel. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with UltaHost?
answers.a: It's the classic budget-host trade-off, with one thing in its favour. The sticker price is a term commitment, not a monthly rate: the headline figures are the 2-year prices, the discount ladder runs -30% yearly, -40% for two years and -50% for three, and paying monthly gives all of it back. What has changed is the renewal. Each plan card now states it renews at the same rate for another 2 years, so the usual trap of a cheap first term followed by a dear one is at least written down. Read that line on the plan you actually pick, because it is quoted per plan. The headline rates also sit under a running 40%-off sale, so treat the crossed-out price as marketing rather than a baseline. Support is generally fast but can be hit-or-miss depending on which agent picks up your ticket, and it's a smaller, less-established brand than the big managed hosts. It's a value play, not a premium-SLA one.

Unbounce is genuinely best for PPC specialists and agencies running paid campaigns who want A/B testing and Smart Traffic (AI routing each visitor to the best-converting variant). Skip it if your traffic or budget is small, or you want cheap unlimited pages — Landingi starts around $29/mo for similar basics.

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page, USD) Five published levels, monthly against yearly at 25% off: Starter $29 / $22, Build $99 / $74, Experiment $149 / $112, Optimize $249 / $187, plus Concierge custom pricing above that. The Starter tier is missing from most summaries, ours included until the August 2026 update, which described the range as beginning at $74. Pages are unlimited on every plan; what pushes you up a tier is the visitor cap, so a traffic spike rather than a page count is what changes your bill. Unlimited A/B testing starts at Experiment, and AI traffic optimization at Optimize. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Unbounce?
answers.a: The entry price is high for a landing-page tool, and the visitor caps bite if a campaign takes off. It's also oddly behind on basics — no URL import, limited file/code management, and still no true AI page generation in 2026.

UniTel Voice is genuinely best for solopreneurs and small teams that want a professional toll-free or local number, auto-attendant and call routing on their existing phones — no hardware. Skip it if you need integrated video meetings, team chat and a full contact center, or you have no need for a separate business line at all.

answers.q: How much does UniTel Voice cost?
answers.a: (re-verified 2026-09-09 on unitelvoice.com/pricing) Three plans, no contracts: Solo $9.99/mo, Team $19.99/mo and Office $29.99/mo, each with one phone number and unlimited minutes. Annual billing takes 30% off, making them $6.99, $13.99 and $20.99 a month. Solo is one user, Team carries unlimited users, and Office includes three with additional users at $9.99 each a month. The plan set we recorded in August — Start-Up, Unlimited at $24.99 and Office-Max at $69.99 — is no longer offered on the page. Support is US-based, there is a 30-day money-back guarantee, and every plan includes a professionally recorded greeting. One caveat on those unlimited minutes: the pricing FAQ offers 3.9¢ per minute above "the minutes on your plan" and still names an Office-Max plan the page no longer sells, so the page contradicts its own cards — probably stale text, but unconfirmed. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with UniTel Voice?
answers.a: It's a virtual phone layer, not a full unified-comms suite — you won't find the deep team messaging, video meetings and contact-center features pricier platforms bundle. For a solo founder or small team that just needs a professional number, auto-attendant and call routing, that focus is exactly the point; for a larger org wanting one platform for everything, it will feel thin.

Uniqode is genuinely best for marketing teams that need dynamic QR codes with real analytics and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, optional HIPAA). Skip it if you only need the occasional static QR code — a free generator does that, and Bitly is better if link-shortening is your main job.

(re-verified 2026-09-13 on their own pricing page, read both as plain HTML and as a live browser render) The plan cards are rendered in the browser and carry no price in either reading, so what we can hold Uniqode to is its own pricing FAQ on that page, read 13 September 2026. Static QR codes are free and there is no limit on how many you create; dynamic QR codes start at a stated minimum of $9/month. NEW since our August reading: the FAQ now prices one named tier, Core at $49/month, which it calls the best value -- it does not say where Core sits in the Starter, Lite, Pro, Plus and Business+ ladder the same FAQ uses elsewhere. A custom domain is a Plus add-on at $2,000 per domain per year. Your first digital business card is free, with extra seats on a Team plan at $6 per user per month; Business+ card pricing is custom. There is a 14-day free trial, and when it expires the dynamic codes made during it go inactive while static codes keep working (without account access). Billing is annual only, in USD, invoice billing is Business+ only, and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee. Third-party listings quote a $5 entry tier; that is not what Uniqode's own page says, and we are not repeating a Lite or Pro figure we could not read at the source. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Uniqode?
answers.a: The tier jumps are steep and a lot is gated: analytics are capped at 60 days on the entry plan, scan limits apply across all tiers, and custom domains sit behind higher pricing. It's a real QR platform — but overkill if you just want the occasional code.

Unleashed Software is genuinely best for manufacturers and wholesalers who have outgrown spreadsheets and need real-time stock across multiple warehouses, with batch and serial tracking, landed costs and purchase-to-sale visibility in one system. Skip it if your order volume is low or steady enough that the included 100 a month covers it and a lighter tool would do — at that size you are buying capacity you do not use, and the per-order tiers only pay back once volume is there.

answers.q: How much does Unleashed Software cost?
answers.a: (prices read 2026-08-17 on unleashedsoftware.com/pricing) Two bundles, in USD and excluding tax. Unleashed Core is $399 a month, or $4,389 a year which the page itself puts at $366 equivalent monthly. Unleashed Pro is $729 a month, or $8,019 a year at $668 equivalent monthly. The toggle promises “Save up to 10%”; the actual saving works out at 8.3% on Core and 8.4% on Pro. Both bundles come with a 14-day free trial with all features enabled. What the headline covers is the part worth reading twice: Core includes 3 user licences, Pro 5, and both include just 100 sales orders a month and 250,000 or 500,000 API calls. Everything past that is priced separately. Extra users are $69 a month on Core and $89 on Pro. Sales-order upgrades run $70 (up to 500), $200 (up to 1,500), $320 (up to 3,000) or $490 (unlimited) a month. And support is a paid add-on at $99 a month for Standard or $239 for Premier. Onboarding is a one-off fee on top: $449 self-service, $799 standard, $5,549 full. Optional modules start at $119 a month for Advanced Inventory Manager, $262 for Marketing Accelerator and $450 for CRM. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Unleashed Software?
answers.a: The 100 sales orders a month included on both bundles is the number that decides your bill, not the $399. A wholesaler running 1,500 orders with six users who wants phone support pays $399 for Core, $200 for the order tier, $207 for three extra seats and $99 for Standard support. That is $905 a month, or 2.3 times the headline, before a one-off onboarding fee of at least $449. Support being a paid add-on rather than part of the plan is the detail most comparison tables miss. Price the bundle you will actually be on: count your busiest month's orders, your real seat count, and decide whether you can live without phone support, then compare that total against the alternatives rather than comparing entry prices.

Upsell.com is genuinely best for shopify merchants who want one funnel covering product page, cart, post-purchase and thank-you offers with AI recommendations and A/B testing, and who are either under 2,000 orders a month — where the whole feature set costs $9.99 — or well past it, where $199 buys priority support rather than more product. Skip it if you are close to 2,000 orders a month, because the next rung is $199 and there is nothing between the two — or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells, which stay closed to you.

(prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on upsell.com/pricing and on the Shopify listing apps.shopify.com/reconvert-upsell-cross-sell; both now show the same ladder, which replaces the $4.99/$9.99/$19.99 tiers we recorded on 2 September) Billed in USD. Every tier carries the same feature set — the vendor's own comparison says so in as many words, "Every feature is included on every plan. Tiers differ by order volume and support" — so you are buying volume and support, not features. Free: up to 50 monthly store orders or $50 of upsell revenue, whichever is hit first. Growth $9.99 a month: from 51 orders or $51 of upsell revenue, up to 2,000. Scale $199 a month, or $149 a month billed annually, up to 10,000. Elite $499 a month, or $399 a month billed annually, up to 20,000. Enterprise is quote-only above 20,000 and adds one invoice across multiple stores. The annual saving is 25% on both paid tiers; the Shopify listing renders it as "$149/year and save 94%", which is its own arithmetic and not what the vendor's page says. Two contradictions on upsell.com/pricing itself: the Scale card says "Billed monthly" while the comparison table one screen below says Scale is billed "Annual only", and the Growth card is labelled FREE above a volume list that runs to 2,000 orders, while the listing prices anything from the 51st order at $9.99. A 14-day free trial is offered on each paid tier. Checkout upsells remain Shopify Plus only. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Upsell.com?
answers.a: The ladder is public now, and that removes the complaint we had in September, but it leaves a cliff where the old one had a gap. Growth covers you to 2,000 orders a month for $9.99. The next rung is Scale at $199. There is nothing in between, so the store that grows from 1,900 orders to 2,100 does not pay a little more — it pays twenty times more, for a feature set the vendor says is identical on every plan. What Scale actually buys at that price is priority chat, guided onboarding and earlier access to features. The page also argues with itself in two places: the Scale card says billed monthly while the comparison table one screen below says Scale is annual only, and the Growth card is headed FREE above a volume list running to 2,000 orders while the Shopify listing charges $9.99 from the 51st. And checkout upsells are still Shopify Plus only, so on a standard Shopify plan the checkout stage of the funnel you are buying stays shut.

UpsellPlus is genuinely best for shopify merchants who want one app covering product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS offers rather than three, especially Shopify Plus stores, where the checkout half of the product actually unlocks. Skip it if your upsell revenue sits near the $500 ceiling that Free and the $49 plan share — the first paid step buys features, not headroom — or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells.

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout AND on the vendor's own pricing page, USD; listed amounts unchanged since 31 August) Fixed monthly tiers based on the revenue generated through UpsellPlus offers, with no percentage commission. The listing shows four: Free runs one offer, opens all twelve upsell types plus analytics, and allows up to $500 in upsell revenue. Launch is $49 a month or $500 a year (saves 15%) and allows the same $500 of app-generated revenue a month, adding cart, pop-up and drawer upsells, product page and post-purchase upsells, multivariate A/B testing, progress bars and free gifts. The tier named Shopify Plus is $119 a month or $1,149 a year (save 20%), raises the ceiling to $2,000 a month and adds checkout customization, checkout upsells, thank-you page customization and AI recommendations. Scale is $199 a month or $1,899 a year (save 20%) for up to $5,000 a month, live support and multivariate A/B testing. 14-day free trial on the paid tiers; charges billed every 30 days. The vendor's own page adds two things the listing does not carry: a fifth Enterprise tier with no published price, sold through a demo, and a Managed Service at an extra $499 a month. That page also contradicts itself on Scale — the plan card and the listing both say up to $5,000 a month, while its comparison table puts Scale under Unlimited; unresolved on 19 September 2026. Hitting a ceiling is not a stop: their FAQ says you automatically upgrade to the next tier so upsells are not interrupted, so the bill rises by itself. Their FAQ also states Shopify Plus is NOT required except for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is a Shopify restriction; cart, product page, cart drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with UpsellPlus?
answers.a: The plans are capped by the revenue they are allowed to earn you, and the first paid step does not raise that cap: Free and the $49 Launch plan both stop at $500 of upsell revenue a month. The $49 buys offers and features, not headroom — headroom starts at $119. And crossing a ceiling is not something you decide: their FAQ says you are automatically upgraded to the next tier so the offers keep running, so a good week moves the invoice on its own. Read the feature list closely too, because the tier named Shopify Plus is not the same thing as the requirement — their FAQ says Plus is needed only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, so on a standard Shopify store the checkout half of a checkout-upsell app is not what you are buying. The last gap is at the top: the plan card says Scale stops at $5,000 a month and the comparison table on the same page says Unlimited, and above it sits an Enterprise tier with no published price at all.

UptimeRobot is genuinely best for solo builders and small teams monitoring sites, ports and APIs at 60-second resolution with status pages — and honestly, the free 50-monitor tier covers most hobby stacks. Skip it if you need many teammates in the dashboard (seats are a paid add-on) or heavy SMS alerting — credits stack on top of the subscription.

(read 2026-08-26 on uptimerobot.com/pricing over a US connection) Free is $0. Solo starts at $144 a year, Team is $468 and Scale starts at $948 — the page quotes yearly, not monthly, which makes it look cheaper per line than it is against monthly-priced rivals. Login seats are the upsell: none on Solo, three on Team, five on Scale, and more at $15 or $19 each a month. Data retention runs three months on Free, twelve on Solo and twenty-four above that. They publish a machine-readable version of this page for AI agents, which is rare enough to be worth noting. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with UptimeRobot?
answers.a: The famous free tier is real — but the paid ladder has quiet extras: extra login seats cost $15-19 per month EACH beyond the included ones, and SMS or voice-call alerts are pay-per-credit on every plan. The Solo tier includes no team seats at all.

VEA is genuinely best for hands-on entrepreneurs and small-business owners buried in operational detail who want AI that learns their specific business and helps surface what's actually holding it back — explicitly not enterprise software. Skip it if you run a larger organization with established teams and processes (VEA itself positions against that), or you need a task-specific tool rather than a business-level advisor.

(re-verified 2026-09-02 on VEA's own pricing page) Four tiers now, per user per month, monthly against annual: $30 / $25, $50 / $40, $150 / $120 and $597 / $497. The three-tier ladder we read in August ($31.95 / $24.95, $49.95 / $39.95, $77.95 / $59.95) was replaced between our 2 August and 1 September 2026 captures: the two lower tiers were rounded to whole dollars, the old top tier at $77.95 is gone, the new third tier costs roughly double it, and a fourth tier sits above that. The page's marketing line still says 'Starting at $24.95 per user per month', a figure no longer on the plan cards. Annual billing saves roughly 17% to 20%. The tiers are separated by how much the AI does rather than by seats: the entry plan is task tracking and team alignment, First Class adds AI agents handling routine work, and Private Jet adds AI analysis and decision guidance. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with VEA?
answers.a: The pitch is unusually bold: an AI that learns your business the way a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it. That ambition is also the honest caveat — it's a young product making a big promise, its price ladder was rebuilt in August 2026 with a top tier at $597 per user a month, and independent review coverage is still thin. Judge it in the trial on one measurable question: did it identify a constraint you recognize as painfully real? If yes, it earns the next month. If its advice stays generic — the thing its own positioning promises to avoid — walk.

VWO is genuinely best for teams that want an all-in-one experience-optimisation platform (A/B testing + heatmaps + personalisation) with friendlier Bayesian stats and transparent pricing. Skip it if you're a small business wanting advanced targeting/MVT on the entry tier (you'll be priced up), or an enterprise running massive concurrent experiments — Optimizely handles that scale.

No price is published any more. Re-read in a browser on 10 September 2026, vwo.com/pricing/ still lists Growth, Pro and Enterprise as feature tables only: every tier's button is 'Schedule a Demo', and the rendered page contains no currency amount anywhere and no monthly-tracked-user tier or traffic slider — the same picture as the 4 September 2026 reading. vwo.com/llms.txt carries no amount either. The ~$314/mo for 10k MTUs this dossier carried until 4 September 2026 was a published figure the vendor has since withdrawn. Self-serve access is now an 'Explore for Free' route rather than a priced tier. One change since the September reading: the page now also sells Wandz, their AI layer, in Core and Advanced tiers — Core (MCP and AI Analyze) is listed inside Growth, while Advanced adds AI Workflow, AI Autopilot and Synthetic AB Test — and it too carries no price. The tier lines are unchanged: multivariate testing, guardrail metrics, advanced targeting and downloadable reports start at Pro; API access, SSO, mutually exclusive groups and a dedicated CSM only at Enterprise. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with VWO?
answers.a: The jump from Growth to Pro is steep — small businesses get priced out of MVT and complex targeting — and the UI is dense with options. Some users note the reporting breaks more often than pricier tools (though it doesn't affect the tests themselves). The part that costs people money later is what happens to a winner. VWO applies page changes through its SmartCode — their own page says the asynchronous SmartCode “loads page changes asynchronously when the web page loads” — so a variant left running in the editor is rendered by VWO rather than built into your site. Fine while you pay, gone when you stop. Their server-side testing changes the arithmetic here, because those changes live in your own stack; the client-side ones do not.

Velora is genuinely best for nonprofits that want donor CRM, fund accounting and online fundraising from one vendor, purpose-built for charities rather than adapted business tools. Skip it if you're a tiny charity that only needs a donation page (free tools cover that), or you're deeply invested in one best-of-breed piece already.

Quote-only. joinvelora.com (read in a browser on 5 September 2026) has no pricing page and no amount anywhere; every call to action is 'Talk to sales'. Velora bundles Keela (CRM), Aplos (accounting) and Raisely (fundraising) for nonprofits, and the individual product prices we recorded earlier (Keela from about $134 a month, Aplos from about $79) are no longer shown on the unified site, so treat them as historical until sales confirms. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Velora?
answers.a: Velora is three acquired products (Keela, Aplos, Raisely) being unified into one platform, and that's the honest watch-out: integration between them is newer than the marketing suggests, so check how deeply the pieces actually connect for your workflow before committing. Costs also stack per product and per contact count — a growing donor base raises the CRM bill. For nonprofits though, purpose-built beats adapted business software in fund accounting specifically.

VidPal is genuinely best for creators and small brands running faceless or topic-based channels that want the trend-find, generate and auto-publish loop handled in one tool across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. Skip it if you want hands-on creative control over every video, or your brand can't afford auto-published AI content going out without a human check.

(price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Free: 4 lifetime credits, standard-quality exports, "Made with Vidpal.ai" watermark, no card. Starter $12/mo billed annually ($144/yr) or $24 monthly, 15 credits/mo; Pro $23/mo annually ($276/yr) or $46 monthly, 40 credits, auto-publish and scheduling, 2K exports; Business $41/mo annually ($492/yr) or $82 monthly, 100 credits, 4K, three daily slots; Enterprise on quote. One credit is a Reel, a carousel, an editing upload or ten minutes of clip source; an AI Avatar or long-form video is five. Monthly credits do not roll over, annual credits arrive as a yearly pool, and top-up packs expire after 60 days. Refunds cover the unused credit balance within 30 days. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with VidPal?
answers.a: Credits don't carry over month to month, and a few users report slow support/account responses — so run the free plan through a full create-and-publish loop before you pay.

Vida AI is genuinely best for agencies, MSPs and service providers that want to deploy and resell white-label AI voice agents at volume, and that can absorb a scoped pilot before they ever see a production price. Skip it if you're one business wanting one AI receptionist and need a published monthly price to compare (Vida quotes everything after a pilot starting at $1,500), or your call flows are too high-stakes to automate yet.

answers.q: How much does Vida AI cost?
answers.a: (price re-verified 2026-09-10) Vida publishes no public pricing: no plan ladder, no monthly tier and no per-minute rate. Every deployment starts with a scoped pilot from $1,500, credited toward your first month in production, and the production price arrives as a quote afterwards. Its pricing page sells that process — a discovery call of twenty to thirty minutes, scoping and a proof of concept in one to two business days that you sign off before anything is built, an agent build and live pilot in two to ten business days, then production — while the feature table beneath it lists agent, reseller, support and compliance capabilities with no price attached to any of them. All plans are subject to fair use, and the page warns that SMS campaign registration may take up to two weeks. Read 10 September 2026 across vida.io/pricing, /partners, /affiliates, /platform, /features and /faq, all reached from the site's own sitemap: that pilot figure is the only customer-facing number on the site, and the commission tiers on /affiliates are what a reseller earns rather than what a buyer pays. Correction to our own earlier dossier: an agency ladder of about $750 a month for 5 agents and roughly 2,500 AI voice minutes, plus platform plans from about $2,500 and the per-minute rate we derived from them, appear nowhere on vida.io. Always verify the live price.

answers.q: What is the catch with Vida AI?
answers.a: This is priced for agencies and telecoms reselling AI phone agents, not for a single small business wanting one receptionist bot. Every deployment starts with a scoped pilot from $1,500, credited toward your first month, and the production price arrives as a quote afterwards — so you cannot compare it on price until you have spent money finding out. And the universal truth of voice AI: demo calls are rehearsed, your callers aren't. Pilot it on your real call types (accents, interruptions, edge requests) and measure containment rate before betting the front desk on it.

Vista Social is genuinely best for agencies and multi-brand teams that want scheduling, listening, reviews and reporting across many profiles at a notably lower price than legacy suites. Skip it if you manage one or two profiles (free/native tools suffice), or you need enterprise-grade approval chains and support SLAs the big suites specialize in.

answers.q: How much does Vista Social cost?
answers.a: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Professional $79/mo ($758/yr) — 15 profiles, 2 users, 10,000 DM contacts, 1,000 AI credits/mo; Advanced $149/mo ($1,430/yr) — 30 profiles, 4 users, 25,000 contacts, 2,000 credits, Zapier/Make/MCP; Scale $349/mo ($3,638/yr) — 70 profiles, 8 users, 100,000 contacts, 3,500 credits, white label and client connect; Enterprise custom with unlimited profiles and users. Yearly billing is 20% off on Professional and Advanced but 13% on Scale.
